verses.original: εἰ δὲ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου ὁ δεξιὸς σκανδαλίζει σε, ἔξελε αὐτὸν καὶ βάλε ἀπὸ σοῦ, συμφέρει γάρ σοι ἵνα ἀπόληται ἓν τῶν μελῶν σου καὶ μὴ ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου βληθῇ εἰς γέενναν.
verses.translit: ei de o ofthalmos soy o dexios skandalizei se, exele auton kai vale apo sou, symferei gar soi ina apolitai en ton melon soy kai me olon to soma soy vlithe eis geennan.
verses.translation: And if thy right eye offend thee, pluck it out, and cast it from thee: for it is profitable for thee that one of thy members should perish, and not that thy whole body should be cast into hell.

verses.original: καὶ εἰ ἡ δεξιά σου χεὶρ σκανδαλίζει σε, ἔκκοψον αὐτὴν καὶ βάλε ἀπὸ σοῦ, συμφέρει γάρ σοι ἵνα ἀπόληται ἓν τῶν μελῶν σου καὶ μὴ ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου ⸂εἰς γέενναν ἀπέλθῃ⸃.
verses.translit: kai ei e dexia soy heir skandalizei se, ekkopson auten kai vale apo sou, symferei gar soi ina apolitai en ton melon soy kai me olon to soma soy eis geennan apelthe.
verses.translation: And if thy right hand offend thee, cut it off, and cast it from thee: for it is profitable for thee that one of thy members should perish, and not that thy whole body should be cast into hell.

verses.original: Ἐρρέθη ⸀δέ· Ὃς ἂν ἀπολύσῃ τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ, δότω αὐτῇ ἀποστάσιον.
verses.translit: Errethi de* Os an apolyse ten gynaika autou, doto aute apostasion.
verses.translation: It hath been said, Whosoever shall put away his wife, let him give her a writing of divorcement:

verses.original: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ⸂πᾶς ὁ ἀπολύων⸃ τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ παρεκτὸς λόγου πορνείας ποιεῖ αὐτὴν ⸀μοιχευθῆναι, καὶ ὃς ἐὰν ἀπολελυμένην γαμήσῃ μοιχᾶται.
verses.translit: ego de lego umin oti pas o apolyon ten gynaika autou parektos logoy porneias poiei auten moiheythenai, kai os ean apolelymenin gamise moihatai.
verses.translation: But I say unto you, That whosoever shall put away his wife, saving for the cause of fornication, causeth her to commit adultery: and whosoever shall marry her that is divorced committeth adultery.

verses.original: Πάλιν ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη τοῖς ἀρχαίοις· Οὐκ ἐπιορκήσεις, ἀποδώσεις δὲ τῷ κυρίῳ τοὺς ὅρκους σου.
verses.translit: Palin ekoysate oti errethi tois arhaiois* Ouk epiorkiseis, apodoseis de to kyrio tous orkoys soy.
verses.translation: Again, ye have heard that it hath been said by them of old time, Thou shalt not forswear thyself, but shalt perform unto the Lord thine oaths:

verses.original: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν μὴ ὀμόσαι ὅλως· μήτε ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, ὅτι θρόνος ἐστὶν τοῦ θεοῦ·
verses.translit: ego de lego umin me omosai olos* mite en to ourano, oti thronos estin tou theou*
verses.translation: But I say unto you, Swear not at all; neither by heaven; for it is God’s throne:

verses.original: μήτε ἐν τῇ γῇ, ὅτι ὑποπόδιόν ἐστιν τῶν ποδῶν αὐτοῦ· μήτε εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα, ὅτι πόλις ἐστὶν τοῦ μεγάλου βασιλέως·
verses.translit: mite en te ge, oti upopodion estin ton podon autou* mite eis Ierosolyma, oti polis estin tou megaloy vasileos*
verses.translation: Nor by the earth; for it is his footstool: neither by Jerusalem; for it is the city of the great King.

verses.original: μήτε ἐν τῇ κεφαλῇ σου ὀμόσῃς, ὅτι οὐ δύνασαι μίαν τρίχα λευκὴν ⸂ποιῆσαι ἢ μέλαιναν⸃.
verses.translit: mite en te kefale soy omoses, oti ou dynasai mian triha leyken poiesai e melainan.
verses.translation: Neither shalt thou swear by thy head, because thou canst not make one hair white or black.

verses.original: ἔστω δὲ ὁ λόγος ὑμῶν ναὶ ναί, οὒ οὔ· τὸ δὲ περισσὸν τούτων ἐκ τοῦ πονηροῦ ἐστιν.
verses.translit: esto de o logos umon nai nai, ou ou* to de perisson toyton ek tou ponirou estin.
verses.translation: But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.

verses.original: Ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη· Ὀφθαλμὸν ἀντὶ ὀφθαλμοῦ καὶ ὀδόντα ἀντὶ ὀδόντος.
verses.translit: Ekoysate oti errethi* Ofthalmon anti ofthalmou kai odonta anti odontos.
verses.translation: Ye have heard that it hath been said, An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth:

verses.original: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν μὴ ἀντιστῆναι τῷ πονηρῷ· ἀλλʼ ὅστις σε ⸀ῥαπίζει ⸀εἰς τὴν δεξιὰν ⸀σιαγόνα, στρέψον αὐτῷ καὶ τὴν ἄλλην·
verses.translit: ego de lego umin me antistenai to poniro* all' ostis se Rapizei eis ten dexian siagona, strepson auto kai ten allin*
verses.translation: But I say unto you, That ye resist not evil: but whosoever shall smite thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also.

verses.original: καὶ τῷ θέλοντί σοι κριθῆναι καὶ τὸν χιτῶνά σου λαβεῖν, ἄφες αὐτῷ καὶ τὸ ἱμάτιον·
verses.translit: kai to thelonti soi krithenai kai ton hitona soy lavein, afes auto kai to imation*
verses.translation: And if any man will sue thee at the law, and take away thy coat, let him have thy cloke also.

verses.original: καὶ ὅστις σε ἀγγαρεύσει μίλιον ἕν, ὕπαγε μετʼ αὐτοῦ δύο.
verses.translit: kai ostis se aggareysei milion en, upage met' autou dyo.
verses.translation: And whosoever shall compel thee to go a mile, go with him twain.

verses.original: τῷ αἰτοῦντί σε ⸀δός, καὶ τὸν θέλοντα ἀπὸ σοῦ δανίσασθαι μὴ ἀποστραφῇς.
verses.translit: to aitounti se dos, kai ton thelonta apo sou danisasthai me apostrafes.
verses.translation: Give to him that asketh thee, and from him that would borrow of thee turn not thou away.

verses.original: Ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη· Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου καὶ μισήσεις τὸν ἐχθρόν σου.
verses.translit: Ekoysate oti errethi* Agapiseis ton plision soy kai misiseis ton ehthron soy.
verses.translation: Ye have heard that it hath been said, Thou shalt love thy neighbour, and hate thine enemy.

verses.original: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς ἐχθροὺς ⸀ὑμῶν καὶ προσεύχεσθε ὑπὲρ ⸀τῶν διωκόντων ὑμᾶς·
verses.translit: ego de lego umin, agapate tous ehthrous umon kai proseyhesthe uper ton diokonton umas*
verses.translation: But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you;

verses.original: ὅπως γένησθε υἱοὶ τοῦ πατρὸς ὑμῶν τοῦ ⸀ἐν οὐρανοῖς, ὅτι τὸν ἥλιον αὐτοῦ ἀνατέλλει ἐπὶ πονηροὺς καὶ ἀγαθοὺς καὶ βρέχει ἐπὶ δικαίους καὶ ἀδίκους.
verses.translit: opos genisthe yioi tou patros umon tou en ouranois, oti ton elion autou anatellei epi ponirous kai agathous kai vrehei epi dikaioys kai adikoys.
verses.translation: That ye may be the children of your Father which is in heaven: for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust.

verses.original: ἐὰν γὰρ ἀγαπήσητε τοὺς ἀγαπῶντας ὑμᾶς, τίνα μισθὸν ἔχετε; οὐχὶ καὶ οἱ τελῶναι ⸂τὸ αὐτὸ⸃ ποιοῦσιν;
verses.translit: ean gar agapisite tous agapontas umas, tina misthon ehete; ouhi kai oi telonai to auto poiousin;
verses.translation: For if ye love them which love you, what reward have ye? do not even the publicans the same?

verses.original: καὶ ἐὰν ἀσπάσησθε τοὺς ⸀ἀδελφοὺς ὑμῶν μόνον, τί περισσὸν ποιεῖτε; οὐχὶ καὶ οἱ ⸀ἐθνικοὶ ⸂τὸ αὐτὸ⸃ ποιοῦσιν;
verses.translit: kai ean aspasisthe tous adelfous umon monon, ti perisson poieite; ouhi kai oi ethnikoi to auto poiousin;
verses.translation: And if ye salute your brethren only, what do ye more than others ? do not even the publicans so?

verses.original: Ἔσεσθε οὖν ὑμεῖς τέλειοι ⸀ὡς ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ ⸀οὐράνιος τέλειός ἐστιν.
verses.translit: Esesthe oun umeis teleioi os o pater umon o ouranios teleios estin.
verses.translation: Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.

verses.original: Προσέχετε ⸀δὲ τὴν ⸀δικαιοσύνην ὑμῶν μὴ ποιεῖν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων πρὸς τὸ θεαθῆναι αὐτοῖς· εἰ δὲ μή γε, μισθὸν οὐκ ἔχετε παρὰ τῷ πατρὶ ὑμῶν τῷ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.
verses.translit: Prosehete de ten dikaiosynin umon me poiein emprosthen ton anthropon pros to theathenai autois* ei de mi ge, misthon ouk ehete para to patri umon to en tois ouranois.
verses.translation: Take heed that ye do not your alms before men, to be seen of them: otherwise ye have no reward of your Father which is in heaven.

verses.original: Ὅταν οὖν ποιῇς ἐλεημοσύνην, μὴ σαλπίσῃς ἔμπροσθέν σου, ὥσπερ οἱ ὑποκριταὶ ποιοῦσιν ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ ἐν ταῖς ῥύμαις, ὅπως δοξασθῶσιν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων· ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀπέχουσιν τὸν μισθὸν αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: Otan oun poies eleimosynin, me salpises emprosthen soy, osper oi upokritai poiousin en tais synagogais kai en tais Rymais, opos doxasthosin upo ton anthropon* amen lego umin, apehoysin ton misthon auton.
verses.translation: Therefore when thou doest thine alms, do not sound a trumpet before thee, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, that they may have glory of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.

verses.original: σοῦ δὲ ποιοῦντος ἐλεημοσύνην μὴ γνώτω ἡ ἀριστερά σου τί ποιεῖ ἡ δεξιά σου,
verses.translit: sou de poiountos eleimosynin me gnoto e aristera soy ti poiei e dexia soy,
verses.translation: But when thou doest alms, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth:

verses.original: ὅπως ᾖ σου ἡ ἐλεημοσύνη ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ· καὶ ὁ πατήρ σου ὁ βλέπων ἐν τῷ ⸀κρυπτῷ ἀποδώσει ⸀σοι.
verses.translit: opos e soy e eleimosyni en to krypto* kai o patir soy o vlepon en to krypto apodosei soi.
verses.translation: That thine alms may be in secret: and thy Father which seeth in secret himself shall reward thee openly.

verses.original: Καὶ ὅταν ⸂προσεύχησθε, οὐκ ἔσεσθε ὡς⸃ οἱ ὑποκριταί· ὅτι φιλοῦσιν ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ ἐν ταῖς γωνίαις τῶν πλατειῶν ἑστῶτες προσεύχεσθαι, ⸀ὅπως φανῶσιν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις· ἀμὴν λέγω ⸀ὑμῖν, ἀπέχουσι τὸν μισθὸν αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: Kai otan proseyhisthe, ouk esesthe os oi upokritai* oti filousin en tais synagogais kai en tais goniais ton plateion estotes proseyhesthai, opos fanosin tois anthropois* amen lego umin, apehoysi ton misthon auton.
verses.translation: And when thou prayest, thou shalt not be as the hypocrites are : for they love to pray standing in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.

verses.original: σὺ δὲ ὅταν προσεύχῃ, εἴσελθε εἰς τὸ ταμεῖόν σου καὶ κλείσας τὴν θύραν σου πρόσευξαι τῷ πατρί σου τῷ ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ· καὶ ὁ πατήρ σου ὁ βλέπων ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ ἀποδώσει ⸀σοι.
verses.translit: su de otan proseyhe, eiselthe eis to tameion soy kai kleisas ten thyran soy proseyxai to patri soy to en to krypto* kai o patir soy o vlepon en to krypto apodosei soi.
verses.translation: But thou, when thou prayest, enter into thy closet, and when thou hast shut thy door, pray to thy Father which is in secret; and thy Father which seeth in secret shall reward thee openly.

verses.original: Προσευχόμενοι δὲ μὴ βατταλογήσητε ὥσπερ οἱ ἐθνικοί, δοκοῦσιν γὰρ ὅτι ἐν τῇ πολυλογίᾳ αὐτῶν εἰσακουσθήσονται·
verses.translit: Proseyhomenoi de me vattalogisite osper oi ethnikoi, dokousin gar oti en te polylogia auton eisakoysthisontai*
verses.translation: But when ye pray, use not vain repetitions, as the heathen do : for they think that they shall be heard for their much speaking.

verses.original: μὴ οὖν ὁμοιωθῆτε αὐτοῖς, οἶδεν γὰρ ⸀ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὧν χρείαν ἔχετε πρὸ τοῦ ὑμᾶς αἰτῆσαι αὐτόν.
verses.translit: me oun omoiothete autois, oiden gar o pater umon on hreian ehete pro tou umas aitesai auton.
verses.translation: Be not ye therefore like unto them: for your Father knoweth what things ye have need of, before ye ask him.

verses.original: Οὕτως οὖν προσεύχεσθε ὑμεῖς· Πάτερ ἡμῶν ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς· ἁγιασθήτω τὸ ὄνομά σου,
verses.translit: Outos oun proseyhesthe umeis* Pater emon o en tois ouranois* agiasthito to onoma soy,
verses.translation: After this manner therefore pray ye: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name.

verses.original: ἐλθέτω ἡ βασιλεία σου, γενηθήτω τὸ θέλημά σου, ὡς ἐν οὐρανῷ καὶ ⸀ἐπὶ γῆς·
verses.translit: eltheto e vasileia soy, genithito to thelima soy, os en ourano kai epi ges*
verses.translation: Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven.

verses.original: τὸν ἄρτον ἡμῶν τὸν ἐπιούσιον δὸς ἡμῖν σήμερον·
verses.translit: ton arton emon ton epioysion dos emin simeron*
verses.translation: Give us this day our daily bread.

verses.original: καὶ ἄφες ἡμῖν τὰ ὀφειλήματα ἡμῶν, ὡς καὶ ἡμεῖς ⸀ἀφήκαμεν τοῖς ὀφειλέταις ἡμῶν·
verses.translit: kai afes emin ta ofeilimata emon, os kai emeis afikamen tois ofeiletais emon*
verses.translation: And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors.

verses.original: καὶ μὴ εἰσενέγκῃς ἡμᾶς εἰς πειρασμόν, ἀλλὰ ῥῦσαι ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ τοῦ ⸀πονηροῦ.
verses.translit: kai me eisenegkes emas eis peirasmon, alla Rusai emas apo tou ponirou.
verses.translation: And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil: For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.

verses.original: ἐὰν γὰρ ἀφῆτε τοῖς ἀνθρώποις τὰ παραπτώματα αὐτῶν, ἀφήσει καὶ ὑμῖν ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος·
verses.translit: ean gar afete tois anthropois ta paraptomata auton, afisei kai umin o pater umon o ouranios*
verses.translation: For if ye forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you:

verses.original: ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ἀφῆτε τοῖς ⸀ἀνθρώποις, οὐδὲ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ἀφήσει τὰ παραπτώματα ὑμῶν.
verses.translit: ean de me afete tois anthropois, oude o pater umon afisei ta paraptomata umon.
verses.translation: But if ye forgive not men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.

verses.original: Ὅταν δὲ νηστεύητε, μὴ γίνεσθε ⸀ὡς οἱ ὑποκριταὶ σκυθρωποί, ἀφανίζουσιν γὰρ τὰ πρόσωπα αὐτῶν ὅπως φανῶσιν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις νηστεύοντες· ἀμὴν λέγω ⸀ὑμῖν, ἀπέχουσιν τὸν μισθὸν αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: Otan de nisteyite, me ginesthe os oi upokritai skythropoi, afanizoysin gar ta prosopa auton opos fanosin tois anthropois nisteyontes* amen lego umin, apehoysin ton misthon auton.
verses.translation: Moreover when ye fast, be not, as the hypocrites, of a sad countenance: for they disfigure their faces, that they may appear unto men to fast. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.

verses.original: σὺ δὲ νηστεύων ἄλειψαί σου τὴν κεφαλὴν καὶ τὸ πρόσωπόν σου νίψαι,
verses.translit: su de nisteyon aleipsai soy ten kefalen kai to prosopon soy nipsai,
verses.translation: But thou, when thou fastest, anoint thine head, and wash thy face;

verses.original: ὅπως μὴ φανῇς τοῖς ἀνθρώποις νηστεύων ἀλλὰ τῷ πατρί σου τῷ ἐν τῷ ⸀κρυφαίῳ· καὶ ὁ πατήρ σου ὁ βλέπων ἐν τῷ ⸁κρυφαίῳ ἀποδώσει σοι.
verses.translit: opos me fanes tois anthropois nisteyon alla to patri soy to en to kryfaio* kai o patir soy o vlepon en to kryfaio apodosei soi.
verses.translation: That thou appear not unto men to fast, but unto thy Father which is in secret: and thy Father, which seeth in secret, shall reward thee openly.

verses.original: Μὴ θησαυρίζετε ὑμῖν θησαυροὺς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ὅπου σὴς καὶ βρῶσις ἀφανίζει, καὶ ὅπου κλέπται διορύσσουσιν καὶ κλέπτουσιν·
verses.translit: Me thisayrizete umin thisayrous epi tes ges, opoy ses kai vrosis afanizei, kai opoy kleptai dioryssoysin kai kleptoysin*
verses.translation: Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal:

verses.original: θησαυρίζετε δὲ ὑμῖν θησαυροὺς ἐν οὐρανῷ, ὅπου οὔτε σὴς οὔτε βρῶσις ἀφανίζει, καὶ ὅπου κλέπται οὐ διορύσσουσιν οὐδὲ κλέπτουσιν·
verses.translit: thisayrizete de umin thisayrous en ourano, opoy oute ses oute vrosis afanizei, kai opoy kleptai ou dioryssoysin oude kleptoysin*
verses.translation: But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal:

verses.original: ὅπου γάρ ἐστιν ὁ θησαυρός ⸀σου, ἐκεῖ ἔσται καὶ ἡ καρδία ⸁σου.
verses.translit: opoy gar estin o thisayros soy, ekei estai kai e kardia soy.
verses.translation: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.

verses.original: Ὁ λύχνος τοῦ σώματός ἐστιν ὁ ὀφθαλμός. ἐὰν οὖν ⸂ᾖ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου ἁπλοῦς⸃, ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου φωτεινὸν ἔσται·
verses.translit: O lyhnos tou somatos estin o ofthalmos. ean oun e o ofthalmos soy aplous, olon to soma soy foteinon estai*
verses.translation: The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light.

verses.original: ἐὰν δὲ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου πονηρὸς ᾖ, ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου σκοτεινὸν ἔσται. εἰ οὖν τὸ φῶς τὸ ἐν σοὶ σκότος ἐστίν, τὸ σκότος πόσον.
verses.translit: ean de o ofthalmos soy poniros e, olon to soma soy skoteinon estai. ei oun to fos to en soi skotos estin, to skotos poson.
verses.translation: But if thine eye be evil, thy whole body shall be full of darkness. If therefore the light that is in thee be darkness, how great is that darkness!

verses.original: Οὐδεὶς δύναται δυσὶ κυρίοις δουλεύειν· ἢ γὰρ τὸν ἕνα μισήσει καὶ τὸν ἕτερον ἀγαπήσει, ἢ ἑνὸς ἀνθέξεται καὶ τοῦ ἑτέρου καταφρονήσει. οὐ δύνασθε θεῷ δουλεύειν καὶ μαμωνᾷ.
verses.translit: Oudeis dynatai dysi kyriois doyleyein* e gar ton ena misisei kai ton eteron agapisei, e enos anthexetai kai tou eteroy katafronisei. ou dynasthe theo doyleyein kai mamona.
verses.translation: No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.

verses.original: Διὰ τοῦτο λέγω ὑμῖν· μὴ μεριμνᾶτε τῇ ψυχῇ ὑμῶν τί ⸀φάγητε, μηδὲ τῷ σώματι ὑμῶν τί ἐνδύσησθε· οὐχὶ ἡ ψυχὴ πλεῖόν ἐστι τῆς τροφῆς καὶ τὸ σῶμα τοῦ ἐνδύματος;
verses.translit: Dia touto lego umin* me merimnate te psyhe umon ti fagite, mide to somati umon ti endysisthe* ouhi e psyhe pleion esti tes trofes kai to soma tou endymatos;
verses.translation: Therefore I say unto you, Take no thought for your life, what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink; nor yet for your body, what ye shall put on. Is not the life more than meat, and the body than raiment?

verses.original: ἐμβλέψατε εἰς τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ὅτι οὐ σπείρουσιν οὐδὲ θερίζουσιν οὐδὲ συνάγουσιν εἰς ἀποθήκας, καὶ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος τρέφει αὐτά· οὐχ ὑμεῖς μᾶλλον διαφέρετε αὐτῶν;
verses.translit: emvlepsate eis ta peteina tou ouranou oti ou speiroysin oude therizoysin oude synagoysin eis apothikas, kai o pater umon o ouranios trefei auta* ouh umeis mallon diaferete auton;
verses.translation: Behold the fowls of the air: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are ye not much better than they?

verses.original: τίς δὲ ἐξ ὑμῶν μεριμνῶν δύναται προσθεῖναι ἐπὶ τὴν ἡλικίαν αὐτοῦ πῆχυν ἕνα;
verses.translit: tis de ex umon merimnon dynatai prostheinai epi ten elikian autou pehyn ena;
verses.translation: Which of you by taking thought can add one cubit unto his stature?

verses.original: καὶ περὶ ἐνδύματος τί μεριμνᾶτε; καταμάθετε τὰ κρίνα τοῦ ἀγροῦ πῶς ⸂αὐξάνουσιν· οὐ κοπιῶσιν οὐδὲ νήθουσιν⸃·
verses.translit: kai peri endymatos ti merimnate; katamathete ta krina tou agrou pos auxanoysin* ou kopiosin oude nithoysin*
verses.translation: And why take ye thought for raiment? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow; they toil not, neither do they spin:

verses.original: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδὲ Σολομὼν ἐν πάσῃ τῇ δόξῃ αὐτοῦ περιεβάλετο ὡς ἓν τούτων.
verses.translit: lego de umin oti oude Solomon en pase te doxe autou perievaleto os en toyton.
verses.translation: And yet I say unto you, That even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.

verses.original: εἰ δὲ τὸν χόρτον τοῦ ἀγροῦ σήμερον ὄντα καὶ αὔριον εἰς κλίβανον βαλλόμενον ὁ θεὸς οὕτως ἀμφιέννυσιν, οὐ πολλῷ μᾶλλον ὑμᾶς, ὀλιγόπιστοι;
verses.translit: ei de ton horton tou agrou simeron onta kai aurion eis klivanon vallomenon o theos outos amfiennysin, ou pollo mallon umas, oligopistoi;
verses.translation: Wherefore, if God so clothe the grass of the field, which to day is, and to morrow is cast into the oven, shall he not much more clothe you, O ye of little faith?

verses.original: μὴ οὖν μεριμνήσητε λέγοντες· Τί φάγωμεν; ἤ· Τί πίωμεν; ἤ· Τί περιβαλώμεθα;
verses.translit: me oun merimnisite legontes* Ti fagomen; e* Ti piomen; e* Ti perivalometha;
verses.translation: Therefore take no thought, saying, What shall we eat? or, What shall we drink? or, Wherewithal shall we be clothed?

verses.original: πάντα γὰρ ταῦτα τὰ ἔθνη ⸀ἐπιζητοῦσιν· οἶδεν γὰρ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος ὅτι χρῄζετε τούτων ἁπάντων.
verses.translit: panta gar tauta ta ethni epizitousin* oiden gar o pater umon o ouranios oti hrezete toyton apanton.
verses.translation: (For after all these things do the Gentiles seek:) for your heavenly Father knoweth that ye have need of all these things.

verses.original: ζητεῖτε δὲ πρῶτον τὴν ⸀βασιλείαν καὶ τὴν δικαιοσύνην αὐτοῦ, καὶ ταῦτα πάντα προστεθήσεται ὑμῖν.
verses.translit: ziteite de proton ten vasileian kai ten dikaiosynin autou, kai tauta panta prostethisetai umin.
verses.translation: But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.

verses.original: μὴ οὖν μεριμνήσητε εἰς τὴν αὔριον, ἡ γὰρ αὔριον μεριμνήσει ⸀αὑτῆς· ἀρκετὸν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἡ κακία αὐτῆς.
verses.translit: me oun merimnisite eis ten aurion, e gar aurion merimnisei autes* arketon te emera e kakia autes.
verses.translation: Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.

verses.original: Μὴ κρίνετε, ἵνα μὴ κριθῆτε·
verses.translit: Me krinete, ina me krithete*
verses.translation: Judge not, that ye be not judged.

verses.original: ἐν ᾧ γὰρ κρίματι κρίνετε κριθήσεσθε, καὶ ἐν ᾧ μέτρῳ μετρεῖτε μετρηθήσεται ὑμῖν.
verses.translit: en o gar krimati krinete krithisesthe, kai en o metro metreite metrithisetai umin.
verses.translation: For with what judgment ye judge, ye shall be judged: and with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured to you again.

verses.original: τί δὲ βλέπεις τὸ κάρφος τὸ ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου, τὴν δὲ ἐν τῷ σῷ ὀφθαλμῷ δοκὸν οὐ κατανοεῖς;
verses.translit: ti de vlepeis to karfos to en to ofthalmo tou adelfou soy, ten de en to so ofthalmo dokon ou katanoeis;
verses.translation: And why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brother’s eye, but considerest not the beam that is in thine own eye?

verses.original: ἢ πῶς ἐρεῖς τῷ ἀδελφῷ σου· Ἄφες ἐκβάλω τὸ κάρφος ⸀ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ σου, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἡ δοκὸς ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ σοῦ;
verses.translit: e pos ereis to adelfo soy* Afes ekvalo to karfos ek tou ofthalmou soy, kai idou e dokos en to ofthalmo sou;
verses.translation: Or how wilt thou say to thy brother, Let me pull out the mote out of thine eye; and, behold, a beam is in thine own eye?

verses.original: ὑποκριτά, ἔκβαλε πρῶτον ⸂ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ σοῦ τὴν δοκόν⸃, καὶ τότε διαβλέψεις ἐκβαλεῖν τὸ κάρφος ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου.
verses.translit: upokrita, ekvale proton ek tou ofthalmou sou ten dokon, kai tote diavlepseis ekvalein to karfos ek tou ofthalmou tou adelfou soy.
verses.translation: Thou hypocrite, first cast out the beam out of thine own eye; and then shalt thou see clearly to cast out the mote out of thy brother’s eye.

verses.original: Μὴ δῶτε τὸ ἅγιον τοῖς κυσίν, μηδὲ βάλητε τοὺς μαργαρίτας ὑμῶν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν χοίρων, μήποτε ⸀καταπατήσουσιν αὐτοὺς ἐν τοῖς ποσὶν αὐτῶν καὶ στραφέντες ῥήξωσιν ὑμᾶς.
verses.translit: Me dote to agion tois kysin, mide valite tous margaritas umon emprosthen ton hoiron, mipote katapatisoysin autous en tois posin auton kai strafentes Rixosin umas.
verses.translation: Give not that which is holy unto the dogs, neither cast ye your pearls before swine, lest they trample them under their feet, and turn again and rend you.

verses.original: Αἰτεῖτε, καὶ δοθήσεται ὑμῖν· ζητεῖτε, καὶ εὑρήσετε· κρούετε, καὶ ἀνοιγήσεται ὑμῖν.
verses.translit: Aiteite, kai dothisetai umin* ziteite, kai eurisete* kroyete, kai anoigisetai umin.
verses.translation: Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you:

verses.original: πᾶς γὰρ ὁ αἰτῶν λαμβάνει καὶ ὁ ζητῶν εὑρίσκει καὶ τῷ κρούοντι ⸀ἀνοιγήσεται.
verses.translit: pas gar o aiton lamvanei kai o ziton euriskei kai to kroyonti anoigisetai.
verses.translation: For every one that asketh receiveth; and he that seeketh findeth; and to him that knocketh it shall be opened.

verses.original: ἢ τίς ⸀ἐστιν ἐξ ὑμῶν ἄνθρωπος, ὃν ⸀αἰτήσει ὁ υἱὸς αὐτοῦ ἄρτον— μὴ λίθον ἐπιδώσει αὐτῷ;
verses.translit: e tis estin ex umon anthropos, on aitisei o yios autou arton-- me lithon epidosei auto;
verses.translation: Or what man is there of you, whom if his son ask bread, will he give him a stone?

verses.original: ⸀ἢ καὶ ⸂ἰχθὺν αἰτήσει⸃— μὴ ὄφιν ἐπιδώσει αὐτῷ;
verses.translit: e kai ihthun aitisei-- me ofin epidosei auto;
verses.translation: Or if he ask a fish, will he give him a serpent?

verses.original: εἰ οὖν ὑμεῖς πονηροὶ ὄντες οἴδατε δόματα ἀγαθὰ διδόναι τοῖς τέκνοις ὑμῶν, πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς δώσει ἀγαθὰ τοῖς αἰτοῦσιν αὐτόν.
verses.translit: ei oun umeis poniroi ontes oidate domata agatha didonai tois teknois umon, poso mallon o pater umon o en tois ouranois dosei agatha tois aitousin auton.
verses.translation: If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children, how much more shall your Father which is in heaven give good things to them that ask him?

verses.original: Πάντα οὖν ὅσα ⸀ἐὰν θέλητε ἵνα ποιῶσιν ὑμῖν οἱ ἄνθρωποι, οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς ποιεῖτε αὐτοῖς· οὗτος γάρ ἐστιν ὁ νόμος καὶ οἱ προφῆται.
verses.translit: Panta oun osa ean thelite ina poiosin umin oi anthropoi, outos kai umeis poieite autois* outos gar estin o nomos kai oi profetai.
verses.translation: Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them: for this is the law and the prophets.

verses.original: Εἰσέλθατε διὰ τῆς στενῆς πύλης· ὅτι πλατεῖα ⸂ἡ πύλη⸃ καὶ εὐρύχωρος ἡ ὁδὸς ἡ ἀπάγουσα εἰς τὴν ἀπώλειαν, καὶ πολλοί εἰσιν οἱ εἰσερχόμενοι διʼ αὐτῆς·
verses.translit: Eiselthate dia tes stenes pylis* oti plateia e pyli kai euryhoros e odos e apagoysa eis ten apoleian, kai polloi eisin oi eiserhomenoi di' autes*
verses.translation: Enter ye in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat:

verses.original: ⸀ὅτι στενὴ ἡ πύλη καὶ τεθλιμμένη ἡ ὁδὸς ἡ ἀπάγουσα εἰς τὴν ζωήν, καὶ ὀλίγοι εἰσὶν οἱ εὑρίσκοντες αὐτήν.
verses.translit: oti stene e pyli kai tethlimmeni e odos e apagoysa eis ten zoin, kai oligoi eisin oi euriskontes autin.
verses.translation: Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it.

verses.original: ⸀Προσέχετε ἀπὸ τῶν ψευδοπροφητῶν, οἵτινες ἔρχονται πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐν ἐνδύμασι προβάτων ἔσωθεν δέ εἰσιν λύκοι ἅρπαγες.
verses.translit: Prosehete apo ton pseydoprofiton, oitines erhontai pros umas en endymasi provaton esothen de eisin lykoi arpages.
verses.translation: Beware of false prophets, which come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves.

verses.original: ἀπὸ τῶν καρπῶν αὐτῶν ἐπιγνώσεσθε αὐτούς. μήτι συλλέγουσιν ἀπὸ ἀκανθῶν ⸀σταφυλὰς ἢ ἀπὸ τριβόλων σῦκα;
verses.translit: apo ton karpon auton epignosesthe autoys. miti syllegoysin apo akanthon stafylas e apo trivolon suka;
verses.translation: Ye shall know them by their fruits. Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles?

verses.original: οὕτως πᾶν δένδρον ἀγαθὸν καρποὺς καλοὺς ποιεῖ, τὸ δὲ σαπρὸν δένδρον καρποὺς πονηροὺς ποιεῖ·
verses.translit: outos pan dendron agathon karpous kalous poiei, to de sapron dendron karpous ponirous poiei*
verses.translation: Even so every good tree bringeth forth good fruit; but a corrupt tree bringeth forth evil fruit.

verses.original: οὐ δύναται δένδρον ἀγαθὸν καρποὺς πονηροὺς ⸀ποιεῖν, οὐδὲ δένδρον σαπρὸν καρποὺς καλοὺς ποιεῖν.
verses.translit: ou dynatai dendron agathon karpous ponirous poiein, oude dendron sapron karpous kalous poiein.
verses.translation: A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit, neither can a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit.

verses.original: πᾶν δένδρον μὴ ποιοῦν καρπὸν καλὸν ἐκκόπτεται καὶ εἰς πῦρ βάλλεται.
verses.translit: pan dendron me poioun karpon kalon ekkoptetai kai eis pur valletai.
verses.translation: Every tree that bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire.

verses.original: ἄρα γε ἀπὸ τῶν καρπῶν αὐτῶν ἐπιγνώσεσθε αὐτούς.
verses.translit: ara ge apo ton karpon auton epignosesthe autoys.
verses.translation: Wherefore by their fruits ye shall know them.

verses.original: Οὐ πᾶς ὁ λέγων μοι· Κύριε κύριε εἰσελεύσεται εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν, ἀλλʼ ὁ ποιῶν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πατρός μου τοῦ ἐν ⸀τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.
verses.translit: Ou pas o legon moi* Kyrie kyrie eiseleysetai eis ten vasileian ton ouranon, all' o poion to thelima tou patros moy tou en tois ouranois.
verses.translation: Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven.

verses.original: πολλοὶ ἐροῦσίν μοι ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ· Κύριε κύριε, οὐ τῷ σῷ ὀνόματι ἐπροφητεύσαμεν, καὶ τῷ σῷ ὀνόματι δαιμόνια ἐξεβάλομεν, καὶ τῷ σῷ ὀνόματι δυνάμεις πολλὰς ἐποιήσαμεν;
verses.translit: polloi erousin moi en ekeine te emera* Kyrie kyrie, ou to so onomati eprofiteysamen, kai to so onomati daimonia exevalomen, kai to so onomati dynameis pollas epoiisamen;
verses.translation: Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name? and in thy name have cast out devils? and in thy name done many wonderful works?

verses.original: καὶ τότε ὁμολογήσω αὐτοῖς ὅτι Οὐδέποτε ἔγνων ὑμᾶς· ἀποχωρεῖτε ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ οἱ ἐργαζόμενοι τὴν ἀνομίαν.
verses.translit: kai tote omologiso autois oti Oudepote egnon umas* apohoreite ap' emou oi ergazomenoi ten anomian.
verses.translation: And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.

verses.original: Πᾶς οὖν ὅστις ἀκούει μου τοὺς λόγους τούτους καὶ ποιεῖ αὐτούς, ⸀ὁμοιωθήσεται ἀνδρὶ φρονίμῳ, ὅστις ᾠκοδόμησεν ⸂αὐτοῦ τὴν οἰκίαν⸃ ἐπὶ τὴν πέτραν.
verses.translit: Pas oun ostis akoyei moy tous logoys toytoys kai poiei autoys, omoiothisetai andri fronimo, ostis okodomisen autou ten oikian epi ten petran.
verses.translation: Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock:

verses.original: καὶ κατέβη ἡ βροχὴ καὶ ἦλθον οἱ ποταμοὶ καὶ ἔπνευσαν οἱ ἄνεμοι καὶ προσέπεσαν τῇ οἰκίᾳ ἐκείνῃ, καὶ οὐκ ἔπεσεν, τεθεμελίωτο γὰρ ἐπὶ τὴν πέτραν.
verses.translit: kai katevi e vrohe kai elthon oi potamoi kai epneysan oi anemoi kai prosepesan te oikia ekeine, kai ouk epesen, tethemelioto gar epi ten petran.
verses.translation: And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell not: for it was founded upon a rock.

verses.original: καὶ πᾶς ὁ ἀκούων μου τοὺς λόγους τούτους καὶ μὴ ποιῶν αὐτοὺς ὁμοιωθήσεται ἀνδρὶ μωρῷ, ὅστις ᾠκοδόμησεν ⸂αὐτοῦ τὴν οἰκίαν⸃ ἐπὶ τὴν ἄμμον.
verses.translit: kai pas o akoyon moy tous logoys toytoys kai me poion autous omoiothisetai andri moro, ostis okodomisen autou ten oikian epi ten ammon.
verses.translation: And every one that heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them not, shall be likened unto a foolish man, which built his house upon the sand:

verses.original: καὶ κατέβη ἡ βροχὴ καὶ ἦλθον οἱ ποταμοὶ καὶ ἔπνευσαν οἱ ἄνεμοι καὶ προσέκοψαν τῇ οἰκίᾳ ἐκείνῃ, καὶ ἔπεσεν, καὶ ἦν ἡ πτῶσις αὐτῆς μεγάλη.
verses.translit: kai katevi e vrohe kai elthon oi potamoi kai epneysan oi anemoi kai prosekopsan te oikia ekeine, kai epesen, kai en e ptosis autes megali.
verses.translation: And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell: and great was the fall of it.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ὅτε ⸀ἐτέλεσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοὺς λόγους τούτους, ἐξεπλήσσοντο οἱ ὄχλοι ἐπὶ τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ·
verses.translit: Kai egeneto ote etelesen o Iisous tous logoys toytoys, exeplissonto oi ohloi epi te didahe autou*
verses.translation: And it came to pass, when Jesus had ended these sayings, the people were astonished at his doctrine:

verses.original: ἦν γὰρ διδάσκων αὐτοὺς ὡς ἐξουσίαν ἔχων καὶ οὐχ ὡς οἱ γραμματεῖς ⸀αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: en gar didaskon autous os exoysian ehon kai ouh os oi grammateis auton.
verses.translation: For he taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.

verses.original: ⸂Καταβάντος δὲ αὐτοῦ⸃ ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄρους ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ ὄχλοι πολλοί.
verses.translit: Katavantos de autou apo tou oroys ekoloythisan auto ohloi polloi.
verses.translation: When he was come down from the mountain, great multitudes followed him.

verses.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ λεπρὸς ⸀προσελθὼν προσεκύνει αὐτῷ λέγων· Κύριε, ἐὰν θέλῃς δύνασαί με καθαρίσαι.
verses.translit: kai idou lepros proselthon prosekynei auto legon* Kyrie, ean theles dynasai me katharisai.
verses.translation: And, behold, there came a leper and worshipped him, saying, Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.

verses.original: καὶ ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα ἥψατο ⸀αὐτοῦ λέγων· Θέλω, καθαρίσθητι· καὶ εὐθέως ἐκαθαρίσθη αὐτοῦ ἡ λέπρα.
verses.translit: kai ekteinas ten heira epsato autou legon* Thelo, katharisthiti* kai eutheos ekatharisthi autou e lepra.
verses.translation: And Jesus put forth his hand, and touched him, saying, I will; be thou clean. And immediately his leprosy was cleansed.

verses.original: καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ὅρα μηδενὶ εἴπῃς, ἀλλὰ ὕπαγε σεαυτὸν δεῖξον τῷ ἱερεῖ, καὶ προσένεγκον τὸ δῶρον ὃ προσέταξεν Μωϋσῆς εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς.
verses.translit: kai legei auto o Iisous* Ora mideni eipes, alla upage seayton deixon to ierei, kai prosenegkon to doron o prosetaxen Moyses eis martyrion autois.
verses.translation: And Jesus saith unto him, See thou tell no man; but go thy way, shew thyself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.

verses.original: ⸂Εἰσελθόντος δὲ αὐτοῦ⸃ εἰς Καφαρναοὺμ προσῆλθεν αὐτῷ ἑκατόνταρχος παρακαλῶν αὐτὸν
verses.translit: Eiselthontos de autou eis Kafarnaoum proselthen auto ekatontarhos parakalon auton
verses.translation: And when Jesus was entered into Capernaum, there came unto him a centurion, beseeching him,

verses.original: καὶ λέγων· Κύριε, ὁ παῖς μου βέβληται ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ παραλυτικός, δεινῶς βασανιζόμενος.
verses.translit: kai legon* Kyrie, o pais moy vevlitai en te oikia paralytikos, deinos vasanizomenos.
verses.translation: And saying, Lord, my servant lieth at home sick of the palsy, grievously tormented.

verses.original: ⸀καὶ λέγει ⸀αὐτῷ· Ἐγὼ ἐλθὼν θεραπεύσω αὐτόν.
verses.translit: kai legei auto* Ego elthon therapeyso auton.
verses.translation: And Jesus saith unto him, I will come and heal him.

verses.original: ⸂καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς⸃ ὁ ἑκατόνταρχος ἔφη· Κύριε, οὐκ εἰμὶ ἱκανὸς ἵνα μου ὑπὸ τὴν στέγην εἰσέλθῃς· ἀλλὰ μόνον εἰπὲ λόγῳ, καὶ ἰαθήσεται ὁ παῖς μου·
verses.translit: kai apokritheis o ekatontarhos efi* Kyrie, ouk eimi ikanos ina moy upo ten stegin eiselthes* alla monon eipe logo, kai iathisetai o pais moy*
verses.translation: The centurion answered and said, Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldest come under my roof: but speak the word only, and my servant shall be healed.

verses.original: καὶ γὰρ ἐγὼ ἄνθρωπός εἰμι ὑπὸ ⸀ἐξουσίαν, ἔχων ὑπʼ ἐμαυτὸν στρατιώτας, καὶ λέγω τούτῳ· Πορεύθητι, καὶ πορεύεται, καὶ ἄλλῳ· Ἔρχου, καὶ ἔρχεται, καὶ τῷ δούλῳ μου· Ποίησον τοῦτο, καὶ ποιεῖ.
verses.translit: kai gar ego anthropos eimi upo exoysian, ehon up' emayton stratiotas, kai lego toyto* Poreythiti, kai poreyetai, kai allo* Erhoy, kai erhetai, kai to doylo moy* Poiison touto, kai poiei.
verses.translation: For I am a man under authority, having soldiers under me: and I say to this man , Go, and he goeth; and to another, Come, and he cometh; and to my servant, Do this, and he doeth it .

verses.original: ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐθαύμασεν καὶ εἶπεν τοῖς ἀκολουθοῦσιν· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ⸂παρʼ οὐδενὶ τοσαύτην πίστιν ἐν τῷ Ἰσραὴλ⸃ εὗρον.
verses.translit: akoysas de o Iisous ethaymasen kai eipen tois akoloythousin* Amen lego umin, par' oudeni tosaytin pistin en to Israel euron.
verses.translation: When Jesus heard it , he marvelled, and said to them that followed, Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel.

verses.original: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι πολλοὶ ἀπὸ ἀνατολῶν καὶ δυσμῶν ἥξουσιν καὶ ἀνακλιθήσονται μετὰ Ἀβραὰμ καὶ Ἰσαὰκ καὶ Ἰακὼβ ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν·
verses.translit: lego de umin oti polloi apo anatolon kai dysmon exoysin kai anaklithisontai meta Avraam kai Isaak kai Iakov en te vasileia ton ouranon*
verses.translation: And I say unto you, That many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ υἱοὶ τῆς βασιλείας ἐκβληθήσονται εἰς τὸ σκότος τὸ ἐξώτερον· ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων.
verses.translit: oi de yioi tes vasileias ekvlithisontai eis to skotos to exoteron* ekei estai o klaythmos kai o vrygmos ton odonton.
verses.translation: But the children of the kingdom shall be cast out into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

verses.original: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τῷ ἑκατοντάρχῃ· Ὕπαγε, ⸀ὡς ἐπίστευσας γενηθήτω σοι· καὶ ἰάθη ὁ ⸀παῖς ἐν τῇ ὥρᾳ ἐκείνῃ.
verses.translit: kai eipen o Iisous to ekatontarhe* Upage, os episteysas genithito soi* kai iathi o pais en te ora ekeine.
verses.translation: And Jesus said unto the centurion, Go thy way; and as thou hast believed, so be it done unto thee. And his servant was healed in the selfsame hour.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐλθὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν Πέτρου εἶδεν τὴν πενθερὰν αὐτοῦ βεβλημένην καὶ πυρέσσουσαν·
verses.translit: Kai elthon o Iisous eis ten oikian Petroy eiden ten pentheran autou vevlimenin kai pyressoysan*
verses.translation: And when Jesus was come into Peter’s house, he saw his wife’s mother laid, and sick of a fever.

verses.original: καὶ ἥψατο τῆς χειρὸς αὐτῆς, καὶ ἀφῆκεν αὐτὴν ὁ πυρετός, καὶ ἠγέρθη καὶ διηκόνει αὐτῷ.
verses.translit: kai epsato tes heiros autes, kai afeken auten o pyretos, kai egerthi kai diikonei auto.
verses.translation: And he touched her hand, and the fever left her: and she arose, and ministered unto them.

verses.original: Ὀψίας δὲ γενομένης προσήνεγκαν αὐτῷ δαιμονιζομένους πολλούς· καὶ ἐξέβαλεν τὰ πνεύματα λόγῳ, καὶ πάντας τοὺς κακῶς ἔχοντας ἐθεράπευσεν·
verses.translit: Opsias de genomenis prosinegkan auto daimonizomenoys polloys* kai exevalen ta pneymata logo, kai pantas tous kakos ehontas etherapeysen*
verses.translation: When the even was come, they brought unto him many that were possessed with devils: and he cast out the spirits with his word, and healed all that were sick:

verses.original: ὅπως πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ Ἠσαΐου τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος· Αὐτὸς τὰς ἀσθενείας ἡμῶν ἔλαβεν καὶ τὰς νόσους ἐβάστασεν.
verses.translit: opos plirothe to Rithen dia EsaIoy tou profitoy legontos* Autos tas astheneias emon elaven kai tas nosoys evastasen.
verses.translation: That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Esaias the prophet, saying, Himself took our infirmities, and bare our sicknesses.

verses.original: Ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ⸂πολλοὺς ὄχλους⸃ περὶ αὐτὸν ἐκέλευσεν ἀπελθεῖν εἰς τὸ πέραν.
verses.translit: Idon de o Iisous pollous ohloys peri auton ekeleysen apelthein eis to peran.
verses.translation: Now when Jesus saw great multitudes about him, he gave commandment to depart unto the other side.

verses.original: καὶ προσελθὼν εἷς γραμματεὺς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Διδάσκαλε, ἀκολουθήσω σοι ὅπου ἐὰν ἀπέρχῃ.
verses.translit: kai proselthon eis grammateus eipen auto* Didaskale, akoloythiso soi opoy ean aperhe.
verses.translation: And a certain scribe came, and said unto him, Master, I will follow thee whithersoever thou goest.

verses.original: καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Αἱ ἀλώπεκες φωλεοὺς ἔχουσιν καὶ τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ κατασκηνώσεις, ὁ δὲ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου οὐκ ἔχει ποῦ τὴν κεφαλὴν κλίνῃ.
verses.translit: kai legei auto o Iisous* Ai alopekes foleous ehoysin kai ta peteina tou ouranou kataskinoseis, o de yios tou anthropoy ouk ehei pou ten kefalen kline.
verses.translation: And Jesus saith unto him, The foxes have holes, and the birds of the air have nests; but the Son of man hath not where to lay his head.

verses.original: ἕτερος δὲ τῶν ⸀μαθητῶν εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Κύριε, ἐπίτρεψόν μοι πρῶτον ἀπελθεῖν καὶ θάψαι τὸν πατέρα μου.
verses.translit: eteros de ton mathiton eipen auto* Kyrie, epitrepson moi proton apelthein kai thapsai ton patera moy.
verses.translation: And another of his disciples said unto him, Lord, suffer me first to go and bury my father.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ⸀λέγει αὐτῷ· Ἀκολούθει μοι, καὶ ἄφες τοὺς νεκροὺς θάψαι τοὺς ἑαυτῶν νεκρούς.
verses.translit: o de Iisous legei auto* Akoloythei moi, kai afes tous nekrous thapsai tous eayton nekroys.
verses.translation: But Jesus said unto him, Follow me; and let the dead bury their dead.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐμβάντι αὐτῷ ⸀εἰς πλοῖον ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: Kai emvanti auto eis ploion ekoloythisan auto oi mathitai autou.
verses.translation: And when he was entered into a ship, his disciples followed him.

verses.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ σεισμὸς μέγας ἐγένετο ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ, ὥστε τὸ πλοῖον καλύπτεσθαι ὑπὸ τῶν κυμάτων, αὐτὸς δὲ ἐκάθευδεν.
verses.translit: kai idou seismos megas egeneto en te thalasse, oste to ploion kalyptesthai upo ton kymaton, autos de ekatheyden.
verses.translation: And, behold, there arose a great tempest in the sea, insomuch that the ship was covered with the waves: but he was asleep.

verses.original: καὶ ⸀προσελθόντες ἤγειραν αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Κύριε, ⸀σῶσον, ἀπολλύμεθα.
verses.translit: kai proselthontes egeiran auton legontes* Kyrie, soson, apollymetha.
verses.translation: And his disciples came to him , and awoke him, saying, Lord, save us: we perish.

verses.original: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τί δειλοί ἐστε, ὀλιγόπιστοι; τότε ἐγερθεὶς ἐπετίμησεν τοῖς ἀνέμοις καὶ τῇ θαλάσσῃ, καὶ ἐγένετο γαλήνη μεγάλη.
verses.translit: kai legei autois* Ti deiloi este, oligopistoi; tote egertheis epetimisen tois anemois kai te thalasse, kai egeneto galini megali.
verses.translation: And he saith unto them, Why are ye fearful, O ye of little faith? Then he arose, and rebuked the winds and the sea; and there was a great calm.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ ἄνθρωποι ἐθαύμασαν λέγοντες· Ποταπός ἐστιν οὗτος ὅτι καὶ οἱ ἄνεμοι καὶ ἡ θάλασσα ⸂αὐτῷ ὑπακούουσιν⸃;
verses.translit: oi de anthropoi ethaymasan legontes* Potapos estin outos oti kai oi anemoi kai e thalassa auto upakoyoysin;
verses.translation: But the men marvelled, saying, What manner of man is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him!

verses.original: Καὶ ⸂ἐλθόντος αὐτοῦ⸃ εἰς τὸ πέραν εἰς τὴν χώραν τῶν ⸀Γαδαρηνῶν ὑπήντησαν αὐτῷ δύο δαιμονιζόμενοι ἐκ τῶν μνημείων ἐξερχόμενοι, χαλεποὶ λίαν ὥστε μὴ ἰσχύειν τινὰ παρελθεῖν διὰ τῆς ὁδοῦ ἐκείνης.
verses.translit: Kai elthontos autou eis to peran eis ten horan ton Gadarinon upintisan auto dyo daimonizomenoi ek ton mnimeion exerhomenoi, halepoi lian oste me ishyein tina parelthein dia tes odou ekeinis.
verses.translation: And when he was come to the other side into the country of the Gergesenes, there met him two possessed with devils, coming out of the tombs, exceeding fierce, so that no man might pass by that way.

verses.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἔκραξαν λέγοντες· Τί ἡμῖν καὶ ⸀σοί, υἱὲ τοῦ θεοῦ; ἦλθες ὧδε πρὸ καιροῦ βασανίσαι ἡμᾶς;
verses.translit: kai idou ekraxan legontes* Ti emin kai soi, yie tou theou; elthes ode pro kairou vasanisai emas;
verses.translation: And, behold, they cried out, saying, What have we to do with thee, Jesus, thou Son of God? art thou come hither to torment us before the time?

verses.original: ἦν δὲ μακρὰν ἀπʼ αὐτῶν ἀγέλη χοίρων πολλῶν βοσκομένη.
verses.translit: en de makran ap' auton ageli hoiron pollon voskomeni.
verses.translation: And there was a good way off from them an herd of many swine feeding.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ δαίμονες παρεκάλουν αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Εἰ ἐκβάλλεις ἡμᾶς, ⸂ἀπόστειλον ἡμᾶς⸃ εἰς τὴν ἀγέλην τῶν χοίρων.
verses.translit: oi de daimones parekaloyn auton legontes* Ei ekvalleis emas, aposteilon emas eis ten agelin ton hoiron.
verses.translation: So the devils besought him, saying, If thou cast us out, suffer us to go away into the herd of swine.

verses.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὑπάγετε. οἱ δὲ ἐξελθόντες ἀπῆλθον εἰς ⸂τοὺς χοίρους⸃· καὶ ἰδοὺ ὥρμησεν πᾶσα ἡ ⸀ἀγέλη κατὰ τοῦ κρημνοῦ εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν, καὶ ἀπέθανον ἐν τοῖς ὕδασιν.
verses.translit: kai eipen autois* Upagete. oi de exelthontes apelthon eis tous hoiroys* kai idou ormisen pasa e ageli kata tou krimnou eis ten thalassan, kai apethanon en tois udasin.
verses.translation: And he said unto them, Go. And when they were come out, they went into the herd of swine: and, behold, the whole herd of swine ran violently down a steep place into the sea, and perished in the waters.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ βόσκοντες ἔφυγον, καὶ ἀπελθόντες εἰς τὴν πόλιν ἀπήγγειλαν πάντα καὶ τὰ τῶν δαιμονιζομένων.
verses.translit: oi de voskontes efygon, kai apelthontes eis ten polin apiggeilan panta kai ta ton daimonizomenon.
verses.translation: And they that kept them fled, and went their ways into the city, and told every thing, and what was befallen to the possessed of the devils.

verses.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ πᾶσα ἡ πόλις ἐξῆλθεν εἰς ⸀ὑπάντησιν τῷ Ἰησοῦ, καὶ ἰδόντες αὐτὸν παρεκάλεσαν ὅπως μεταβῇ ἀπὸ τῶν ὁρίων αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: kai idou pasa e polis exelthen eis upantisin to Iisou, kai idontes auton parekalesan opos metave apo ton orion auton.
verses.translation: And, behold, the whole city came out to meet Jesus: and when they saw him, they besought him that he would depart out of their coasts.

verses.original: Καὶ ⸀ἐμβὰς ⸀εἰς πλοῖον διεπέρασεν καὶ ἦλθεν εἰς τὴν ἰδίαν πόλιν.
verses.translit: Kai emvas eis ploion dieperasen kai elthen eis ten idian polin.
verses.translation: And he entered into a ship, and passed over, and came into his own city.

verses.original: Καὶ ἰδοὺ προσέφερον αὐτῷ παραλυτικὸν ἐπὶ κλίνης βεβλημένον. καὶ ἰδὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὴν πίστιν αὐτῶν εἶπεν τῷ παραλυτικῷ· Θάρσει, τέκνον· ⸀ἀφίενταί ⸂σου αἱ ἁμαρτίαι⸃.
verses.translit: Kai idou proseferon auto paralytikon epi klinis vevlimenon. kai idon o Iisous ten pistin auton eipen to paralytiko* Tharsei, teknon* afientai soy ai amartiai.
verses.translation: And, behold, they brought to him a man sick of the palsy, lying on a bed: and Jesus seeing their faith said unto the sick of the palsy; Son, be of good cheer; thy sins be forgiven thee.

verses.original: καὶ ἰδού τινες τῶν γραμματέων εἶπαν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς· Οὗτος βλασφημεῖ.
verses.translit: kai idoy tines ton grammateon eipan en eaytois* Outos vlasfimei.
verses.translation: And, behold, certain of the scribes said within themselves, This man blasphemeth.

verses.original: καὶ ⸀εἰδὼς ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὰς ἐνθυμήσεις αὐτῶν εἶπεν· ⸀Ἱνατί ἐνθυμεῖσθε πονηρὰ ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν;
verses.translit: kai eidos o Iisous tas enthymiseis auton eipen* Inati enthymeisthe ponira en tais kardiais umon;
verses.translation: And Jesus knowing their thoughts said, Wherefore think ye evil in your hearts?

verses.original: τί γάρ ἐστιν εὐκοπώτερον, εἰπεῖν· ⸀Ἀφίενταί σου αἱ ἁμαρτίαι, ἢ εἰπεῖν· ⸀Ἔγειρε καὶ περιπάτει;
verses.translit: ti gar estin eukopoteron, eipein* Afientai soy ai amartiai, e eipein* Egeire kai peripatei;
verses.translation: For whether is easier, to say, Thy sins be forgiven thee; or to say, Arise, and walk?

verses.original: ἵνα δὲ εἰδῆτε ὅτι ἐξουσίαν ἔχει ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἀφιέναι ἁμαρτίας— τότε λέγει τῷ παραλυτικῷ· ⸀Ἐγερθεὶς ἆρόν σου τὴν κλίνην καὶ ὕπαγε εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου.
verses.translit: ina de eidete oti exoysian ehei o yios tou anthropoy epi tes ges afienai amartias-- tote legei to paralytiko* Egertheis aron soy ten klinin kai upage eis ton oikon soy.
verses.translation: But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power on earth to forgive sins, (then saith he to the sick of the palsy,) Arise, take up thy bed, and go unto thine house.

verses.original: καὶ ἐγερθεὶς ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai egertheis apelthen eis ton oikon autou.
verses.translation: And he arose, and departed to his house.

verses.original: ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ ὄχλοι ⸀ἐφοβήθησαν καὶ ἐδόξασαν τὸν θεὸν τὸν δόντα ἐξουσίαν τοιαύτην τοῖς ἀνθρώποις.
verses.translit: idontes de oi ohloi efovithisan kai edoxasan ton theon ton donta exoysian toiaytin tois anthropois.
verses.translation: But when the multitudes saw it , they marvelled, and glorified God, which had given such power unto men.

verses.original: Καὶ παράγων ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐκεῖθεν εἶδεν ἄνθρωπον καθήμενον ἐπὶ τὸ τελώνιον, Μαθθαῖον λεγόμενον, καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Ἀκολούθει μοι· καὶ ἀναστὰς ἠκολούθησεν αὐτῷ.
verses.translit: Kai paragon o Iisous ekeithen eiden anthropon kathimenon epi to telonion, Maththaion legomenon, kai legei auto* Akoloythei moi* kai anastas ekoloythisen auto.
verses.translation: And as Jesus passed forth from thence, he saw a man, named Matthew, sitting at the receipt of custom: and he saith unto him, Follow me. And he arose, and followed him.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο αὐτοῦ ἀνακειμένου ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ, ⸀καὶ ἰδοὺ πολλοὶ τελῶναι καὶ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἐλθόντες συνανέκειντο τῷ Ἰησοῦ καὶ τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: Kai egeneto autou anakeimenoy en te oikia, kai idou polloi telonai kai amartoloi elthontes synanekeinto to Iisou kai tois mathitais autou.
verses.translation: And it came to pass, as Jesus sat at meat in the house, behold, many publicans and sinners came and sat down with him and his disciples.

verses.original: καὶ ἰδόντες οἱ Φαρισαῖοι ⸀ἔλεγον τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ· Διὰ τί μετὰ τῶν τελωνῶν καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν ἐσθίει ὁ διδάσκαλος ὑμῶν;
verses.translit: kai idontes oi Farisaioi elegon tois mathitais autou* Dia ti meta ton telonon kai amartolon esthiei o didaskalos umon;
verses.translation: And when the Pharisees saw it , they said unto his disciples, Why eateth your Master with publicans and sinners?

verses.original: ὁ ⸀δὲ ἀκούσας ⸀εἶπεν· Οὐ χρείαν ἔχουσιν οἱ ἰσχύοντες ἰατροῦ ἀλλὰ οἱ κακῶς ἔχοντες.
verses.translit: o de akoysas eipen* Ou hreian ehoysin oi ishyontes iatrou alla oi kakos ehontes.
verses.translation: But when Jesus heard that , he said unto them, They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick.

verses.original: πορευθέντες δὲ μάθετε τί ἐστιν· Ἔλεος θέλω καὶ οὐ θυσίαν· οὐ γὰρ ἦλθον καλέσαι δικαίους ἀλλὰ ⸀ἁμαρτωλούς.
verses.translit: poreythentes de mathete ti estin* Eleos thelo kai ou thysian* ou gar elthon kalesai dikaioys alla amartoloys.
verses.translation: But go ye and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.

verses.original: Τότε προσέρχονται αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ Ἰωάννου λέγοντες· Διὰ τί ἡμεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι νηστεύομεν ⸀πολλά, οἱ δὲ μαθηταί σου οὐ νηστεύουσιν;
verses.translit: Tote proserhontai auto oi mathitai Ioannoy legontes* Dia ti emeis kai oi Farisaioi nisteyomen polla, oi de mathitai soy ou nisteyoysin;
verses.translation: Then came to him the disciples of John, saying, Why do we and the Pharisees fast oft, but thy disciples fast not?

verses.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Μὴ δύνανται οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ νυμφῶνος πενθεῖν ἐφʼ ὅσον μετʼ αὐτῶν ἐστιν ὁ νυμφίος; ἐλεύσονται δὲ ἡμέραι ὅταν ἀπαρθῇ ἀπʼ αὐτῶν ὁ νυμφίος, καὶ τότε νηστεύσουσιν.
verses.translit: kai eipen autois o Iisous* Me dynantai oi yioi tou nymfonos penthein ef' oson met' auton estin o nymfios; eleysontai de emerai otan aparthe ap' auton o nymfios, kai tote nisteysoysin.
verses.translation: And Jesus said unto them, Can the children of the bridechamber mourn, as long as the bridegroom is with them? but the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken from them, and then shall they fast.

verses.original: οὐδεὶς δὲ ἐπιβάλλει ἐπίβλημα ῥάκους ἀγνάφου ἐπὶ ἱματίῳ παλαιῷ· αἴρει γὰρ τὸ πλήρωμα αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἱματίου, καὶ χεῖρον σχίσμα γίνεται.
verses.translit: oudeis de epivallei epivlima Rakoys agnafoy epi imatio palaio* airei gar to pliroma autou apo tou imatioy, kai heiron shisma ginetai.
verses.translation: No man putteth a piece of new cloth unto an old garment, for that which is put in to fill it up taketh from the garment, and the rent is made worse.

verses.original: οὐδὲ βάλλουσιν οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς παλαιούς· εἰ δὲ μή γε, ῥήγνυνται οἱ ἀσκοί, καὶ ὁ οἶνος ἐκχεῖται καὶ οἱ ἀσκοὶ ⸀ἀπόλλυνται· ἀλλὰ βάλλουσιν οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς καινούς, καὶ ἀμφότεροι συντηροῦνται.
verses.translit: oude valloysin oinon neon eis askous palaioys* ei de mi ge, Rignyntai oi askoi, kai o oinos ekheitai kai oi askoi apollyntai* alla valloysin oinon neon eis askous kainoys, kai amfoteroi syntirountai.
verses.translation: Neither do men put new wine into old bottles: else the bottles break, and the wine runneth out, and the bottles perish: but they put new wine into new bottles, and both are preserved.

verses.original: Ταῦτα αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος αὐτοῖς ἰδοὺ ἄρχων εἷς ⸀ἐλθὼν προσεκύνει αὐτῷ λέγων ὅτι Ἡ θυγάτηρ μου ἄρτι ἐτελεύτησεν· ἀλλὰ ἐλθὼν ἐπίθες τὴν χεῖρά σου ἐπʼ αὐτήν, καὶ ζήσεται.
verses.translit: Tauta autou lalountos autois idou arhon eis elthon prosekynei auto legon oti E thygatir moy arti eteleytisen* alla elthon epithes ten heira soy ep' autin, kai zisetai.
verses.translation: While he spake these things unto them, behold, there came a certain ruler, and worshipped him, saying, My daughter is even now dead: but come and lay thy hand upon her, and she shall live.

verses.original: καὶ ἐγερθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ⸀ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai egertheis o Iisous ekoloythei auto kai oi mathitai autou.
verses.translation: And Jesus arose, and followed him, and so did his disciples.

verses.original: Καὶ ἰδοὺ γυνὴ αἱμορροοῦσα δώδεκα ἔτη προσελθοῦσα ὄπισθεν ἥψατο τοῦ κρασπέδου τοῦ ἱματίου αὐτοῦ·
verses.translit: Kai idou gyne aimorroousa dodeka eti proselthousa opisthen epsato tou kraspedoy tou imatioy autou*
verses.translation: And, behold, a woman, which was diseased with an issue of blood twelve years, came behind him , and touched the hem of his garment:

verses.original: ἔλεγεν γὰρ ἐν ἑαυτῇ· Ἐὰν μόνον ἅψωμαι τοῦ ἱματίου αὐτοῦ σωθήσομαι.
verses.translit: elegen gar en eayte* Ean monon apsomai tou imatioy autou sothisomai.
verses.translation: For she said within herself, If I may but touch his garment, I shall be whole.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ⸀στραφεὶς καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτὴν εἶπεν· Θάρσει, θύγατερ· ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε. καὶ ἐσώθη ἡ γυνὴ ἀπὸ τῆς ὥρας ἐκείνης.
verses.translit: o de Iisous strafeis kai idon auten eipen* Tharsei, thygater* e pistis soy sesoken se. kai esothi e gyne apo tes oras ekeinis.
verses.translation: But Jesus turned him about, and when he saw her, he said, Daughter, be of good comfort; thy faith hath made thee whole. And the woman was made whole from that hour.

verses.original: καὶ ἐλθὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν τοῦ ἄρχοντος καὶ ἰδὼν τοὺς αὐλητὰς καὶ τὸν ὄχλον θορυβούμενον
verses.translit: kai elthon o Iisous eis ten oikian tou arhontos kai idon tous aulitas kai ton ohlon thoryvoymenon
verses.translation: And when Jesus came into the ruler’s house, and saw the minstrels and the people making a noise,

verses.original: ⸀ἔλεγεν· Ἀναχωρεῖτε, οὐ γὰρ ἀπέθανεν τὸ κοράσιον ἀλλὰ καθεύδει· καὶ κατεγέλων αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: elegen* Anahoreite, ou gar apethanen to korasion alla katheydei* kai kategelon autou.
verses.translation: He said unto them, Give place: for the maid is not dead, but sleepeth. And they laughed him to scorn.

verses.original: ὅτε δὲ ἐξεβλήθη ὁ ὄχλος, εἰσελθὼν ἐκράτησεν τῆς χειρὸς αὐτῆς, καὶ ἠγέρθη τὸ κοράσιον.
verses.translit: ote de exevlithi o ohlos, eiselthon ekratisen tes heiros autes, kai egerthi to korasion.
verses.translation: But when the people were put forth, he went in, and took her by the hand, and the maid arose.

verses.original: καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἡ φήμη αὕτη εἰς ὅλην τὴν γῆν ἐκείνην.
verses.translit: kai exelthen e fimi auti eis olin ten gen ekeinin.
verses.translation: And the fame hereof went abroad into all that land.

verses.original: Καὶ παράγοντι ἐκεῖθεν τῷ Ἰησοῦ ἠκολούθησαν ⸀αὐτῷ δύο τυφλοὶ κράζοντες καὶ λέγοντες· Ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς, ⸀υἱὲ Δαυίδ.
verses.translit: Kai paragonti ekeithen to Iisou ekoloythisan auto dyo tyfloi krazontes kai legontes* Eleison emas, yie Dayid.
verses.translation: And when Jesus departed thence, two blind men followed him, crying, and saying, Thou Son of David, have mercy on us.

verses.original: ἐλθόντι δὲ εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν προσῆλθον αὐτῷ οἱ τυφλοί, καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Πιστεύετε ὅτι δύναμαι τοῦτο ποιῆσαι; λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Ναί, κύριε.
verses.translit: elthonti de eis ten oikian proselthon auto oi tyfloi, kai legei autois o Iisous* Pisteyete oti dynamai touto poiesai; legoysin auto* Nai, kyrie.
verses.translation: And when he was come into the house, the blind men came to him: and Jesus saith unto them, Believe ye that I am able to do this? They said unto him, Yea, Lord.

verses.original: τότε ἥψατο τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν αὐτῶν λέγων· Κατὰ τὴν πίστιν ὑμῶν γενηθήτω ὑμῖν.
verses.translit: tote epsato ton ofthalmon auton legon* Kata ten pistin umon genithito umin.
verses.translation: Then touched he their eyes, saying, According to your faith be it unto you.

verses.original: καὶ ἠνεῴχθησαν αὐτῶν οἱ ὀφθαλμοί. καὶ ⸀ἐνεβριμήθη αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγων· Ὁρᾶτε μηδεὶς γινωσκέτω·
verses.translit: kai eneohthisan auton oi ofthalmoi. kai enevrimithi autois o Iisous legon* Orate mideis ginosketo*
verses.translation: And their eyes were opened; and Jesus straitly charged them, saying, See that no man know it .

verses.original: οἱ δὲ ἐξελθόντες διεφήμισαν αὐτὸν ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ γῇ ἐκείνῃ.
verses.translit: oi de exelthontes diefimisan auton en ole te ge ekeine.
verses.translation: But they, when they were departed, spread abroad his fame in all that country.

verses.original: Αὐτῶν δὲ ἐξερχομένων ἰδοὺ προσήνεγκαν αὐτῷ ⸀ἄνθρωπον κωφὸν δαιμονιζόμενον·
verses.translit: Auton de exerhomenon idou prosinegkan auto anthropon kofon daimonizomenon*
verses.translation: As they went out, behold, they brought to him a dumb man possessed with a devil.

verses.original: καὶ ἐκβληθέντος τοῦ δαιμονίου ἐλάλησεν ὁ κωφός. καὶ ἐθαύμασαν οἱ ὄχλοι λέγοντες· Οὐδέποτε ἐφάνη οὕτως ἐν τῷ Ἰσραήλ.
verses.translit: kai ekvlithentos tou daimonioy elalisen o kofos. kai ethaymasan oi ohloi legontes* Oudepote efani outos en to Israil.
verses.translation: And when the devil was cast out, the dumb spake: and the multitudes marvelled, saying, It was never so seen in Israel.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ Φαρισαῖοι ἔλεγον· Ἐν τῷ ἄρχοντι τῶν δαιμονίων ἐκβάλλει τὰ δαιμόνια.
verses.translit: oi de Farisaioi elegon* En to arhonti ton daimonion ekvallei ta daimonia.
verses.translation: But the Pharisees said, He casteth out devils through the prince of the devils.

verses.original: Καὶ περιῆγεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὰς πόλεις πάσας καὶ τὰς κώμας, διδάσκων ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς αὐτῶν καὶ κηρύσσων τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τῆς βασιλείας καὶ θεραπεύων πᾶσαν νόσον καὶ πᾶσαν ⸀μαλακίαν.
verses.translit: Kai periegen o Iisous tas poleis pasas kai tas komas, didaskon en tais synagogais auton kai kirysson to euaggelion tes vasileias kai therapeyon pasan noson kai pasan malakian.
verses.translation: And Jesus went about all the cities and villages, teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing every sickness and every disease among the people.

verses.original: Ἰδὼν δὲ τοὺς ὄχλους ἐσπλαγχνίσθη περὶ αὐτῶν ὅτι ἦσαν ἐσκυλμένοι καὶ ἐρριμμένοι ⸀ὡσεὶ πρόβατα μὴ ἔχοντα ποιμένα.
verses.translit: Idon de tous ohloys esplaghnisthi peri auton oti esan eskylmenoi kai errimmenoi osei provata me ehonta poimena.
verses.translation: But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd.

verses.original: τότε λέγει τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ· Ὁ μὲν θερισμὸς πολύς, οἱ δὲ ἐργάται ὀλίγοι·
verses.translit: tote legei tois mathitais autou* O men therismos polys, oi de ergatai oligoi*
verses.translation: Then saith he unto his disciples, The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few;

verses.original: δεήθητε οὖν τοῦ κυρίου τοῦ θερισμοῦ ὅπως ἐκβάλῃ ἐργάτας εἰς τὸν θερισμὸν αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: deithite oun tou kyrioy tou therismou opos ekvale ergatas eis ton therismon autou.
verses.translation: Pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest.

verses.original: Καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος τοὺς δώδεκα μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς ἐξουσίαν πνευμάτων ἀκαθάρτων ὥστε ἐκβάλλειν αὐτὰ καὶ θεραπεύειν πᾶσαν νόσον καὶ πᾶσαν μαλακίαν.
verses.translit: Kai proskalesamenos tous dodeka mathitas autou edoken autois exoysian pneymaton akatharton oste ekvallein auta kai therapeyein pasan noson kai pasan malakian.
verses.translation: And when he had called unto him his twelve disciples, he gave them power against unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal all manner of sickness and all manner of disease.

verses.original: τῶν δὲ δώδεκα ἀποστόλων τὰ ὀνόματά ἐστιν ταῦτα· πρῶτος Σίμων ὁ λεγόμενος Πέτρος καὶ Ἀνδρέας ὁ ἀδελφὸς ⸀αὐτοῦ, Ἰάκωβος ὁ τοῦ Ζεβεδαίου καὶ Ἰωάννης ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ,
verses.translit: ton de dodeka apostolon ta onomata estin tauta* protos Simon o legomenos Petros kai Andreas o adelfos autou, Iakovos o tou Zevedaioy kai Ioannis o adelfos autou,
verses.translation: Now the names of the twelve apostles are these; The first, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother;

verses.original: Φίλιππος καὶ Βαρθολομαῖος, Θωμᾶς καὶ Μαθθαῖος ὁ τελώνης, Ἰάκωβος ὁ τοῦ Ἁλφαίου καὶ ⸀Θαδδαῖος,
verses.translit: Filippos kai Vartholomaios, Thomas kai Maththaios o telonis, Iakovos o tou Alfaioy kai Thaddaios,
verses.translation: Philip, and Bartholomew; Thomas, and Matthew the publican; James the son of Alphaeus, and Lebbaeus, whose surname was Thaddaeus;

verses.original: Σίμων ὁ ⸀Καναναῖος καὶ Ἰούδας ⸀ὁ Ἰσκαριώτης ὁ καὶ παραδοὺς αὐτόν.
verses.translit: Simon o Kananaios kai Ioydas o Iskariotis o kai paradous auton.
verses.translation: Simon the Canaanite, and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.

verses.original: Τούτους τοὺς δώδεκα ἀπέστειλεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς παραγγείλας αὐτοῖς λέγων· Εἰς ὁδὸν ἐθνῶν μὴ ἀπέλθητε καὶ εἰς πόλιν Σαμαριτῶν μὴ εἰσέλθητε·
verses.translit: Toytoys tous dodeka apesteilen o Iisous paraggeilas autois legon* Eis odon ethnon me apelthite kai eis polin Samariton me eiselthite*
verses.translation: These twelve Jesus sent forth, and commanded them, saying, Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not:

verses.original: πορεύεσθε δὲ μᾶλλον πρὸς τὰ πρόβατα τὰ ἀπολωλότα οἴκου Ἰσραήλ.
verses.translit: poreyesthe de mallon pros ta provata ta apololota oikoy Israil.
verses.translation: But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.

verses.original: πορευόμενοι δὲ κηρύσσετε λέγοντες ὅτι Ἤγγικεν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν.
verses.translit: poreyomenoi de kiryssete legontes oti Eggiken e vasileia ton ouranon.
verses.translation: And as ye go, preach, saying, The kingdom of heaven is at hand.

verses.original: ἀσθενοῦντας θεραπεύετε, ⸂νεκροὺς ἐγείρετε⸃, λεπροὺς καθαρίζετε, δαιμόνια ἐκβάλλετε· δωρεὰν ἐλάβετε, δωρεὰν δότε.
verses.translit: asthenountas therapeyete, nekrous egeirete, leprous katharizete, daimonia ekvallete* dorean elavete, dorean dote.
verses.translation: Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast out devils: freely ye have received, freely give.

verses.original: μὴ κτήσησθε χρυσὸν μηδὲ ἄργυρον μηδὲ χαλκὸν εἰς τὰς ζώνας ὑμῶν,
verses.translit: me ktisisthe hryson mide argyron mide halkon eis tas zonas umon,
verses.translation: Provide neither gold, nor silver, nor brass in your purses,

verses.original: μὴ πήραν εἰς ὁδὸν μηδὲ δύο χιτῶνας μηδὲ ὑποδήματα μηδὲ ⸀ῥάβδον· ἄξιος γὰρ ὁ ἐργάτης τῆς τροφῆς ⸀αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: me piran eis odon mide dyo hitonas mide upodimata mide Ravdon* axios gar o ergatis tes trofes autou.
verses.translation: Nor scrip for your journey, neither two coats, neither shoes, nor yet staves: for the workman is worthy of his meat.

verses.original: εἰς ἣν δʼ ἂν πόλιν ἢ κώμην εἰσέλθητε, ἐξετάσατε τίς ἐν αὐτῇ ἄξιός ἐστιν· κἀκεῖ μείνατε ἕως ἂν ἐξέλθητε.
verses.translit: eis en d' an polin e komin eiselthite, exetasate tis en aute axios estin* kakei meinate eos an exelthite.
verses.translation: And into whatsoever city or town ye shall enter, enquire who in it is worthy; and there abide till ye go thence.

verses.original: εἰσερχόμενοι δὲ εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν ἀσπάσασθε αὐτήν·
verses.translit: eiserhomenoi de eis ten oikian aspasasthe autin*
verses.translation: And when ye come into an house, salute it.

verses.original: καὶ ἐὰν μὲν ᾖ ἡ οἰκία ἀξία, ἐλθάτω ἡ εἰρήνη ὑμῶν ἐπʼ αὐτήν· ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ᾖ ἀξία, ἡ εἰρήνη ὑμῶν ⸀πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐπιστραφήτω.
verses.translit: kai ean men e e oikia axia, elthato e eirini umon ep' autin* ean de me e axia, e eirini umon pros umas epistrafito.
verses.translation: And if the house be worthy, let your peace come upon it: but if it be not worthy, let your peace return to you.

verses.original: καὶ ὃς ⸀ἂν μὴ δέξηται ὑμᾶς μηδὲ ἀκούσῃ τοὺς λόγους ὑμῶν, ἐξερχόμενοι ⸀ἔξω τῆς οἰκίας ἢ τῆς πόλεως ἐκείνης ἐκτινάξατε τὸν κονιορτὸν τῶν ποδῶν ὑμῶν.
verses.translit: kai os an me dexitai umas mide akoyse tous logoys umon, exerhomenoi exo tes oikias e tes poleos ekeinis ektinaxate ton koniorton ton podon umon.
verses.translation: And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, when ye depart out of that house or city, shake off the dust of your feet.

verses.original: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀνεκτότερον ἔσται γῇ Σοδόμων καὶ Γομόρρων ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κρίσεως ἢ τῇ πόλει ἐκείνῃ.
verses.translit: amen lego umin, anektoteron estai ge Sodomon kai Gomorron en emera kriseos e te polei ekeine.
verses.translation: Verily I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment, than for that city.

verses.original: Ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἀποστέλλω ὑμᾶς ὡς πρόβατα ἐν μέσῳ λύκων· γίνεσθε οὖν φρόνιμοι ὡς οἱ ὄφεις καὶ ἀκέραιοι ὡς αἱ περιστεραί.
verses.translit: Idou ego apostello umas os provata en meso lykon* ginesthe oun fronimoi os oi ofeis kai akeraioi os ai peristerai.
verses.translation: Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves.

verses.original: προσέχετε δὲ ἀπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων· παραδώσουσιν γὰρ ὑμᾶς εἰς συνέδρια, καὶ ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς αὐτῶν μαστιγώσουσιν ὑμᾶς·
verses.translit: prosehete de apo ton anthropon* paradosoysin gar umas eis synedria, kai en tais synagogais auton mastigosoysin umas*
verses.translation: But beware of men: for they will deliver you up to the councils, and they will scourge you in their synagogues;

verses.original: καὶ ἐπὶ ἡγεμόνας δὲ καὶ βασιλεῖς ἀχθήσεσθε ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς καὶ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν.
verses.translit: kai epi egemonas de kai vasileis ahthisesthe eneken emou eis martyrion autois kai tois ethnesin.
verses.translation: And ye shall be brought before governors and kings for my sake, for a testimony against them and the Gentiles.

verses.original: ὅταν δὲ ⸀παραδῶσιν ὑμᾶς, μὴ μεριμνήσητε πῶς ἢ τί λαλήσητε· δοθήσεται γὰρ ὑμῖν ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ τί ⸀λαλήσητε·
verses.translit: otan de paradosin umas, me merimnisite pos e ti lalisite* dothisetai gar umin en ekeine te ora ti lalisite*
verses.translation: But when they deliver you up, take no thought how or what ye shall speak: for it shall be given you in that same hour what ye shall speak.

verses.original: οὐ γὰρ ὑμεῖς ἐστε οἱ λαλοῦντες ἀλλὰ τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ πατρὸς ὑμῶν τὸ λαλοῦν ἐν ὑμῖν.
verses.translit: ou gar umeis este oi lalountes alla to pneuma tou patros umon to laloun en umin.
verses.translation: For it is not ye that speak, but the Spirit of your Father which speaketh in you.

verses.original: παραδώσει δὲ ἀδελφὸς ἀδελφὸν εἰς θάνατον καὶ πατὴρ τέκνον, καὶ ἐπαναστήσονται τέκνα ἐπὶ γονεῖς καὶ θανατώσουσιν αὐτούς.
verses.translit: paradosei de adelfos adelfon eis thanaton kai pater teknon, kai epanastisontai tekna epi goneis kai thanatosoysin autoys.
verses.translation: And the brother shall deliver up the brother to death, and the father the child: and the children shall rise up against their parents, and cause them to be put to death.

verses.original: καὶ ἔσεσθε μισούμενοι ὑπὸ πάντων διὰ τὸ ὄνομά μου· ὁ δὲ ὑπομείνας εἰς τέλος οὗτος σωθήσεται.
verses.translit: kai esesthe misoymenoi upo panton dia to onoma moy* o de upomeinas eis telos outos sothisetai.
verses.translation: And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved.

verses.original: ὅταν δὲ διώκωσιν ὑμᾶς ἐν τῇ πόλει ταύτῃ, φεύγετε εἰς τὴν ⸀ἑτέραν· ἀμὴν γὰρ λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐ μὴ τελέσητε τὰς πόλεις ⸀τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ ἕως ⸀ἂν ἔλθῃ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.
verses.translit: otan de diokosin umas en te polei tayte, feygete eis ten eteran* amen gar lego umin, ou me telesite tas poleis tou Israel eos an elthe o yios tou anthropoy.
verses.translation: But when they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another: for verily I say unto you, Ye shall not have gone over the cities of Israel, till the Son of man be come.

verses.original: Οὐκ ἔστιν μαθητὴς ὑπὲρ τὸν διδάσκαλον οὐδὲ δοῦλος ὑπὲρ τὸν κύριον αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: Ouk estin mathites uper ton didaskalon oude doulos uper ton kyrion autou.
verses.translation: The disciple is not above his master, nor the servant above his lord.

verses.original: ἀρκετὸν τῷ μαθητῇ ἵνα γένηται ὡς ὁ διδάσκαλος αὐτοῦ, καὶ ὁ δοῦλος ὡς ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ. εἰ τὸν οἰκοδεσπότην Βεελζεβοὺλ ⸀ἐπεκάλεσαν, πόσῳ μᾶλλον τοὺς οἰκιακοὺς αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: arketon to mathite ina genitai os o didaskalos autou, kai o doulos os o kyrios autou. ei ton oikodespotin Veelzevoul epekalesan, poso mallon tous oikiakous autou.
verses.translation: It is enough for the disciple that he be as his master, and the servant as his lord. If they have called the master of the house Beelzebub, how much more shall they call them of his household?

verses.original: Μὴ οὖν φοβηθῆτε αὐτούς· οὐδὲν γάρ ἐστιν κεκαλυμμένον ὃ οὐκ ἀποκαλυφθήσεται, καὶ κρυπτὸν ὃ οὐ γνωσθήσεται.
verses.translit: Me oun fovithete autoys* ouden gar estin kekalymmenon o ouk apokalyfthisetai, kai krypton o ou gnosthisetai.
verses.translation: Fear them not therefore: for there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed; and hid, that shall not be known.

verses.original: ὃ λέγω ὑμῖν ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ, εἴπατε ἐν τῷ φωτί· καὶ ὃ εἰς τὸ οὖς ἀκούετε, κηρύξατε ἐπὶ τῶν δωμάτων.
verses.translit: o lego umin en te skotia, eipate en to foti* kai o eis to ous akoyete, kiryxate epi ton domaton.
verses.translation: What I tell you in darkness, that speak ye in light: and what ye hear in the ear, that preach ye upon the housetops.

verses.original: καὶ μὴ ⸀φοβεῖσθε ἀπὸ τῶν ἀποκτεννόντων τὸ σῶμα τὴν δὲ ψυχὴν μὴ δυναμένων ἀποκτεῖναι· ⸁φοβεῖσθε δὲ μᾶλλον τὸν δυνάμενον ⸀καὶ ψυχὴν ⸁καὶ σῶμα ἀπολέσαι ἐν γεέννῃ.
verses.translit: kai me foveisthe apo ton apoktennonton to soma ten de psyhen me dynamenon apokteinai* foveisthe de mallon ton dynamenon kai psyhen kai soma apolesai en geenne.
verses.translation: And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.

verses.original: οὐχὶ δύο στρουθία ἀσσαρίου πωλεῖται; καὶ ἓν ἐξ αὐτῶν οὐ πεσεῖται ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἄνευ τοῦ πατρὸς ὑμῶν.
verses.translit: ouhi dyo stroythia assarioy poleitai; kai en ex auton ou peseitai epi ten gen aney tou patros umon.
verses.translation: Are not two sparrows sold for a farthing? and one of them shall not fall on the ground without your Father.

verses.original: ὑμῶν δὲ καὶ αἱ τρίχες τῆς κεφαλῆς πᾶσαι ἠριθμημέναι εἰσίν.
verses.translit: umon de kai ai trihes tes kefales pasai erithmimenai eisin.
verses.translation: But the very hairs of your head are all numbered.

verses.original: μὴ οὖν ⸀φοβεῖσθε· πολλῶν στρουθίων διαφέρετε ὑμεῖς.
verses.translit: me oun foveisthe* pollon stroythion diaferete umeis.
verses.translation: Fear ye not therefore, ye are of more value than many sparrows.

verses.original: Πᾶς οὖν ὅστις ὁμολογήσει ἐν ἐμοὶ ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ὁμολογήσω κἀγὼ ἐν αὐτῷ ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ πατρός μου τοῦ ⸀ἐν οὐρανοῖς·
verses.translit: Pas oun ostis omologisei en emoi emprosthen ton anthropon, omologiso kago en auto emprosthen tou patros moy tou en ouranois*
verses.translation: Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven.

verses.original: ὅστις ⸂δʼ ἂν⸃ ἀρνήσηταί με ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ἀρνήσομαι ⸂κἀγὼ αὐτὸν⸃ ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ πατρός μου τοῦ ⸀ἐν οὐρανοῖς.
verses.translit: ostis d' an arnisitai me emprosthen ton anthropon, arnisomai kago auton emprosthen tou patros moy tou en ouranois.
verses.translation: But whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father which is in heaven.

verses.original: Μὴ νομίσητε ὅτι ἦλθον βαλεῖν εἰρήνην ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν· οὐκ ἦλθον βαλεῖν εἰρήνην ἀλλὰ μάχαιραν.
verses.translit: Me nomisite oti elthon valein eirinin epi ten gen* ouk elthon valein eirinin alla mahairan.
verses.translation: Think not that I am come to send peace on earth: I came not to send peace, but a sword.

verses.original: ἦλθον γὰρ διχάσαι ἄνθρωπον κατὰ τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ καὶ θυγατέρα κατὰ τῆς μητρὸς αὐτῆς καὶ νύμφην κατὰ τῆς πενθερᾶς αὐτῆς,
verses.translit: elthon gar dihasai anthropon kata tou patros autou kai thygatera kata tes mitros autes kai nymfin kata tes pentheras autes,
verses.translation: For I am come to set a man at variance against his father, and the daughter against her mother, and the daughter in law against her mother in law.

verses.original: καὶ ἐχθροὶ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου οἱ οἰκιακοὶ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai ehthroi tou anthropoy oi oikiakoi autou.
verses.translation: And a man’s foes shall be they of his own household.

verses.original: ὁ φιλῶν πατέρα ἢ μητέρα ὑπὲρ ἐμὲ οὐκ ἔστιν μου ἄξιος· καὶ ὁ φιλῶν υἱὸν ἢ θυγατέρα ὑπὲρ ἐμὲ οὐκ ἔστιν μου ἄξιος·
verses.translit: o filon patera e mitera uper eme ouk estin moy axios* kai o filon yion e thygatera uper eme ouk estin moy axios*
verses.translation: He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me: and he that loveth son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me.

verses.original: καὶ ὃς οὐ λαμβάνει τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀκολουθεῖ ὀπίσω μου, οὐκ ἔστιν μου ἄξιος.
verses.translit: kai os ou lamvanei ton stayron autou kai akoloythei opiso moy, ouk estin moy axios.
verses.translation: And he that taketh not his cross, and followeth after me, is not worthy of me.

verses.original: ὁ εὑρὼν τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἀπολέσει αὐτήν, καὶ ὁ ἀπολέσας τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ εὑρήσει αὐτήν.
verses.translit: o euron ten psyhen autou apolesei autin, kai o apolesas ten psyhen autou eneken emou eurisei autin.
verses.translation: He that findeth his life shall lose it: and he that loseth his life for my sake shall find it.

verses.original: Ὁ δεχόμενος ὑμᾶς ἐμὲ δέχεται, καὶ ὁ ἐμὲ δεχόμενος δέχεται τὸν ἀποστείλαντά με.
verses.translit: O dehomenos umas eme dehetai, kai o eme dehomenos dehetai ton aposteilanta me.
verses.translation: He that receiveth you receiveth me, and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me.

verses.original: ὁ δεχόμενος προφήτην εἰς ὄνομα προφήτου μισθὸν προφήτου λήμψεται, καὶ ὁ δεχόμενος δίκαιον εἰς ὄνομα δικαίου μισθὸν δικαίου λήμψεται.
verses.translit: o dehomenos profitin eis onoma profitoy misthon profitoy limpsetai, kai o dehomenos dikaion eis onoma dikaioy misthon dikaioy limpsetai.
verses.translation: He that receiveth a prophet in the name of a prophet shall receive a prophet’s reward; and he that receiveth a righteous man in the name of a righteous man shall receive a righteous man’s reward.

verses.original: καὶ ὃς ⸀ἂν ποτίσῃ ἕνα τῶν μικρῶν τούτων ποτήριον ψυχροῦ μόνον εἰς ὄνομα μαθητοῦ, ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐ μὴ ἀπολέσῃ τὸν μισθὸν αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai os an potise ena ton mikron toyton potirion psyhrou monon eis onoma mathitou, amen lego umin, ou me apolese ton misthon autou.
verses.translation: And whosoever shall give to drink unto one of these little ones a cup of cold water only in the name of a disciple, verily I say unto you, he shall in no wise lose his reward.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ὅτε ἐτέλεσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς διατάσσων τοῖς δώδεκα μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ, μετέβη ἐκεῖθεν τοῦ διδάσκειν καὶ κηρύσσειν ἐν ταῖς πόλεσιν αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: Kai egeneto ote etelesen o Iisous diatasson tois dodeka mathitais autou, metevi ekeithen tou didaskein kai kiryssein en tais polesin auton.
verses.translation: And it came to pass, when Jesus had made an end of commanding his twelve disciples, he departed thence to teach and to preach in their cities.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰωάννης ἀκούσας ἐν τῷ δεσμωτηρίῳ τὰ ἔργα τοῦ χριστοῦ πέμψας ⸀διὰ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ
verses.translit: O de Ioannis akoysas en to desmotirio ta erga tou hristou pempsas dia ton mathiton autou
verses.translation: Now when John had heard in the prison the works of Christ, he sent two of his disciples,

verses.original: εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Σὺ εἶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἢ ἕτερον προσδοκῶμεν;
verses.translit: eipen auto* Su ei o erhomenos e eteron prosdokomen;
verses.translation: And said unto him, Art thou he that should come, or do we look for another?

verses.original: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πορευθέντες ἀπαγγείλατε Ἰωάννῃ ἃ ἀκούετε καὶ βλέπετε·
verses.translit: kai apokritheis o Iisous eipen autois* Poreythentes apaggeilate Ioanne a akoyete kai vlepete*
verses.translation: Jesus answered and said unto them, Go and shew John again those things which ye do hear and see:

verses.original: τυφλοὶ ἀναβλέπουσιν καὶ χωλοὶ περιπατοῦσιν, λεπροὶ καθαρίζονται καὶ κωφοὶ ἀκούουσιν, ⸀καὶ νεκροὶ ἐγείρονται καὶ πτωχοὶ εὐαγγελίζονται·
verses.translit: tyfloi anavlepoysin kai holoi peripatousin, leproi katharizontai kai kofoi akoyoysin, kai nekroi egeirontai kai ptohoi euaggelizontai*
verses.translation: The blind receive their sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have the gospel preached to them.

verses.original: καὶ μακάριός ἐστιν ὃς ⸀ἐὰν μὴ σκανδαλισθῇ ἐν ἐμοί.
verses.translit: kai makarios estin os ean me skandalisthe en emoi.
verses.translation: And blessed is he , whosoever shall not be offended in me.

verses.original: Τούτων δὲ πορευομένων ἤρξατο ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγειν τοῖς ὄχλοις περὶ Ἰωάννου· Τί ἐξήλθατε εἰς τὴν ἔρημον θεάσασθαι; κάλαμον ὑπὸ ἀνέμου σαλευόμενον;
verses.translit: Toyton de poreyomenon erxato o Iisous legein tois ohlois peri Ioannoy* Ti exilthate eis ten erimon theasasthai; kalamon upo anemoy saleyomenon;
verses.translation: And as they departed, Jesus began to say unto the multitudes concerning John, What went ye out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken with the wind?

verses.original: ἀλλὰ τί ἐξήλθατε ἰδεῖν; ἄνθρωπον ἐν ⸀μαλακοῖς ἠμφιεσμένον; ἰδοὺ οἱ τὰ μαλακὰ φοροῦντες ἐν τοῖς οἴκοις τῶν ⸀βασιλέων ⸀εἰσίν.
verses.translit: alla ti exilthate idein; anthropon en malakois emfiesmenon; idou oi ta malaka forountes en tois oikois ton vasileon eisin.
verses.translation: But what went ye out for to see? A man clothed in soft raiment? behold, they that wear soft clothing are in kings’ houses.

verses.original: ἀλλὰ τί ἐξήλθατε⸂; προφήτην ἰδεῖν⸃; ναί, λέγω ὑμῖν, καὶ περισσότερον προφήτου.
verses.translit: alla ti exilthate; profitin idein; nai, lego umin, kai perissoteron profitoy.
verses.translation: But what went ye out for to see? A prophet? yea, I say unto you, and more than a prophet.

verses.original: ⸀οὗτός ἐστιν περὶ οὗ γέγραπται· Ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἀποστέλλω τὸν ἄγγελόν μου πρὸ προσώπου σου, ὃς κατασκευάσει τὴν ὁδόν σου ἔμπροσθέν σου.
verses.translit: outos estin peri ou gegraptai* Idou ego apostello ton aggelon moy pro prosopoy soy, os kataskeyasei ten odon soy emprosthen soy.
verses.translation: For this is he , of whom it is written, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, which shall prepare thy way before thee.

verses.original: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐκ ἐγήγερται ἐν γεννητοῖς γυναικῶν μείζων Ἰωάννου τοῦ βαπτιστοῦ· ὁ δὲ μικρότερος ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν μείζων αὐτοῦ ἐστιν.
verses.translit: amen lego umin, ouk egigertai en gennitois gynaikon meizon Ioannoy tou vaptistou* o de mikroteros en te vasileia ton ouranon meizon autou estin.
