verses.translation: Verily I say unto you, Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist: notwithstanding he that is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.

verses.original: ἀπὸ δὲ τῶν ἡμερῶν Ἰωάννου τοῦ βαπτιστοῦ ἕως ἄρτι ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν βιάζεται, καὶ βιασταὶ ἁρπάζουσιν αὐτήν.
verses.translit: apo de ton emeron Ioannoy tou vaptistou eos arti e vasileia ton ouranon viazetai, kai viastai arpazoysin autin.
verses.translation: And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force.

verses.original: πάντες γὰρ οἱ προφῆται καὶ ὁ νόμος ἕως Ἰωάννου ἐπροφήτευσαν·
verses.translit: pantes gar oi profetai kai o nomos eos Ioannoy eprofiteysan*
verses.translation: For all the prophets and the law prophesied until John.

verses.original: καὶ εἰ θέλετε δέξασθαι, αὐτός ἐστιν Ἠλίας ὁ μέλλων ἔρχεσθαι.
verses.translit: kai ei thelete dexasthai, autos estin Elias o mellon erhesthai.
verses.translation: And if ye will receive it , this is Elias, which was for to come.

verses.original: ὁ ἔχων ⸀ὦτα ἀκουέτω.
verses.translit: o ehon ota akoyeto.
verses.translation: He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.

verses.original: Τίνι δὲ ὁμοιώσω τὴν γενεὰν ταύτην; ὁμοία ἐστὶν παιδίοις ⸂καθημένοις ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς ἃ προσφωνοῦντα τοῖς ἑτέροις⸃
verses.translit: Tini de omoioso ten genean taytin; omoia estin paidiois kathimenois en tais agorais a prosfonounta tois eterois
verses.translation: But whereunto shall I liken this generation? It is like unto children sitting in the markets, and calling unto their fellows,

verses.original: ⸀λέγουσιν· Ηὐλήσαμεν ὑμῖν καὶ οὐκ ὠρχήσασθε· ⸀ἐθρηνήσαμεν καὶ οὐκ ἐκόψασθε·
verses.translit: legoysin* Iulisamen umin kai ouk orhisasthe* ethrinisamen kai ouk ekopsasthe*
verses.translation: And saying, We have piped unto you, and ye have not danced; we have mourned unto you, and ye have not lamented.

verses.original: ἦλθεν γὰρ Ἰωάννης μήτε ἐσθίων μήτε πίνων, καὶ λέγουσιν· Δαιμόνιον ἔχει·
verses.translit: elthen gar Ioannis mite esthion mite pinon, kai legoysin* Daimonion ehei*
verses.translation: For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, He hath a devil.

verses.original: ἦλθεν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐσθίων καὶ πίνων, καὶ λέγουσιν· Ἰδοὺ ἄνθρωπος φάγος καὶ οἰνοπότης, τελωνῶν φίλος καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν. καὶ ἐδικαιώθη ἡ σοφία ἀπὸ τῶν ⸀ἔργων αὐτῆς.
verses.translit: elthen o yios tou anthropoy esthion kai pinon, kai legoysin* Idou anthropos fagos kai oinopotis, telonon filos kai amartolon. kai edikaiothi e sofia apo ton ergon autes.
verses.translation: The Son of man came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold a man gluttonous, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children.

verses.original: Τότε ⸀ἤρξατο ὀνειδίζειν τὰς πόλεις ἐν αἷς ἐγένοντο αἱ πλεῖσται δυνάμεις αὐτοῦ, ὅτι οὐ μετενόησαν·
verses.translit: Tote erxato oneidizein tas poleis en ais egenonto ai pleistai dynameis autou, oti ou metenoisan*
verses.translation: Then began he to upbraid the cities wherein most of his mighty works were done, because they repented not:

verses.original: Οὐαί σοι, Χοραζίν· οὐαί σοι, Βηθσαϊδά· ὅτι εἰ ἐν Τύρῳ καὶ Σιδῶνι ἐγένοντο αἱ δυνάμεις αἱ γενόμεναι ἐν ὑμῖν, πάλαι ἂν ἐν σάκκῳ καὶ σποδῷ μετενόησαν.
verses.translit: Ouai soi, Horazin* ouai soi, Vithsaida* oti ei en Tyro kai Sidoni egenonto ai dynameis ai genomenai en umin, palai an en sakko kai spodo metenoisan.
verses.translation: Woe unto thee, Chorazin! woe unto thee, Bethsaida! for if the mighty works, which were done in you, had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.

verses.original: πλὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, Τύρῳ καὶ Σιδῶνι ἀνεκτότερον ἔσται ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κρίσεως ἢ ὑμῖν.
verses.translit: plen lego umin, Tyro kai Sidoni anektoteron estai en emera kriseos e umin.
verses.translation: But I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the day of judgment, than for you.

verses.original: καὶ σύ, Καφαρναούμ, ⸂μὴ ἕως οὐρανοῦ ὑψωθήσῃ⸃; ἕως ᾅδου ⸀καταβήσῃ· ὅτι εἰ ἐν Σοδόμοις ⸀ἐγενήθησαν αἱ δυνάμεις αἱ γενόμεναι ἐν σοί, ⸀ἔμεινεν ἂν μέχρι τῆς σήμερον.
verses.translit: kai sy, Kafarnaoym, me eos ouranou upsothise; eos adoy katavise* oti ei en Sodomois egenithisan ai dynameis ai genomenai en soi, emeinen an mehri tes simeron.
verses.translation: And thou, Capernaum, which art exalted unto heaven, shalt be brought down to hell: for if the mighty works, which have been done in thee, had been done in Sodom, it would have remained until this day.

verses.original: πλὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι γῇ Σοδόμων ἀνεκτότερον ἔσται ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κρίσεως ἢ σοί.
verses.translit: plen lego umin oti ge Sodomon anektoteron estai en emera kriseos e soi.
verses.translation: But I say unto you, That it shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom in the day of judgment, than for thee.

verses.original: Ἐν ἐκείνῳ τῷ καιρῷ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Ἐξομολογοῦμαί σοι, πάτερ κύριε τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ τῆς γῆς, ὅτι ⸀ἔκρυψας ταῦτα ἀπὸ σοφῶν καὶ συνετῶν, καὶ ἀπεκάλυψας αὐτὰ νηπίοις·
verses.translit: En ekeino to kairo apokritheis o Iisous eipen* Exomologoumai soi, pater kyrie tou ouranou kai tes ges, oti ekrypsas tauta apo sofon kai syneton, kai apekalypsas auta nipiois*
verses.translation: At that time Jesus answered and said, I thank thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes.

verses.original: ναί, ὁ πατήρ, ὅτι οὕτως ⸂εὐδοκία ἐγένετο⸃ ἔμπροσθέν σου.
verses.translit: nai, o patir, oti outos eudokia egeneto emprosthen soy.
verses.translation: Even so, Father: for so it seemed good in thy sight.

verses.original: Πάντα μοι παρεδόθη ὑπὸ τοῦ πατρός μου, καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐπιγινώσκει τὸν υἱὸν εἰ μὴ ὁ πατήρ, οὐδὲ τὸν πατέρα τις ἐπιγινώσκει εἰ μὴ ὁ υἱὸς καὶ ᾧ ἐὰν βούληται ὁ υἱὸς ἀποκαλύψαι.
verses.translit: Panta moi paredothi upo tou patros moy, kai oudeis epiginoskei ton yion ei me o patir, oude ton patera tis epiginoskei ei me o yios kai o ean voylitai o yios apokalypsai.
verses.translation: All things are delivered unto me of my Father: and no man knoweth the Son, but the Father; neither knoweth any man the Father, save the Son, and he to whomsoever the Son will reveal him.

verses.original: Δεῦτε πρός με πάντες οἱ κοπιῶντες καὶ πεφορτισμένοι, κἀγὼ ἀναπαύσω ὑμᾶς.
verses.translit: Deute pros me pantes oi kopiontes kai pefortismenoi, kago anapayso umas.
verses.translation: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.

verses.original: ἄρατε τὸν ζυγόν μου ἐφʼ ὑμᾶς καὶ μάθετε ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ, ὅτι πραΰς εἰμι καὶ ταπεινὸς τῇ καρδίᾳ, καὶ εὑρήσετε ἀνάπαυσιν ταῖς ψυχαῖς ὑμῶν·
verses.translit: arate ton zygon moy ef' umas kai mathete ap' emou, oti prays eimi kai tapeinos te kardia, kai eurisete anapaysin tais psyhais umon*
verses.translation: Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.

verses.original: ὁ γὰρ ζυγός μου χρηστὸς καὶ τὸ φορτίον μου ἐλαφρόν ἐστιν.
verses.translit: o gar zygos moy hristos kai to fortion moy elafron estin.
verses.translation: For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.

verses.original: Ἐν ἐκείνῳ τῷ καιρῷ ἐπορεύθη ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοῖς σάββασιν διὰ τῶν σπορίμων· οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἐπείνασαν καὶ ἤρξαντο τίλλειν στάχυας καὶ ἐσθίειν.
verses.translit: En ekeino to kairo eporeythi o Iisous tois savvasin dia ton sporimon* oi de mathitai autou epeinasan kai erxanto tillein stahyas kai esthiein.
verses.translation: At that time Jesus went on the sabbath day through the corn; and his disciples were an hungred, and began to pluck the ears of corn, and to eat.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ Φαρισαῖοι ἰδόντες εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Ἰδοὺ οἱ μαθηταί σου ποιοῦσιν ὃ οὐκ ἔξεστιν ποιεῖν ἐν σαββάτῳ.
verses.translit: oi de Farisaioi idontes eipan auto* Idou oi mathitai soy poiousin o ouk exestin poiein en savvato.
verses.translation: But when the Pharisees saw it , they said unto him, Behold, thy disciples do that which is not lawful to do upon the sabbath day.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Οὐκ ἀνέγνωτε τί ἐποίησεν Δαυὶδ ὅτε ⸀ἐπείνασεν καὶ οἱ μετʼ αὐτοῦ;
verses.translit: o de eipen autois* Ouk anegnote ti epoiisen Dayid ote epeinasen kai oi met' autou?
verses.translation: But he said unto them, Have ye not read what David did, when he was an hungred, and they that were with him;

verses.original: πῶς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τοὺς ἄρτους τῆς προθέσεως ⸂ἔφαγον, ὃ⸃ οὐκ ἐξὸν ἦν αὐτῷ φαγεῖν οὐδὲ τοῖς μετʼ αὐτοῦ, εἰ μὴ τοῖς ἱερεῦσιν μόνοις;
verses.translit: pos eiselthen eis ton oikon tou theou kai tous artoys tes protheseos efagon, o ouk exon en auto fagein oude tois met' autou, ei me tois iereusin monois;
verses.translation: How he entered into the house of God, and did eat the shewbread, which was not lawful for him to eat, neither for them which were with him, but only for the priests?

verses.original: ἢ οὐκ ἀνέγνωτε ἐν τῷ νόμῳ ὅτι τοῖς σάββασιν οἱ ἱερεῖς ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ τὸ σάββατον βεβηλοῦσιν καὶ ἀναίτιοί εἰσιν;
verses.translit: e ouk anegnote en to nomo oti tois savvasin oi iereis en to iero to savvaton vevilousin kai anaitioi eisin;
verses.translation: Or have ye not read in the law, how that on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless?

verses.original: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι τοῦ ἱεροῦ μεῖζόν ἐστιν ὧδε.
verses.translit: lego de umin oti tou ierou meizon estin ode.
verses.translation: But I say unto you, That in this place is one greater than the temple.

verses.original: εἰ δὲ ἐγνώκειτε τί ἐστιν· Ἔλεος θέλω καὶ οὐ θυσίαν, οὐκ ἂν κατεδικάσατε τοὺς ἀναιτίους.
verses.translit: ei de egnokeite ti estin* Eleos thelo kai ou thysian, ouk an katedikasate tous anaitioys.
verses.translation: But if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.

verses.original: κύριος γάρ ἐστιν τοῦ σαββάτου ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.
verses.translit: kyrios gar estin tou savvatoy o yios tou anthropoy.
verses.translation: For the Son of man is Lord even of the sabbath day.

verses.original: Καὶ μεταβὰς ἐκεῖθεν ἦλθεν εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν αὐτῶν·
verses.translit: Kai metavas ekeithen elthen eis ten synagogen auton*
verses.translation: And when he was departed thence, he went into their synagogue:

verses.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ ⸀ἄνθρωπος χεῖρα ἔχων ξηράν. καὶ ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Εἰ ἔξεστι τοῖς σάββασιν ⸀θεραπεύειν; ἵνα κατηγορήσωσιν αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai idou anthropos heira ehon xiran. kai epirotisan auton legontes* Ei exesti tois savvasin therapeyein; ina katigorisosin autou.
verses.translation: And, behold, there was a man which had his hand withered. And they asked him, saying, Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath days? that they might accuse him.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τίς ⸀ἔσται ἐξ ὑμῶν ἄνθρωπος ὃς ἕξει πρόβατον ἕν, καὶ ἐὰν ἐμπέσῃ τοῦτο τοῖς σάββασιν εἰς βόθυνον, οὐχὶ κρατήσει αὐτὸ καὶ ἐγερεῖ;
verses.translit: o de eipen autois* Tis estai ex umon anthropos os exei provaton en, kai ean empese touto tois savvasin eis vothynon, ouhi kratisei auto kai egerei;
verses.translation: And he said unto them, What man shall there be among you, that shall have one sheep, and if it fall into a pit on the sabbath day, will he not lay hold on it, and lift it out?

verses.original: πόσῳ οὖν διαφέρει ἄνθρωπος προβάτου. ὥστε ἔξεστιν τοῖς σάββασιν καλῶς ποιεῖν.
verses.translit: poso oun diaferei anthropos provatoy. oste exestin tois savvasin kalos poiein.
verses.translation: How much then is a man better than a sheep? Wherefore it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.

verses.original: τότε λέγει τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ· Ἔκτεινόν ⸂σου τὴν χεῖρα⸃· καὶ ἐξέτεινεν, καὶ ἀπεκατεστάθη ὑγιὴς ὡς ἡ ἄλλη.
verses.translit: tote legei to anthropo* Ekteinon soy ten heira* kai exeteinen, kai apekatestathi ugies os e alli.
verses.translation: Then saith he to the man, Stretch forth thine hand. And he stretched it forth; and it was restored whole, like as the other.

verses.original: ⸂ἐξελθόντες δὲ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι συμβούλιον ἔλαβον κατʼ αὐτοῦ⸃ ὅπως αὐτὸν ἀπολέσωσιν.
verses.translit: exelthontes de oi Farisaioi symvoylion elavon kat' autou opos auton apolesosin.
verses.translation: Then the Pharisees went out, and held a council against him, how they might destroy him.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς γνοὺς ἀνεχώρησεν ἐκεῖθεν. καὶ ἠκολούθησαν ⸀αὐτῷ πολλοί, καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν αὐτοὺς πάντας,
verses.translit: O de Iisous gnous anehorisen ekeithen. kai ekoloythisan auto polloi, kai etherapeysen autous pantas,
verses.translation: But when Jesus knew it , he withdrew himself from thence: and great multitudes followed him, and he healed them all;

verses.original: καὶ ἐπετίμησεν αὐτοῖς ἵνα μὴ φανερὸν αὐτὸν ποιήσωσιν,
verses.translit: kai epetimisen autois ina me faneron auton poiisosin,
verses.translation: And charged them that they should not make him known:

verses.original: ⸀ἵνα πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ Ἠσαΐου τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος·
verses.translit: ina plirothe to Rithen dia EsaIoy tou profitoy legontos*
verses.translation: That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Esaias the prophet, saying,

verses.original: Ἰδοὺ ὁ παῖς μου ὃν ᾑρέτισα, ὁ ἀγαπητός μου ⸂εἰς ὃν⸃ εὐδόκησεν ἡ ψυχή μου· θήσω τὸ πνεῦμά μου ἐπʼ αὐτόν, καὶ κρίσιν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ἀπαγγελεῖ.
verses.translit: Idou o pais moy on eretisa, o agapitos moy eis on eudokisen e psyhi moy* thiso to pneuma moy ep' auton, kai krisin tois ethnesin apaggelei.
verses.translation: Behold my servant, whom I have chosen; my beloved, in whom my soul is well pleased: I will put my spirit upon him, and he shall shew judgment to the Gentiles.

verses.original: οὐκ ἐρίσει οὐδὲ κραυγάσει, οὐδὲ ἀκούσει τις ἐν ταῖς πλατείαις τὴν φωνὴν αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: ouk erisei oude kraygasei, oude akoysei tis en tais plateiais ten fonen autou.
verses.translation: He shall not strive, nor cry; neither shall any man hear his voice in the streets.

verses.original: κάλαμον συντετριμμένον οὐ κατεάξει καὶ λίνον τυφόμενον οὐ σβέσει, ἕως ἂν ἐκβάλῃ εἰς νῖκος τὴν κρίσιν.
verses.translit: kalamon syntetrimmenon ou kateaxei kai linon tyfomenon ou svesei, eos an ekvale eis nikos ten krisin.
verses.translation: A bruised reed shall he not break, and smoking flax shall he not quench, till he send forth judgment unto victory.

verses.original: καὶ τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ ἔθνη ἐλπιοῦσιν.
verses.translit: kai to onomati autou ethni elpiousin.
verses.translation: And in his name shall the Gentiles trust.

verses.original: Τότε ⸂προσηνέχθη αὐτῷ δαιμονιζόμενος τυφλὸς καὶ κωφός⸃· καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν αὐτόν, ὥστε τὸν ⸀κωφὸν λαλεῖν καὶ βλέπειν.
verses.translit: Tote prosinehthi auto daimonizomenos tyflos kai kofos* kai etherapeysen auton, oste ton kofon lalein kai vlepein.
verses.translation: Then was brought unto him one possessed with a devil, blind, and dumb: and he healed him, insomuch that the blind and dumb both spake and saw.

verses.original: καὶ ἐξίσταντο πάντες οἱ ὄχλοι καὶ ἔλεγον· Μήτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς Δαυίδ;
verses.translit: kai existanto pantes oi ohloi kai elegon* Miti outos estin o yios Dayid;
verses.translation: And all the people were amazed, and said, Is not this the son of David?

verses.original: οἱ δὲ Φαρισαῖοι ἀκούσαντες εἶπον· Οὗτος οὐκ ἐκβάλλει τὰ δαιμόνια εἰ μὴ ἐν τῷ Βεελζεβοὺλ ἄρχοντι τῶν δαιμονίων.
verses.translit: oi de Farisaioi akoysantes eipon* Outos ouk ekvallei ta daimonia ei me en to Veelzevoul arhonti ton daimonion.
verses.translation: But when the Pharisees heard it , they said, This fellow doth not cast out devils, but by Beelzebub the prince of the devils.

verses.original: εἰδὼς ⸀δὲ τὰς ἐνθυμήσεις αὐτῶν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πᾶσα βασιλεία μερισθεῖσα καθʼ ἑαυτῆς ἐρημοῦται, καὶ πᾶσα πόλις ἢ οἰκία μερισθεῖσα καθʼ ἑαυτῆς οὐ σταθήσεται.
verses.translit: eidos de tas enthymiseis auton eipen autois* Pasa vasileia meristheisa kath' eaytes erimoutai, kai pasa polis e oikia meristheisa kath' eaytes ou stathisetai.
verses.translation: And Jesus knew their thoughts, and said unto them, Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation; and every city or house divided against itself shall not stand:

verses.original: καὶ εἰ ὁ Σατανᾶς τὸν Σατανᾶν ἐκβάλλει, ἐφʼ ἑαυτὸν ἐμερίσθη· πῶς οὖν σταθήσεται ἡ βασιλεία αὐτοῦ;
verses.translit: kai ei o Satanas ton Satanan ekvallei, ef' eayton emeristhi* pos oun stathisetai e vasileia autou;
verses.translation: And if Satan cast out Satan, he is divided against himself; how shall then his kingdom stand?

verses.original: καὶ εἰ ἐγὼ ἐν Βεελζεβοὺλ ἐκβάλλω τὰ δαιμόνια, οἱ υἱοὶ ὑμῶν ἐν τίνι ἐκβάλλουσιν; διὰ τοῦτο αὐτοὶ ⸂κριταὶ ἔσονται ὑμῶν⸃.
verses.translit: kai ei ego en Veelzevoul ekvallo ta daimonia, oi yioi umon en tini ekvalloysin; dia touto autoi kritai esontai umon.
verses.translation: And if I by Beelzebub cast out devils, by whom do your children cast them out? therefore they shall be your judges.

verses.original: εἰ δὲ ἐν πνεύματι θεοῦ ἐγὼ ἐκβάλλω τὰ δαιμόνια, ἄρα ἔφθασεν ἐφʼ ὑμᾶς ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: ei de en pneymati theou ego ekvallo ta daimonia, ara efthasen ef' umas e vasileia tou theou.
verses.translation: But if I cast out devils by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God is come unto you.

verses.original: ἢ πῶς δύναταί τις εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν τοῦ ἰσχυροῦ καὶ τὰ σκεύη αὐτοῦ ⸀ἁρπάσαι, ἐὰν μὴ πρῶτον δήσῃ τὸν ἰσχυρόν; καὶ τότε τὴν οἰκίαν αὐτοῦ ⸀διαρπάσει.
verses.translit: e pos dynatai tis eiselthein eis ten oikian tou ishyrou kai ta skeyi autou arpasai, ean me proton dise ton ishyron; kai tote ten oikian autou diarpasei.
verses.translation: Or else how can one enter into a strong man’s house, and spoil his goods, except he first bind the strong man? and then he will spoil his house.

verses.original: ὁ μὴ ὢν μετʼ ἐμοῦ κατʼ ἐμοῦ ἐστιν, καὶ ὁ μὴ συνάγων μετʼ ἐμοῦ σκορπίζει.
verses.translit: o me on met' emou kat' emou estin, kai o me synagon met' emou skorpizei.
verses.translation: He that is not with me is against me; and he that gathereth not with me scattereth abroad.

verses.original: διὰ τοῦτο λέγω ὑμῖν, πᾶσα ἁμαρτία καὶ βλασφημία ἀφεθήσεται τοῖς ἀνθρώποις, ἡ δὲ τοῦ πνεύματος βλασφημία οὐκ ⸀ἀφεθήσεται.
verses.translit: dia touto lego umin, pasa amartia kai vlasfimia afethisetai tois anthropois, e de tou pneymatos vlasfimia ouk afethisetai.
verses.translation: Wherefore I say unto you, All manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men: but the blasphemy against the Holy Ghost shall not be forgiven unto men.

verses.original: καὶ ὃς ἐὰν εἴπῃ λόγον κατὰ τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, ἀφεθήσεται αὐτῷ· ὃς δʼ ἂν εἴπῃ κατὰ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἁγίου, οὐκ ἀφεθήσεται αὐτῷ οὔτε ἐν ⸂τούτῳ τῷ⸃ αἰῶνι οὔτε ἐν τῷ μέλλοντι.
verses.translit: kai os ean eipe logon kata tou yiou tou anthropoy, afethisetai auto* os d' an eipe kata tou pneymatos tou agioy, ouk afethisetai auto oute en toyto to aioni oute en to mellonti.
verses.translation: And whosoever speaketh a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but whosoever speaketh against the Holy Ghost, it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, neither in the world to come.

verses.original: Ἢ ποιήσατε τὸ δένδρον καλὸν καὶ τὸν καρπὸν αὐτοῦ καλόν, ἢ ποιήσατε τὸ δένδρον σαπρὸν καὶ τὸν καρπὸν αὐτοῦ σαπρόν· ἐκ γὰρ τοῦ καρποῦ τὸ δένδρον γινώσκεται.
verses.translit: E poiisate to dendron kalon kai ton karpon autou kalon, e poiisate to dendron sapron kai ton karpon autou sapron* ek gar tou karpou to dendron ginosketai.
verses.translation: Either make the tree good, and his fruit good; or else make the tree corrupt, and his fruit corrupt: for the tree is known by his fruit.

verses.original: γεννήματα ἐχιδνῶν, πῶς δύνασθε ἀγαθὰ λαλεῖν πονηροὶ ὄντες; ἐκ γὰρ τοῦ περισσεύματος τῆς καρδίας τὸ στόμα λαλεῖ.
verses.translit: gennimata ehidnon, pos dynasthe agatha lalein poniroi ontes; ek gar tou perisseymatos tes kardias to stoma lalei.
verses.translation: O generation of vipers, how can ye, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh.

verses.original: ὁ ἀγαθὸς ἄνθρωπος ἐκ τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ θησαυροῦ ἐκβάλλει ἀγαθά, καὶ ὁ πονηρὸς ἄνθρωπος ἐκ τοῦ πονηροῦ θησαυροῦ ἐκβάλλει πονηρά.
verses.translit: o agathos anthropos ek tou agathou thisayrou ekvallei agatha, kai o poniros anthropos ek tou ponirou thisayrou ekvallei ponira.
verses.translation: A good man out of the good treasure of the heart bringeth forth good things: and an evil man out of the evil treasure bringeth forth evil things.

verses.original: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶν ῥῆμα ἀργὸν ὃ ⸀λαλήσουσιν οἱ ἄνθρωποι, ἀποδώσουσιν περὶ αὐτοῦ λόγον ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κρίσεως·
verses.translit: lego de umin oti pan Rema argon o lalisoysin oi anthropoi, apodosoysin peri autou logon en emera kriseos*
verses.translation: But I say unto you, That every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment.

verses.original: ἐκ γὰρ τῶν λόγων σου δικαιωθήσῃ, καὶ ἐκ τῶν λόγων σου καταδικασθήσῃ.
verses.translit: ek gar ton logon soy dikaiothise, kai ek ton logon soy katadikasthise.
verses.translation: For by thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words thou shalt be condemned.

verses.original: Τότε ἀπεκρίθησαν ⸀αὐτῷ τινες τῶν γραμματέων καὶ Φαρισαίων λέγοντες· Διδάσκαλε, θέλομεν ἀπὸ σοῦ σημεῖον ἰδεῖν.
verses.translit: Tote apekrithisan auto tines ton grammateon kai Farisaion legontes* Didaskale, thelomen apo sou simeion idein.
verses.translation: Then certain of the scribes and of the Pharisees answered, saying, Master, we would see a sign from thee.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Γενεὰ πονηρὰ καὶ μοιχαλὶς σημεῖον ἐπιζητεῖ, καὶ σημεῖον οὐ δοθήσεται αὐτῇ εἰ μὴ τὸ σημεῖον Ἰωνᾶ τοῦ προφήτου.
verses.translit: o de apokritheis eipen autois* Genea ponira kai moihalis simeion epizitei, kai simeion ou dothisetai aute ei me to simeion Iona tou profitoy.
verses.translation: But he answered and said unto them, An evil and adulterous generation seeketh after a sign; and there shall no sign be given to it, but the sign of the prophet Jonas:

verses.original: ὥσπερ γὰρ ἦν Ἰωνᾶς ἐν τῇ κοιλίᾳ τοῦ κήτους τρεῖς ἡμέρας καὶ τρεῖς νύκτας, οὕτως ἔσται ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ τῆς γῆς τρεῖς ἡμέρας καὶ τρεῖς νύκτας.
verses.translit: osper gar en Ionas en te koilia tou kitoys treis emeras kai treis nyktas, outos estai o yios tou anthropoy en te kardia tes ges treis emeras kai treis nyktas.
verses.translation: For as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale’s belly; so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.

verses.original: ἄνδρες Νινευῖται ἀναστήσονται ἐν τῇ κρίσει μετὰ τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης καὶ κατακρινοῦσιν αὐτήν· ὅτι μετενόησαν εἰς τὸ κήρυγμα Ἰωνᾶ, καὶ ἰδοὺ πλεῖον Ἰωνᾶ ὧδε.
verses.translit: andres Nineyitai anastisontai en te krisei meta tes geneas taytis kai katakrinousin autin* oti metenoisan eis to kirygma Iona, kai idou pleion Iona ode.
verses.translation: The men of Nineveh shall rise in judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: because they repented at the preaching of Jonas; and, behold, a greater than Jonas is here.

verses.original: βασίλισσα νότου ἐγερθήσεται ἐν τῇ κρίσει μετὰ τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης καὶ κατακρινεῖ αὐτήν· ὅτι ἦλθεν ἐκ τῶν περάτων τῆς γῆς ἀκοῦσαι τὴν σοφίαν Σολομῶνος, καὶ ἰδοὺ πλεῖον Σολομῶνος ὧδε.
verses.translit: vasilissa notoy egerthisetai en te krisei meta tes geneas taytis kai katakrinei autin* oti elthen ek ton peraton tes ges akousai ten sofian Solomonos, kai idou pleion Solomonos ode.
verses.translation: The queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: for she came from the uttermost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and, behold, a greater than Solomon is here.

verses.original: Ὅταν δὲ τὸ ἀκάθαρτον πνεῦμα ἐξέλθῃ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, διέρχεται διʼ ἀνύδρων τόπων ζητοῦν ἀνάπαυσιν, καὶ οὐχ εὑρίσκει.
verses.translit: Otan de to akatharton pneuma exelthe apo tou anthropoy, dierhetai di' anydron topon zitoun anapaysin, kai ouh euriskei.
verses.translation: When the unclean spirit is gone out of a man, he walketh through dry places, seeking rest, and findeth none.

verses.original: τότε λέγει· ⸂Εἰς τὸν οἶκόν μου ἐπιστρέψω⸃ ὅθεν ἐξῆλθον· καὶ ἐλθὸν ⸀εὑρίσκει ⸀σχολάζοντα σεσαρωμένον καὶ κεκοσμημένον.
verses.translit: tote legei* Eis ton oikon moy epistrepso othen exelthon* kai elthon euriskei sholazonta sesaromenon kai kekosmimenon.
verses.translation: Then he saith, I will return into my house from whence I came out; and when he is come, he findeth it empty, swept, and garnished.

verses.original: τότε πορεύεται καὶ παραλαμβάνει μεθʼ ἑαυτοῦ ἑπτὰ ἕτερα πνεύματα πονηρότερα ἑαυτοῦ, καὶ εἰσελθόντα κατοικεῖ ἐκεῖ· καὶ γίνεται τὰ ἔσχατα τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκείνου χείρονα τῶν πρώτων. οὕτως ἔσται καὶ τῇ γενεᾷ ταύτῃ τῇ πονηρᾷ.
verses.translit: tote poreyetai kai paralamvanei meth' eaytou epta etera pneymata ponirotera eaytou, kai eiselthonta katoikei ekei* kai ginetai ta eshata tou anthropoy ekeinoy heirona ton proton. outos estai kai te genea tayte te ponira.
verses.translation: Then goeth he, and taketh with himself seven other spirits more wicked than himself, and they enter in and dwell there: and the last state of that man is worse than the first. Even so shall it be also unto this wicked generation.

verses.original: Ἔτι ⸀δὲ αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος τοῖς ὄχλοις ἰδοὺ ἡ μήτηρ καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ εἱστήκεισαν ἔξω ζητοῦντες αὐτῷ λαλῆσαι.
verses.translit: Eti de autou lalountos tois ohlois idou e mitir kai oi adelfoi autou eistikeisan exo zitountes auto lalesai.
verses.translation: While he yet talked to the people, behold, his mother and his brethren stood without, desiring to speak with him.

verses.original: ⸂εἶπεν δέ τις αὐτῷ· Ἰδοὺ ἡ μήτηρ σου καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοί σου ἔξω ἑστήκασιν, ζητοῦντές σοι λαλῆσαι.⸃
verses.translit: eipen de tis auto* Idou e mitir soy kai oi adelfoi soy exo estikasin, zitountes soi lalesai.
verses.translation: Then one said unto him, Behold, thy mother and thy brethren stand without, desiring to speak with thee.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν τῷ ⸀λέγοντι αὐτῷ· Τίς ἐστιν ἡ μήτηρ μου, καὶ τίνες εἰσὶν οἱ ἀδελφοί μου;
verses.translit: o de apokritheis eipen to legonti auto* Tis estin e mitir moy, kai tines eisin oi adelfoi moy;
verses.translation: But he answered and said unto him that told him, Who is my mother? and who are my brethren?

verses.original: καὶ ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ εἶπεν· Ἰδοὺ ἡ μήτηρ μου καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοί μου·
verses.translit: kai ekteinas ten heira autou epi tous mathitas autou eipen* Idou e mitir moy kai oi adelfoi moy*
verses.translation: And he stretched forth his hand toward his disciples, and said, Behold my mother and my brethren!

verses.original: ὅστις γὰρ ἂν ποιήσῃ τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πατρός μου τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς, αὐτός μου ἀδελφὸς καὶ ἀδελφὴ καὶ μήτηρ ἐστίν.
verses.translit: ostis gar an poiise to thelima tou patros moy tou en ouranois, autos moy adelfos kai adelfe kai mitir estin.
verses.translation: For whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother.

verses.original: ⸀Ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ ἐξελθὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ⸀τῆς οἰκίας ἐκάθητο παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν·
verses.translit: En te emera ekeine exelthon o Iisous tes oikias ekathito para ten thalassan*
verses.translation: The same day went Jesus out of the house, and sat by the sea side.

verses.original: καὶ συνήχθησαν πρὸς αὐτὸν ὄχλοι πολλοί, ὥστε αὐτὸν ⸀εἰς πλοῖον ἐμβάντα καθῆσθαι, καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος ἐπὶ τὸν αἰγιαλὸν εἱστήκει.
verses.translit: kai synihthisan pros auton ohloi polloi, oste auton eis ploion emvanta kathesthai, kai pas o ohlos epi ton aigialon eistikei.
verses.translation: And great multitudes were gathered together unto him, so that he went into a ship, and sat; and the whole multitude stood on the shore.

verses.original: καὶ ἐλάλησεν αὐτοῖς πολλὰ ἐν παραβολαῖς λέγων· Ἰδοὺ ἐξῆλθεν ὁ σπείρων τοῦ σπείρειν.
verses.translit: kai elalisen autois polla en paravolais legon* Idou exelthen o speiron tou speirein.
verses.translation: And he spake many things unto them in parables, saying, Behold, a sower went forth to sow;

verses.original: καὶ ἐν τῷ σπείρειν αὐτὸν ἃ μὲν ἔπεσεν παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν, καὶ ⸂ἐλθόντα τὰ πετεινὰ⸃ κατέφαγεν αὐτά.
verses.translit: kai en to speirein auton a men epesen para ten odon, kai elthonta ta peteina katefagen auta.
verses.translation: And when he sowed, some seeds fell by the way side, and the fowls came and devoured them up:

verses.original: ἄλλα δὲ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὰ πετρώδη ὅπου οὐκ εἶχεν γῆν πολλήν, καὶ εὐθέως ἐξανέτειλεν διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν βάθος γῆς,
verses.translit: alla de epesen epi ta petrodi opoy ouk eihen gen pollin, kai eutheos exaneteilen dia to me ehein vathos ges,
verses.translation: Some fell upon stony places, where they had not much earth: and forthwith they sprung up, because they had no deepness of earth:

verses.original: ἡλίου δὲ ἀνατείλαντος ἐκαυματίσθη καὶ διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν ῥίζαν ἐξηράνθη.
verses.translit: elioy de anateilantos ekaymatisthi kai dia to me ehein Rizan exiranthi.
verses.translation: And when the sun was up, they were scorched; and because they had no root, they withered away.

verses.original: ἄλλα δὲ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὰς ἀκάνθας, καὶ ἀνέβησαν αἱ ἄκανθαι καὶ ⸀ἔπνιξαν αὐτά.
verses.translit: alla de epesen epi tas akanthas, kai anevisan ai akanthai kai epnixan auta.
verses.translation: And some fell among thorns; and the thorns sprung up, and choked them:

verses.original: ἄλλα δὲ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν τὴν καλὴν καὶ ἐδίδου καρπόν, ὃ μὲν ἑκατὸν ὃ δὲ ἑξήκοντα ὃ δὲ τριάκοντα.
verses.translit: alla de epesen epi ten gen ten kalen kai edidoy karpon, o men ekaton o de exikonta o de triakonta.
verses.translation: But other fell into good ground, and brought forth fruit, some an hundredfold, some sixtyfold, some thirtyfold.

verses.original: ὁ ἔχων ⸀ὦτα ἀκουέτω.
verses.translit: o ehon ota akoyeto.
verses.translation: Who hath ears to hear, let him hear.

verses.original: Καὶ προσελθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Διὰ τί ἐν παραβολαῖς λαλεῖς αὐτοῖς;
verses.translit: Kai proselthontes oi mathitai eipan auto* Dia ti en paravolais laleis autois;
verses.translation: And the disciples came, and said unto him, Why speakest thou unto them in parables?

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν ⸀αὐτοῖς· Ὅτι ὑμῖν δέδοται γνῶναι τὰ μυστήρια τῆς βασιλείας τῶν οὐρανῶν, ἐκείνοις δὲ οὐ δέδοται.
verses.translit: o de apokritheis eipen autois* Oti umin dedotai gnonai ta mystiria tes vasileias ton ouranon, ekeinois de ou dedotai.
verses.translation: He answered and said unto them, Because it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given.

verses.original: ὅστις γὰρ ἔχει, δοθήσεται αὐτῷ καὶ περισσευθήσεται· ὅστις δὲ οὐκ ἔχει, καὶ ὃ ἔχει ἀρθήσεται ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: ostis gar ehei, dothisetai auto kai perisseythisetai* ostis de ouk ehei, kai o ehei arthisetai ap' autou.
verses.translation: For whosoever hath, to him shall be given, and he shall have more abundance: but whosoever hath not, from him shall be taken away even that he hath.

verses.original: διὰ τοῦτο ἐν παραβολαῖς αὐτοῖς λαλῶ, ὅτι βλέποντες οὐ βλέπουσιν καὶ ἀκούοντες οὐκ ἀκούουσιν οὐδὲ συνίουσιν·
verses.translit: dia touto en paravolais autois lalo, oti vlepontes ou vlepoysin kai akoyontes ouk akoyoysin oude synioysin*
verses.translation: Therefore speak I to them in parables: because they seeing see not; and hearing they hear not, neither do they understand.

verses.original: καὶ ἀναπληροῦται αὐτοῖς ἡ προφητεία Ἠσαΐου ἡ λέγουσα· Ἀκοῇ ἀκούσετε καὶ οὐ μὴ συνῆτε, καὶ βλέποντες βλέψετε καὶ οὐ μὴ ἴδητε.
verses.translit: kai anapliroutai autois e profiteia EsaIoy e legoysa* Akoe akoysete kai ou me synete, kai vlepontes vlepsete kai ou me idite.
verses.translation: And in them is fulfilled the prophecy of Esaias, which saith, By hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing ye shall see, and shall not perceive:

verses.original: ἐπαχύνθη γὰρ ἡ καρδία τοῦ λαοῦ τούτου, καὶ τοῖς ὠσὶν βαρέως ἤκουσαν, καὶ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτῶν ἐκάμμυσαν· μήποτε ἴδωσιν τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς καὶ τοῖς ὠσὶν ἀκούσωσιν καὶ τῇ καρδίᾳ συνῶσιν καὶ ἐπιστρέψωσιν, καὶ ἰάσομαι αὐτούς.
verses.translit: epahynthi gar e kardia tou laou toytoy, kai tois osin vareos ekoysan, kai tous ofthalmous auton ekammysan* mipote idosin tois ofthalmois kai tois osin akoysosin kai te kardia synosin kai epistrepsosin, kai iasomai autoys.
verses.translation: For this people’s heart is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes they have closed; lest at any time they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and should understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them.

verses.original: ὑμῶν δὲ μακάριοι οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ ὅτι βλέπουσιν, καὶ τὰ ὦτα ὑμῶν ὅτι ⸀ἀκούουσιν.
verses.translit: umon de makarioi oi ofthalmoi oti vlepoysin, kai ta ota umon oti akoyoysin.
verses.translation: But blessed are your eyes, for they see: and your ears, for they hear.

verses.original: ἀμὴν γὰρ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πολλοὶ προφῆται καὶ δίκαιοι ἐπεθύμησαν ἰδεῖν ἃ βλέπετε καὶ οὐκ εἶδαν, καὶ ἀκοῦσαι ἃ ἀκούετε καὶ οὐκ ἤκουσαν.
verses.translit: amen gar lego umin oti polloi profetai kai dikaioi epethymisan idein a vlepete kai ouk eidan, kai akousai a akoyete kai ouk ekoysan.
verses.translation: For verily I say unto you, That many prophets and righteous men have desired to see those things which ye see, and have not seen them ; and to hear those things which ye hear, and have not heard them.

verses.original: Ὑμεῖς οὖν ἀκούσατε τὴν παραβολὴν τοῦ ⸀σπείραντος.
verses.translit: Umeis oun akoysate ten paravolen tou speirantos.
verses.translation: Hear ye therefore the parable of the sower.

verses.original: παντὸς ἀκούοντος τὸν λόγον τῆς βασιλείας καὶ μὴ συνιέντος, ἔρχεται ὁ πονηρὸς καὶ ἁρπάζει τὸ ἐσπαρμένον ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ· οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ παρὰ τὴν ὁδὸν σπαρείς.
verses.translit: pantos akoyontos ton logon tes vasileias kai me synientos, erhetai o poniros kai arpazei to esparmenon en te kardia autou* outos estin o para ten odon spareis.
verses.translation: When any one heareth the word of the kingdom, and understandeth it not, then cometh the wicked one , and catcheth away that which was sown in his heart. This is he which received seed by the way side.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ἐπὶ τὰ πετρώδη σπαρείς, οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τὸν λόγον ἀκούων καὶ εὐθὺς μετὰ χαρᾶς λαμβάνων αὐτόν,
verses.translit: o de epi ta petrodi spareis, outos estin o ton logon akoyon kai euthus meta haras lamvanon auton,
verses.translation: But he that received the seed into stony places, the same is he that heareth the word, and anon with joy receiveth it;

verses.original: οὐκ ἔχει δὲ ῥίζαν ἐν ἑαυτῷ ἀλλὰ πρόσκαιρός ἐστιν, γενομένης δὲ θλίψεως ἢ διωγμοῦ διὰ τὸν λόγον εὐθὺς σκανδαλίζεται.
verses.translit: ouk ehei de Rizan en eayto alla proskairos estin, genomenis de thlipseos e diogmou dia ton logon euthus skandalizetai.
verses.translation: Yet hath he not root in himself, but dureth for a while: for when tribulation or persecution ariseth because of the word, by and by he is offended.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ εἰς τὰς ἀκάνθας σπαρείς, οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τὸν λόγον ἀκούων, καὶ ἡ μέριμνα τοῦ αἰῶνος ⸀τούτου καὶ ἡ ἀπάτη τοῦ πλούτου συμπνίγει τὸν λόγον, καὶ ἄκαρπος γίνεται.
verses.translit: o de eis tas akanthas spareis, outos estin o ton logon akoyon, kai e merimna tou aionos toytoy kai e apati tou ploytoy sympnigei ton logon, kai akarpos ginetai.
verses.translation: He also that received seed among the thorns is he that heareth the word; and the care of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, choke the word, and he becometh unfruitful.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ἐπὶ τὴν ⸂καλὴν γῆν⸃ σπαρείς, οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τὸν λόγον ἀκούων καὶ ⸀συνιείς, ὃς δὴ καρποφορεῖ καὶ ποιεῖ ὃ μὲν ἑκατὸν ὃ δὲ ἑξήκοντα ὃ δὲ τριάκοντα.
verses.translit: o de epi ten kalen gen spareis, outos estin o ton logon akoyon kai synieis, os de karpoforei kai poiei o men ekaton o de exikonta o de triakonta.
verses.translation: But he that received seed into the good ground is he that heareth the word, and understandeth it ; which also beareth fruit, and bringeth forth, some an hundredfold, some sixty, some thirty.

verses.original: Ἄλλην παραβολὴν παρέθηκεν αὐτοῖς λέγων· Ὡμοιώθη ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀνθρώπῳ ⸀σπείραντι καλὸν σπέρμα ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: Allin paravolen parethiken autois legon* Omoiothi e vasileia ton ouranon anthropo speiranti kalon sperma en to agro autou.
verses.translation: Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is likened unto a man which sowed good seed in his field:

verses.original: ἐν δὲ τῷ καθεύδειν τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ἦλθεν αὐτοῦ ὁ ἐχθρὸς καὶ ⸀ἐπέσπειρεν ζιζάνια ἀνὰ μέσον τοῦ σίτου καὶ ἀπῆλθεν.
verses.translit: en de to katheydein tous anthropoys elthen autou o ehthros kai epespeiren zizania ana meson tou sitoy kai apelthen.
verses.translation: But while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat, and went his way.

verses.original: ὅτε δὲ ἐβλάστησεν ὁ χόρτος καὶ καρπὸν ἐποίησεν, τότε ἐφάνη καὶ τὰ ζιζάνια.
verses.translit: ote de evlastisen o hortos kai karpon epoiisen, tote efani kai ta zizania.
verses.translation: But when the blade was sprung up, and brought forth fruit, then appeared the tares also.

verses.original: προσελθόντες δὲ οἱ δοῦλοι τοῦ οἰκοδεσπότου εἶπον αὐτῷ· Κύριε, οὐχὶ καλὸν σπέρμα ⸀ἔσπειρας ἐν τῷ σῷ ἀγρῷ; πόθεν οὖν ἔχει ζιζάνια;
verses.translit: proselthontes de oi douloi tou oikodespotoy eipon auto* Kyrie, ouhi kalon sperma espeiras en to so agro; pothen oun ehei zizania;
verses.translation: So the servants of the householder came and said unto him, Sir, didst not thou sow good seed in thy field? from whence then hath it tares?

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ἔφη αὐτοῖς· Ἐχθρὸς ἄνθρωπος τοῦτο ἐποίησεν. οἱ δὲ ⸂δοῦλοι αὐτῷ λέγουσιν⸃· Θέλεις οὖν ἀπελθόντες ⸀συλλέξωμεν αὐτά;
verses.translit: o de efi autois* Ehthros anthropos touto epoiisen. oi de douloi auto legoysin* Theleis oun apelthontes syllexomen auta;
verses.translation: He said unto them, An enemy hath done this. The servants said unto him, Wilt thou then that we go and gather them up?

verses.original: ὁ δέ ⸀φησιν· Οὔ, μήποτε συλλέγοντες τὰ ζιζάνια ἐκριζώσητε ἅμα αὐτοῖς τὸν σῖτον·
verses.translit: o de fisin* Ou, mipote syllegontes ta zizania ekrizosite ama autois ton siton*
verses.translation: But he said, Nay; lest while ye gather up the tares, ye root up also the wheat with them.

verses.original: ἄφετε συναυξάνεσθαι ἀμφότερα ⸀μέχρι τοῦ θερισμοῦ· καὶ ἐν καιρῷ τοῦ θερισμοῦ ἐρῶ τοῖς θερισταῖς· Συλλέξατε πρῶτον τὰ ζιζάνια καὶ δήσατε αὐτὰ εἰς δέσμας πρὸς τὸ κατακαῦσαι αὐτά, τὸν δὲ σῖτον ⸀συναγάγετε εἰς τὴν ἀποθήκην μου.
verses.translit: afete synayxanesthai amfotera mehri tou therismou* kai en kairo tou therismou ero tois theristais* Syllexate proton ta zizania kai disate auta eis desmas pros to katakausai auta, ton de siton synagagete eis ten apothikin moy.
verses.translation: Let both grow together until the harvest: and in the time of harvest I will say to the reapers, Gather ye together first the tares, and bind them in bundles to burn them: but gather the wheat into my barn.

verses.original: Ἄλλην παραβολὴν παρέθηκεν αὐτοῖς λέγων· Ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν κόκκῳ σινάπεως, ὃν λαβὼν ἄνθρωπος ἔσπειρεν ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ αὐτοῦ·
verses.translit: Allin paravolen parethiken autois legon* Omoia estin e vasileia ton ouranon kokko sinapeos, on lavon anthropos espeiren en to agro autou*
verses.translation: Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field:

verses.original: ὃ μικρότερον μέν ἐστιν πάντων τῶν σπερμάτων, ὅταν δὲ αὐξηθῇ μεῖζον τῶν λαχάνων ἐστὶν καὶ γίνεται δένδρον, ὥστε ἐλθεῖν τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ κατασκηνοῦν ἐν τοῖς κλάδοις αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: o mikroteron men estin panton ton spermaton, otan de auxithe meizon ton lahanon estin kai ginetai dendron, oste elthein ta peteina tou ouranou kai kataskinoun en tois kladois autou.
verses.translation: Which indeed is the least of all seeds: but when it is grown, it is the greatest among herbs, and becometh a tree, so that the birds of the air come and lodge in the branches thereof.

verses.original: Ἄλλην παραβολὴν ἐλάλησεν αὐτοῖς· Ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ζύμῃ, ἣν λαβοῦσα γυνὴ ⸀ἐνέκρυψεν εἰς ἀλεύρου σάτα τρία ἕως οὗ ἐζυμώθη ὅλον.
verses.translit: Allin paravolen elalisen autois* Omoia estin e vasileia ton ouranon zyme, en lavousa gyne enekrypsen eis aleyroy sata tria eos ou ezymothi olon.
verses.translation: Another parable spake he unto them; The kingdom of heaven is like unto leaven, which a woman took, and hid in three measures of meal, till the whole was leavened.

verses.original: Ταῦτα πάντα ἐλάλησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐν παραβολαῖς τοῖς ὄχλοις, καὶ χωρὶς παραβολῆς ⸀οὐδὲν ἐλάλει αὐτοῖς·
verses.translit: Tauta panta elalisen o Iisous en paravolais tois ohlois, kai horis paravoles ouden elalei autois*
verses.translation: All these things spake Jesus unto the multitude in parables; and without a parable spake he not unto them:

verses.original: ὅπως πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος· Ἀνοίξω ἐν παραβολαῖς τὸ στόμα μου, ἐρεύξομαι κεκρυμμένα ἀπὸ ⸀καταβολῆς.
verses.translit: opos plirothe to Rithen dia tou profitoy legontos* Anoixo en paravolais to stoma moy, ereyxomai kekrymmena apo katavoles.
verses.translation: That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, saying, I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things which have been kept secret from the foundation of the world.

verses.original: Τότε ἀφεὶς τοὺς ὄχλους ἦλθεν εἰς τὴν ⸀οἰκίαν. καὶ προσῆλθον αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ λέγοντες· ⸀Διασάφησον ἡμῖν τὴν παραβολὴν τῶν ζιζανίων τοῦ ἀγροῦ.
verses.translit: Tote afeis tous ohloys elthen eis ten oikian. kai proselthon auto oi mathitai autou legontes* Diasafison emin ten paravolen ton zizanion tou agrou.
verses.translation: Then Jesus sent the multitude away, and went into the house: and his disciples came unto him, saying, Declare unto us the parable of the tares of the field.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς ⸀εἶπεν· Ὁ σπείρων τὸ καλὸν σπέρμα ἐστὶν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου·
verses.translit: o de apokritheis eipen* O speiron to kalon sperma estin o yios tou anthropoy*
verses.translation: He answered and said unto them, He that soweth the good seed is the Son of man;

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ἀγρός ἐστιν ὁ κόσμος· τὸ δὲ καλὸν σπέρμα, οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ υἱοὶ τῆς βασιλείας· τὰ δὲ ζιζάνιά εἰσιν οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ πονηροῦ,
verses.translit: o de agros estin o kosmos* to de kalon sperma, outoi eisin oi yioi tes vasileias* ta de zizania eisin oi yioi tou ponirou,
verses.translation: The field is the world; the good seed are the children of the kingdom; but the tares are the children of the wicked one ;

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ἐχθρὸς ὁ σπείρας αὐτά ἐστιν ὁ διάβολος· ὁ δὲ θερισμὸς συντέλεια ⸀αἰῶνός ἐστιν, οἱ δὲ θερισταὶ ἄγγελοί εἰσιν.
verses.translit: o de ehthros o speiras auta estin o diavolos* o de therismos synteleia aionos estin, oi de theristai aggeloi eisin.
verses.translation: The enemy that sowed them is the devil; the harvest is the end of the world; and the reapers are the angels.

verses.original: ὥσπερ οὖν συλλέγεται τὰ ζιζάνια καὶ πυρὶ ⸀καίεται, οὕτως ἔσται ἐν τῇ συντελείᾳ τοῦ ⸀αἰῶνος·
verses.translit: osper oun syllegetai ta zizania kai pyri kaietai, outos estai en te synteleia tou aionos*
verses.translation: As therefore the tares are gathered and burned in the fire; so shall it be in the end of this world.

verses.original: ἀποστελεῖ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τοὺς ἀγγέλους αὐτοῦ, καὶ συλλέξουσιν ἐκ τῆς βασιλείας αὐτοῦ πάντα τὰ σκάνδαλα καὶ τοὺς ποιοῦντας τὴν ἀνομίαν,
verses.translit: apostelei o yios tou anthropoy tous aggeloys autou, kai syllexoysin ek tes vasileias autou panta ta skandala kai tous poiountas ten anomian,
verses.translation: The Son of man shall send forth his angels, and they shall gather out of his kingdom all things that offend, and them which do iniquity;

verses.original: καὶ βαλοῦσιν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν κάμινον τοῦ πυρός· ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων.
verses.translit: kai valousin autous eis ten kaminon tou pyros* ekei estai o klaythmos kai o vrygmos ton odonton.
verses.translation: And shall cast them into a furnace of fire: there shall be wailing and gnashing of teeth.

verses.original: Τότε οἱ δίκαιοι ἐκλάμψουσιν ὡς ὁ ἥλιος ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτῶν. ὁ ἔχων ⸀ὦτα ἀκουέτω.
verses.translit: Tote oi dikaioi eklampsoysin os o elios en te vasileia tou patros auton. o ehon ota akoyeto.
verses.translation: Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father. Who hath ears to hear, let him hear.

verses.original: ⸀Ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν θησαυρῷ κεκρυμμένῳ ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ, ὃν εὑρὼν ἄνθρωπος ἔκρυψεν, καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς χαρᾶς αὐτοῦ ὑπάγει καὶ ⸂πωλεῖ πάντα ὅσα ἔχει⸃ καὶ ἀγοράζει τὸν ἀγρὸν ἐκεῖνον.
verses.translit: Omoia estin e vasileia ton ouranon thisayro kekrymmeno en to agro, on euron anthropos ekrypsen, kai apo tes haras autou upagei kai polei panta osa ehei kai agorazei ton agron ekeinon.
verses.translation: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto treasure hid in a field; the which when a man hath found, he hideth, and for joy thereof goeth and selleth all that he hath, and buyeth that field.

verses.original: Πάλιν ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ⸀ἀνθρώπῳ ἐμπόρῳ ζητοῦντι καλοὺς μαργαρίτας·
verses.translit: Palin omoia estin e vasileia ton ouranon anthropo emporo zitounti kalous margaritas*
verses.translation: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto a merchant man, seeking goodly pearls:

verses.original: ⸂εὑρὼν δὲ⸃ ἕνα πολύτιμον μαργαρίτην ἀπελθὼν πέπρακεν πάντα ὅσα εἶχεν καὶ ἠγόρασεν αὐτόν.
verses.translit: euron de ena polytimon margaritin apelthon pepraken panta osa eihen kai egorasen auton.
verses.translation: Who, when he had found one pearl of great price, went and sold all that he had, and bought it.

verses.original: Πάλιν ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν σαγήνῃ βληθείσῃ εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ ἐκ παντὸς γένους συναγαγούσῃ·
verses.translit: Palin omoia estin e vasileia ton ouranon sagine vlitheise eis ten thalassan kai ek pantos genoys synagagoyse*
verses.translation: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto a net, that was cast into the sea, and gathered of every kind:

verses.original: ἣν ὅτε ἐπληρώθη ἀναβιβάσαντες ἐπὶ τὸν αἰγιαλὸν καὶ καθίσαντες συνέλεξαν τὰ καλὰ εἰς ⸀ἄγγη, τὰ δὲ σαπρὰ ἔξω ἔβαλον.
verses.translit: en ote eplirothi anavivasantes epi ton aigialon kai kathisantes synelexan ta kala eis aggi, ta de sapra exo evalon.
verses.translation: Which, when it was full, they drew to shore, and sat down, and gathered the good into vessels, but cast the bad away.

verses.original: οὕτως ἔσται ἐν τῇ συντελείᾳ τοῦ αἰῶνος· ἐξελεύσονται οἱ ἄγγελοι καὶ ἀφοριοῦσιν τοὺς πονηροὺς ἐκ μέσου τῶν δικαίων
verses.translit: outos estai en te synteleia tou aionos* exeleysontai oi aggeloi kai aforiousin tous ponirous ek mesoy ton dikaion
verses.translation: So shall it be at the end of the world: the angels shall come forth, and sever the wicked from among the just,

verses.original: καὶ βαλοῦσιν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν κάμινον τοῦ πυρός· ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων.
verses.translit: kai valousin autous eis ten kaminon tou pyros* ekei estai o klaythmos kai o vrygmos ton odonton.
verses.translation: And shall cast them into the furnace of fire: there shall be wailing and gnashing of teeth.

verses.original: ⸀Συνήκατε ταῦτα πάντα; λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· ⸀Ναί.
verses.translit: Synikate tauta panta; legoysin auto* Nai.
verses.translation: Jesus saith unto them, Have ye understood all these things? They say unto him, Yea, Lord.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Διὰ τοῦτο πᾶς γραμματεὺς μαθητευθεὶς ⸂τῇ βασιλείᾳ⸃ τῶν οὐρανῶν ὅμοιός ἐστιν ἀνθρώπῳ οἰκοδεσπότῃ ὅστις ἐκβάλλει ἐκ τοῦ θησαυροῦ αὐτοῦ καινὰ καὶ παλαιά.
verses.translit: o de eipen autois* Dia touto pas grammateus mathiteytheis te vasileia ton ouranon omoios estin anthropo oikodespote ostis ekvallei ek tou thisayrou autou kaina kai palaia.
verses.translation: Then said he unto them, Therefore every scribe which is instructed unto the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is an householder, which bringeth forth out of his treasure things new and old.

verses.original: καὶ ἐγένετο ὅτε ἐτέλεσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὰς παραβολὰς ταύτας, μετῆρεν ἐκεῖθεν.
verses.translit: kai egeneto ote etelesen o Iisous tas paravolas taytas, meteren ekeithen.
verses.translation: And it came to pass, that when Jesus had finished these parables, he departed thence.

verses.original: καὶ ἐλθὼν εἰς τὴν πατρίδα αὐτοῦ ἐδίδασκεν αὐτοὺς ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ αὐτῶν, ὥστε ἐκπλήσσεσθαι αὐτοὺς καὶ λέγειν· Πόθεν τούτῳ ἡ σοφία αὕτη καὶ αἱ δυνάμεις;
verses.translit: kai elthon eis ten patrida autou edidasken autous en te synagoge auton, oste ekplissesthai autous kai legein* Pothen toyto e sofia auti kai ai dynameis;
verses.translation: And when he was come into his own country, he taught them in their synagogue, insomuch that they were astonished, and said, Whence hath this man this wisdom, and these mighty works?

verses.original: οὐχ οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τοῦ τέκτονος υἱός; ⸀οὐχ ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ λέγεται Μαριὰμ καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ Ἰάκωβος καὶ ⸀Ἰωσὴφ καὶ Σίμων καὶ Ἰούδας;
verses.translit: ouh outos estin o tou tektonos yios? ouh e mitir autou legetai Mariam kai oi adelfoi autou Iakovos kai Iosef kai Simon kai Ioydas;
verses.translation: Is not this the carpenter’s son? is not his mother called Mary? and his brethren, James, and Joses, and Simon, and Judas?

verses.original: καὶ αἱ ἀδελφαὶ αὐτοῦ οὐχὶ πᾶσαι πρὸς ἡμᾶς εἰσιν; πόθεν οὖν τούτῳ ταῦτα πάντα;
verses.translit: kai ai adelfai autou ouhi pasai pros emas eisin; pothen oun toyto tauta panta;
verses.translation: And his sisters, are they not all with us? Whence then hath this man all these things?

verses.original: καὶ ἐσκανδαλίζοντο ἐν αὐτῷ. ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Οὐκ ἔστιν προφήτης ἄτιμος εἰ μὴ ἐν τῇ ⸀πατρίδι καὶ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai eskandalizonto en auto. o de Iisous eipen autois* Ouk estin profitis atimos ei me en te patridi kai en te oikia autou.
verses.translation: And they were offended in him. But Jesus said unto them, A prophet is not without honour, save in his own country, and in his own house.

verses.original: καὶ οὐκ ἐποίησεν ἐκεῖ δυνάμεις πολλὰς διὰ τὴν ἀπιστίαν αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: kai ouk epoiisen ekei dynameis pollas dia ten apistian auton.
verses.translation: And he did not many mighty works there because of their unbelief.

verses.original: Ἐν ἐκείνῳ τῷ καιρῷ ἤκουσεν Ἡρῴδης ὁ τετραάρχης τὴν ἀκοὴν Ἰησοῦ,
verses.translit: En ekeino to kairo ekoysen Erodis o tetraarhis ten akoen Iisou,
verses.translation: At that time Herod the tetrarch heard of the fame of Jesus,

verses.original: καὶ εἶπεν τοῖς παισὶν αὐτοῦ· Οὗτός ἐστιν Ἰωάννης ὁ βαπτιστής· αὐτὸς ἠγέρθη ἀπὸ τῶν νεκρῶν, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο αἱ δυνάμεις ἐνεργοῦσιν ἐν αὐτῷ.
verses.translit: kai eipen tois paisin autou* Outos estin Ioannis o vaptistis* autos egerthi apo ton nekron, kai dia touto ai dynameis energousin en auto.
verses.translation: And said unto his servants, This is John the Baptist; he is risen from the dead; and therefore mighty works do shew forth themselves in him.

verses.original: Ὁ γὰρ Ἡρῴδης κρατήσας τὸν Ἰωάννην ἔδησεν ⸀αὐτὸν καὶ ⸂ἐν φυλακῇ ἀπέθετο⸃ διὰ Ἡρῳδιάδα τὴν γυναῖκα Φιλίππου τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ,
verses.translit: O gar Erodis kratisas ton Ioannin edisen auton kai en fylake apetheto dia Erodiada ten gynaika Filippoy tou adelfou autou,
verses.translation: For Herod had laid hold on John, and bound him, and put him in prison for Herodias’ sake, his brother Philip’s wife.

verses.original: ἔλεγεν γὰρ ⸂αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰωάννης⸃· Οὐκ ἔξεστίν σοι ἔχειν αὐτήν·
verses.translit: elegen gar auto o Ioannis* Ouk exestin soi ehein autin*
verses.translation: For John said unto him, It is not lawful for thee to have her.

verses.original: καὶ θέλων αὐτὸν ἀποκτεῖναι ἐφοβήθη τὸν ὄχλον, ὅτι ὡς προφήτην αὐτὸν εἶχον.
verses.translit: kai thelon auton apokteinai efovithi ton ohlon, oti os profitin auton eihon.
verses.translation: And when he would have put him to death, he feared the multitude, because they counted him as a prophet.

verses.original: ⸂γενεσίοις δὲ γενομένοις⸃ τοῦ Ἡρῴδου ὠρχήσατο ἡ θυγάτηρ τῆς Ἡρῳδιάδος ἐν τῷ μέσῳ καὶ ἤρεσεν τῷ Ἡρῴδῃ,
verses.translit: genesiois de genomenois tou Erodoy orhisato e thygatir tes Erodiados en to meso kai eresen to Erode,
verses.translation: But when Herod’s birthday was kept, the daughter of Herodias danced before them, and pleased Herod.

verses.original: ὅθεν μετὰ ὅρκου ὡμολόγησεν αὐτῇ δοῦναι ὃ ⸀ἐὰν αἰτήσηται.
verses.translit: othen meta orkoy omologisen aute dounai o ean aitisitai.
verses.translation: Whereupon he promised with an oath to give her whatsoever she would ask.

verses.original: ἡ δὲ προβιβασθεῖσα ὑπὸ τῆς μητρὸς αὐτῆς· Δός μοι, φησίν, ὧδε ἐπὶ πίνακι τὴν κεφαλὴν Ἰωάννου τοῦ βαπτιστοῦ.
verses.translit: e de provivastheisa upo tes mitros autes* Dos moi, fisin, ode epi pinaki ten kefalen Ioannoy tou vaptistou.
verses.translation: And she, being before instructed of her mother, said, Give me here John Baptist’s head in a charger.

verses.original: καὶ ⸂λυπηθεὶς ὁ βασιλεὺς διὰ⸃ τοὺς ὅρκους καὶ τοὺς συνανακειμένους ἐκέλευσεν δοθῆναι,
verses.translit: kai lypitheis o vasileus dia tous orkoys kai tous synanakeimenoys ekeleysen dothenai,
verses.translation: And the king was sorry: nevertheless for the oath’s sake, and them which sat with him at meat, he commanded it to be given her .

verses.original: καὶ πέμψας ἀπεκεφάλισεν ⸀τὸν Ἰωάννην ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ·
verses.translit: kai pempsas apekefalisen ton Ioannin en te fylake*
verses.translation: And he sent, and beheaded John in the prison.

verses.original: καὶ ἠνέχθη ἡ κεφαλὴ αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ πίνακι καὶ ἐδόθη τῷ κορασίῳ, καὶ ἤνεγκεν τῇ μητρὶ αὐτῆς.
verses.translit: kai enehthi e kefale autou epi pinaki kai edothi to korasio, kai enegken te mitri autes.
verses.translation: And his head was brought in a charger, and given to the damsel: and she brought it to her mother.

verses.original: καὶ προσελθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἦραν τὸ ⸀πτῶμα καὶ ἔθαψαν ⸀αὐτόν, καὶ ἐλθόντες ἀπήγγειλαν τῷ Ἰησοῦ.
verses.translit: kai proselthontes oi mathitai autou eran to ptoma kai ethapsan auton, kai elthontes apiggeilan to Iisou.
verses.translation: And his disciples came, and took up the body, and buried it, and went and told Jesus.

verses.original: ⸂Ἀκούσας δὲ⸃ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀνεχώρησεν ἐκεῖθεν ἐν πλοίῳ εἰς ἔρημον τόπον κατʼ ἰδίαν· καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ ὄχλοι ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ πεζῇ ἀπὸ τῶν πόλεων.
verses.translit: Akoysas de o Iisous anehorisen ekeithen en ploio eis erimon topon kat' idian* kai akoysantes oi ohloi ekoloythisan auto peze apo ton poleon.
verses.translation: When Jesus heard of it , he departed thence by ship into a desert place apart: and when the people had heard thereof , they followed him on foot out of the cities.

verses.original: καὶ ⸀ἐξελθὼν εἶδεν πολὺν ὄχλον, καὶ ἐσπλαγχνίσθη ἐπʼ αὐτοῖς καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν τοὺς ἀρρώστους αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: kai exelthon eiden polun ohlon, kai esplaghnisthi ep' autois kai etherapeysen tous arrostoys auton.
verses.translation: And Jesus went forth, and saw a great multitude, and was moved with compassion toward them, and he healed their sick.

verses.original: ὀψίας δὲ γενομένης προσῆλθον αὐτῷ οἱ ⸀μαθηταὶ λέγοντες· Ἔρημός ἐστιν ὁ τόπος καὶ ἡ ὥρα ἤδη παρῆλθεν· ἀπόλυσον τοὺς ὄχλους, ἵνα ἀπελθόντες εἰς τὰς κώμας ἀγοράσωσιν ἑαυτοῖς βρώματα.
verses.translit: opsias de genomenis proselthon auto oi mathitai legontes* Erimos estin o topos kai e ora edi parelthen* apolyson tous ohloys, ina apelthontes eis tas komas agorasosin eaytois vromata.
verses.translation: And when it was evening, his disciples came to him, saying, This is a desert place, and the time is now past; send the multitude away, that they may go into the villages, and buy themselves victuals.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Οὐ χρείαν ἔχουσιν ἀπελθεῖν· δότε αὐτοῖς ὑμεῖς φαγεῖν.
verses.translit: o de Iisous eipen autois* Ou hreian ehoysin apelthein* dote autois umeis fagein.
verses.translation: But Jesus said unto them, They need not depart; give ye them to eat.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Οὐκ ἔχομεν ὧδε εἰ μὴ πέντε ἄρτους καὶ δύο ἰχθύας.
verses.translit: oi de legoysin auto* Ouk ehomen ode ei me pente artoys kai dyo ihthyas.
verses.translation: And they say unto him, We have here but five loaves, and two fishes.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Φέρετέ μοι ⸂ὧδε αὐτούς⸃.
verses.translit: o de eipen* Ferete moi ode autoys.
verses.translation: He said, Bring them hither to me.

verses.original: καὶ κελεύσας τοὺς ὄχλους ἀνακλιθῆναι ἐπὶ ⸂τοῦ χόρτου⸃, λαβὼν τοὺς πέντε ἄρτους καὶ τοὺς δύο ἰχθύας, ἀναβλέψας εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν εὐλόγησεν καὶ κλάσας ἔδωκεν τοῖς μαθηταῖς τοὺς ἄρτους οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ τοῖς ὄχλοις.
verses.translit: kai keleysas tous ohloys anaklithenai epi tou hortoy, lavon tous pente artoys kai tous dyo ihthyas, anavlepsas eis ton ouranon eulogisen kai klasas edoken tois mathitais tous artoys oi de mathitai tois ohlois.
verses.translation: And he commanded the multitude to sit down on the grass, and took the five loaves, and the two fishes, and looking up to heaven, he blessed, and brake, and gave the loaves to his disciples, and the disciples to the multitude.

verses.original: καὶ ἔφαγον πάντες καὶ ἐχορτάσθησαν, καὶ ἦραν τὸ περισσεῦον τῶν κλασμάτων δώδεκα κοφίνους πλήρεις.
verses.translit: kai efagon pantes kai ehortasthisan, kai eran to perisseuon ton klasmaton dodeka kofinoys plireis.
verses.translation: And they did all eat, and were filled: and they took up of the fragments that remained twelve baskets full.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ ἐσθίοντες ἦσαν ἄνδρες ὡσεὶ πεντακισχίλιοι χωρὶς γυναικῶν καὶ παιδίων.
verses.translit: oi de esthiontes esan andres osei pentakishilioi horis gynaikon kai paidion.
verses.translation: And they that had eaten were about five thousand men, beside women and children.

verses.original: Καὶ εὐθέως ⸀ἠνάγκασεν τοὺς μαθητὰς ἐμβῆναι ⸀εἰς πλοῖον καὶ προάγειν αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ πέραν, ἕως οὗ ἀπολύσῃ τοὺς ὄχλους.
verses.translit: Kai eutheos enagkasen tous mathitas emvenai eis ploion kai proagein auton eis to peran, eos ou apolyse tous ohloys.
verses.translation: And straightway Jesus constrained his disciples to get into a ship, and to go before him unto the other side, while he sent the multitudes away.

verses.original: καὶ ἀπολύσας τοὺς ὄχλους ἀνέβη εἰς τὸ ὄρος κατʼ ἰδίαν προσεύξασθαι. ὀψίας δὲ γενομένης μόνος ἦν ἐκεῖ.
verses.translit: kai apolysas tous ohloys anevi eis to oros kat' idian proseyxasthai. opsias de genomenis monos en ekei.
verses.translation: And when he had sent the multitudes away, he went up into a mountain apart to pray: and when the evening was come, he was there alone.

verses.original: τὸ δὲ πλοῖον ἤδη ⸂σταδίους πολλοὺς ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς ἀπεῖχεν⸃, βασανιζόμενον ὑπὸ τῶν κυμάτων, ἦν γὰρ ἐναντίος ὁ ἄνεμος.
verses.translit: to de ploion edi stadioys pollous apo tes ges apeihen, vasanizomenon upo ton kymaton, en gar enantios o anemos.
verses.translation: But the ship was now in the midst of the sea, tossed with waves: for the wind was contrary.

verses.original: τετάρτῃ δὲ φυλακῇ τῆς νυκτὸς ⸀ἦλθεν πρὸς ⸀αὐτοὺς περιπατῶν ἐπὶ ⸂τὴν θάλασσαν⸃.
verses.translit: tetarte de fylake tes nyktos elthen pros autous peripaton epi ten thalassan.
verses.translation: And in the fourth watch of the night Jesus went unto them, walking on the sea.

verses.original: ⸂οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ ἰδόντες αὐτὸν⸃ ἐπὶ ⸂τῆς θαλάσσης⸃ περιπατοῦντα ἐταράχθησαν λέγοντες ὅτι Φάντασμά ἐστιν, καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ φόβου ἔκραξαν.
verses.translit: oi de mathitai idontes auton epi tes thalassis peripatounta etarahthisan legontes oti Fantasma estin, kai apo tou fovoy ekraxan.
verses.translation: And when the disciples saw him walking on the sea, they were troubled, saying, It is a spirit; and they cried out for fear.

verses.original: ⸀εὐθὺς δὲ ἐλάλησεν ⸂αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς⸃ λέγων· Θαρσεῖτε, ἐγώ εἰμι· μὴ φοβεῖσθε.
verses.translit: euthus de elalisen autois o Iisous legon* Tharseite, ego eimi* me foveisthe.
verses.translation: But straightway Jesus spake unto them, saying, Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid.

verses.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ⸂αὐτῷ ὁ Πέτρος εἶπεν⸃· Κύριε, εἰ σὺ εἶ, κέλευσόν με ⸂ἐλθεῖν πρὸς σὲ⸃ ἐπὶ τὰ ὕδατα·
verses.translit: Apokritheis de auto o Petros eipen* Kyrie, ei su ei, keleyson me elthein pros se epi ta udata*
verses.translation: And Peter answered him and said, Lord, if it be thou, bid me come unto thee on the water.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ἐλθέ. καὶ καταβὰς ἀπὸ τοῦ ⸀πλοίου Πέτρος περιεπάτησεν ἐπὶ τὰ ὕδατα ⸂καὶ ἦλθεν⸃ πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν.
verses.translit: o de eipen* Elthe. kai katavas apo tou ploioy Petros periepatisen epi ta udata kai elthen pros ton Iisoun.
verses.translation: And he said, Come. And when Peter was come down out of the ship, he walked on the water, to go to Jesus.

verses.original: βλέπων δὲ τὸν ἄνεμον ⸀ἰσχυρὸν ἐφοβήθη, καὶ ἀρξάμενος καταποντίζεσθαι ἔκραξεν λέγων· Κύριε, σῶσόν με.
verses.translit: vlepon de ton anemon ishyron efovithi, kai arxamenos katapontizesthai ekraxen legon* Kyrie, soson me.
verses.translation: But when he saw the wind boisterous, he was afraid; and beginning to sink, he cried, saying, Lord, save me.

verses.original: εὐθέως δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα ἐπελάβετο αὐτοῦ καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Ὀλιγόπιστε, εἰς τί ἐδίστασας;
verses.translit: eutheos de o Iisous ekteinas ten heira epelaveto autou kai legei auto* Oligopiste, eis ti edistasas;
verses.translation: And immediately Jesus stretched forth his hand, and caught him, and said unto him, O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt?

verses.original: καὶ ⸀ἀναβάντων αὐτῶν εἰς τὸ πλοῖον ἐκόπασεν ὁ ἄνεμος.
verses.translit: kai anavanton auton eis to ploion ekopasen o anemos.
verses.translation: And when they were come into the ship, the wind ceased.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ ἐν τῷ ⸀πλοίῳ προσεκύνησαν αὐτῷ λέγοντες· Ἀληθῶς θεοῦ υἱὸς εἶ.
verses.translit: oi de en to ploio prosekynisan auto legontes* Alithos theou yios ei.
verses.translation: Then they that were in the ship came and worshipped him, saying, Of a truth thou art the Son of God.

verses.original: Καὶ διαπεράσαντες ἦλθον ⸂ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν εἰς⸃ Γεννησαρέτ.
verses.translit: Kai diaperasantes elthon epi ten gen eis Gennisaret.
verses.translation: And when they were gone over, they came into the land of Gennesaret.

verses.original: καὶ ἐπιγνόντες αὐτὸν οἱ ἄνδρες τοῦ τόπου ἐκείνου ἀπέστειλαν εἰς ὅλην τὴν περίχωρον ἐκείνην, καὶ προσήνεγκαν αὐτῷ πάντας τοὺς κακῶς ἔχοντας,
verses.translit: kai epignontes auton oi andres tou topoy ekeinoy apesteilan eis olin ten perihoron ekeinin, kai prosinegkan auto pantas tous kakos ehontas,
verses.translation: And when the men of that place had knowledge of him, they sent out into all that country round about, and brought unto him all that were diseased;

verses.original: καὶ παρεκάλουν αὐτὸν ἵνα μόνον ἅψωνται τοῦ κρασπέδου τοῦ ἱματίου αὐτοῦ· καὶ ὅσοι ἥψαντο διεσώθησαν.
verses.translit: kai parekaloyn auton ina monon apsontai tou kraspedoy tou imatioy autou* kai osoi epsanto diesothisan.
verses.translation: And besought him that they might only touch the hem of his garment: and as many as touched were made perfectly whole.

verses.original: Τότε προσέρχονται τῷ ⸀Ἰησοῦ ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων ⸂Φαρισαῖοι καὶ γραμματεῖς⸃ λέγοντες
verses.translit: Tote proserhontai to Iisou apo Ierosolymon Farisaioi kai grammateis legontes
verses.translation: Then came to Jesus scribes and Pharisees, which were of Jerusalem, saying,

verses.original: Διὰ τί οἱ μαθηταί σου παραβαίνουσιν τὴν παράδοσιν τῶν πρεσβυτέρων; οὐ γὰρ νίπτονται τὰς χεῖρας ⸀αὐτῶν ὅταν ἄρτον ἐσθίωσιν.
verses.translit: Dia ti oi mathitai soy paravainoysin ten paradosin ton presvyteron; ou gar niptontai tas heiras auton otan arton esthiosin.
verses.translation: Why do thy disciples transgress the tradition of the elders? for they wash not their hands when they eat bread.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Διὰ τί καὶ ὑμεῖς παραβαίνετε τὴν ἐντολὴν τοῦ θεοῦ διὰ τὴν παράδοσιν ὑμῶν;
verses.translit: o de apokritheis eipen autois* Dia ti kai umeis paravainete ten entolen tou theou dia ten paradosin umon;
verses.translation: But he answered and said unto them, Why do ye also transgress the commandment of God by your tradition?

verses.original: ὁ γὰρ θεὸς ⸀εἶπεν· Τίμα τὸν πατέρα καὶ τὴν μητέρα, καί· Ὁ κακολογῶν πατέρα ἢ μητέρα θανάτῳ τελευτάτω·
verses.translit: o gar theos eipen* Tima ton patera kai ten mitera, kai* O kakologon patera e mitera thanato teleytato*
verses.translation: For God commanded, saying, Honour thy father and mother: and, He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death.

verses.original: ὑμεῖς δὲ λέγετε· Ὃς ἂν εἴπῃ τῷ πατρὶ ἢ τῇ μητρί· Δῶρον ὃ ἐὰν ἐξ ἐμοῦ ὠφεληθῇς,
verses.translit: umeis de legete* Os an eipe to patri e te mitri* Doron o ean ex emou ofelithes,
verses.translation: But ye say, Whosoever shall say to his father or his mother, It is a gift, by whatsoever thou mightest be profited by me;

verses.original: ⸀οὐ μὴ ⸀τιμήσει τὸν πατέρα ⸀αὐτοῦ· καὶ ἠκυρώσατε ⸂τὸν λόγον⸃ τοῦ θεοῦ διὰ τὴν παράδοσιν ὑμῶν.
verses.translit: ou me timisei ton patera autou* kai ekyrosate ton logon tou theou dia ten paradosin umon.
verses.translation: And honour not his father or his mother, he shall be free . Thus have ye made the commandment of God of none effect by your tradition.

verses.original: ὑποκριταί, καλῶς ἐπροφήτευσεν περὶ ὑμῶν Ἠσαΐας λέγων·
verses.translit: upokritai, kalos eprofiteysen peri umon EsaIas legon*
verses.translation: Ye hypocrites, well did Esaias prophesy of you, saying,

verses.original: ⸂Ὁ λαὸς οὗτος⸃ τοῖς χείλεσίν με τιμᾷ, ἡ δὲ καρδία αὐτῶν πόρρω ἀπέχει ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ·
verses.translit: O laos outos tois heilesin me tima, e de kardia auton porro apehei ap' emou*
verses.translation: This people draweth nigh unto me with their mouth, and honoureth me with their lips; but their heart is far from me.

verses.original: μάτην δὲ σέβονταί με, διδάσκοντες διδασκαλίας ἐντάλματα ἀνθρώπων.
verses.translit: matin de sevontai me, didaskontes didaskalias entalmata anthropon.
verses.translation: But in vain they do worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.

verses.original: Καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος τὸν ὄχλον εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἀκούετε καὶ συνίετε·
verses.translit: Kai proskalesamenos ton ohlon eipen autois* Akoyete kai syniete*
verses.translation: And he called the multitude, and said unto them, Hear, and understand:

verses.original: οὐ τὸ εἰσερχόμενον εἰς τὸ στόμα κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον, ἀλλὰ τὸ ἐκπορευόμενον ἐκ τοῦ στόματος τοῦτο κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον.
verses.translit: ou to eiserhomenon eis to stoma koinoi ton anthropon, alla to ekporeyomenon ek tou stomatos touto koinoi ton anthropon.
verses.translation: Not that which goeth into the mouth defileth a man; but that which cometh out of the mouth, this defileth a man.

verses.original: Τότε προσελθόντες οἱ ⸀μαθηταὶ ⸀λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Οἶδας ὅτι οἱ Φαρισαῖοι ἀκούσαντες τὸν λόγον ἐσκανδαλίσθησαν;
verses.translit: Tote proselthontes oi mathitai legoysin auto* Oidas oti oi Farisaioi akoysantes ton logon eskandalisthisan;
verses.translation: Then came his disciples, and said unto him, Knowest thou that the Pharisees were offended, after they heard this saying?

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Πᾶσα φυτεία ἣν οὐκ ἐφύτευσεν ὁ πατήρ μου ὁ οὐράνιος ἐκριζωθήσεται.
verses.translit: o de apokritheis eipen* Pasa fyteia en ouk efyteysen o patir moy o ouranios ekrizothisetai.
verses.translation: But he answered and said, Every plant, which my heavenly Father hath not planted, shall be rooted up.

verses.original: ἄφετε αὐτούς· ⸂τυφλοί εἰσιν ὁδηγοὶ τυφλῶν⸃· τυφλὸς δὲ τυφλὸν ἐὰν ὁδηγῇ, ἀμφότεροι εἰς βόθυνον πεσοῦνται.
verses.translit: afete autoys* tyfloi eisin odigoi tyflon* tyflos de tyflon ean odige, amfoteroi eis vothynon pesountai.
verses.translation: Let them alone: they be blind leaders of the blind. And if the blind lead the blind, both shall fall into the ditch.

verses.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Πέτρος εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Φράσον ἡμῖν τὴν παραβολὴν ⸀ταύτην.
verses.translit: Apokritheis de o Petros eipen auto* Frason emin ten paravolen taytin.
verses.translation: Then answered Peter and said unto him, Declare unto us this parable.

verses.original: ὁ ⸀δὲ εἶπεν· Ἀκμὴν καὶ ὑμεῖς ἀσύνετοί ἐστε;
verses.translit: o de eipen* Akmen kai umeis asynetoi este;
verses.translation: And Jesus said, Are ye also yet without understanding?

verses.original: ⸀οὐ νοεῖτε ὅτι πᾶν τὸ εἰσπορευόμενον εἰς τὸ στόμα εἰς τὴν κοιλίαν χωρεῖ καὶ εἰς ἀφεδρῶνα ἐκβάλλεται;
verses.translit: ou noeite oti pan to eisporeyomenon eis to stoma eis ten koilian horei kai eis afedrona ekvalletai;
verses.translation: Do not ye yet understand, that whatsoever entereth in at the mouth goeth into the belly, and is cast out into the draught?

verses.original: τὰ δὲ ἐκπορευόμενα ἐκ τοῦ στόματος ἐκ τῆς καρδίας ἐξέρχεται, κἀκεῖνα κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον.
verses.translit: ta de ekporeyomena ek tou stomatos ek tes kardias exerhetai, kakeina koinoi ton anthropon.
verses.translation: But those things which proceed out of the mouth come forth from the heart; and they defile the man.

verses.original: ἐκ γὰρ τῆς καρδίας ἐξέρχονται διαλογισμοὶ πονηροί, φόνοι, μοιχεῖαι, πορνεῖαι, κλοπαί, ψευδομαρτυρίαι, βλασφημίαι.
verses.translit: ek gar tes kardias exerhontai dialogismoi poniroi, fonoi, moiheiai, porneiai, klopai, pseydomartyriai, vlasfimiai.
verses.translation: For out of the heart proceed evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false witness, blasphemies:

verses.original: ταῦτά ἐστιν τὰ κοινοῦντα τὸν ἄνθρωπον, τὸ δὲ ἀνίπτοις χερσὶν φαγεῖν οὐ κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον.
verses.translit: tauta estin ta koinounta ton anthropon, to de aniptois hersin fagein ou koinoi ton anthropon.
verses.translation: These are the things which defile a man: but to eat with unwashen hands defileth not a man.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐξελθὼν ἐκεῖθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀνεχώρησεν εἰς τὰ μέρη Τύρου καὶ Σιδῶνος.
verses.translit: Kai exelthon ekeithen o Iisous anehorisen eis ta meri Tyroy kai Sidonos.
verses.translation: Then Jesus went thence, and departed into the coasts of Tyre and Sidon.

verses.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ γυνὴ Χαναναία ἀπὸ τῶν ὁρίων ἐκείνων ἐξελθοῦσα ⸀ἔκραζεν λέγουσα· Ἐλέησόν με, κύριε ⸀υἱὸς Δαυίδ· ἡ θυγάτηρ μου κακῶς δαιμονίζεται.
verses.translit: kai idou gyne Hananaia apo ton orion ekeinon exelthousa ekrazen legoysa* Eleison me, kyrie yios Dayid* e thygatir moy kakos daimonizetai.
verses.translation: And, behold, a woman of Canaan came out of the same coasts, and cried unto him, saying, Have mercy on me, O Lord, thou Son of David; my daughter is grievously vexed with a devil.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ οὐκ ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῇ λόγον. καὶ προσελθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ⸀ἠρώτουν αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Ἀπόλυσον αὐτήν, ὅτι κράζει ὄπισθεν ἡμῶν.
verses.translit: o de ouk apekrithi aute logon. kai proselthontes oi mathitai autou erotoyn auton legontes* Apolyson autin, oti krazei opisthen emon.
verses.translation: But he answered her not a word. And his disciples came and besought him, saying, Send her away; for she crieth after us.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Οὐκ ἀπεστάλην εἰ μὴ εἰς τὰ πρόβατα τὰ ἀπολωλότα οἴκου Ἰσραήλ.
verses.translit: o de apokritheis eipen* Ouk apestalin ei me eis ta provata ta apololota oikoy Israil.
verses.translation: But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.

verses.original: ἡ δὲ ἐλθοῦσα ⸀προσεκύνει αὐτῷ λέγουσα· Κύριε, βοήθει μοι.
verses.translit: e de elthousa prosekynei auto legoysa* Kyrie, voithei moi.
verses.translation: Then came she and worshipped him, saying, Lord, help me.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Οὐκ ἔστιν καλὸν λαβεῖν τὸν ἄρτον τῶν τέκνων καὶ βαλεῖν τοῖς κυναρίοις.
verses.translit: o de apokritheis eipen* Ouk estin kalon lavein ton arton ton teknon kai valein tois kynariois.
verses.translation: But he answered and said, It is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it to dogs.

verses.original: ἡ δὲ εἶπεν· Ναί, κύριε, καὶ γὰρ τὰ κυνάρια ἐσθίει ἀπὸ τῶν ψιχίων τῶν πιπτόντων ἀπὸ τῆς τραπέζης τῶν κυρίων αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: e de eipen* Nai, kyrie, kai gar ta kynaria esthiei apo ton psihion ton piptonton apo tes trapezis ton kyrion auton.
verses.translation: And she said, Truth, Lord: yet the dogs eat of the crumbs which fall from their masters’ table.

verses.original: τότε ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῇ· Ὦ γύναι, μεγάλη σου ἡ πίστις· γενηθήτω σοι ὡς θέλεις. καὶ ἰάθη ἡ θυγάτηρ αὐτῆς ἀπὸ τῆς ὥρας ἐκείνης.
verses.translit: tote apokritheis o Iisous eipen aute* O gynai, megali soy e pistis* genithito soi os theleis. kai iathi e thygatir autes apo tes oras ekeinis.
verses.translation: Then Jesus answered and said unto her, O woman, great is thy faith: be it unto thee even as thou wilt. And her daughter was made whole from that very hour.

verses.original: Καὶ μεταβὰς ἐκεῖθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἦλθεν παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν τῆς Γαλιλαίας, καὶ ἀναβὰς εἰς τὸ ὄρος ἐκάθητο ἐκεῖ.
verses.translit: Kai metavas ekeithen o Iisous elthen para ten thalassan tes Galilaias, kai anavas eis to oros ekathito ekei.
verses.translation: And Jesus departed from thence, and came nigh unto the sea of Galilee; and went up into a mountain, and sat down there.

verses.original: καὶ προσῆλθον αὐτῷ ὄχλοι πολλοὶ ἔχοντες μεθʼ ἑαυτῶν ⸂κωφούς, τυφλούς, χωλούς, κυλλούς⸃, καὶ ἑτέρους πολλούς, καὶ ἔρριψαν αὐτοὺς παρὰ τοὺς πόδας ⸀αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν αὐτούς·
verses.translit: kai proselthon auto ohloi polloi ehontes meth' eayton kofoys, tyfloys, holoys, kylloys, kai eteroys polloys, kai erripsan autous para tous podas autou, kai etherapeysen autoys*
verses.translation: And great multitudes came unto him, having with them those that were lame, blind, dumb, maimed, and many others, and cast them down at Jesus’ feet; and he healed them:

verses.original: ὥστε ⸂τὸν ὄχλον⸃ θαυμάσαι βλέποντας κωφοὺς λαλοῦντας ⸂κυλλοὺς ὑγιεῖς⸃ ⸀καὶ χωλοὺς περιπατοῦντας καὶ τυφλοὺς βλέποντας· καὶ ἐδόξασαν τὸν θεὸν Ἰσραήλ.
verses.translit: oste ton ohlon thaymasai vlepontas kofous lalountas kyllous ugieis kai holous peripatountas kai tyflous vlepontas* kai edoxasan ton theon Israil.
verses.translation: Insomuch that the multitude wondered, when they saw the dumb to speak, the maimed to be whole, the lame to walk, and the blind to see: and they glorified the God of Israel.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς προσκαλεσάμενος τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ εἶπεν· Σπλαγχνίζομαι ἐπὶ τὸν ὄχλον, ὅτι ἤδη ἡμέραι τρεῖς προσμένουσίν μοι καὶ οὐκ ἔχουσιν τί φάγωσιν· καὶ ἀπολῦσαι αὐτοὺς νήστεις οὐ θέλω, μήποτε ἐκλυθῶσιν ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ.
verses.translit: O de Iisous proskalesamenos tous mathitas autou eipen* Splaghnizomai epi ton ohlon, oti edi emerai treis prosmenoysin moi kai ouk ehoysin ti fagosin* kai apolusai autous nisteis ou thelo, mipote eklythosin en te odo.
verses.translation: Then Jesus called his disciples unto him , and said, I have compassion on the multitude, because they continue with me now three days, and have nothing to eat: and I will not send them away fasting, lest they faint in the way.

verses.original: καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ οἱ ⸀μαθηταί· Πόθεν ἡμῖν ἐν ἐρημίᾳ ἄρτοι τοσοῦτοι ὥστε χορτάσαι ὄχλον τοσοῦτον;
verses.translit: kai legoysin auto oi mathitai* Pothen emin en erimia artoi tosoutoi oste hortasai ohlon tosouton;
verses.translation: And his disciples say unto him, Whence should we have so much bread in the wilderness, as to fill so great a multitude?

verses.original: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Πόσους ἄρτους ἔχετε; οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Ἑπτά, καὶ ὀλίγα ἰχθύδια.
verses.translit: kai legei autois o Iisous* Posoys artoys ehete; oi de eipan* Epta, kai oliga ihthydia.
verses.translation: And Jesus saith unto them, How many loaves have ye? And they said, Seven, and a few little fishes.

verses.original: καὶ ⸀παραγγείλας ⸂τῷ ὄχλῳ⸃ ἀναπεσεῖν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν
verses.translit: kai paraggeilas to ohlo anapesein epi ten gen
verses.translation: And he commanded the multitude to sit down on the ground.

verses.original: ⸀ἔλαβεν τοὺς ἑπτὰ ἄρτους καὶ τοὺς ἰχθύας ⸀καὶ εὐχαριστήσας ἔκλασεν καὶ ⸀ἐδίδου τοῖς ⸀μαθηταῖς οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ ⸂τοῖς ὄχλοις⸃.
verses.translit: elaven tous epta artoys kai tous ihthyas kai euharistisas eklasen kai edidoy tois mathitais oi de mathitai tois ohlois.
verses.translation: And he took the seven loaves and the fishes, and gave thanks, and brake them , and gave to his disciples, and the disciples to the multitude.

verses.original: καὶ ἔφαγον πάντες καὶ ἐχορτάσθησαν, καὶ ⸂τὸ περισσεῦον τῶν κλασμάτων ἦραν⸃ ἑπτὰ σπυρίδας πλήρεις.
verses.translit: kai efagon pantes kai ehortasthisan, kai to perisseuon ton klasmaton eran epta spyridas plireis.
verses.translation: And they did all eat, and were filled: and they took up of the broken meat that was left seven baskets full.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ ἐσθίοντες ἦσαν τετρακισχίλιοι ἄνδρες χωρὶς γυναικῶν καὶ παιδίων.
verses.translit: oi de esthiontes esan tetrakishilioi andres horis gynaikon kai paidion.
verses.translation: And they that did eat were four thousand men, beside women and children.

verses.original: καὶ ἀπολύσας τοὺς ὄχλους ἐνέβη εἰς τὸ πλοῖον, καὶ ἦλθεν εἰς τὰ ὅρια ⸀Μαγαδάν.
verses.translit: kai apolysas tous ohloys enevi eis to ploion, kai elthen eis ta oria Magadan.
verses.translation: And he sent away the multitude, and took ship, and came into the coasts of Magdala.

verses.original: Καὶ προσελθόντες οἱ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ Σαδδουκαῖοι πειράζοντες ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν σημεῖον ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἐπιδεῖξαι αὐτοῖς.
verses.translit: Kai proselthontes oi Farisaioi kai Saddoykaioi peirazontes epirotisan auton simeion ek tou ouranou epideixai autois.
verses.translation: The Pharisees also with the Sadducees came, and tempting desired him that he would shew them a sign from heaven.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· ⸂Ὀψίας γενομένης λέγετε· Εὐδία, πυρράζει γὰρ ὁ οὐρανός·
verses.translit: o de apokritheis eipen autois* Opsias genomenis legete* Eudia, pyrrazei gar o ouranos*
verses.translation: He answered and said unto them, When it is evening, ye say, It will be fair weather: for the sky is red.

verses.original: καὶ πρωΐ· Σήμερον χειμών, πυρράζει γὰρ στυγνάζων ὁ οὐρανός. ⸀τὸ μὲν πρόσωπον τοῦ οὐρανοῦ γινώσκετε διακρίνειν, τὰ δὲ σημεῖα τῶν καιρῶν οὐ δύνασθε.⸃
verses.translit: kai proI* Simeron heimon, pyrrazei gar stygnazon o ouranos. to men prosopon tou ouranou ginoskete diakrinein, ta de simeia ton kairon ou dynasthe.
verses.translation: And in the morning, It will be foul weather to day: for the sky is red and lowring. O ye hypocrites, ye can discern the face of the sky; but can ye not discern the signs of the times?

verses.original: Γενεὰ πονηρὰ καὶ μοιχαλὶς σημεῖον ἐπιζητεῖ, καὶ σημεῖον οὐ δοθήσεται αὐτῇ εἰ μὴ τὸ σημεῖον ⸀Ἰωνᾶ. καὶ καταλιπὼν αὐτοὺς ἀπῆλθεν.
verses.translit: Genea ponira kai moihalis simeion epizitei, kai simeion ou dothisetai aute ei me to simeion Iona. kai katalipon autous apelthen.
verses.translation: A wicked and adulterous generation seeketh after a sign; and there shall no sign be given unto it, but the sign of the prophet Jonas. And he left them, and departed.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐλθόντες οἱ ⸀μαθηταὶ εἰς τὸ πέραν ἐπελάθοντο ἄρτους λαβεῖν.
verses.translit: Kai elthontes oi mathitai eis to peran epelathonto artoys lavein.
verses.translation: And when his disciples were come to the other side, they had forgotten to take bread.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὁρᾶτε καὶ προσέχετε ἀπὸ τῆς ζύμης τῶν Φαρισαίων καὶ Σαδδουκαίων.
verses.translit: o de Iisous eipen autois* Orate kai prosehete apo tes zymis ton Farisaion kai Saddoykaion.
verses.translation: Then Jesus said unto them, Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ διελογίζοντο ἐν ἑαυτοῖς λέγοντες ὅτι Ἄρτους οὐκ ἐλάβομεν.
verses.translit: oi de dielogizonto en eaytois legontes oti Artoys ouk elavomen.
verses.translation: And they reasoned among themselves, saying, It is because we have taken no bread.
