verses.translit: o de vasileus orgisthi, kai pempsas ta strateymata autou apolesen tous foneis ekeinoys kai ten polin auton eneprisen.
verses.translation: But when the king heard thereof , he was wroth: and he sent forth his armies, and destroyed those murderers, and burned up their city.

verses.original: τότε λέγει τοῖς δούλοις αὐτοῦ· Ὁ μὲν γάμος ἕτοιμός ἐστιν, οἱ δὲ κεκλημένοι οὐκ ἦσαν ἄξιοι·
verses.translit: tote legei tois doylois autou* O men gamos etoimos estin, oi de keklimenoi ouk esan axioi*
verses.translation: Then saith he to his servants, The wedding is ready, but they which were bidden were not worthy.

verses.original: πορεύεσθε οὖν ἐπὶ τὰς διεξόδους τῶν ὁδῶν, καὶ ὅσους ⸀ἐὰν εὕρητε καλέσατε εἰς τοὺς γάμους.
verses.translit: poreyesthe oun epi tas diexodoys ton odon, kai osoys ean eurite kalesate eis tous gamoys.
verses.translation: Go ye therefore into the highways, and as many as ye shall find, bid to the marriage.

verses.original: καὶ ἐξελθόντες οἱ δοῦλοι ἐκεῖνοι εἰς τὰς ὁδοὺς συνήγαγον πάντας ⸀οὓς εὗρον, πονηρούς τε καὶ ἀγαθούς· καὶ ἐπλήσθη ὁ ⸀γάμος ἀνακειμένων.
verses.translit: kai exelthontes oi douloi ekeinoi eis tas odous synigagon pantas ous euron, poniroys te kai agathoys* kai eplisthi o gamos anakeimenon.
verses.translation: So those servants went out into the highways, and gathered together all as many as they found, both bad and good: and the wedding was furnished with guests.

verses.original: εἰσελθὼν δὲ ὁ βασιλεὺς θεάσασθαι τοὺς ἀνακειμένους εἶδεν ἐκεῖ ἄνθρωπον οὐκ ἐνδεδυμένον ἔνδυμα γάμου·
verses.translit: eiselthon de o vasileus theasasthai tous anakeimenoys eiden ekei anthropon ouk endedymenon endyma gamoy*
verses.translation: And when the king came in to see the guests, he saw there a man which had not on a wedding garment:

verses.original: καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Ἑταῖρε, πῶς εἰσῆλθες ὧδε μὴ ἔχων ἔνδυμα γάμου; ὁ δὲ ἐφιμώθη.
verses.translit: kai legei auto* Etaire, pos eiselthes ode me ehon endyma gamoy; o de efimothi.
verses.translation: And he saith unto him, Friend, how camest thou in hither not having a wedding garment? And he was speechless.

verses.original: τότε ⸂ὁ βασιλεὺς εἶπεν⸃ τοῖς διακόνοις· Δήσαντες αὐτοῦ πόδας καὶ χεῖρας ⸂ἐκβάλετε αὐτὸν⸃ εἰς τὸ σκότος τὸ ἐξώτερον· ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων.
verses.translit: tote o vasileus eipen tois diakonois* Disantes autou podas kai heiras ekvalete auton eis to skotos to exoteron* ekei estai o klaythmos kai o vrygmos ton odonton.
verses.translation: Then said the king to the servants, Bind him hand and foot, and take him away, and cast him into outer darkness; there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

verses.original: πολλοὶ γάρ εἰσιν κλητοὶ ὀλίγοι δὲ ἐκλεκτοί.
verses.translit: polloi gar eisin klitoi oligoi de eklektoi.
verses.translation: For many are called, but few are chosen.

verses.original: Τότε πορευθέντες οἱ Φαρισαῖοι συμβούλιον ἔλαβον ὅπως αὐτὸν παγιδεύσωσιν ἐν λόγῳ.
verses.translit: Tote poreythentes oi Farisaioi symvoylion elavon opos auton pagideysosin en logo.
verses.translation: Then went the Pharisees, and took counsel how they might entangle him in his talk.

verses.original: καὶ ἀποστέλλουσιν αὐτῷ τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτῶν μετὰ τῶν Ἡρῳδιανῶν ⸀λέγοντες· Διδάσκαλε, οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἀληθὴς εἶ καὶ τὴν ὁδὸν τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν ἀληθείᾳ διδάσκεις, καὶ οὐ μέλει σοι περὶ οὐδενός, οὐ γὰρ βλέπεις εἰς πρόσωπον ἀνθρώπων·
verses.translit: kai apostelloysin auto tous mathitas auton meta ton Erodianon legontes* Didaskale, oidamen oti alithes ei kai ten odon tou theou en alitheia didaskeis, kai ou melei soi peri oudenos, ou gar vlepeis eis prosopon anthropon*
verses.translation: And they sent out unto him their disciples with the Herodians, saying, Master, we know that thou art true, and teachest the way of God in truth, neither carest thou for any man : for thou regardest not the person of men.

verses.original: εἰπὸν οὖν ἡμῖν τί σοι δοκεῖ· ἔξεστιν δοῦναι κῆνσον Καίσαρι ἢ οὔ;
verses.translit: eipon oun emin ti soi dokei* exestin dounai kenson Kaisari e ou;
verses.translation: Tell us therefore, What thinkest thou? Is it lawful to give tribute unto Caesar, or not?

verses.original: γνοὺς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὴν πονηρίαν αὐτῶν εἶπεν· Τί με πειράζετε, ὑποκριταί;
verses.translit: gnous de o Iisous ten ponirian auton eipen* Ti me peirazete, upokritai;
verses.translation: But Jesus perceived their wickedness, and said, Why tempt ye me, ye hypocrites?

verses.original: ἐπιδείξατέ μοι τὸ νόμισμα τοῦ κήνσου. οἱ δὲ προσήνεγκαν αὐτῷ δηνάριον.
verses.translit: epideixate moi to nomisma tou kinsoy. oi de prosinegkan auto dinarion.
verses.translation: Shew me the tribute money. And they brought unto him a penny.

verses.original: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τίνος ἡ εἰκὼν αὕτη καὶ ἡ ἐπιγραφή;
verses.translit: kai legei autois* Tinos e eikon auti kai e epigrafi;
verses.translation: And he saith unto them, Whose is this image and superscription?

verses.original: λέγουσιν ⸀αὐτῷ· Καίσαρος. τότε λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ἀπόδοτε οὖν τὰ Καίσαρος Καίσαρι καὶ τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ τῷ θεῷ.
verses.translit: legoysin auto* Kaisaros. tote legei autois* Apodote oun ta Kaisaros Kaisari kai ta tou theou to theo.
verses.translation: They say unto him, Cæsar’s. Then saith he unto them, Render therefore unto Cæsar the things which are Cæsar’s; and unto God the things that are God’s.

verses.original: καὶ ἀκούσαντες ἐθαύμασαν, καὶ ἀφέντες αὐτὸν ἀπῆλθαν.
verses.translit: kai akoysantes ethaymasan, kai afentes auton apelthan.
verses.translation: When they had heard these words , they marvelled, and left him, and went their way.

verses.original: Ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ προσῆλθον αὐτῷ Σαδδουκαῖοι, ⸀λέγοντες μὴ εἶναι ἀνάστασιν, καὶ ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν
verses.translit: En ekeine te emera proselthon auto Saddoykaioi, legontes me einai anastasin, kai epirotisan auton
verses.translation: The same day came to him the Sadducees, which say that there is no resurrection, and asked him,

verses.original: λέγοντες· Διδάσκαλε, Μωϋσῆς εἶπεν· Ἐάν τις ἀποθάνῃ μὴ ἔχων τέκνα, ἐπιγαμβρεύσει ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀναστήσει σπέρμα τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: legontes* Didaskale, Moyses eipen* Ean tis apothane me ehon tekna, epigamvreysei o adelfos autou ten gynaika autou kai anastisei sperma to adelfo autou.
verses.translation: Saying, Master, Moses said, If a man die, having no children, his brother shall marry his wife, and raise up seed unto his brother.

verses.original: ἦσαν δὲ παρʼ ἡμῖν ἑπτὰ ἀδελφοί· καὶ ὁ πρῶτος ⸀γήμας ἐτελεύτησεν, καὶ μὴ ἔχων σπέρμα ἀφῆκεν τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ·
verses.translit: esan de par' emin epta adelfoi* kai o protos gimas eteleytisen, kai me ehon sperma afeken ten gynaika autou to adelfo autou*
verses.translation: Now there were with us seven brethren: and the first, when he had married a wife, deceased, and, having no issue, left his wife unto his brother:

verses.original: ὁμοίως καὶ ὁ δεύτερος καὶ ὁ τρίτος, ἕως τῶν ἑπτά·
verses.translit: omoios kai o deyteros kai o tritos, eos ton epta*
verses.translation: Likewise the second also, and the third, unto the seventh.

verses.original: ὕστερον δὲ πάντων ἀπέθανεν ⸀ἡ γυνή.
verses.translit: usteron de panton apethanen e gyni.
verses.translation: And last of all the woman died also.

verses.original: ἐν τῇ ⸂ἀναστάσει οὖν⸃ τίνος τῶν ἑπτὰ ἔσται γυνή; πάντες γὰρ ἔσχον αὐτήν.
verses.translit: en te anastasei oun tinos ton epta estai gyni; pantes gar eshon autin.
verses.translation: Therefore in the resurrection whose wife shall she be of the seven? for they all had her.

verses.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πλανᾶσθε μὴ εἰδότες τὰς γραφὰς μηδὲ τὴν δύναμιν τοῦ θεοῦ·
verses.translit: Apokritheis de o Iisous eipen autois* Planasthe me eidotes tas grafas mide ten dynamin tou theou*
verses.translation: Jesus answered and said unto them, Ye do err, not knowing the scriptures, nor the power of God.

verses.original: ἐν γὰρ τῇ ἀναστάσει οὔτε γαμοῦσιν οὔτε ⸀γαμίζονται, ἀλλʼ ὡς ἄγγελοι ⸀θεοῦ ἐν ⸀τῷ οὐρανῷ εἰσιν·
verses.translit: en gar te anastasei oute gamousin oute gamizontai, all' os aggeloi theou en to ourano eisin*
verses.translation: For in the resurrection they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are as the angels of God in heaven.

verses.original: περὶ δὲ τῆς ἀναστάσεως τῶν νεκρῶν οὐκ ἀνέγνωτε τὸ ῥηθὲν ὑμῖν ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ λέγοντος·
verses.translit: peri de tes anastaseos ton nekron ouk anegnote to Rithen umin upo tou theou legontos*
verses.translation: But as touching the resurrection of the dead, have ye not read that which was spoken unto you by God, saying,

verses.original: Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ θεὸς Ἀβραὰμ καὶ ὁ θεὸς Ἰσαὰκ καὶ ὁ θεὸς Ἰακώβ; οὐκ ἔστιν ⸂ὁ θεὸς⸃ νεκρῶν ἀλλὰ ζώντων.
verses.translit: Ego eimi o theos Avraam kai o theos Isaak kai o theos Iakov; ouk estin o theos nekron alla zonton.
verses.translation: I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob? God is not the God of the dead, but of the living.

verses.original: καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ ὄχλοι ἐξεπλήσσοντο ἐπὶ τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai akoysantes oi ohloi exeplissonto epi te didahe autou.
verses.translation: And when the multitude heard this , they were astonished at his doctrine.

verses.original: Οἱ δὲ Φαρισαῖοι ἀκούσαντες ὅτι ἐφίμωσεν τοὺς Σαδδουκαίους συνήχθησαν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό.
verses.translit: Oi de Farisaioi akoysantes oti efimosen tous Saddoykaioys synihthisan epi to auto.
verses.translation: But when the Pharisees had heard that he had put the Sadducees to silence, they were gathered together.

verses.original: καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν εἷς ἐξ αὐτῶν νομικὸς πειράζων ⸀αὐτόν·
verses.translit: kai epirotisen eis ex auton nomikos peirazon auton*
verses.translation: Then one of them, which was a lawyer, asked him a question , tempting him, and saying,

verses.original: Διδάσκαλε, ποία ἐντολὴ μεγάλη ἐν τῷ νόμῳ;
verses.translit: Didaskale, poia entole megali en to nomo;
verses.translation: Master, which is the great commandment in the law?

verses.original: ὁ ⸀δὲ ἔφη αὐτῷ· Ἀγαπήσεις κύριον τὸν θεόν σου ἐν ὅλῃ ⸀τῇ καρδίᾳ σου καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ ⸁τῇ ψυχῇ σου καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ διανοίᾳ σου·
verses.translit: o de efi auto* Agapiseis kyrion ton theon soy en ole te kardia soy kai en ole te psyhe soy kai en ole te dianoia soy*
verses.translation: Jesus said unto him, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind.

verses.original: αὕτη ἐστὶν ⸂ἡ μεγάλη καὶ πρώτη⸃ ἐντολή.
verses.translit: auti estin e megali kai proti entoli.
verses.translation: This is the first and great commandment.

verses.original: Δευτέρα ⸀δὲ ὁμοία ⸀αὐτῇ· Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν.
verses.translit: Deytera de omoia aute* Agapiseis ton plision soy os seayton.
verses.translation: And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.

verses.original: ἐν ταύταις ταῖς δυσὶν ἐντολαῖς ὅλος ὁ νόμος ⸂κρέμαται καὶ οἱ προφῆται⸃.
verses.translit: en taytais tais dysin entolais olos o nomos krematai kai oi profetai.
verses.translation: On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.

verses.original: Συνηγμένων δὲ τῶν Φαρισαίων ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτοὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς
verses.translit: Synigmenon de ton Farisaion epirotisen autous o Iisous
verses.translation: While the Pharisees were gathered together, Jesus asked them,

verses.original: λέγων· Τί ὑμῖν δοκεῖ περὶ τοῦ χριστοῦ; τίνος υἱός ἐστιν; λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Τοῦ Δαυίδ.
verses.translit: legon* Ti umin dokei peri tou hristou; tinos yios estin; legoysin auto* Tou Dayid.
verses.translation: Saying, What think ye of Christ? whose son is he? They say unto him, The Son of David.

verses.original: λέγει αὐτοῖς· Πῶς οὖν Δαυὶδ ἐν πνεύματι ⸂καλεῖ αὐτὸν κύριον⸃ λέγων·
verses.translit: legei autois* Pos oun Dayid en pneymati kalei auton kyrion legon*
verses.translation: He saith unto them, How then doth David in spirit call him Lord, saying,

verses.original: ⸀Εἶπεν κύριος τῷ κυρίῳ μου· Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου ⸀ὑποκάτω τῶν ποδῶν σου;
verses.translit: Eipen kyrios to kyrio moy* Kathoy ek dexion moy eos an tho tous ehthroys soy upokato ton podon soy;
verses.translation: The LORD said unto my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand, till I make thine enemies thy footstool?

verses.original: εἰ οὖν Δαυὶδ καλεῖ αὐτὸν κύριον, πῶς υἱὸς αὐτοῦ ἐστιν;
verses.translit: ei oun Dayid kalei auton kyrion, pos yios autou estin;
verses.translation: If David then call him Lord, how is he his son?

verses.original: καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐδύνατο ⸂ἀποκριθῆναι αὐτῷ⸃ λόγον, οὐδὲ ἐτόλμησέν τις ἀπʼ ἐκείνης τῆς ἡμέρας ἐπερωτῆσαι αὐτὸν οὐκέτι.
verses.translit: kai oudeis edynato apokrithenai auto logon, oude etolmisen tis ap' ekeinis tes emeras eperotesai auton ouketi.
verses.translation: And no man was able to answer him a word, neither durst any man from that day forth ask him any more questions.

verses.original: Τότε ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐλάλησεν τοῖς ὄχλοις καὶ τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ
verses.translit: Tote o Iisous elalisen tois ohlois kai tois mathitais autou
verses.translation: Then spake Jesus to the multitude, and to his disciples,

verses.original: λέγων· Ἐπὶ τῆς Μωϋσέως καθέδρας ἐκάθισαν οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι.
verses.translit: legon* Epi tes Moyseos kathedras ekathisan oi grammateis kai oi Farisaioi.
verses.translation: Saying, The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat:

verses.original: πάντα οὖν ὅσα ⸀ἐὰν εἴπωσιν ὑμῖν ⸂ποιήσατε καὶ τηρεῖτε⸃, κατὰ δὲ τὰ ἔργα αὐτῶν μὴ ποιεῖτε, λέγουσιν γὰρ καὶ οὐ ποιοῦσιν.
verses.translit: panta oun osa ean eiposin umin poiisate kai tireite, kata de ta erga auton me poieite, legoysin gar kai ou poiousin.
verses.translation: All therefore whatsoever they bid you observe, that observe and do; but do not ye after their works: for they say, and do not.

verses.original: δεσμεύουσιν ⸀δὲ φορτία ⸀βαρέα καὶ ἐπιτιθέασιν ἐπὶ τοὺς ὤμους τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ⸂αὐτοὶ δὲ τῷ⸃ δακτύλῳ αὐτῶν οὐ θέλουσιν κινῆσαι αὐτά.
verses.translit: desmeyoysin de fortia varea kai epititheasin epi tous omoys ton anthropon, autoi de to daktylo auton ou theloysin kinesai auta.
verses.translation: For they bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men’s shoulders; but they themselves will not move them with one of their fingers.

verses.original: πάντα δὲ τὰ ἔργα αὐτῶν ποιοῦσιν πρὸς τὸ θεαθῆναι τοῖς ἀνθρώποις· πλατύνουσι ⸀γὰρ τὰ φυλακτήρια αὐτῶν καὶ μεγαλύνουσι τὰ ⸀κράσπεδα,
verses.translit: panta de ta erga auton poiousin pros to theathenai tois anthropois* platynoysi gar ta fylaktiria auton kai megalynoysi ta kraspeda,
verses.translation: But all their works they do for to be seen of men: they make broad their phylacteries, and enlarge the borders of their garments,

verses.original: φιλοῦσι ⸀δὲ τὴν πρωτοκλισίαν ἐν τοῖς δείπνοις καὶ τὰς πρωτοκαθεδρίας ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς
verses.translit: filousi de ten protoklisian en tois deipnois kai tas protokathedrias en tais synagogais
verses.translation: And love the uppermost rooms at feasts, and the chief seats in the synagogues,

verses.original: καὶ τοὺς ἀσπασμοὺς ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς καὶ καλεῖσθαι ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων· ⸀Ῥαββί.
verses.translit: kai tous aspasmous en tais agorais kai kaleisthai upo ton anthropon* Ravvi.
verses.translation: And greetings in the markets, and to be called of men, Rabbi, Rabbi.

verses.original: ὑμεῖς δὲ μὴ κληθῆτε· Ῥαββί, εἷς γάρ ἐστιν ὑμῶν ὁ ⸀διδάσκαλος, πάντες δὲ ὑμεῖς ἀδελφοί ἐστε·
verses.translit: umeis de me klithete* Ravvi, eis gar estin umon o didaskalos, pantes de umeis adelfoi este*
verses.translation: But be not ye called Rabbi: for one is your Master, even Christ; and all ye are brethren.

verses.original: καὶ πατέρα μὴ καλέσητε ὑμῶν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, εἷς γάρ ἐστιν ⸂ὑμῶν ὁ πατὴρ⸃ ὁ ⸀οὐράνιος·
verses.translit: kai patera me kalesite umon epi tes ges, eis gar estin umon o pater o ouranios*
verses.translation: And call no man your father upon the earth: for one is your Father, which is in heaven.

verses.original: μηδὲ κληθῆτε καθηγηταί, ⸂ὅτι καθηγητὴς ὑμῶν ἐστιν εἷς⸃ ὁ χριστός·
verses.translit: mide klithete kathigitai, oti kathigites umon estin eis o hristos*
verses.translation: Neither be ye called masters: for one is your Master, even Christ.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ μείζων ὑμῶν ἔσται ὑμῶν διάκονος.
verses.translit: o de meizon umon estai umon diakonos.
verses.translation: But he that is greatest among you shall be your servant.

verses.original: ὅστις δὲ ὑψώσει ἑαυτὸν ταπεινωθήσεται, καὶ ὅστις ταπεινώσει ἑαυτὸν ⸀ὑψωθήσεται.
verses.translit: ostis de upsosei eayton tapeinothisetai, kai ostis tapeinosei eayton upsothisetai.
verses.translation: And whosoever shall exalt himself shall be abased; and he that shall humble himself shall be exalted.

verses.original: Οὐαὶ ⸀δὲ ὑμῖν, γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταί, ὅτι κλείετε τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων· ὑμεῖς γὰρ οὐκ εἰσέρχεσθε, οὐδὲ τοὺς εἰσερχομένους ἀφίετε ⸀εἰσελθεῖν.
verses.translit: Ouai de umin, grammateis kai Farisaioi upokritai, oti kleiete ten vasileian ton ouranon emprosthen ton anthropon* umeis gar ouk eiserhesthe, oude tous eiserhomenoys afiete eiselthein.
verses.translation: But woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye shut up the kingdom of heaven against men: for ye neither go in yourselves , neither suffer ye them that are entering to go in.
Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye devour widows’ houses, and for a pretence make long prayer: therefore ye shall receive the greater damnation.

verses.original: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταί, ὅτι περιάγετε τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ τὴν ξηρὰν ποιῆσαι ἕνα προσήλυτον, καὶ ὅταν γένηται ποιεῖτε αὐτὸν υἱὸν γεέννης διπλότερον ὑμῶν.
verses.translit: Ouai umin, grammateis kai Farisaioi upokritai, oti periagete ten thalassan kai ten xiran poiesai ena prosilyton, kai otan genitai poieite auton yion geennis diploteron umon.
verses.translation: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he is made, ye make him twofold more the child of hell than yourselves.

verses.original: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, ὁδηγοὶ τυφλοὶ οἱ λέγοντες· Ὃς ἂν ὀμόσῃ ἐν τῷ ναῷ, οὐδέν ἐστιν, ὃς δʼ ἂν ὀμόσῃ ἐν τῷ χρυσῷ τοῦ ναοῦ ὀφείλει.
verses.translit: Ouai umin, odigoi tyfloi oi legontes* Os an omose en to nao, ouden estin, os d' an omose en to hryso tou naou ofeilei.
verses.translation: Woe unto you, ye blind guides, which say, Whosoever shall swear by the temple, it is nothing; but whosoever shall swear by the gold of the temple, he is a debtor!

verses.original: μωροὶ καὶ τυφλοί, τίς γὰρ μείζων ἐστίν, ὁ χρυσὸς ἢ ὁ ναὸς ὁ ⸀ἁγιάσας τὸν χρυσόν;
verses.translit: moroi kai tyfloi, tis gar meizon estin, o hrysos e o naos o agiasas ton hryson;
verses.translation: Ye fools and blind: for whether is greater, the gold, or the temple that sanctifieth the gold?

verses.original: καί· Ὃς ⸀ἂν ὀμόσῃ ἐν τῷ θυσιαστηρίῳ, οὐδέν ἐστιν, ὃς δʼ ἂν ὀμόσῃ ἐν τῷ δώρῳ τῷ ἐπάνω αὐτοῦ ὀφείλει.
verses.translit: kai* Os an omose en to thysiastirio, ouden estin, os d' an omose en to doro to epano autou ofeilei.
verses.translation: And, Whosoever shall swear by the altar, it is nothing; but whosoever sweareth by the gift that is upon it, he is guilty.

verses.original: ⸀τυφλοί, τί γὰρ μεῖζον, τὸ δῶρον ἢ τὸ θυσιαστήριον τὸ ἁγιάζον τὸ δῶρον;
verses.translit: tyfloi, ti gar meizon, to doron e to thysiastirion to agiazon to doron;
verses.translation: Ye fools and blind: for whether is greater, the gift, or the altar that sanctifieth the gift?

verses.original: ὁ οὖν ὀμόσας ἐν τῷ θυσιαστηρίῳ ὀμνύει ἐν αὐτῷ καὶ ἐν πᾶσι τοῖς ἐπάνω αὐτοῦ·
verses.translit: o oun omosas en to thysiastirio omnyei en auto kai en pasi tois epano autou*
verses.translation: Whoso therefore shall swear by the altar, sweareth by it, and by all things thereon.

verses.original: καὶ ὁ ὀμόσας ἐν τῷ ναῷ ὀμνύει ἐν αὐτῷ καὶ ἐν τῷ ⸀κατοικοῦντι αὐτόν·
verses.translit: kai o omosas en to nao omnyei en auto kai en to katoikounti auton*
verses.translation: And whoso shall swear by the temple, sweareth by it, and by him that dwelleth therein.

verses.original: καὶ ὁ ὀμόσας ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ ὀμνύει ἐν τῷ θρόνῳ τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ἐν τῷ καθημένῳ ἐπάνω αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai o omosas en to ourano omnyei en to throno tou theou kai en to kathimeno epano autou.
verses.translation: And he that shall swear by heaven, sweareth by the throne of God, and by him that sitteth thereon.

verses.original: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταί, ὅτι ἀποδεκατοῦτε τὸ ἡδύοσμον καὶ τὸ ἄνηθον καὶ τὸ κύμινον, καὶ ἀφήκατε τὰ βαρύτερα τοῦ νόμου, τὴν κρίσιν καὶ ⸂τὸ ἔλεος⸃ καὶ τὴν πίστιν· ⸀ταῦτα ἔδει ποιῆσαι κἀκεῖνα μὴ ⸀ἀφιέναι.
verses.translit: Ouai umin, grammateis kai Farisaioi upokritai, oti apodekatoute to edyosmon kai to anithon kai to kyminon, kai afikate ta varytera tou nomoy, ten krisin kai to eleos kai ten pistin* tauta edei poiesai kakeina me afienai.
verses.translation: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin, and have omitted the weightier matters of the law, judgment, mercy, and faith: these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone.

verses.original: ὁδηγοὶ τυφλοί, ⸀οἱ διϋλίζοντες τὸν κώνωπα τὴν δὲ κάμηλον καταπίνοντες.
verses.translit: odigoi tyfloi, oi diylizontes ton konopa ten de kamilon katapinontes.
verses.translation: Ye blind guides, which strain at a gnat, and swallow a camel.

verses.original: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταί, ὅτι καθαρίζετε τὸ ἔξωθεν τοῦ ποτηρίου καὶ τῆς παροψίδος, ἔσωθεν δὲ γέμουσιν ἐξ ἁρπαγῆς καὶ ⸀ἀκρασίας.
verses.translit: Ouai umin, grammateis kai Farisaioi upokritai, oti katharizete to exothen tou potirioy kai tes paropsidos, esothen de gemoysin ex arpages kai akrasias.
verses.translation: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye make clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess.

verses.original: Φαρισαῖε τυφλέ, καθάρισον πρῶτον τὸ ἐντὸς τοῦ ποτηρίου ⸂καὶ τῆς παροψίδος⸃, ἵνα γένηται καὶ τὸ ἐκτὸς ⸀αὐτοῦ καθαρόν.
verses.translit: Farisaie tyfle, katharison proton to entos tou potirioy kai tes paropsidos, ina genitai kai to ektos autou katharon.
verses.translation: Thou blind Pharisee, cleanse first that which is within the cup and platter, that the outside of them may be clean also.

verses.original: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταί, ὅτι ⸀παρομοιάζετε τάφοις κεκονιαμένοις, οἵτινες ἔξωθεν μὲν φαίνονται ὡραῖοι ἔσωθεν δὲ γέμουσιν ὀστέων νεκρῶν καὶ πάσης ἀκαθαρσίας·
verses.translit: Ouai umin, grammateis kai Farisaioi upokritai, oti paromoiazete tafois kekoniamenois, oitines exothen men fainontai oraioi esothen de gemoysin osteon nekron kai pasis akatharsias*
verses.translation: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye are like unto whited sepulchres, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men’s bones, and of all uncleanness.

verses.original: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς ἔξωθεν μὲν φαίνεσθε τοῖς ἀνθρώποις δίκαιοι, ἔσωθεν δέ ⸂ἐστε μεστοὶ⸃ ὑποκρίσεως καὶ ἀνομίας.
verses.translit: outos kai umeis exothen men fainesthe tois anthropois dikaioi, esothen de este mestoi upokriseos kai anomias.
verses.translation: Even so ye also outwardly appear righteous unto men, but within ye are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.

verses.original: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταί, ὅτι οἰκοδομεῖτε τοὺς τάφους τῶν προφητῶν καὶ κοσμεῖτε τὰ μνημεῖα τῶν δικαίων,
verses.translit: Ouai umin, grammateis kai Farisaioi upokritai, oti oikodomeite tous tafoys ton profiton kai kosmeite ta mnimeia ton dikaion,
verses.translation: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because ye build the tombs of the prophets, and garnish the sepulchres of the righteous,

verses.original: καὶ λέγετε· Εἰ ⸀ἤμεθα ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν, οὐκ ἂν ⸁ἤμεθα ⸂αὐτῶν κοινωνοὶ⸃ ἐν τῷ αἵματι τῶν προφητῶν·
verses.translit: kai legete* Ei emetha en tais emerais ton pateron emon, ouk an emetha auton koinonoi en to aimati ton profiton*
verses.translation: And say, If we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partakers with them in the blood of the prophets.

verses.original: ὥστε μαρτυρεῖτε ἑαυτοῖς ὅτι υἱοί ἐστε τῶν φονευσάντων τοὺς προφήτας.
verses.translit: oste martyreite eaytois oti yioi este ton foneysanton tous profitas.
verses.translation: Wherefore ye be witnesses unto yourselves, that ye are the children of them which killed the prophets.

verses.original: καὶ ὑμεῖς πληρώσατε τὸ μέτρον τῶν πατέρων ὑμῶν.
verses.translit: kai umeis plirosate to metron ton pateron umon.
verses.translation: Fill ye up then the measure of your fathers.

verses.original: ὄφεις γεννήματα ἐχιδνῶν, πῶς φύγητε ἀπὸ τῆς κρίσεως τῆς γεέννης;
verses.translit: ofeis gennimata ehidnon, pos fygite apo tes kriseos tes geennis;
verses.translation: Ye serpents, ye generation of vipers, how can ye escape the damnation of hell?

verses.original: διὰ τοῦτο ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἀποστέλλω πρὸς ὑμᾶς προφήτας καὶ σοφοὺς καὶ γραμματεῖς· ⸀ἐξ αὐτῶν ἀποκτενεῖτε καὶ σταυρώσετε, καὶ ἐξ αὐτῶν μαστιγώσετε ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς ὑμῶν καὶ διώξετε ἀπὸ πόλεως εἰς πόλιν·
verses.translit: dia touto idou ego apostello pros umas profitas kai sofous kai grammateis* ex auton apokteneite kai stayrosete, kai ex auton mastigosete en tais synagogais umon kai dioxete apo poleos eis polin*
verses.translation: Wherefore, behold, I send unto you prophets, and wise men, and scribes: and some of them ye shall kill and crucify; and some of them shall ye scourge in your synagogues, and persecute them from city to city:

verses.original: ὅπως ἔλθῃ ἐφʼ ὑμᾶς πᾶν αἷμα δίκαιον ἐκχυννόμενον ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἀπὸ τοῦ αἵματος Ἅβελ τοῦ δικαίου ἕως τοῦ αἵματος Ζαχαρίου υἱοῦ Βαραχίου, ὃν ἐφονεύσατε μεταξὺ τοῦ ναοῦ καὶ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου.
verses.translit: opos elthe ef' umas pan aima dikaion ekhynnomenon epi tes ges apo tou aimatos Avel tou dikaioy eos tou aimatos Zaharioy yiou Varahioy, on efoneysate metaxu tou naou kai tou thysiastirioy.
verses.translation: That upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias, whom ye slew between the temple and the altar.

verses.original: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ⸀ἥξει ⸂ταῦτα πάντα⸃ ἐπὶ τὴν γενεὰν ταύτην.
verses.translit: amen lego umin, exei tauta panta epi ten genean taytin.
verses.translation: Verily I say unto you, All these things shall come upon this generation.

verses.original: Ἰερουσαλὴμ Ἰερουσαλήμ, ἡ ⸀ἀποκτείνουσα τοὺς προφήτας καὶ λιθοβολοῦσα τοὺς ἀπεσταλμένους πρὸς αὐτήν— ποσάκις ἠθέλησα ἐπισυναγαγεῖν τὰ τέκνα σου, ὃν τρόπον ⸂ὄρνις ἐπισυνάγει⸃ τὰ νοσσία ⸀αὐτῆς ὑπὸ τὰς πτέρυγας, καὶ οὐκ ἠθελήσατε;
verses.translit: Ieroysalem Ieroysalim, e apokteinoysa tous profitas kai lithovolousa tous apestalmenoys pros autin-- posakis ethelisa episynagagein ta tekna soy, on tropon ornis episynagei ta nossia autes upo tas pterygas, kai ouk ethelisate;
verses.translation: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!

verses.original: ἰδοὺ ἀφίεται ὑμῖν ὁ οἶκος ὑμῶν ⸀ἔρημος.
verses.translit: idou afietai umin o oikos umon erimos.
verses.translation: Behold, your house is left unto you desolate.

verses.original: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν, οὐ μή με ἴδητε ἀπʼ ἄρτι ἕως ἂν εἴπητε· Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι κυρίου.
verses.translit: lego gar umin, ou mi me idite ap' arti eos an eipite* Eulogimenos o erhomenos en onomati kyrioy.
verses.translation: For I say unto you, Ye shall not see me henceforth, till ye shall say, Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐξελθὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ⸂ἀπὸ τοῦ ἱεροῦ ἐπορεύετο⸃, καὶ προσῆλθον οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἐπιδεῖξαι αὐτῷ τὰς οἰκοδομὰς τοῦ ἱεροῦ·
verses.translit: Kai exelthon o Iisous apo tou ierou eporeyeto, kai proselthon oi mathitai autou epideixai auto tas oikodomas tou ierou*
verses.translation: And Jesus went out, and departed from the temple: and his disciples came to him for to shew him the buildings of the temple.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ⸀ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Οὐ βλέπετε ⸂ταῦτα πάντα⸃; ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐ μὴ ἀφεθῇ ὧδε λίθος ἐπὶ λίθον ὃς οὐ καταλυθήσεται.
verses.translit: o de apokritheis eipen autois* Ou vlepete tauta panta; amen lego umin, ou me afethe ode lithos epi lithon os ou katalythisetai.
verses.translation: And Jesus said unto them, See ye not all these things? verily I say unto you, There shall not be left here one stone upon another, that shall not be thrown down.

verses.original: Καθημένου δὲ αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τοῦ Ὄρους τῶν Ἐλαιῶν προσῆλθον αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ κατʼ ἰδίαν λέγοντες· Εἰπὸν ἡμῖν πότε ταῦτα ἔσται, καὶ τί τὸ σημεῖον τῆς σῆς παρουσίας ⸀καὶ συντελείας τοῦ αἰῶνος.
verses.translit: Kathimenoy de autou epi tou Oroys ton Elaion proselthon auto oi mathitai kat' idian legontes* Eipon emin pote tauta estai, kai ti to simeion tes ses paroysias kai synteleias tou aionos.
verses.translation: And as he sat upon the mount of Olives, the disciples came unto him privately, saying, Tell us, when shall these things be? and what shall be the sign of thy coming, and of the end of the world?

verses.original: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Βλέπετε μή τις ὑμᾶς πλανήσῃ·
verses.translit: kai apokritheis o Iisous eipen autois* Vlepete mi tis umas planise*
verses.translation: And Jesus answered and said unto them, Take heed that no man deceive you.

verses.original: πολλοὶ γὰρ ἐλεύσονται ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου λέγοντες· Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ χριστός, καὶ πολλοὺς πλανήσουσιν.
verses.translit: polloi gar eleysontai epi to onomati moy legontes* Ego eimi o hristos, kai pollous planisoysin.
verses.translation: For many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and shall deceive many.

verses.original: μελλήσετε δὲ ἀκούειν πολέμους καὶ ἀκοὰς πολέμων· ὁρᾶτε, μὴ θροεῖσθε· δεῖ ⸀γὰρ γενέσθαι, ἀλλʼ οὔπω ἐστὶν τὸ τέλος.
verses.translit: mellisete de akoyein polemoys kai akoas polemon* orate, me throeisthe* dei gar genesthai, all' oupo estin to telos.
verses.translation: And ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars: see that ye be not troubled: for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet.

verses.original: ἐγερθήσεται γὰρ ἔθνος ἐπὶ ἔθνος καὶ βασιλεία ἐπὶ βασιλείαν, καὶ ἔσονται ⸀λιμοὶ καὶ σεισμοὶ κατὰ τόπους·
verses.translit: egerthisetai gar ethnos epi ethnos kai vasileia epi vasileian, kai esontai limoi kai seismoi kata topoys*
verses.translation: For nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom: and there shall be famines, and pestilences, and earthquakes, in divers places.

verses.original: πάντα δὲ ταῦτα ἀρχὴ ὠδίνων.
verses.translit: panta de tauta arhe odinon.
verses.translation: All these are the beginning of sorrows.

verses.original: Τότε παραδώσουσιν ὑμᾶς εἰς θλῖψιν καὶ ἀποκτενοῦσιν ὑμᾶς, καὶ ἔσεσθε μισούμενοι ὑπὸ πάντων τῶν ἐθνῶν διὰ τὸ ὄνομά μου.
verses.translit: Tote paradosoysin umas eis thlipsin kai apoktenousin umas, kai esesthe misoymenoi upo panton ton ethnon dia to onoma moy.
verses.translation: Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, and shall kill you: and ye shall be hated of all nations for my name’s sake.

verses.original: καὶ τότε σκανδαλισθήσονται πολλοὶ καὶ ἀλλήλους παραδώσουσιν καὶ μισήσουσιν ἀλλήλους·
verses.translit: kai tote skandalisthisontai polloi kai alliloys paradosoysin kai misisoysin alliloys*
verses.translation: And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another.

verses.original: καὶ πολλοὶ ψευδοπροφῆται ἐγερθήσονται καὶ πλανήσουσιν πολλούς·
verses.translit: kai polloi pseydoprofetai egerthisontai kai planisoysin polloys*
verses.translation: And many false prophets shall rise, and shall deceive many.

verses.original: καὶ διὰ τὸ πληθυνθῆναι τὴν ἀνομίαν ψυγήσεται ἡ ἀγάπη τῶν πολλῶν.
verses.translit: kai dia to plithynthenai ten anomian psygisetai e agapi ton pollon.
verses.translation: And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ὑπομείνας εἰς τέλος οὗτος σωθήσεται.
verses.translit: o de upomeinas eis telos outos sothisetai.
verses.translation: But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved.

verses.original: καὶ κηρυχθήσεται τοῦτο τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τῆς βασιλείας ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ οἰκουμένῃ εἰς μαρτύριον πᾶσιν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν, καὶ τότε ἥξει τὸ τέλος.
verses.translit: kai kiryhthisetai touto to euaggelion tes vasileias en ole te oikoymene eis martyrion pasin tois ethnesin, kai tote exei to telos.
verses.translation: And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness unto all nations; and then shall the end come.

verses.original: Ὅταν οὖν ἴδητε τὸ βδέλυγμα τῆς ἐρημώσεως τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ Δανιὴλ τοῦ προφήτου ⸀ἑστὸς ἐν τόπῳ ἁγίῳ, ὁ ἀναγινώσκων νοείτω,
verses.translit: Otan oun idite to vdelygma tes erimoseos to Rithen dia Daniel tou profitoy estos en topo agio, o anaginoskon noeito,
verses.translation: When ye therefore shall see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, stand in the holy place, (whoso readeth, let him understand:)

verses.original: τότε οἱ ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ φευγέτωσαν ⸀ἐπὶ τὰ ὄρη,
verses.translit: tote oi en te Ioydaia feygetosan epi ta ori,
verses.translation: Then let them which be in Judaea flee into the mountains:

verses.original: ὁ ἐπὶ τοῦ δώματος μὴ ⸀καταβάτω ἆραι τὰ ἐκ τῆς οἰκίας αὐτοῦ,
verses.translit: o epi tou domatos me katavato arai ta ek tes oikias autou,
verses.translation: Let him which is on the housetop not come down to take any thing out of his house:

verses.original: καὶ ὁ ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ μὴ ἐπιστρεψάτω ὀπίσω ἆραι ⸂τὸ ἱμάτιον⸃ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai o en to agro me epistrepsato opiso arai to imation autou.
verses.translation: Neither let him which is in the field return back to take his clothes.

verses.original: οὐαὶ δὲ ταῖς ἐν γαστρὶ ἐχούσαις καὶ ταῖς θηλαζούσαις ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις.
verses.translit: ouai de tais en gastri ehoysais kai tais thilazoysais en ekeinais tais emerais.
verses.translation: And woe unto them that are with child, and to them that give suck in those days!

verses.original: προσεύχεσθε δὲ ἵνα μὴ γένηται ἡ φυγὴ ὑμῶν χειμῶνος μηδὲ σαββάτῳ·
verses.translit: proseyhesthe de ina me genitai e fyge umon heimonos mide savvato*
verses.translation: But pray ye that your flight be not in the winter, neither on the sabbath day:

verses.original: ἔσται γὰρ τότε θλῖψις μεγάλη οἵα οὐ γέγονεν ἀπʼ ἀρχῆς κόσμου ἕως τοῦ νῦν οὐδʼ οὐ μὴ γένηται.
verses.translit: estai gar tote thlipsis megali oia ou gegonen ap' arhes kosmoy eos tou nun oud' ou me genitai.
verses.translation: For then shall be great tribulation, such as was not since the beginning of the world to this time, no, nor ever shall be.

verses.original: καὶ εἰ μὴ ἐκολοβώθησαν αἱ ἡμέραι ἐκεῖναι, οὐκ ἂν ἐσώθη πᾶσα σάρξ· διὰ δὲ τοὺς ἐκλεκτοὺς κολοβωθήσονται αἱ ἡμέραι ἐκεῖναι.
verses.translit: kai ei me ekolovothisan ai emerai ekeinai, ouk an esothi pasa sarx* dia de tous eklektous kolovothisontai ai emerai ekeinai.
verses.translation: And except those days should be shortened, there should no flesh be saved: but for the elect’s sake those days shall be shortened.

verses.original: τότε ἐάν τις ὑμῖν εἴπῃ· Ἰδοὺ ὧδε ὁ χριστός, ἤ· Ὧδε, μὴ πιστεύσητε·
verses.translit: tote ean tis umin eipe* Idou ode o hristos, e* Ode, me pisteysite*
verses.translation: Then if any man shall say unto you, Lo, here is Christ, or there; believe it not.

verses.original: ἐγερθήσονται γὰρ ψευδόχριστοι καὶ ψευδοπροφῆται, καὶ δώσουσιν σημεῖα μεγάλα καὶ τέρατα ὥστε ⸀πλανῆσαι εἰ δυνατὸν καὶ τοὺς ἐκλεκτούς·
verses.translit: egerthisontai gar pseydohristoi kai pseydoprofetai, kai dosoysin simeia megala kai terata oste planesai ei dynaton kai tous eklektoys*
verses.translation: For there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall shew great signs and wonders; insomuch that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect.

verses.original: ἰδοὺ προείρηκα ὑμῖν.
verses.translit: idou proeirika umin.
verses.translation: Behold, I have told you before.

verses.original: ἐὰν οὖν εἴπωσιν ὑμῖν· Ἰδοὺ ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ ἐστίν, μὴ ἐξέλθητε· Ἰδοὺ ἐν τοῖς ταμείοις, μὴ πιστεύσητε·
verses.translit: ean oun eiposin umin* Idou en te erimo estin, me exelthite* Idou en tois tameiois, me pisteysite*
verses.translation: Wherefore if they shall say unto you, Behold, he is in the desert; go not forth: behold, he is in the secret chambers; believe it not.

verses.original: ὥσπερ γὰρ ἡ ἀστραπὴ ἐξέρχεται ἀπὸ ἀνατολῶν καὶ φαίνεται ἕως δυσμῶν, οὕτως ⸀ἔσται ἡ παρουσία τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου·
verses.translit: osper gar e astrape exerhetai apo anatolon kai fainetai eos dysmon, outos estai e paroysia tou yiou tou anthropoy*
verses.translation: For as the lightning cometh out of the east, and shineth even unto the west; so shall also the coming of the Son of man be.

verses.original: ⸀ὅπου ἐὰν ᾖ τὸ πτῶμα, ἐκεῖ συναχθήσονται οἱ ἀετοί.
verses.translit: opoy ean e to ptoma, ekei synahthisontai oi aetoi.
verses.translation: For wheresoever the carcase is, there will the eagles be gathered together.

verses.original: Εὐθέως δὲ μετὰ τὴν θλῖψιν τῶν ἡμερῶν ἐκείνων ὁ ἥλιος σκοτισθήσεται, καὶ ἡ σελήνη οὐ δώσει τὸ φέγγος αὐτῆς, καὶ οἱ ἀστέρες πεσοῦνται ἀπὸ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ αἱ δυνάμεις τῶν οὐρανῶν σαλευθήσονται.
verses.translit: Eutheos de meta ten thlipsin ton emeron ekeinon o elios skotisthisetai, kai e selini ou dosei to feggos autes, kai oi asteres pesountai apo tou ouranou, kai ai dynameis ton ouranon saleythisontai.
verses.translation: Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken:

verses.original: καὶ τότε φανήσεται τὸ σημεῖον τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐν ⸀τῷ οὐρανῷ, καὶ τότε κόψονται πᾶσαι αἱ φυλαὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ ὄψονται τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐρχόμενον ἐπὶ τῶν νεφελῶν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ μετὰ δυνάμεως καὶ δόξης πολλῆς·
verses.translit: kai tote fanisetai to simeion tou yiou tou anthropoy en to ourano, kai tote kopsontai pasai ai fylai tes ges kai opsontai ton yion tou anthropoy erhomenon epi ton nefelon tou ouranou meta dynameos kai doxis polles*
verses.translation: And then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.

verses.original: καὶ ἀποστελεῖ τοὺς ἀγγέλους αὐτοῦ μετὰ ⸀σάλπιγγος μεγάλης, καὶ ἐπισυνάξουσιν τοὺς ἐκλεκτοὺς αὐτοῦ ἐκ τῶν τεσσάρων ἀνέμων ἀπʼ ἄκρων οὐρανῶν ἕως ⸀τῶν ἄκρων αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: kai apostelei tous aggeloys autou meta salpiggos megalis, kai episynaxoysin tous eklektous autou ek ton tessaron anemon ap' akron ouranon eos ton akron auton.
verses.translation: And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.

verses.original: Ἀπὸ δὲ τῆς συκῆς μάθετε τὴν παραβολήν· ὅταν ἤδη ὁ κλάδος αὐτῆς γένηται ἁπαλὸς καὶ τὰ φύλλα ἐκφύῃ, γινώσκετε ὅτι ἐγγὺς τὸ θέρος·
verses.translit: Apo de tes sykes mathete ten paravolin* otan edi o klados autes genitai apalos kai ta fylla ekfye, ginoskete oti eggus to theros*
verses.translation: Now learn a parable of the fig tree; When his branch is yet tender, and putteth forth leaves, ye know that summer is nigh:

verses.original: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς, ὅταν ἴδητε ⸂πάντα ταῦτα⸃, γινώσκετε ὅτι ἐγγύς ἐστιν ἐπὶ θύραις.
verses.translit: outos kai umeis, otan idite panta tauta, ginoskete oti eggys estin epi thyrais.
verses.translation: So likewise ye, when ye shall see all these things, know that it is near, even at the doors.

verses.original: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ⸀ὅτι οὐ μὴ παρέλθῃ ἡ γενεὰ αὕτη ἕως ἂν πάντα ταῦτα γένηται.
verses.translit: amen lego umin oti ou me parelthe e genea auti eos an panta tauta genitai.
verses.translation: Verily I say unto you, This generation shall not pass, till all these things be fulfilled.

verses.original: ὁ οὐρανὸς καὶ ἡ γῆ ⸀παρελεύσεται, οἱ δὲ λόγοι μου οὐ μὴ παρέλθωσιν.
verses.translit: o ouranos kai e ge pareleysetai, oi de logoi moy ou me parelthosin.
verses.translation: Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away.

verses.original: Περὶ δὲ τῆς ἡμέρας ἐκείνης καὶ ὥρας οὐδεὶς οἶδεν, οὐδὲ οἱ ἄγγελοι τῶν οὐρανῶν ⸂οὐδὲ ὁ υἱός⸃, εἰ μὴ ὁ ⸀πατὴρ μόνος.
verses.translit: Peri de tes emeras ekeinis kai oras oudeis oiden, oude oi aggeloi ton ouranon oude o yios, ei me o pater monos.
verses.translation: But of that day and hour knoweth no man , no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only.

verses.original: ὥσπερ ⸀γὰρ αἱ ἡμέραι τοῦ Νῶε, οὕτως ⸀ἔσται ἡ παρουσία τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου·
verses.translit: osper gar ai emerai tou Noe, outos estai e paroysia tou yiou tou anthropoy*
verses.translation: But as the days of Noe were , so shall also the coming of the Son of man be.

verses.original: ⸀ὡς γὰρ ἦσαν ἐν ταῖς ⸀ἡμέραις ταῖς πρὸ τοῦ κατακλυσμοῦ τρώγοντες καὶ πίνοντες, γαμοῦντες καὶ ⸀γαμίζοντες, ἄχρι ἧς ἡμέρας εἰσῆλθεν Νῶε εἰς τὴν κιβωτόν,
verses.translit: os gar esan en tais emerais tais pro tou kataklysmou trogontes kai pinontes, gamountes kai gamizontes, ahri es emeras eiselthen Noe eis ten kivoton,
verses.translation: For as in the days that were before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day that Noe entered into the ark,

verses.original: καὶ οὐκ ἔγνωσαν ἕως ἦλθεν ὁ κατακλυσμὸς καὶ ἦρεν ἅπαντας, οὕτως ἔσται ⸀καὶ ἡ παρουσία τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.
verses.translit: kai ouk egnosan eos elthen o kataklysmos kai eren apantas, outos estai kai e paroysia tou yiou tou anthropoy.
verses.translation: And knew not until the flood came, and took them all away; so shall also the coming of the Son of man be.

verses.original: τότε ⸂δύο ἔσονται⸃ ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ, ⸀εἷς παραλαμβάνεται καὶ ⸁εἷς ἀφίεται·
verses.translit: tote dyo esontai en to agro, eis paralamvanetai kai eis afietai*
verses.translation: Then shall two be in the field; the one shall be taken, and the other left.

verses.original: δύο ἀλήθουσαι ἐν τῷ ⸀μύλῳ, μία παραλαμβάνεται καὶ μία ἀφίεται.
verses.translit: dyo alithoysai en to mylo, mia paralamvanetai kai mia afietai.
verses.translation: Two women shall be grinding at the mill; the one shall be taken, and the other left.

verses.original: γρηγορεῖτε οὖν, ὅτι οὐκ οἴδατε ποίᾳ ⸀ἡμέρᾳ ὁ κύριος ὑμῶν ἔρχεται.
verses.translit: grigoreite oun, oti ouk oidate poia emera o kyrios umon erhetai.
verses.translation: Watch therefore: for ye know not what hour your Lord doth come.

verses.original: ἐκεῖνο δὲ γινώσκετε ὅτι εἰ ᾔδει ὁ οἰκοδεσπότης ποίᾳ φυλακῇ ὁ κλέπτης ἔρχεται, ἐγρηγόρησεν ἂν καὶ οὐκ ἂν εἴασεν διορυχθῆναι τὴν οἰκίαν αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: ekeino de ginoskete oti ei edei o oikodespotis poia fylake o kleptis erhetai, egrigorisen an kai ouk an eiasen dioryhthenai ten oikian autou.
verses.translation: But know this, that if the goodman of the house had known in what watch the thief would come, he would have watched, and would not have suffered his house to be broken up.

verses.original: διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ὑμεῖς γίνεσθε ἕτοιμοι, ὅτι ᾗ ⸂οὐ δοκεῖτε ὥρᾳ⸃ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἔρχεται.
verses.translit: dia touto kai umeis ginesthe etoimoi, oti e ou dokeite ora o yios tou anthropoy erhetai.
verses.translation: Therefore be ye also ready: for in such an hour as ye think not the Son of man cometh.

verses.original: Τίς ἄρα ἐστὶν ὁ πιστὸς δοῦλος καὶ φρόνιμος ὃν κατέστησεν ὁ ⸀κύριος ἐπὶ τῆς ⸀οἰκετείας αὐτοῦ τοῦ ⸀δοῦναι αὐτοῖς τὴν τροφὴν ἐν καιρῷ;
verses.translit: Tis ara estin o pistos doulos kai fronimos on katestisen o kyrios epi tes oiketeias autou tou dounai autois ten trofen en kairo;
verses.translation: Who then is a faithful and wise servant, whom his lord hath made ruler over his household, to give them meat in due season?

verses.original: μακάριος ὁ δοῦλος ἐκεῖνος ὃν ἐλθὼν ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ εὑρήσει ⸂οὕτως ποιοῦντα⸃·
verses.translit: makarios o doulos ekeinos on elthon o kyrios autou eurisei outos poiounta*
verses.translation: Blessed is that servant, whom his lord when he cometh shall find so doing.

verses.original: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐπὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς ὑπάρχουσιν αὐτοῦ καταστήσει αὐτόν.
verses.translit: amen lego umin oti epi pasin tois uparhoysin autou katastisei auton.
verses.translation: Verily I say unto you, That he shall make him ruler over all his goods.

verses.original: ἐὰν δὲ εἴπῃ ὁ κακὸς δοῦλος ἐκεῖνος ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ· Χρονίζει ⸂μου ὁ κύριος⸃,
verses.translit: ean de eipe o kakos doulos ekeinos en te kardia autou* Hronizei moy o kyrios,
verses.translation: But and if that evil servant shall say in his heart, My lord delayeth his coming;

verses.original: καὶ ἄρξηται τύπτειν τοὺς συνδούλους ⸂αὐτοῦ, ἐσθίῃ δὲ καὶ πίνῃ⸃ μετὰ τῶν μεθυόντων,
verses.translit: kai arxitai typtein tous syndoyloys autou, esthie de kai pine meta ton methyonton,
verses.translation: And shall begin to smite his fellowservants, and to eat and drink with the drunken;

verses.original: ἥξει ὁ κύριος τοῦ δούλου ἐκείνου ἐν ἡμέρᾳ ᾗ οὐ προσδοκᾷ καὶ ἐν ὥρᾳ ᾗ οὐ γινώσκει,
verses.translit: exei o kyrios tou doyloy ekeinoy en emera e ou prosdoka kai en ora e ou ginoskei,
verses.translation: The lord of that servant shall come in a day when he looketh not for him , and in an hour that he is not aware of,

verses.original: καὶ διχοτομήσει αὐτὸν καὶ τὸ μέρος αὐτοῦ μετὰ τῶν ὑποκριτῶν θήσει· ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων.
verses.translit: kai dihotomisei auton kai to meros autou meta ton upokriton thisei* ekei estai o klaythmos kai o vrygmos ton odonton.
verses.translation: And shall cut him asunder, and appoint him his portion with the hypocrites: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

verses.original: Τότε ὁμοιωθήσεται ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν δέκα παρθένοις, αἵτινες λαβοῦσαι τὰς λαμπάδας ⸀ἑαυτῶν ἐξῆλθον εἰς ⸀ὑπάντησιν τοῦ νυμφίου.
verses.translit: Tote omoiothisetai e vasileia ton ouranon deka parthenois, aitines lavousai tas lampadas eayton exelthon eis upantisin tou nymfioy.
verses.translation: Then shall the kingdom of heaven be likened unto ten virgins, which took their lamps, and went forth to meet the bridegroom.

verses.original: πέντε δὲ ⸂ἐξ αὐτῶν ἦσαν⸃ ⸂μωραὶ καὶ πέντε φρόνιμοι⸃.
verses.translit: pente de ex auton esan morai kai pente fronimoi.
verses.translation: And five of them were wise, and five were foolish.

verses.original: ⸂αἱ γὰρ⸃ μωραὶ λαβοῦσαι τὰς λαμπάδας αὐτῶν οὐκ ἔλαβον μεθʼ ἑαυτῶν ἔλαιον·
verses.translit: ai gar morai lavousai tas lampadas auton ouk elavon meth' eayton elaion*
verses.translation: They that were foolish took their lamps, and took no oil with them:

verses.original: αἱ δὲ φρόνιμοι ἔλαβον ἔλαιον ἐν τοῖς ⸀ἀγγείοις μετὰ τῶν λαμπάδων ⸀ἑαυτῶν.
verses.translit: ai de fronimoi elavon elaion en tois aggeiois meta ton lampadon eayton.
verses.translation: But the wise took oil in their vessels with their lamps.

verses.original: χρονίζοντος δὲ τοῦ νυμφίου ἐνύσταξαν πᾶσαι καὶ ἐκάθευδον.
verses.translit: hronizontos de tou nymfioy enystaxan pasai kai ekatheydon.
verses.translation: While the bridegroom tarried, they all slumbered and slept.

verses.original: μέσης δὲ νυκτὸς κραυγὴ γέγονεν· Ἰδοὺ ὁ ⸀νυμφίος, ἐξέρχεσθε εἰς ἀπάντησιν ⸀αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: mesis de nyktos krayge gegonen* Idou o nymfios, exerhesthe eis apantisin autou.
verses.translation: And at midnight there was a cry made, Behold, the bridegroom cometh; go ye out to meet him.

verses.original: τότε ἠγέρθησαν πᾶσαι αἱ παρθένοι ἐκεῖναι καὶ ἐκόσμησαν τὰς λαμπάδας ⸀ἑαυτῶν.
verses.translit: tote egerthisan pasai ai parthenoi ekeinai kai ekosmisan tas lampadas eayton.
verses.translation: Then all those virgins arose, and trimmed their lamps.

verses.original: αἱ δὲ μωραὶ ταῖς φρονίμοις εἶπαν· Δότε ἡμῖν ἐκ τοῦ ἐλαίου ὑμῶν, ὅτι αἱ λαμπάδες ἡμῶν σβέννυνται.
verses.translit: ai de morai tais fronimois eipan* Dote emin ek tou elaioy umon, oti ai lampades emon svennyntai.
verses.translation: And the foolish said unto the wise, Give us of your oil; for our lamps are gone out.

verses.original: ἀπεκρίθησαν δὲ αἱ φρόνιμοι λέγουσαι· Μήποτε ⸂οὐ μὴ⸃ ἀρκέσῃ ἡμῖν καὶ ὑμῖν· ⸀πορεύεσθε μᾶλλον πρὸς τοὺς πωλοῦντας καὶ ἀγοράσατε ἑαυταῖς.
verses.translit: apekrithisan de ai fronimoi legoysai* Mipote ou me arkese emin kai umin* poreyesthe mallon pros tous polountas kai agorasate eaytais.
verses.translation: But the wise answered, saying, Not so ; lest there be not enough for us and you: but go ye rather to them that sell, and buy for yourselves.

verses.original: ἀπερχομένων δὲ αὐτῶν ἀγοράσαι ἦλθεν ὁ νυμφίος, καὶ αἱ ἕτοιμοι εἰσῆλθον μετʼ αὐτοῦ εἰς τοὺς γάμους, καὶ ἐκλείσθη ἡ θύρα.
verses.translit: aperhomenon de auton agorasai elthen o nymfios, kai ai etoimoi eiselthon met' autou eis tous gamoys, kai ekleisthi e thyra.
verses.translation: And while they went to buy, the bridegroom came; and they that were ready went in with him to the marriage: and the door was shut.

verses.original: ὕστερον δὲ ἔρχονται καὶ αἱ λοιπαὶ παρθένοι λέγουσαι· Κύριε κύριε, ἄνοιξον ἡμῖν·
verses.translit: usteron de erhontai kai ai loipai parthenoi legoysai* Kyrie kyrie, anoixon emin*
verses.translation: Afterward came also the other virgins, saying, Lord, Lord, open to us.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐκ οἶδα ὑμᾶς.
verses.translit: o de apokritheis eipen* Amen lego umin, ouk oida umas.
verses.translation: But he answered and said, Verily I say unto you, I know you not.

verses.original: γρηγορεῖτε οὖν, ὅτι οὐκ οἴδατε τὴν ἡμέραν οὐδὲ τὴν ⸀ὥραν.
verses.translit: grigoreite oun, oti ouk oidate ten emeran oude ten oran.
verses.translation: Watch therefore, for ye know neither the day nor the hour wherein the Son of man cometh.

verses.original: Ὥσπερ γὰρ ἄνθρωπος ἀποδημῶν ἐκάλεσεν τοὺς ἰδίους δούλους καὶ παρέδωκεν αὐτοῖς τὰ ὑπάρχοντα αὐτοῦ,
verses.translit: Osper gar anthropos apodimon ekalesen tous idioys doyloys kai paredoken autois ta uparhonta autou,
verses.translation: For the kingdom of heaven is as a man travelling into a far country, who called his own servants, and delivered unto them his goods.

verses.original: καὶ ᾧ μὲν ἔδωκεν πέντε τάλαντα ᾧ δὲ δύο ᾧ δὲ ἕν, ἑκάστῳ κατὰ τὴν ἰδίαν δύναμιν, καὶ ἀπεδήμησεν. εὐθέως
verses.translit: kai o men edoken pente talanta o de dyo o de en, ekasto kata ten idian dynamin, kai apedimisen. eutheos
verses.translation: And unto one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one; to every man according to his several ability; and straightway took his journey.

verses.original: ⸀πορευθεὶς ὁ τὰ πέντε τάλαντα λαβὼν ἠργάσατο ἐν αὐτοῖς καὶ ⸀ἐκέρδησεν ἄλλα ⸀πέντε·
verses.translit: poreytheis o ta pente talanta lavon ergasato en autois kai ekerdisen alla pente*
verses.translation: Then he that had received the five talents went and traded with the same, and made them other five talents.

verses.original: ⸀ὡσαύτως ὁ τὰ δύο ⸀ἐκέρδησεν ἄλλα δύο·
verses.translit: osaytos o ta dyo ekerdisen alla dyo*
verses.translation: And likewise he that had received two, he also gained other two.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ τὸ ἓν λαβὼν ἀπελθὼν ὤρυξεν ⸀γῆν καὶ ⸀ἔκρυψεν τὸ ἀργύριον τοῦ κυρίου αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: o de to en lavon apelthon oryxen gen kai ekrypsen to argyrion tou kyrioy autou.
verses.translation: But he that had received one went and digged in the earth, and hid his lord’s money.

verses.original: μετὰ δὲ ⸂πολὺν χρόνον⸃ ἔρχεται ὁ κύριος τῶν δούλων ἐκείνων καὶ συναίρει ⸂λόγον μετʼ αὐτῶν⸃
verses.translit: meta de polun hronon erhetai o kyrios ton doylon ekeinon kai synairei logon met' auton
verses.translation: After a long time the lord of those servants cometh, and reckoneth with them.

verses.original: καὶ προσελθὼν ὁ τὰ πέντε τάλαντα λαβὼν προσήνεγκεν ἄλλα πέντε τάλαντα λέγων· Κύριε, πέντε τάλαντά μοι παρέδωκας· ἴδε ἄλλα πέντε τάλαντα ⸀ἐκέρδησα.
verses.translit: kai proselthon o ta pente talanta lavon prosinegken alla pente talanta legon* Kyrie, pente talanta moi paredokas* ide alla pente talanta ekerdisa.
verses.translation: And so he that had received five talents came and brought other five talents, saying, Lord, thou deliveredst unto me five talents: behold, I have gained beside them five talents more.

verses.original: ⸀ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ· Εὖ, δοῦλε ἀγαθὲ καὶ πιστέ, ἐπὶ ὀλίγα ἦς πιστός, ἐπὶ πολλῶν σε καταστήσω· εἴσελθε εἰς τὴν χαρὰν τοῦ κυρίου σου.
verses.translit: efi auto o kyrios autou* Eu, doule agathe kai piste, epi oliga es pistos, epi pollon se katastiso* eiselthe eis ten haran tou kyrioy soy.
verses.translation: His lord said unto him, Well done, thou good and faithful servant: thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord.

verses.original: προσελθὼν ⸀δὲ καὶ ὁ τὰ δύο ⸀τάλαντα εἶπεν· Κύριε, δύο τάλαντά μοι παρέδωκας· ἴδε ἄλλα δύο τάλαντα ⸀ἐκέρδησα.
verses.translit: proselthon de kai o ta dyo talanta eipen* Kyrie, dyo talanta moi paredokas* ide alla dyo talanta ekerdisa.
verses.translation: He also that had received two talents came and said, Lord, thou deliveredst unto me two talents: behold, I have gained two other talents beside them.

verses.original: ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ· Εὖ, δοῦλε ἀγαθὲ καὶ πιστέ, ἐπὶ ὀλίγα ἦς πιστός, ἐπὶ πολλῶν σε καταστήσω· εἴσελθε εἰς τὴν χαρὰν τοῦ κυρίου σου.
verses.translit: efi auto o kyrios autou* Eu, doule agathe kai piste, epi oliga es pistos, epi pollon se katastiso* eiselthe eis ten haran tou kyrioy soy.
verses.translation: His lord said unto him, Well done, good and faithful servant; thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord.

verses.original: προσελθὼν δὲ καὶ ὁ τὸ ἓν τάλαντον εἰληφὼς εἶπεν· Κύριε, ἔγνων σε ὅτι σκληρὸς εἶ ἄνθρωπος, θερίζων ὅπου οὐκ ἔσπειρας καὶ συνάγων ὅθεν οὐ διεσκόρπισας·
verses.translit: proselthon de kai o to en talanton eilifos eipen* Kyrie, egnon se oti skliros ei anthropos, therizon opoy ouk espeiras kai synagon othen ou dieskorpisas*
verses.translation: Then he which had received the one talent came and said, Lord, I knew thee that thou art an hard man, reaping where thou hast not sown, and gathering where thou hast not strawed:

verses.original: καὶ φοβηθεὶς ἀπελθὼν ἔκρυψα τὸ τάλαντόν σου ἐν τῇ γῇ· ἴδε ἔχεις τὸ σόν.
verses.translit: kai fovitheis apelthon ekrypsa to talanton soy en te ge* ide eheis to son.
verses.translation: And I was afraid, and went and hid thy talent in the earth: lo, there thou hast that is thine.

verses.original: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Πονηρὲ δοῦλε καὶ ὀκνηρέ, ᾔδεις ὅτι θερίζω ὅπου οὐκ ἔσπειρα καὶ συνάγω ὅθεν οὐ διεσκόρπισα;
verses.translit: apokritheis de o kyrios autou eipen auto* Ponire doule kai oknire, edeis oti therizo opoy ouk espeira kai synago othen ou dieskorpisa;
verses.translation: His lord answered and said unto him, Thou wicked and slothful servant, thou knewest that I reap where I sowed not, and gather where I have not strawed:

verses.original: ἔδει ⸂σε οὖν⸃ βαλεῖν ⸂τὰ ἀργύριά⸃ μου τοῖς τραπεζίταις, καὶ ἐλθὼν ἐγὼ ἐκομισάμην ἂν τὸ ἐμὸν σὺν τόκῳ.
verses.translit: edei se oun valein ta argyria moy tois trapezitais, kai elthon ego ekomisamin an to emon sun toko.
verses.translation: Thou oughtest therefore to have put my money to the exchangers, and then at my coming I should have received mine own with usury.

verses.original: ἄρατε οὖν ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ τὸ τάλαντον καὶ δότε τῷ ἔχοντι τὰ δέκα τάλαντα·
verses.translit: arate oun ap' autou to talanton kai dote to ehonti ta deka talanta*
verses.translation: Take therefore the talent from him, and give it unto him which hath ten talents.

verses.original: τῷ γὰρ ἔχοντι παντὶ δοθήσεται καὶ περισσευθήσεται· ⸂τοῦ δὲ⸃ μὴ ἔχοντος καὶ ὃ ἔχει ἀρθήσεται ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: to gar ehonti panti dothisetai kai perisseythisetai* tou de me ehontos kai o ehei arthisetai ap' autou.
verses.translation: For unto every one that hath shall be given, and he shall have abundance: but from him that hath not shall be taken away even that which he hath.

verses.original: καὶ τὸν ἀχρεῖον δοῦλον ἐκβάλετε εἰς τὸ σκότος τὸ ἐξώτερον· ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων.
verses.translit: kai ton ahreion doulon ekvalete eis to skotos to exoteron* ekei estai o klaythmos kai o vrygmos ton odonton.
verses.translation: And cast ye the unprofitable servant into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

verses.original: Ὅταν δὲ ἔλθῃ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐν τῇ δόξῃ αὐτοῦ καὶ πάντες ⸀οἱ ἄγγελοι μετʼ αὐτοῦ, τότε καθίσει ἐπὶ θρόνου δόξης αὐτοῦ·
verses.translit: Otan de elthe o yios tou anthropoy en te doxe autou kai pantes oi aggeloi met' autou, tote kathisei epi thronoy doxis autou*
verses.translation: When the Son of man shall come in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then shall he sit upon the throne of his glory:

verses.original: καὶ ⸀συναχθήσονται ἔμπροσθεν αὐτοῦ πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, καὶ ἀφορίσει αὐτοὺς ἀπʼ ἀλλήλων, ὥσπερ ὁ ποιμὴν ἀφορίζει τὰ πρόβατα ἀπὸ τῶν ἐρίφων,
verses.translit: kai synahthisontai emprosthen autou panta ta ethni, kai aforisei autous ap' allilon, osper o poimen aforizei ta provata apo ton erifon,
verses.translation: And before him shall be gathered all nations: and he shall separate them one from another, as a shepherd divideth his sheep from the goats:

verses.original: καὶ στήσει τὰ μὲν πρόβατα ἐκ δεξιῶν αὐτοῦ τὰ δὲ ἐρίφια ἐξ εὐωνύμων.
verses.translit: kai stisei ta men provata ek dexion autou ta de erifia ex euonymon.
verses.translation: And he shall set the sheep on his right hand, but the goats on the left.

verses.original: τότε ἐρεῖ ὁ βασιλεὺς τοῖς ἐκ δεξιῶν αὐτοῦ· Δεῦτε, οἱ εὐλογημένοι τοῦ πατρός μου, κληρονομήσατε τὴν ἡτοιμασμένην ὑμῖν βασιλείαν ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου.
verses.translit: tote erei o vasileus tois ek dexion autou* Deute, oi eulogimenoi tou patros moy, klironomisate ten etoimasmenin umin vasileian apo katavoles kosmoy.
verses.translation: Then shall the King say unto them on his right hand, Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world:

verses.original: ἐπείνασα γὰρ καὶ ἐδώκατέ μοι φαγεῖν, ἐδίψησα καὶ ἐποτίσατέ με, ξένος ἤμην καὶ συνηγάγετέ με,
verses.translit: epeinasa gar kai edokate moi fagein, edipsisa kai epotisate me, xenos emin kai synigagete me,
verses.translation: For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in:

verses.original: γυμνὸς καὶ περιεβάλετέ με, ἠσθένησα καὶ ἐπεσκέψασθέ με, ἐν φυλακῇ ἤμην καὶ ἤλθατε πρός με.
verses.translit: gymnos kai perievalete me, esthenisa kai epeskepsasthe me, en fylake emin kai elthate pros me.
verses.translation: Naked, and ye clothed me: I was sick, and ye visited me: I was in prison, and ye came unto me.

verses.original: τότε ἀποκριθήσονται αὐτῷ οἱ δίκαιοι λέγοντες· Κύριε, πότε σε εἴδομεν πεινῶντα καὶ ἐθρέψαμεν, ἢ διψῶντα καὶ ἐποτίσαμεν;
verses.translit: tote apokrithisontai auto oi dikaioi legontes* Kyrie, pote se eidomen peinonta kai ethrepsamen, e dipsonta kai epotisamen;
verses.translation: Then shall the righteous answer him, saying, Lord, when saw we thee an hungred, and fed thee ? or thirsty, and gave thee drink?

verses.original: πότε δέ σε εἴδομεν ξένον καὶ συνηγάγομεν, ἢ γυμνὸν καὶ περιεβάλομεν;
verses.translit: pote de se eidomen xenon kai synigagomen, e gymnon kai perievalomen;
verses.translation: When saw we thee a stranger, and took thee in? or naked, and clothed thee ?

verses.original: πότε δέ σε εἴδομεν ⸀ἀσθενοῦντα ἢ ἐν φυλακῇ καὶ ἤλθομεν πρός σε;
verses.translit: pote de se eidomen asthenounta e en fylake kai elthomen pros se;
verses.translation: Or when saw we thee sick, or in prison, and came unto thee?

verses.original: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ βασιλεὺς ἐρεῖ αὐτοῖς· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐφʼ ὅσον ἐποιήσατε ἑνὶ τούτων τῶν ἀδελφῶν μου τῶν ἐλαχίστων, ἐμοὶ ἐποιήσατε.
verses.translit: kai apokritheis o vasileus erei autois* Amen lego umin, ef' oson epoiisate eni toyton ton adelfon moy ton elahiston, emoi epoiisate.
verses.translation: And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.

verses.original: τότε ἐρεῖ καὶ τοῖς ἐξ εὐωνύμων· Πορεύεσθε ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ ⸀οἱ κατηραμένοι εἰς τὸ πῦρ τὸ αἰώνιον τὸ ἡτοιμασμένον τῷ διαβόλῳ καὶ τοῖς ἀγγέλοις αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: tote erei kai tois ex euonymon* Poreyesthe ap' emou oi katiramenoi eis to pur to aionion to etoimasmenon to diavolo kai tois aggelois autou.
verses.translation: Then shall he say also unto them on the left hand, Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels:

verses.original: ἐπείνασα γὰρ καὶ οὐκ ἐδώκατέ μοι φαγεῖν, ⸀ἐδίψησα καὶ οὐκ ἐποτίσατέ με,
verses.translit: epeinasa gar kai ouk edokate moi fagein, edipsisa kai ouk epotisate me,
verses.translation: For I was an hungred, and ye gave me no meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me no drink:

verses.original: ξένος ἤμην καὶ οὐ συνηγάγετέ με, γυμνὸς καὶ οὐ περιεβάλετέ με, ἀσθενὴς καὶ ἐν φυλακῇ καὶ οὐκ ἐπεσκέψασθέ με.
verses.translit: xenos emin kai ou synigagete me, gymnos kai ou perievalete me, asthenes kai en fylake kai ouk epeskepsasthe me.
verses.translation: I was a stranger, and ye took me not in: naked, and ye clothed me not: sick, and in prison, and ye visited me not.

verses.original: τότε ἀποκριθήσονται καὶ αὐτοὶ λέγοντες· Κύριε, πότε σε εἴδομεν πεινῶντα ἢ διψῶντα ἢ ξένον ἢ γυμνὸν ἢ ἀσθενῆ ἢ ἐν φυλακῇ καὶ οὐ διηκονήσαμέν σοι;
verses.translit: tote apokrithisontai kai autoi legontes* Kyrie, pote se eidomen peinonta e dipsonta e xenon e gymnon e asthene e en fylake kai ou diikonisamen soi;
verses.translation: Then shall they also answer him, saying, Lord, when saw we thee an hungred, or athirst, or a stranger, or naked, or sick, or in prison, and did not minister unto thee?

verses.original: τότε ἀποκριθήσεται αὐτοῖς λέγων· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐφʼ ὅσον οὐκ ἐποιήσατε ἑνὶ τούτων τῶν ἐλαχίστων, οὐδὲ ἐμοὶ ἐποιήσατε.
verses.translit: tote apokrithisetai autois legon* Amen lego umin, ef' oson ouk epoiisate eni toyton ton elahiston, oude emoi epoiisate.
verses.translation: Then shall he answer them, saying, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye did it not to one of the least of these, ye did it not to me.

verses.original: καὶ ἀπελεύσονται οὗτοι εἰς κόλασιν αἰώνιον, οἱ δὲ δίκαιοι εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον.
verses.translit: kai apeleysontai outoi eis kolasin aionion, oi de dikaioi eis zoen aionion.
verses.translation: And these shall go away into everlasting punishment: but the righteous into life eternal.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ὅτε ἐτέλεσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς πάντας τοὺς λόγους τούτους, εἶπεν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ·
verses.translit: Kai egeneto ote etelesen o Iisous pantas tous logoys toytoys, eipen tois mathitais autou*
verses.translation: And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished all these sayings, he said unto his disciples,

verses.original: Οἴδατε ὅτι μετὰ δύο ἡμέρας τὸ πάσχα γίνεται, καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδοται εἰς τὸ σταυρωθῆναι.
verses.translit: Oidate oti meta dyo emeras to pasha ginetai, kai o yios tou anthropoy paradidotai eis to stayrothenai.
verses.translation: Ye know that after two days is the feast of the passover, and the Son of man is betrayed to be crucified.

verses.original: Τότε συνήχθησαν οἱ ⸀ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι τοῦ λαοῦ εἰς τὴν αὐλὴν τοῦ ἀρχιερέως τοῦ λεγομένου Καϊάφα,
verses.translit: Tote synihthisan oi arhiereis kai oi presvyteroi tou laou eis ten aulen tou arhiereos tou legomenoy Kaiafa,
verses.translation: Then assembled together the chief priests, and the scribes, and the elders of the people, unto the palace of the high priest, who was called Caiaphas,

verses.original: καὶ συνεβουλεύσαντο ἵνα τὸν Ἰησοῦν δόλῳ κρατήσωσιν καὶ ἀποκτείνωσιν·
verses.translit: kai synevoyleysanto ina ton Iisoun dolo kratisosin kai apokteinosin*
verses.translation: And consulted that they might take Jesus by subtilty, and kill him .

verses.original: ἔλεγον δέ· Μὴ ἐν τῇ ἑορτῇ, ἵνα μὴ θόρυβος γένηται ἐν τῷ λαῷ.
verses.translit: elegon de* Me en te eorte, ina me thoryvos genitai en to lao.
verses.translation: But they said, Not on the feast day , lest there be an uproar among the people.

verses.original: Τοῦ δὲ Ἰησοῦ γενομένου ἐν Βηθανίᾳ ἐν οἰκίᾳ Σίμωνος τοῦ λεπροῦ,
verses.translit: Tou de Iisou genomenoy en Vithania en oikia Simonos tou leprou,
verses.translation: Now when Jesus was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper,

verses.original: προσῆλθεν αὐτῷ γυνὴ ⸂ἔχουσα ἀλάβαστρον μύρου⸃ βαρυτίμου καὶ κατέχεεν ἐπὶ ⸂τῆς κεφαλῆς⸃ αὐτοῦ ἀνακειμένου.
verses.translit: proselthen auto gyne ehoysa alavastron myroy varytimoy kai kateheen epi tes kefales autou anakeimenoy.
verses.translation: There came unto him a woman having an alabaster box of very precious ointment, and poured it on his head, as he sat at meat .

verses.original: ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ ⸀μαθηταὶ ἠγανάκτησαν λέγοντες· Εἰς τί ἡ ἀπώλεια αὕτη;
verses.translit: idontes de oi mathitai eganaktisan legontes* Eis ti e apoleia auti;
verses.translation: But when his disciples saw it , they had indignation, saying, To what purpose is this waste?

verses.original: ἐδύνατο γὰρ ⸀τοῦτο πραθῆναι πολλοῦ καὶ δοθῆναι πτωχοῖς.
verses.translit: edynato gar touto prathenai pollou kai dothenai ptohois.
verses.translation: For this ointment might have been sold for much, and given to the poor.

verses.original: γνοὺς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τί κόπους παρέχετε τῇ γυναικί; ἔργον γὰρ καλὸν ἠργάσατο εἰς ἐμέ·
verses.translit: gnous de o Iisous eipen autois* Ti kopoys parehete te gynaiki; ergon gar kalon ergasato eis eme*
verses.translation: When Jesus understood it , he said unto them, Why trouble ye the woman? for she hath wrought a good work upon me.

verses.original: πάντοτε γὰρ τοὺς πτωχοὺς ἔχετε μεθʼ ἑαυτῶν, ἐμὲ δὲ οὐ πάντοτε ἔχετε·
verses.translit: pantote gar tous ptohous ehete meth' eayton, eme de ou pantote ehete*
verses.translation: For ye have the poor always with you; but me ye have not always.

verses.original: βαλοῦσα γὰρ αὕτη τὸ μύρον τοῦτο ἐπὶ τοῦ σώματός μου πρὸς τὸ ἐνταφιάσαι με ἐποίησεν.
verses.translit: valousa gar auti to myron touto epi tou somatos moy pros to entafiasai me epoiisen.
verses.translation: For in that she hath poured this ointment on my body, she did it for my burial.

verses.original: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ὅπου ἐὰν κηρυχθῇ τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦτο ἐν ὅλῳ τῷ κόσμῳ, λαληθήσεται καὶ ὃ ἐποίησεν αὕτη εἰς μνημόσυνον αὐτῆς.
verses.translit: amen lego umin, opoy ean kiryhthe to euaggelion touto en olo to kosmo, lalithisetai kai o epoiisen auti eis mnimosynon autes.
verses.translation: Verily I say unto you, Wheresoever this gospel shall be preached in the whole world, there shall also this, that this woman hath done, be told for a memorial of her.

verses.original: Τότε πορευθεὶς εἷς τῶν δώδεκα, ὁ λεγόμενος Ἰούδας Ἰσκαριώτης, πρὸς τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς
verses.translit: Tote poreytheis eis ton dodeka, o legomenos Ioydas Iskariotis, pros tous arhiereis
verses.translation: Then one of the twelve, called Judas Iscariot, went unto the chief priests,

verses.original: εἶπεν· Τί θέλετέ μοι δοῦναι κἀγὼ ὑμῖν παραδώσω αὐτόν; οἱ δὲ ἔστησαν αὐτῷ τριάκοντα ἀργύρια.
verses.translit: eipen* Ti thelete moi dounai kago umin paradoso auton; oi de estisan auto triakonta argyria.
verses.translation: And said unto them , What will ye give me, and I will deliver him unto you? And they covenanted with him for thirty pieces of silver.

verses.original: καὶ ἀπὸ τότε ἐζήτει εὐκαιρίαν ἵνα αὐτὸν παραδῷ.
verses.translit: kai apo tote ezitei eukairian ina auton parado.
verses.translation: And from that time he sought opportunity to betray him.

verses.original: Τῇ δὲ πρώτῃ τῶν ἀζύμων προσῆλθον οἱ μαθηταὶ τῷ Ἰησοῦ ⸀λέγοντες· Ποῦ θέλεις ⸀ἑτοιμάσωμέν σοι φαγεῖν τὸ πάσχα;
verses.translit: Te de prote ton azymon proselthon oi mathitai to Iisou legontes* Pou theleis etoimasomen soi fagein to pasha;
verses.translation: Now the first day of the feast of unleavened bread the disciples came to Jesus, saying unto him, Where wilt thou that we prepare for thee to eat the passover?

verses.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ὑπάγετε εἰς τὴν πόλιν πρὸς τὸν δεῖνα καὶ εἴπατε αὐτῷ· Ὁ διδάσκαλος λέγει· Ὁ καιρός μου ἐγγύς ἐστιν· πρὸς σὲ ποιῶ τὸ πάσχα μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν μου.
verses.translit: o de eipen* Upagete eis ten polin pros ton deina kai eipate auto* O didaskalos legei* O kairos moy eggys estin* pros se poio to pasha meta ton mathiton moy.
verses.translation: And he said, Go into the city to such a man, and say unto him, The Master saith, My time is at hand; I will keep the passover at thy house with my disciples.

verses.original: καὶ ἐποίησαν οἱ μαθηταὶ ὡς συνέταξεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς, καὶ ἡτοίμασαν τὸ πάσχα.
verses.translit: kai epoiisan oi mathitai os synetaxen autois o Iisous, kai etoimasan to pasha.
verses.translation: And the disciples did as Jesus had appointed them; and they made ready the passover.

verses.original: Ὀψίας δὲ γενομένης ἀνέκειτο μετὰ τῶν δώδεκα ⸀μαθητῶν
verses.translit: Opsias de genomenis anekeito meta ton dodeka mathiton
verses.translation: Now when the even was come, he sat down with the twelve.

verses.original: καὶ ἐσθιόντων αὐτῶν εἶπεν· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι εἷς ἐξ ὑμῶν παραδώσει με.
verses.translit: kai esthionton auton eipen* Amen lego umin oti eis ex umon paradosei me.
verses.translation: And as they did eat, he said, Verily I say unto you, that one of you shall betray me.

verses.original: καὶ λυπούμενοι σφόδρα ἤρξαντο λέγειν αὐτῷ ⸂εἷς ἕκαστος⸃· Μήτι ἐγώ εἰμι, κύριε;
verses.translit: kai lypoymenoi sfodra erxanto legein auto eis ekastos* Miti ego eimi, kyrie;
verses.translation: And they were exceeding sorrowful, and began every one of them to say unto him, Lord, is it I?

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Ὁ ἐμβάψας μετʼ ἐμοῦ ⸂τὴν χεῖρα ἐν τῷ τρυβλίῳ⸃ οὗτός με παραδώσει·
verses.translit: o de apokritheis eipen* O emvapsas met' emou ten heira en to tryvlio outos me paradosei*
verses.translation: And he answered and said, He that dippeth his hand with me in the dish, the same shall betray me.

verses.original: ὁ μὲν υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ὑπάγει καθὼς γέγραπται περὶ αὐτοῦ, οὐαὶ δὲ τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ ἐκείνῳ διʼ οὗ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδοται· καλὸν ἦν αὐτῷ εἰ οὐκ ἐγεννήθη ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος.
verses.translit: o men yios tou anthropoy upagei kathos gegraptai peri autou, ouai de to anthropo ekeino di' ou o yios tou anthropoy paradidotai* kalon en auto ei ouk egennithi o anthropos ekeinos.
verses.translation: The Son of man goeth as it is written of him: but woe unto that man by whom the Son of man is betrayed! it had been good for that man if he had not been born.

verses.original: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ Ἰούδας ὁ παραδιδοὺς αὐτὸν εἶπεν· Μήτι ἐγώ εἰμι, ῥαββί; λέγει αὐτῷ· Σὺ εἶπας.
verses.translit: apokritheis de Ioydas o paradidous auton eipen* Miti ego eimi, Ravvi; legei auto* Su eipas.
verses.translation: Then Judas, which betrayed him, answered and said, Master, is it I? He said unto him, Thou hast said.

verses.original: Ἐσθιόντων δὲ αὐτῶν λαβὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ⸀ἄρτον καὶ ⸀εὐλογήσας ἔκλασεν καὶ ⸂δοὺς τοῖς μαθηταῖς⸃ εἶπεν· Λάβετε φάγετε, τοῦτό ἐστιν τὸ σῶμά μου.
verses.translit: Esthionton de auton lavon o Iisous arton kai eulogisas eklasen kai dous tois mathitais eipen* Lavete fagete, touto estin to soma moy.
verses.translation: And as they were eating, Jesus took bread, and blessed it , and brake it , and gave it to the disciples, and said, Take, eat; this is my body.

verses.original: καὶ ⸀λαβὼν ποτήριον καὶ εὐχαριστήσας ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς λέγων· Πίετε ἐξ αὐτοῦ πάντες,
verses.translit: kai lavon potirion kai euharistisas edoken autois legon* Piete ex autou pantes,
verses.translation: And he took the cup, and gave thanks, and gave it to them, saying, Drink ye all of it;

verses.original: τοῦτο γάρ ἐστιν τὸ αἷμά ⸀μου ⸀τῆς διαθήκης τὸ περὶ πολλῶν ἐκχυννόμενον εἰς ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν·
verses.translit: touto gar estin to aima moy tes diathikis to peri pollon ekhynnomenon eis afesin amartion*
verses.translation: For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.

verses.original: λέγω δὲ ⸀ὑμῖν, οὐ μὴ πίω ἀπʼ ἄρτι ἐκ τούτου τοῦ γενήματος τῆς ἀμπέλου ἕως τῆς ἡμέρας ἐκείνης ὅταν αὐτὸ πίνω μεθʼ ὑμῶν καινὸν ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ πατρός μου.
verses.translit: lego de umin, ou me pio ap' arti ek toytoy tou genimatos tes ampeloy eos tes emeras ekeinis otan auto pino meth' umon kainon en te vasileia tou patros moy.
verses.translation: But I say unto you, I will not drink henceforth of this fruit of the vine, until that day when I drink it new with you in my Father’s kingdom.

verses.original: καὶ ὑμνήσαντες ἐξῆλθον εἰς τὸ Ὄρος τῶν Ἐλαιῶν.
verses.translit: kai umnisantes exelthon eis to Oros ton Elaion.
verses.translation: And when they had sung an hymn, they went out into the mount of Olives.

verses.original: Τότε λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Πάντες ὑμεῖς σκανδαλισθήσεσθε ἐν ἐμοὶ ἐν τῇ νυκτὶ ταύτῃ, γέγραπται γάρ· Πατάξω τὸν ποιμένα, καὶ ⸀διασκορπισθήσονται τὰ πρόβατα τῆς ποίμνης·
verses.translit: Tote legei autois o Iisous* Pantes umeis skandalisthisesthe en emoi en te nykti tayte, gegraptai gar* Pataxo ton poimena, kai diaskorpisthisontai ta provata tes poimnis*
verses.translation: Then saith Jesus unto them, All ye shall be offended because of me this night: for it is written, I will smite the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock shall be scattered abroad.

verses.original: μετὰ δὲ τὸ ἐγερθῆναί με προάξω ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν.
verses.translit: meta de to egerthenai me proaxo umas eis ten Galilaian.
verses.translation: But after I am risen again, I will go before you into Galilee.

verses.original: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Πέτρος εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Εἰ πάντες σκανδαλισθήσονται ἐν σοί, ⸀ἐγὼ οὐδέποτε σκανδαλισθήσομαι.
verses.translit: apokritheis de o Petros eipen auto* Ei pantes skandalisthisontai en soi, ego oudepote skandalisthisomai.
verses.translation: Peter answered and said unto him, Though all men shall be offended because of thee, yet will I never be offended.

verses.original: ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἀμὴν λέγω σοι ὅτι ἐν ταύτῃ τῇ νυκτὶ πρὶν ἀλέκτορα φωνῆσαι τρὶς ἀπαρνήσῃ με.
verses.translit: efi auto o Iisous* Amen lego soi oti en tayte te nykti prin alektora fonesai tris aparnise me.
verses.translation: Jesus said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, That this night, before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice.

verses.original: λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Πέτρος· Κἂν δέῃ με σὺν σοὶ ἀποθανεῖν, οὐ μή σε ⸀ἀπαρνήσομαι. ⸀ὁμοίως καὶ πάντες οἱ μαθηταὶ εἶπαν.
verses.translit: legei auto o Petros* Kan dee me sun soi apothanein, ou mi se aparnisomai. omoios kai pantes oi mathitai eipan.
verses.translation: Peter said unto him, Though I should die with thee, yet will I not deny thee. Likewise also said all the disciples.

verses.original: Τότε ἔρχεται μετʼ αὐτῶν ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς χωρίον λεγόμενον Γεθσημανί, καὶ λέγει τοῖς μαθηταῖς· Καθίσατε αὐτοῦ ἕως οὗ ἀπελθὼν ⸂ἐκεῖ προσεύξωμαι⸃.
verses.translit: Tote erhetai met' auton o Iisous eis horion legomenon Gethsimani, kai legei tois mathitais* Kathisate autou eos ou apelthon ekei proseyxomai.
verses.translation: Then cometh Jesus with them unto a place called Gethsemane, and saith unto the disciples, Sit ye here, while I go and pray yonder.

verses.original: καὶ παραλαβὼν τὸν Πέτρον καὶ τοὺς δύο υἱοὺς Ζεβεδαίου ἤρξατο λυπεῖσθαι καὶ ἀδημονεῖν.
verses.translit: kai paralavon ton Petron kai tous dyo yious Zevedaioy erxato lypeisthai kai adimonein.
verses.translation: And he took with him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, and began to be sorrowful and very heavy.

verses.original: τότε λέγει ⸀αὐτοῖς· Περίλυπός ἐστιν ἡ ψυχή μου ἕως θανάτου· μείνατε ὧδε καὶ γρηγορεῖτε μετʼ ἐμοῦ.
verses.translit: tote legei autois* Perilypos estin e psyhi moy eos thanatoy* meinate ode kai grigoreite met' emou.
verses.translation: Then saith he unto them, My soul is exceeding sorrowful, even unto death: tarry ye here, and watch with me.

verses.original: καὶ ⸀προελθὼν μικρὸν ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ προσευχόμενος καὶ λέγων· Πάτερ μου, εἰ δυνατόν ἐστιν, παρελθάτω ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ τὸ ποτήριον τοῦτο· πλὴν οὐχ ὡς ἐγὼ θέλω ἀλλʼ ὡς σύ.
verses.translit: kai proelthon mikron epesen epi prosopon autou proseyhomenos kai legon* Pater moy, ei dynaton estin, parelthato ap' emou to potirion touto* plen ouh os ego thelo all' os sy.
verses.translation: And he went a little further, and fell on his face, and prayed, saying, O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt .

verses.original: καὶ ἔρχεται πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς καὶ εὑρίσκει αὐτοὺς καθεύδοντας, καὶ λέγει τῷ Πέτρῳ· Οὕτως οὐκ ἰσχύσατε μίαν ὥραν γρηγορῆσαι μετʼ ἐμοῦ;
verses.translit: kai erhetai pros tous mathitas kai euriskei autous katheydontas, kai legei to Petro* Outos ouk ishysate mian oran grigoresai met' emou;
verses.translation: And he cometh unto the disciples, and findeth them asleep, and saith unto Peter, What, could ye not watch with me one hour?

verses.original: γρηγορεῖτε καὶ προσεύχεσθε, ἵνα μὴ εἰσέλθητε εἰς πειρασμόν· τὸ μὲν πνεῦμα πρόθυμον ἡ δὲ σὰρξ ἀσθενής.
verses.translit: grigoreite kai proseyhesthe, ina me eiselthite eis peirasmon* to men pneuma prothymon e de sarx asthenis.
verses.translation: Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.

verses.original: πάλιν ἐκ δευτέρου ἀπελθὼν προσηύξατο λέγων· Πάτερ μου, εἰ οὐ δύναται ⸀τοῦτο ⸀παρελθεῖν ἐὰν μὴ αὐτὸ πίω, γενηθήτω τὸ θέλημά σου.
verses.translit: palin ek deyteroy apelthon prosiyxato legon* Pater moy, ei ou dynatai touto parelthein ean me auto pio, genithito to thelima soy.
verses.translation: He went away again the second time, and prayed, saying, O my Father, if this cup may not pass away from me, except I drink it, thy will be done.

verses.original: καὶ ἐλθὼν ⸂πάλιν εὗρεν αὐτοὺς⸃ καθεύδοντας, ἦσαν γὰρ αὐτῶν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ βεβαρημένοι.
verses.translit: kai elthon palin euren autous katheydontas, esan gar auton oi ofthalmoi vevarimenoi.
verses.translation: And he came and found them asleep again: for their eyes were heavy.

verses.original: καὶ ἀφεὶς αὐτοὺς ⸂πάλιν ἀπελθὼν⸃ προσηύξατο ἐκ τρίτου τὸν αὐτὸν λόγον εἰπὼν ⸀πάλιν.
verses.translit: kai afeis autous palin apelthon prosiyxato ek tritoy ton auton logon eipon palin.
verses.translation: And he left them, and went away again, and prayed the third time, saying the same words.

verses.original: τότε ἔρχεται πρὸς τοὺς ⸀μαθητὰς καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Καθεύδετε ⸀τὸ λοιπὸν καὶ ἀναπαύεσθε· ἰδοὺ ἤγγικεν ἡ ὥρα καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδοται εἰς χεῖρας ἁμαρτωλῶν.
verses.translit: tote erhetai pros tous mathitas kai legei autois* Katheydete to loipon kai anapayesthe* idou eggiken e ora kai o yios tou anthropoy paradidotai eis heiras amartolon.
verses.translation: Then cometh he to his disciples, and saith unto them, Sleep on now, and take your rest: behold, the hour is at hand, and the Son of man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.

verses.original: ἐγείρεσθε ἄγωμεν· ἰδοὺ ἤγγικεν ὁ παραδιδούς με.
verses.translit: egeiresthe agomen* idou eggiken o paradidoys me.
verses.translation: Rise, let us be going: behold, he is at hand that doth betray me.

verses.original: Καὶ ἔτι αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος ἰδοὺ Ἰούδας εἷς τῶν δώδεκα ἦλθεν καὶ μετʼ αὐτοῦ ὄχλος πολὺς μετὰ μαχαιρῶν καὶ ξύλων ἀπὸ τῶν ἀρχιερέων καὶ πρεσβυτέρων τοῦ λαοῦ.
verses.translit: Kai eti autou lalountos idou Ioydas eis ton dodeka elthen kai met' autou ohlos polus meta mahairon kai xylon apo ton arhiereon kai presvyteron tou laou.
verses.translation: And while he yet spake, lo, Judas, one of the twelve, came, and with him a great multitude with swords and staves, from the chief priests and elders of the people.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ παραδιδοὺς αὐτὸν ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς σημεῖον λέγων· Ὃν ἂν φιλήσω αὐτός ἐστιν· κρατήσατε αὐτόν.
verses.translit: o de paradidous auton edoken autois simeion legon* On an filiso autos estin* kratisate auton.
verses.translation: Now he that betrayed him gave them a sign, saying, Whomsoever I shall kiss, that same is he: hold him fast.

verses.original: καὶ εὐθέως προσελθὼν τῷ Ἰησοῦ εἶπεν· Χαῖρε, ῥαββί· καὶ κατεφίλησεν αὐτόν.
