verses.translit: kai eutheos proselthon to Iisou eipen* Haire, Ravvi* kai katefilisen auton.
verses.translation: And forthwith he came to Jesus, and said, Hail, master; and kissed him.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἑταῖρε, ἐφʼ ⸀ὃ πάρει. τότε προσελθόντες ἐπέβαλον τὰς χεῖρας ἐπὶ τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ ἐκράτησαν αὐτόν.
verses.translit: o de Iisous eipen auto* Etaire, ef' o parei. tote proselthontes epevalon tas heiras epi ton Iisoun kai ekratisan auton.
verses.translation: And Jesus said unto him, Friend, wherefore art thou come? Then came they, and laid hands on Jesus, and took him.

verses.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ εἷς τῶν μετὰ Ἰησοῦ ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα ἀπέσπασεν τὴν μάχαιραν αὐτοῦ καὶ πατάξας τὸν δοῦλον τοῦ ἀρχιερέως ἀφεῖλεν αὐτοῦ τὸ ὠτίον.
verses.translit: kai idou eis ton meta Iisou ekteinas ten heira apespasen ten mahairan autou kai pataxas ton doulon tou arhiereos afeilen autou to otion.
verses.translation: And, behold, one of them which were with Jesus stretched out his hand, and drew his sword, and struck a servant of the high priest’s, and smote off his ear.

verses.original: τότε λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἀπόστρεψον ⸂τὴν μάχαιράν σου⸃ εἰς τὸν τόπον αὐτῆς, πάντες γὰρ οἱ λαβόντες μάχαιραν ἐν μαχαίρῃ ⸀ἀπολοῦνται·
verses.translit: tote legei auto o Iisous* Apostrepson ten mahairan soy eis ton topon autes, pantes gar oi lavontes mahairan en mahaire apolountai*
verses.translation: Then said Jesus unto him, Put up again thy sword into his place: for all they that take the sword shall perish with the sword.

verses.original: ἢ δοκεῖς ὅτι οὐ ⸀δύναμαι παρακαλέσαι τὸν πατέρα μου, καὶ παραστήσει μοι ⸂ἄρτι πλείω⸃ δώδεκα λεγιῶνας ἀγγέλων;
verses.translit: e dokeis oti ou dynamai parakalesai ton patera moy, kai parastisei moi arti pleio dodeka legionas aggelon;
verses.translation: Thinkest thou that I cannot now pray to my Father, and he shall presently give me more than twelve legions of angels?

verses.original: πῶς οὖν πληρωθῶσιν αἱ γραφαὶ ὅτι οὕτως δεῖ γενέσθαι;
verses.translit: pos oun plirothosin ai grafai oti outos dei genesthai;
verses.translation: But how then shall the scriptures be fulfilled, that thus it must be?

verses.original: ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοῖς ὄχλοις· Ὡς ἐπὶ λῃστὴν ἐξήλθατε μετὰ μαχαιρῶν καὶ ξύλων συλλαβεῖν με; καθʼ ⸀ἡμέραν ⸂ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ἐκαθεζόμην διδάσκων⸃ καὶ οὐκ ἐκρατήσατέ με.
verses.translit: en ekeine te ora eipen o Iisous tois ohlois* Os epi lesten exilthate meta mahairon kai xylon syllavein me; kath' emeran en to iero ekathezomin didaskon kai ouk ekratisate me.
verses.translation: In that same hour said Jesus to the multitudes, Are ye come out as against a thief with swords and staves for to take me? I sat daily with you teaching in the temple, and ye laid no hold on me.

verses.original: τοῦτο δὲ ὅλον γέγονεν ἵνα πληρωθῶσιν αἱ γραφαὶ τῶν προφητῶν. τότε οἱ μαθηταὶ πάντες ἀφέντες αὐτὸν ἔφυγον.
verses.translit: touto de olon gegonen ina plirothosin ai grafai ton profiton. tote oi mathitai pantes afentes auton efygon.
verses.translation: But all this was done, that the scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled. Then all the disciples forsook him, and fled.

verses.original: Οἱ δὲ κρατήσαντες τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀπήγαγον πρὸς Καϊάφαν τὸν ἀρχιερέα, ὅπου οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι συνήχθησαν.
verses.translit: Oi de kratisantes ton Iisoun apigagon pros Kaiafan ton arhierea, opoy oi grammateis kai oi presvyteroi synihthisan.
verses.translation: And they that had laid hold on Jesus led him away to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and the elders were assembled.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἕως τῆς αὐλῆς τοῦ ἀρχιερέως, καὶ εἰσελθὼν ἔσω ἐκάθητο μετὰ τῶν ὑπηρετῶν ἰδεῖν τὸ τέλος.
verses.translit: o de Petros ekoloythei auto apo makrothen eos tes aules tou arhiereos, kai eiselthon eso ekathito meta ton upireton idein to telos.
verses.translation: But Peter followed him afar off unto the high priest’s palace, and went in, and sat with the servants, to see the end.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ ἀρχιερεῖς ⸀καὶ τὸ συνέδριον ὅλον ἐζήτουν ψευδομαρτυρίαν κατὰ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ὅπως ⸂αὐτὸν θανατώσωσιν⸃,
verses.translit: oi de arhiereis kai to synedrion olon ezitoyn pseydomartyrian kata tou Iisou opos auton thanatososin,
verses.translation: Now the chief priests, and elders, and all the council, sought false witness against Jesus, to put him to death;

verses.original: καὶ οὐχ εὗρον ⸂πολλῶν προσελθόντων ψευδομαρτύρων. ὕστερον δὲ προσελθόντες δύο⸃
verses.translit: kai ouh euron pollon proselthonton pseydomartyron. usteron de proselthontes dyo
verses.translation: But found none: yea, though many false witnesses came, yet found they none. At the last came two false witnesses,

verses.original: εἶπαν· Οὗτος ἔφη· Δύναμαι καταλῦσαι τὸν ναὸν τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ διὰ τριῶν ἡμερῶν ⸀οἰκοδομῆσαι.
verses.translit: eipan* Outos efi* Dynamai katalusai ton naon tou theou kai dia trion emeron oikodomesai.
verses.translation: And said, This fellow said, I am able to destroy the temple of God, and to build it in three days.

verses.original: καὶ ἀναστὰς ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Οὐδὲν ἀποκρίνῃ; τί οὗτοί σου καταμαρτυροῦσιν;
verses.translit: kai anastas o arhiereus eipen auto* Ouden apokrine; ti outoi soy katamartyrousin;
verses.translation: And the high priest arose, and said unto him, Answerest thou nothing? what is it which these witness against thee?

verses.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἐσιώπα. ⸀καὶ ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἐξορκίζω σε κατὰ τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ζῶντος ἵνα ἡμῖν εἴπῃς εἰ σὺ εἶ ὁ χριστὸς ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: o de Iisous esiopa. kai o arhiereus eipen auto* Exorkizo se kata tou theou tou zontos ina emin eipes ei su ei o hristos o yios tou theou.
verses.translation: But Jesus held his peace. And the high priest answered and said unto him, I adjure thee by the living God, that thou tell us whether thou be the Christ, the Son of God.

verses.original: λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Σὺ εἶπας· πλὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀπʼ ἄρτι ὄψεσθε τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου καθήμενον ἐκ δεξιῶν τῆς δυνάμεως καὶ ἐρχόμενον ἐπὶ τῶν νεφελῶν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ.
verses.translit: legei auto o Iisous* Su eipas* plen lego umin, ap' arti opsesthe ton yion tou anthropoy kathimenon ek dexion tes dynameos kai erhomenon epi ton nefelon tou ouranou.
verses.translation: Jesus saith unto him, Thou hast said: nevertheless I say unto you, Hereafter shall ye see the Son of man sitting on the right hand of power, and coming in the clouds of heaven.

verses.original: τότε ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς διέρρηξεν τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ ⸀λέγων· Ἐβλασφήμησεν· τί ἔτι χρείαν ἔχομεν μαρτύρων; ἴδε νῦν ἠκούσατε τὴν ⸀βλασφημίαν·
verses.translit: tote o arhiereus dierrixen ta imatia autou legon* Evlasfimisen* ti eti hreian ehomen martyron; ide nun ekoysate ten vlasfimian*
verses.translation: Then the high priest rent his clothes, saying, He hath spoken blasphemy; what further need have we of witnesses? behold, now ye have heard his blasphemy.

verses.original: τί ὑμῖν δοκεῖ; οἱ δὲ ἀποκριθέντες εἶπαν· Ἔνοχος θανάτου ἐστίν.
verses.translit: ti umin dokei; oi de apokrithentes eipan* Enohos thanatoy estin.
verses.translation: What think ye? They answered and said, He is guilty of death.

verses.original: τότε ἐνέπτυσαν εἰς τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐκολάφισαν αὐτόν, οἱ δὲ ἐράπισαν
verses.translit: tote eneptysan eis to prosopon autou kai ekolafisan auton, oi de erapisan
verses.translation: Then did they spit in his face, and buffeted him; and others smote him with the palms of their hands,

verses.original: λέγοντες· Προφήτευσον ἡμῖν, χριστέ, τίς ἐστιν ὁ παίσας σε;
verses.translit: legontes* Profiteyson emin, hriste, tis estin o paisas se;
verses.translation: Saying, Prophesy unto us, thou Christ, Who is he that smote thee?

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ⸂ἐκάθητο ἔξω⸃ ἐν τῇ αὐλῇ· καὶ προσῆλθεν αὐτῷ μία παιδίσκη λέγουσα· Καὶ σὺ ἦσθα μετὰ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Γαλιλαίου·
verses.translit: O de Petros ekathito exo en te aule* kai proselthen auto mia paidiski legoysa* Kai su estha meta Iisou tou Galilaioy*
verses.translation: Now Peter sat without in the palace: and a damsel came unto him, saying, Thou also wast with Jesus of Galilee.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ἠρνήσατο ⸀ἔμπροσθεν πάντων λέγων· Οὐκ οἶδα τί λέγεις.
verses.translit: o de ernisato emprosthen panton legon* Ouk oida ti legeis.
verses.translation: But he denied before them all, saying, I know not what thou sayest.

verses.original: ἐξελθόντα ⸀δὲ εἰς τὸν πυλῶνα εἶδεν αὐτὸν ἄλλη καὶ λέγει ⸀τοῖς ἐκεῖ· ⸀Οὗτος ἦν μετὰ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Ναζωραίου·
verses.translit: exelthonta de eis ton pylona eiden auton alli kai legei tois ekei* Outos en meta Iisou tou Nazoraioy*
verses.translation: And when he was gone out into the porch, another maid saw him, and said unto them that were there, This fellow was also with Jesus of Nazareth.

verses.original: καὶ πάλιν ἠρνήσατο μετὰ ὅρκου ὅτι Οὐκ οἶδα τὸν ἄνθρωπον.
verses.translit: kai palin ernisato meta orkoy oti Ouk oida ton anthropon.
verses.translation: And again he denied with an oath, I do not know the man.

verses.original: μετὰ μικρὸν δὲ προσελθόντες οἱ ἑστῶτες εἶπον τῷ Πέτρῳ· Ἀληθῶς καὶ σὺ ἐξ αὐτῶν εἶ, καὶ γὰρ ἡ λαλιά σου δῆλόν σε ποιεῖ·
verses.translit: meta mikron de proselthontes oi estotes eipon to Petro* Alithos kai su ex auton ei, kai gar e lalia soy delon se poiei*
verses.translation: And after a while came unto him they that stood by, and said to Peter, Surely thou also art one of them; for thy speech bewrayeth thee.

verses.original: τότε ἤρξατο καταθεματίζειν καὶ ὀμνύειν ὅτι Οὐκ οἶδα τὸν ἄνθρωπον. καὶ ⸀εὐθέως ἀλέκτωρ ἐφώνησεν·
verses.translit: tote erxato katathematizein kai omnyein oti Ouk oida ton anthropon. kai eutheos alektor efonisen*
verses.translation: Then began he to curse and to swear, saying , I know not the man. And immediately the cock crew.

verses.original: καὶ ἐμνήσθη ὁ Πέτρος τοῦ ⸀ῥήματος Ἰησοῦ ⸀εἰρηκότος ὅτι Πρὶν ἀλέκτορα φωνῆσαι τρὶς ἀπαρνήσῃ με, καὶ ἐξελθὼν ἔξω ἔκλαυσεν πικρῶς.
verses.translit: kai emnisthi o Petros tou Rimatos Iisou eirikotos oti Prin alektora fonesai tris aparnise me, kai exelthon exo eklaysen pikros.
verses.translation: And Peter remembered the word of Jesus, which said unto him, Before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice. And he went out, and wept bitterly.

verses.original: Πρωΐας δὲ γενομένης συμβούλιον ἔλαβον πάντες οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι τοῦ λαοῦ κατὰ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ὥστε θανατῶσαι αὐτόν·
verses.translit: ProIas de genomenis symvoylion elavon pantes oi arhiereis kai oi presvyteroi tou laou kata tou Iisou oste thanatosai auton*
verses.translation: When the morning was come, all the chief priests and elders of the people took counsel against Jesus to put him to death:

verses.original: καὶ δήσαντες αὐτὸν ἀπήγαγον καὶ ⸀παρέδωκαν Πιλάτῳ τῷ ἡγεμόνι.
verses.translit: kai disantes auton apigagon kai paredokan Pilato to egemoni.
verses.translation: And when they had bound him, they led him away, and delivered him to Pontius Pilate the governor.

verses.original: Τότε ἰδὼν Ἰούδας ὁ ⸀παραδιδοὺς αὐτὸν ὅτι κατεκρίθη μεταμεληθεὶς ⸀ἔστρεψεν τὰ τριάκοντα ἀργύρια τοῖς ἀρχιερεῦσιν ⸀καὶ πρεσβυτέροις
verses.translit: Tote idon Ioydas o paradidous auton oti katekrithi metamelitheis estrepsen ta triakonta argyria tois arhiereusin kai presvyterois
verses.translation: Then Judas, which had betrayed him, when he saw that he was condemned, repented himself, and brought again the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders,

verses.original: λέγων· Ἥμαρτον παραδοὺς αἷμα ⸀ἀθῷον. οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Τί πρὸς ἡμᾶς; σὺ ⸀ὄψῃ.
verses.translit: legon* Emarton paradous aima athoon. oi de eipan* Ti pros emas; su opse.
verses.translation: Saying, I have sinned in that I have betrayed the innocent blood. And they said, What is that to us? see thou to that .

verses.original: καὶ ῥίψας τὰ ἀργύρια ⸂εἰς τὸν ναὸν⸃ ἀνεχώρησεν, καὶ ἀπελθὼν ἀπήγξατο.
verses.translit: kai Ripsas ta argyria eis ton naon anehorisen, kai apelthon apigxato.
verses.translation: And he cast down the pieces of silver in the temple, and departed, and went and hanged himself.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ ἀρχιερεῖς λαβόντες τὰ ἀργύρια εἶπαν· Οὐκ ἔξεστιν βαλεῖν αὐτὰ εἰς τὸν κορβανᾶν, ἐπεὶ τιμὴ αἵματός ἐστιν·
verses.translit: oi de arhiereis lavontes ta argyria eipan* Ouk exestin valein auta eis ton korvanan, epei time aimatos estin*
verses.translation: And the chief priests took the silver pieces, and said, It is not lawful for to put them into the treasury, because it is the price of blood.

verses.original: συμβούλιον δὲ λαβόντες ἠγόρασαν ἐξ αὐτῶν τὸν Ἀγρὸν τοῦ Κεραμέως εἰς ταφὴν τοῖς ξένοις.
verses.translit: symvoylion de lavontes egorasan ex auton ton Agron tou Kerameos eis tafen tois xenois.
verses.translation: And they took counsel, and bought with them the potter’s field, to bury strangers in.

verses.original: διὸ ἐκλήθη ὁ ἀγρὸς ἐκεῖνος Ἀγρὸς Αἵματος ἕως τῆς σήμερον.
verses.translit: dio eklithi o agros ekeinos Agros Aimatos eos tes simeron.
verses.translation: Wherefore that field was called, The field of blood, unto this day.

verses.original: τότε ἐπληρώθη τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ Ἰερεμίου τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος· Καὶ ἔλαβον τὰ τριάκοντα ἀργύρια, τὴν τιμὴν τοῦ τετιμημένου ὃν ἐτιμήσαντο ἀπὸ υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ,
verses.translit: tote eplirothi to Rithen dia Ieremioy tou profitoy legontos* Kai elavon ta triakonta argyria, ten timen tou tetimimenoy on etimisanto apo yion Israil,
verses.translation: Then was fulfilled that which was spoken by Jeremy the prophet, saying, And they took the thirty pieces of silver, the price of him that was valued, whom they of the children of Israel did value;

verses.original: καὶ ἔδωκαν αὐτὰ εἰς τὸν ἀγρὸν τοῦ κεραμέως, καθὰ συνέταξέν μοι κύριος.
verses.translit: kai edokan auta eis ton agron tou kerameos, katha synetaxen moi kyrios.
verses.translation: And gave them for the potter’s field, as the Lord appointed me.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ⸀ἐστάθη ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ ἡγεμόνος· καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτὸν ὁ ἡγεμὼν λέγων· Σὺ εἶ ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων; ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ⸀ἔφη· Σὺ λέγεις.
verses.translit: O de Iisous estathi emprosthen tou egemonos* kai epirotisen auton o egemon legon* Su ei o vasileus ton Ioydaion; o de Iisous efi* Su legeis.
verses.translation: And Jesus stood before the governor: and the governor asked him, saying, Art thou the King of the Jews? And Jesus said unto him, Thou sayest.

verses.original: καὶ ἐν τῷ κατηγορεῖσθαι αὐτὸν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀρχιερέων ⸀καὶ πρεσβυτέρων οὐδὲν ἀπεκρίνατο.
verses.translit: kai en to katigoreisthai auton upo ton arhiereon kai presvyteron ouden apekrinato.
verses.translation: And when he was accused of the chief priests and elders, he answered nothing.

verses.original: τότε λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Οὐκ ἀκούεις πόσα σου καταμαρτυροῦσιν;
verses.translit: tote legei auto o Pilatos* Ouk akoyeis posa soy katamartyrousin;
verses.translation: Then said Pilate unto him, Hearest thou not how many things they witness against thee?

verses.original: καὶ οὐκ ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῷ πρὸς οὐδὲ ἓν ῥῆμα, ὥστε θαυμάζειν τὸν ἡγεμόνα λίαν.
verses.translit: kai ouk apekrithi auto pros oude en Rema, oste thaymazein ton egemona lian.
verses.translation: And he answered him to never a word; insomuch that the governor marvelled greatly.

verses.original: Κατὰ δὲ ἑορτὴν εἰώθει ὁ ἡγεμὼν ἀπολύειν ἕνα τῷ ὄχλῳ δέσμιον ὃν ἤθελον.
verses.translit: Kata de eorten eiothei o egemon apolyein ena to ohlo desmion on ethelon.
verses.translation: Now at that feast the governor was wont to release unto the people a prisoner, whom they would.

verses.original: εἶχον δὲ τότε δέσμιον ἐπίσημον λεγόμενον ⸀Ἰησοῦν Βαραββᾶν.
verses.translit: eihon de tote desmion episimon legomenon Iisoun Varavvan.
verses.translation: And they had then a notable prisoner, called Barabbas.

verses.original: συνηγμένων οὖν αὐτῶν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Τίνα θέλετε ἀπολύσω ὑμῖν, ⸂Ἰησοῦν τὸν⸃ Βαραββᾶν ἢ Ἰησοῦν τὸν λεγόμενον χριστόν;
verses.translit: synigmenon oun auton eipen autois o Pilatos* Tina thelete apolyso umin, Iisoun ton Varavvan e Iisoun ton legomenon hriston;
verses.translation: Therefore when they were gathered together, Pilate said unto them, Whom will ye that I release unto you? Barabbas, or Jesus which is called Christ?

verses.original: ᾔδει γὰρ ὅτι διὰ φθόνον παρέδωκαν αὐτόν.
verses.translit: edei gar oti dia fthonon paredokan auton.
verses.translation: For he knew that for envy they had delivered him.

verses.original: Καθημένου δὲ αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τοῦ βήματος ἀπέστειλεν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἡ γυνὴ αὐτοῦ λέγουσα· Μηδὲν σοὶ καὶ τῷ δικαίῳ ἐκείνῳ, πολλὰ γὰρ ἔπαθον σήμερον κατʼ ὄναρ διʼ αὐτόν.
verses.translit: Kathimenoy de autou epi tou vimatos apesteilen pros auton e gyne autou legoysa* Miden soi kai to dikaio ekeino, polla gar epathon simeron kat' onar di' auton.
verses.translation: When he was set down on the judgment seat, his wife sent unto him, saying, Have thou nothing to do with that just man: for I have suffered many things this day in a dream because of him.

verses.original: Οἱ δὲ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι ἔπεισαν τοὺς ὄχλους ἵνα αἰτήσωνται τὸν Βαραββᾶν τὸν δὲ Ἰησοῦν ἀπολέσωσιν.
verses.translit: Oi de arhiereis kai oi presvyteroi epeisan tous ohloys ina aitisontai ton Varavvan ton de Iisoun apolesosin.
verses.translation: But the chief priests and elders persuaded the multitude that they should ask Barabbas, and destroy Jesus.

verses.original: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ ἡγεμὼν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τίνα θέλετε ἀπὸ τῶν δύο ἀπολύσω ὑμῖν; οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· ⸀Τὸν Βαραββᾶν.
verses.translit: apokritheis de o egemon eipen autois* Tina thelete apo ton dyo apolyso umin; oi de eipan* Ton Varavvan.
verses.translation: The governor answered and said unto them, Whether of the twain will ye that I release unto you? They said, Barabbas.

verses.original: λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Τί οὖν ποιήσω Ἰησοῦν τὸν λεγόμενον χριστόν; ⸀λέγουσιν πάντες· Σταυρωθήτω.
verses.translit: legei autois o Pilatos* Ti oun poiiso Iisoun ton legomenon hriston; legoysin pantes* Stayrothito.
verses.translation: Pilate saith unto them, What shall I do then with Jesus which is called Christ? They all say unto him, Let him be crucified.

verses.original: ὁ ⸀δὲ ἔφη· Τί γὰρ κακὸν ἐποίησεν; οἱ δὲ περισσῶς ἔκραζον λέγοντες· Σταυρωθήτω.
verses.translit: o de efi* Ti gar kakon epoiisen; oi de perissos ekrazon legontes* Stayrothito.
verses.translation: And the governor said, Why, what evil hath he done? But they cried out the more, saying, Let him be crucified.

verses.original: Ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Πιλᾶτος ὅτι οὐδὲν ὠφελεῖ ἀλλὰ μᾶλλον θόρυβος γίνεται λαβὼν ὕδωρ ἀπενίψατο τὰς χεῖρας ⸀ἀπέναντι τοῦ ὄχλου λέγων· Ἀθῷός εἰμι ἀπὸ τοῦ ⸀αἵματος τούτου· ὑμεῖς ὄψεσθε.
verses.translit: Idon de o Pilatos oti ouden ofelei alla mallon thoryvos ginetai lavon udor apenipsato tas heiras apenanti tou ohloy legon* Athoos eimi apo tou aimatos toytoy* umeis opsesthe.
verses.translation: When Pilate saw that he could prevail nothing, but that rather a tumult was made, he took water, and washed his hands before the multitude, saying, I am innocent of the blood of this just person: see ye to it .

verses.original: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς πᾶς ὁ λαὸς εἶπεν· Τὸ αἷμα αὐτοῦ ἐφʼ ἡμᾶς καὶ ἐπὶ τὰ τέκνα ἡμῶν.
verses.translit: kai apokritheis pas o laos eipen* To aima autou ef' emas kai epi ta tekna emon.
verses.translation: Then answered all the people, and said, His blood be on us, and on our children.

verses.original: τότε ἀπέλυσεν αὐτοῖς τὸν Βαραββᾶν, τὸν δὲ Ἰησοῦν φραγελλώσας παρέδωκεν ἵνα σταυρωθῇ.
verses.translit: tote apelysen autois ton Varavvan, ton de Iisoun fragellosas paredoken ina stayrothe.
verses.translation: Then released he Barabbas unto them: and when he had scourged Jesus, he delivered him to be crucified.

verses.original: Τότε οἱ στρατιῶται τοῦ ἡγεμόνος παραλαβόντες τὸν Ἰησοῦν εἰς τὸ πραιτώριον συνήγαγον ἐπʼ αὐτὸν ὅλην τὴν σπεῖραν.
verses.translit: Tote oi stratiotai tou egemonos paralavontes ton Iisoun eis to praitorion synigagon ep' auton olin ten speiran.
verses.translation: Then the soldiers of the governor took Jesus into the common hall, and gathered unto him the whole band of soldiers .

verses.original: καὶ ἐκδύσαντες αὐτὸν ⸂χλαμύδα κοκκίνην περιέθηκαν αὐτῷ⸃,
verses.translit: kai ekdysantes auton hlamyda kokkinin periethikan auto,
verses.translation: And they stripped him, and put on him a scarlet robe.

verses.original: καὶ πλέξαντες στέφανον ἐξ ἀκανθῶν ἐπέθηκαν ἐπὶ ⸂τῆς κεφαλῆς⸃ αὐτοῦ καὶ κάλαμον ⸂ἐν τῇ δεξιᾷ⸃ αὐτοῦ, καὶ γονυπετήσαντες ἔμπροσθεν αὐτοῦ ⸀ἐνέπαιξαν αὐτῷ λέγοντες· Χαῖρε, ⸀βασιλεῦ τῶν Ἰουδαίων,
verses.translit: kai plexantes stefanon ex akanthon epethikan epi tes kefales autou kai kalamon en te dexia autou, kai gonypetisantes emprosthen autou enepaixan auto legontes* Haire, vasileu ton Ioydaion,
verses.translation: And when they had platted a crown of thorns, they put it upon his head, and a reed in his right hand: and they bowed the knee before him, and mocked him, saying, Hail, King of the Jews!

verses.original: καὶ ἐμπτύσαντες εἰς αὐτὸν ἔλαβον τὸν κάλαμον καὶ ἔτυπτον εἰς τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai emptysantes eis auton elavon ton kalamon kai etypton eis ten kefalen autou.
verses.translation: And they spit upon him, and took the reed, and smote him on the head.

verses.original: καὶ ὅτε ἐνέπαιξαν αὐτῷ, ἐξέδυσαν αὐτὸν τὴν χλαμύδα καὶ ἐνέδυσαν αὐτὸν τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀπήγαγον αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ σταυρῶσαι.
verses.translit: kai ote enepaixan auto, exedysan auton ten hlamyda kai enedysan auton ta imatia autou kai apigagon auton eis to stayrosai.
verses.translation: And after that they had mocked him, they took the robe off from him, and put his own raiment on him, and led him away to crucify him .

verses.original: Ἐξερχόμενοι δὲ εὗρον ἄνθρωπον Κυρηναῖον ὀνόματι Σίμωνα· τοῦτον ἠγγάρευσαν ἵνα ἄρῃ τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: Exerhomenoi de euron anthropon Kyrinaion onomati Simona* touton eggareysan ina are ton stayron autou.
verses.translation: And as they came out, they found a man of Cyrene, Simon by name: him they compelled to bear his cross.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐλθόντες εἰς τόπον λεγόμενον Γολγοθᾶ, ὅ ἐστιν ⸂Κρανίου Τόπος λεγόμενος⸃,
verses.translit: Kai elthontes eis topon legomenon Golgotha, o estin Kranioy Topos legomenos,
verses.translation: And when they were come unto a place called Golgotha, that is to say, a place of a skull,

verses.original: ἔδωκαν αὐτῷ πιεῖν ⸀οἶνον μετὰ χολῆς μεμιγμένον· καὶ γευσάμενος οὐκ ⸀ἠθέλησεν πιεῖν.
verses.translit: edokan auto piein oinon meta holes memigmenon* kai geysamenos ouk ethelisen piein.
verses.translation: They gave him vinegar to drink mingled with gall: and when he had tasted thereof , he would not drink.

verses.original: σταυρώσαντες δὲ αὐτὸν διεμερίσαντο τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ βάλλοντες κλῆρον,
verses.translit: stayrosantes de auton diemerisanto ta imatia autou vallontes kleron,
verses.translation: And they crucified him, and parted his garments, casting lots: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, They parted my garments among them, and upon my vesture did they cast lots.

verses.original: καὶ καθήμενοι ἐτήρουν αὐτὸν ἐκεῖ.
verses.translit: kai kathimenoi etiroyn auton ekei.
verses.translation: And sitting down they watched him there;

verses.original: καὶ ἐπέθηκαν ἐπάνω τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτοῦ τὴν αἰτίαν αὐτοῦ γεγραμμένην· Οὗτός ἐστιν Ἰησοῦς ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων.
verses.translit: kai epethikan epano tes kefales autou ten aitian autou gegrammenin* Outos estin Iisous o vasileus ton Ioydaion.
verses.translation: And set up over his head his accusation written, THIS IS JESUS THE KING OF THE JEWS.

verses.original: Τότε σταυροῦνται σὺν αὐτῷ δύο λῃσταί, εἷς ἐκ δεξιῶν καὶ εἷς ἐξ εὐωνύμων.
verses.translit: Tote stayrountai sun auto dyo lestai, eis ek dexion kai eis ex euonymon.
verses.translation: Then were there two thieves crucified with him, one on the right hand, and another on the left.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ παραπορευόμενοι ἐβλασφήμουν αὐτὸν κινοῦντες τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτῶν
verses.translit: oi de paraporeyomenoi evlasfimoyn auton kinountes tas kefalas auton
verses.translation: And they that passed by reviled him, wagging their heads,

verses.original: καὶ λέγοντες· Ὁ καταλύων τὸν ναὸν καὶ ἐν τρισὶν ἡμέραις οἰκοδομῶν, σῶσον σεαυτόν· εἰ υἱὸς εἶ τοῦ θεοῦ, ⸀κατάβηθι ἀπὸ τοῦ σταυροῦ.
verses.translit: kai legontes* O katalyon ton naon kai en trisin emerais oikodomon, soson seayton* ei yios ei tou theou, katavithi apo tou stayrou.
verses.translation: And saying, Thou that destroyest the temple, and buildest it in three days, save thyself. If thou be the Son of God, come down from the cross.

verses.original: ὁμοίως ⸀καὶ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς ἐμπαίζοντες μετὰ τῶν γραμματέων καὶ ⸀πρεσβυτέρων ἔλεγον·
verses.translit: omoios kai oi arhiereis empaizontes meta ton grammateon kai presvyteron elegon*
verses.translation: Likewise also the chief priests mocking him , with the scribes and elders, said,

verses.original: Ἄλλους ἔσωσεν, ἑαυτὸν οὐ δύναται σῶσαι· ⸀βασιλεὺς Ἰσραήλ ἐστιν, καταβάτω νῦν ἀπὸ τοῦ σταυροῦ καὶ πιστεύσομεν ἐπʼ ⸀αὐτόν.
verses.translit: Alloys esosen, eayton ou dynatai sosai* vasileus Israil estin, katavato nun apo tou stayrou kai pisteysomen ep' auton.
verses.translation: He saved others; himself he cannot save. If he be the King of Israel, let him now come down from the cross, and we will believe him.

verses.original: πέποιθεν ἐπὶ τὸν θεόν, ῥυσάσθω ⸀νῦν εἰ θέλει αὐτόν· εἶπεν γὰρ ὅτι Θεοῦ εἰμι υἱός.
verses.translit: pepoithen epi ton theon, Rysastho nun ei thelei auton* eipen gar oti Theou eimi yios.
verses.translation: He trusted in God; let him deliver him now, if he will have him: for he said, I am the Son of God.

verses.original: τὸ δʼ αὐτὸ καὶ οἱ λῃσταὶ οἱ συσταυρωθέντες ⸀σὺν αὐτῷ ὠνείδιζον αὐτόν.
verses.translit: to d' auto kai oi lestai oi systayrothentes sun auto oneidizon auton.
verses.translation: The thieves also, which were crucified with him, cast the same in his teeth.

verses.original: Ἀπὸ δὲ ἕκτης ὥρας σκότος ἐγένετο ἐπὶ πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν ἕως ὥρας ἐνάτης.
verses.translit: Apo de ektis oras skotos egeneto epi pasan ten gen eos oras enatis.
verses.translation: Now from the sixth hour there was darkness over all the land unto the ninth hour.

verses.original: περὶ δὲ τὴν ἐνάτην ὥραν ⸀ἀνεβόησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς φωνῇ μεγάλῃ λέγων· ⸂Ἠλὶ ἠλὶ⸃ λεμὰ σαβαχθάνι; τοῦτʼ ἔστιν· Θεέ μου θεέ μου, ἱνατί με ἐγκατέλιπες;
verses.translit: peri de ten enatin oran anevoisen o Iisous fone megale legon* Eli eli lema savahthani; tout' estin* Thee moy thee moy, inati me egkatelipes;
verses.translation: And about the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? that is to say, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?

verses.original: τινὲς δὲ τῶν ἐκεῖ ⸀ἑστηκότων ἀκούσαντες ἔλεγον ὅτι Ἠλίαν φωνεῖ οὗτος.
verses.translit: tines de ton ekei estikoton akoysantes elegon oti Elian fonei outos.
verses.translation: Some of them that stood there, when they heard that , said, This man calleth for Elias.

verses.original: καὶ εὐθέως δραμὼν εἷς ἐξ αὐτῶν καὶ λαβὼν σπόγγον πλήσας τε ὄξους καὶ περιθεὶς καλάμῳ ἐπότιζεν αὐτόν.
verses.translit: kai eutheos dramon eis ex auton kai lavon spoggon plisas te oxoys kai peritheis kalamo epotizen auton.
verses.translation: And straightway one of them ran, and took a spunge, and filled it with vinegar, and put it on a reed, and gave him to drink.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ λοιποὶ ⸀ἔλεγον· Ἄφες ἴδωμεν εἰ ἔρχεται Ἠλίας σώσων ⸀αὐτόν.
verses.translit: oi de loipoi elegon* Afes idomen ei erhetai Elias soson auton.
verses.translation: The rest said, Let be, let us see whether Elias will come to save him.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς πάλιν κράξας φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ἀφῆκεν τὸ πνεῦμα.
verses.translit: o de Iisous palin kraxas fone megale afeken to pneuma.
verses.translation: Jesus, when he had cried again with a loud voice, yielded up the ghost.

verses.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ τὸ καταπέτασμα τοῦ ναοῦ ἐσχίσθη ⸂ἀπʼ ἄνωθεν ἕως κάτω εἰς δύο⸃, καὶ ἡ γῆ ἐσείσθη, καὶ αἱ πέτραι ἐσχίσθησαν,
verses.translit: kai idou to katapetasma tou naou eshisthi ap' anothen eos kato eis dyo, kai e ge eseisthi, kai ai petrai eshisthisan,
verses.translation: And, behold, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom; and the earth did quake, and the rocks rent;

verses.original: καὶ τὰ μνημεῖα ἀνεῴχθησαν καὶ πολλὰ σώματα τῶν κεκοιμημένων ἁγίων ⸀ἠγέρθησαν,
verses.translit: kai ta mnimeia aneohthisan kai polla somata ton kekoimimenon agion egerthisan,
verses.translation: And the graves were opened; and many bodies of the saints which slept arose,

verses.original: καὶ ἐξελθόντες ἐκ τῶν μνημείων μετὰ τὴν ἔγερσιν αὐτοῦ εἰσῆλθον εἰς τὴν ἁγίαν πόλιν καὶ ἐνεφανίσθησαν πολλοῖς.
verses.translit: kai exelthontes ek ton mnimeion meta ten egersin autou eiselthon eis ten agian polin kai enefanisthisan pollois.
verses.translation: And came out of the graves after his resurrection, and went into the holy city, and appeared unto many.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ ἑκατόνταρχος καὶ οἱ μετʼ αὐτοῦ τηροῦντες τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἰδόντες τὸν σεισμὸν καὶ τὰ ⸀γενόμενα ἐφοβήθησαν σφόδρα λέγοντες· Ἀληθῶς ⸂θεοῦ υἱὸς⸃ ἦν οὗτος.
verses.translit: O de ekatontarhos kai oi met' autou tirountes ton Iisoun idontes ton seismon kai ta genomena efovithisan sfodra legontes* Alithos theou yios en outos.
verses.translation: Now when the centurion, and they that were with him, watching Jesus, saw the earthquake, and those things that were done, they feared greatly, saying, Truly this was the Son of God.

verses.original: Ἦσαν δὲ ἐκεῖ γυναῖκες πολλαὶ ἀπὸ μακρόθεν θεωροῦσαι, αἵτινες ἠκολούθησαν τῷ Ἰησοῦ ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας διακονοῦσαι αὐτῷ·
verses.translit: Esan de ekei gynaikes pollai apo makrothen theorousai, aitines ekoloythisan to Iisou apo tes Galilaias diakonousai auto*
verses.translation: And many women were there beholding afar off, which followed Jesus from Galilee, ministering unto him:

verses.original: ἐν αἷς ἦν Μαρία ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ καὶ Μαρία ἡ τοῦ Ἰακώβου καὶ ⸀Ἰωσὴφ μήτηρ καὶ ἡ μήτηρ τῶν υἱῶν Ζεβεδαίου.
verses.translit: en ais en Maria e Magdaline kai Maria e tou Iakovoy kai Iosef mitir kai e mitir ton yion Zevedaioy.
verses.translation: Among which was Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James and Joses, and the mother of Zebedee’s children.

verses.original: Ὀψίας δὲ γενομένης ἦλθεν ἄνθρωπος πλούσιος ἀπὸ Ἁριμαθαίας, τοὔνομα Ἰωσήφ, ὃς καὶ αὐτὸς ⸀ἐμαθητεύθη τῷ Ἰησοῦ·
verses.translit: Opsias de genomenis elthen anthropos ploysios apo Arimathaias, tounoma Iosif, os kai autos emathiteythi to Iisou*
verses.translation: When the even was come, there came a rich man of Arimathæa, named Joseph, who also himself was Jesus’ disciple:

verses.original: οὗτος προσελθὼν τῷ Πιλάτῳ ᾐτήσατο τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ. τότε ὁ Πιλᾶτος ἐκέλευσεν ⸀ἀποδοθῆναι.
verses.translit: outos proselthon to Pilato etisato to soma tou Iisou. tote o Pilatos ekeleysen apodothenai.
verses.translation: He went to Pilate, and begged the body of Jesus. Then Pilate commanded the body to be delivered.

verses.original: καὶ λαβὼν τὸ σῶμα ὁ Ἰωσὴφ ἐνετύλιξεν ⸀αὐτὸ σινδόνι καθαρᾷ,
verses.translit: kai lavon to soma o Iosef enetylixen auto sindoni kathara,
verses.translation: And when Joseph had taken the body, he wrapped it in a clean linen cloth,

verses.original: καὶ ἔθηκεν αὐτὸ ἐν τῷ καινῷ αὐτοῦ μνημείῳ ὃ ἐλατόμησεν ἐν τῇ πέτρᾳ, καὶ προσκυλίσας λίθον μέγαν τῇ θύρᾳ τοῦ μνημείου ἀπῆλθεν.
verses.translit: kai ethiken auto en to kaino autou mnimeio o elatomisen en te petra, kai proskylisas lithon megan te thyra tou mnimeioy apelthen.
verses.translation: And laid it in his own new tomb, which he had hewn out in the rock: and he rolled a great stone to the door of the sepulchre, and departed.

verses.original: ἦν δὲ ἐκεῖ ⸀Μαριὰμ ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ καὶ ἡ ἄλλη Μαρία καθήμεναι ἀπέναντι τοῦ τάφου.
verses.translit: en de ekei Mariam e Magdaline kai e alli Maria kathimenai apenanti tou tafoy.
verses.translation: And there was Mary Magdalene, and the other Mary, sitting over against the sepulchre.

verses.original: Τῇ δὲ ἐπαύριον, ἥτις ἐστὶν μετὰ τὴν παρασκευήν, συνήχθησαν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι πρὸς Πιλᾶτον
verses.translit: Te de epayrion, etis estin meta ten paraskeyin, synihthisan oi arhiereis kai oi Farisaioi pros Pilaton
verses.translation: Now the next day, that followed the day of the preparation, the chief priests and Pharisees came together unto Pilate,

verses.original: λέγοντες· Κύριε, ἐμνήσθημεν ὅτι ἐκεῖνος ὁ πλάνος εἶπεν ἔτι ζῶν· Μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας ἐγείρομαι·
verses.translit: legontes* Kyrie, emnisthimen oti ekeinos o planos eipen eti zon* Meta treis emeras egeiromai*
verses.translation: Saying, Sir, we remember that that deceiver said, while he was yet alive, After three days I will rise again.

verses.original: κέλευσον οὖν ἀσφαλισθῆναι τὸν τάφον ἕως τῆς τρίτης ἡμέρας, μήποτε ἐλθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ ⸀αὐτοῦ κλέψωσιν αὐτὸν καὶ εἴπωσιν τῷ λαῷ· Ἠγέρθη ἀπὸ τῶν νεκρῶν, καὶ ἔσται ἡ ἐσχάτη πλάνη χείρων τῆς πρώτης.
verses.translit: keleyson oun asfalisthenai ton tafon eos tes tritis emeras, mipote elthontes oi mathitai autou klepsosin auton kai eiposin to lao* Egerthi apo ton nekron, kai estai e eshati plani heiron tes protis.
verses.translation: Command therefore that the sepulchre be made sure until the third day, lest his disciples come by night, and steal him away, and say unto the people, He is risen from the dead: so the last error shall be worse than the first.

verses.original: ⸀ἔφη αὐτοῖς ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Ἔχετε κουστωδίαν· ὑπάγετε ἀσφαλίσασθε ὡς οἴδατε.
verses.translit: efi autois o Pilatos* Ehete koystodian* upagete asfalisasthe os oidate.
verses.translation: Pilate said unto them, Ye have a watch: go your way, make it as sure as ye can.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ πορευθέντες ἠσφαλίσαντο τὸν τάφον σφραγίσαντες τὸν λίθον μετὰ τῆς κουστωδίας.
verses.translit: oi de poreythentes esfalisanto ton tafon sfragisantes ton lithon meta tes koystodias.
verses.translation: So they went, and made the sepulchre sure, sealing the stone, and setting a watch.

verses.original: Ὀψὲ δὲ σαββάτων, τῇ ἐπιφωσκούσῃ εἰς μίαν σαββάτων, ἦλθεν ⸀Μαριὰμ ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ καὶ ἡ ἄλλη Μαρία θεωρῆσαι τὸν τάφον.
verses.translit: Opse de savvaton, te epifoskoyse eis mian savvaton, elthen Mariam e Magdaline kai e alli Maria theoresai ton tafon.
verses.translation: In the end of the sabbath, as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week, came Mary Magdalene and the other Mary to see the sepulchre.

verses.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ σεισμὸς ἐγένετο μέγας· ἄγγελος γὰρ κυρίου καταβὰς ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ⸀καὶ προσελθὼν ἀπεκύλισε τὸν ⸀λίθον καὶ ἐκάθητο ἐπάνω αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai idou seismos egeneto megas* aggelos gar kyrioy katavas ex ouranou kai proselthon apekylise ton lithon kai ekathito epano autou.
verses.translation: And, behold, there was a great earthquake: for the angel of the Lord descended from heaven, and came and rolled back the stone from the door, and sat upon it.

verses.original: ἦν δὲ ἡ εἰδέα αὐτοῦ ⸀ὡς ἀστραπὴ καὶ τὸ ἔνδυμα αὐτοῦ λευκὸν ὡς χιών.
verses.translit: en de e eidea autou os astrape kai to endyma autou leykon os hion.
verses.translation: His countenance was like lightning, and his raiment white as snow:

verses.original: ἀπὸ δὲ τοῦ φόβου αὐτοῦ ἐσείσθησαν οἱ τηροῦντες καὶ ἐγενήθησαν ⸀ὡς νεκροί.
verses.translit: apo de tou fovoy autou eseisthisan oi tirountes kai egenithisan os nekroi.
verses.translation: And for fear of him the keepers did shake, and became as dead men .

verses.original: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ ἄγγελος εἶπεν ταῖς γυναιξίν· Μὴ φοβεῖσθε ὑμεῖς, οἶδα γὰρ ὅτι Ἰησοῦν τὸν ἐσταυρωμένον ζητεῖτε·
verses.translit: apokritheis de o aggelos eipen tais gynaixin* Me foveisthe umeis, oida gar oti Iisoun ton estayromenon ziteite*
verses.translation: And the angel answered and said unto the women, Fear not ye: for I know that ye seek Jesus, which was crucified.

verses.original: οὐκ ἔστιν ὧδε, ἠγέρθη γὰρ καθὼς εἶπεν· δεῦτε ἴδετε τὸν τόπον ὅπου ⸀ἔκειτο·
verses.translit: ouk estin ode, egerthi gar kathos eipen* deute idete ton topon opoy ekeito*
verses.translation: He is not here: for he is risen, as he said. Come, see the place where the Lord lay.

verses.original: καὶ ταχὺ πορευθεῖσαι εἴπατε τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ ὅτι Ἠγέρθη ἀπὸ τῶν νεκρῶν, καὶ ἰδοὺ προάγει ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν, ἐκεῖ αὐτὸν ὄψεσθε· ἰδοὺ εἶπον ὑμῖν.
verses.translit: kai tahu poreytheisai eipate tois mathitais autou oti Egerthi apo ton nekron, kai idou proagei umas eis ten Galilaian, ekei auton opsesthe* idou eipon umin.
verses.translation: And go quickly, and tell his disciples that he is risen from the dead; and, behold, he goeth before you into Galilee; there shall ye see him: lo, I have told you.

verses.original: καὶ ⸀ἀπελθοῦσαι ταχὺ ἀπὸ τοῦ μνημείου μετὰ φόβου καὶ χαρᾶς μεγάλης ἔδραμον ἀπαγγεῖλαι τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai apelthousai tahu apo tou mnimeioy meta fovoy kai haras megalis edramon apaggeilai tois mathitais autou.
verses.translation: And they departed quickly from the sepulchre with fear and great joy; and did run to bring his disciples word.

verses.original: ⸀καὶ ⸀ἰδοὺ Ἰησοῦς ⸀ὑπήντησεν αὐταῖς λέγων· Χαίρετε· αἱ δὲ προσελθοῦσαι ἐκράτησαν αὐτοῦ τοὺς πόδας καὶ προσεκύνησαν αὐτῷ.
verses.translit: kai idou Iisous upintisen autais legon* Hairete* ai de proselthousai ekratisan autou tous podas kai prosekynisan auto.
verses.translation: And as they went to tell his disciples, behold, Jesus met them, saying, All hail. And they came and held him by the feet, and worshipped him.

verses.original: τότε λέγει αὐταῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Μὴ φοβεῖσθε· ὑπάγετε ἀπαγγείλατε τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς μου ἵνα ἀπέλθωσιν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν, κἀκεῖ με ὄψονται.
verses.translit: tote legei autais o Iisous* Me foveisthe* upagete apaggeilate tois adelfois moy ina apelthosin eis ten Galilaian, kakei me opsontai.
verses.translation: Then said Jesus unto them, Be not afraid: go tell my brethren that they go into Galilee, and there shall they see me.

verses.original: Πορευομένων δὲ αὐτῶν ἰδού τινες τῆς κουστωδίας ἐλθόντες εἰς τὴν πόλιν ἀπήγγειλαν τοῖς ἀρχιερεῦσιν ἅπαντα τὰ γενόμενα.
verses.translit: Poreyomenon de auton idoy tines tes koystodias elthontes eis ten polin apiggeilan tois arhiereusin apanta ta genomena.
verses.translation: Now when they were going, behold, some of the watch came into the city, and shewed unto the chief priests all the things that were done.

verses.original: καὶ συναχθέντες μετὰ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων συμβούλιόν τε λαβόντες ἀργύρια ἱκανὰ ἔδωκαν τοῖς στρατιώταις
verses.translit: kai synahthentes meta ton presvyteron symvoylion te lavontes argyria ikana edokan tois stratiotais
verses.translation: And when they were assembled with the elders, and had taken counsel, they gave large money unto the soldiers,

verses.original: λέγοντες· Εἴπατε ὅτι Οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ νυκτὸς ἐλθόντες ἔκλεψαν αὐτὸν ἡμῶν κοιμωμένων·
verses.translit: legontes* Eipate oti Oi mathitai autou nyktos elthontes eklepsan auton emon koimomenon*
verses.translation: Saying, Say ye, His disciples came by night, and stole him away while we slept.

verses.original: καὶ ἐὰν ἀκουσθῇ τοῦτο ⸀ἐπὶ τοῦ ἡγεμόνος, ἡμεῖς πείσομεν ⸀αὐτὸν καὶ ὑμᾶς ἀμερίμνους ποιήσομεν.
verses.translit: kai ean akoysthe touto epi tou egemonos, emeis peisomen auton kai umas amerimnoys poiisomen.
verses.translation: And if this come to the governor’s ears, we will persuade him, and secure you.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ λαβόντες ⸀τὰ ἀργύρια ἐποίησαν ὡς ἐδιδάχθησαν. Καὶ διεφημίσθη ὁ λόγος οὗτος παρὰ Ἰουδαίοις μέχρι τῆς σήμερον ⸀ἡμέρας.
verses.translit: oi de lavontes ta argyria epoiisan os edidahthisan. Kai diefimisthi o logos outos para Ioydaiois mehri tes simeron emeras.
verses.translation: So they took the money, and did as they were taught: and this saying is commonly reported among the Jews until this day.

verses.original: Οἱ δὲ ἕνδεκα μαθηταὶ ἐπορεύθησαν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν εἰς τὸ ὄρος οὗ ἐτάξατο αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς,
verses.translit: Oi de endeka mathitai eporeythisan eis ten Galilaian eis to oros ou etaxato autois o Iisous,
verses.translation: Then the eleven disciples went away into Galilee, into a mountain where Jesus had appointed them.

verses.original: καὶ ἰδόντες αὐτὸν ⸀προσεκύνησαν, οἱ δὲ ἐδίστασαν.
verses.translit: kai idontes auton prosekynisan, oi de edistasan.
verses.translation: And when they saw him, they worshipped him: but some doubted.

verses.original: καὶ προσελθὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐλάλησεν αὐτοῖς λέγων· Ἐδόθη μοι πᾶσα ἐξουσία ἐν οὐρανῷ καὶ ἐπὶ ⸀τῆς γῆς·
verses.translit: kai proselthon o Iisous elalisen autois legon* Edothi moi pasa exoysia en ourano kai epi tes ges*
verses.translation: And Jesus came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.

verses.original: πορευθέντες ⸀οὖν μαθητεύσατε πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, ⸀βαπτίζοντες αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ καὶ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος,
verses.translit: poreythentes oun mathiteysate panta ta ethni, vaptizontes autous eis to onoma tou patros kai tou yiou kai tou agioy pneymatos,
verses.translation: Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost:

verses.original: διδάσκοντες αὐτοὺς τηρεῖν πάντα ὅσα ἐνετειλάμην ὑμῖν· καὶ ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ μεθʼ ὑμῶν εἰμι πάσας τὰς ἡμέρας ἕως τῆς συντελείας τοῦ ⸀αἰῶνος.
verses.translit: didaskontes autous tirein panta osa eneteilamin umin* kai idou ego meth' umon eimi pasas tas emeras eos tes synteleias tou aionos.
verses.translation: Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world. Amen.

verses.original: Ἀρχὴ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου Ἰησοῦ ⸀χριστοῦ.
verses.translit: Arhe tou euaggelioy Iisou hristou.
verses.translation: The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God;

verses.original: ⸀Καθὼς γέγραπται ἐν ⸂τῷ Ἠσαΐᾳ τῷ προφήτῃ⸃· ⸀Ἰδοὺ ἀποστέλλω τὸν ἄγγελόν μου πρὸ προσώπου σου, ὃς κατασκευάσει τὴν ὁδόν ⸀σου·
verses.translit: Kathos gegraptai en to EsaIa to profite* Idou apostello ton aggelon moy pro prosopoy soy, os kataskeyasei ten odon soy*
verses.translation: As it is written in the prophets, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, which shall prepare thy way before thee.

verses.original: φωνὴ βοῶντος ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ· Ἑτοιμάσατε τὴν ὁδὸν κυρίου, εὐθείας ποιεῖτε τὰς τρίβους αὐτοῦ,
verses.translit: fone voontos en te erimo* Etoimasate ten odon kyrioy, eutheias poieite tas trivoys autou,
verses.translation: The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.

verses.original: ἐγένετο Ἰωάννης ⸀ὁ βαπτίζων ἐν τῇ ⸀ἐρήμῳ κηρύσσων βάπτισμα μετανοίας εἰς ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν.
verses.translit: egeneto Ioannis o vaptizon en te erimo kirysson vaptisma metanoias eis afesin amartion.
verses.translation: John did baptize in the wilderness, and preach the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins.

verses.original: καὶ ἐξεπορεύετο πρὸς αὐτὸν πᾶσα ἡ Ἰουδαία χώρα καὶ οἱ Ἱεροσολυμῖται ⸂πάντες, καὶ ἐβαπτίζοντο⸃ ⸂ὑπʼ αὐτοῦ ἐν τῷ Ἰορδάνῃ ποταμῷ⸃ ἐξομολογούμενοι τὰς ἁμαρτίας αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: kai exeporeyeto pros auton pasa e Ioydaia hora kai oi Ierosolymitai pantes, kai evaptizonto up' autou en to Iordane potamo exomologoymenoi tas amartias auton.
verses.translation: And there went out unto him all the land of Judæa, and they of Jerusalem, and were all baptized of him in the river of Jordan, confessing their sins.

verses.original: ⸂καὶ ἦν⸃ ὁ Ἰωάννης ἐνδεδυμένος τρίχας καμήλου καὶ ζώνην δερματίνην περὶ τὴν ὀσφὺν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔσθων ἀκρίδας καὶ μέλι ἄγριον.
verses.translit: kai en o Ioannis endedymenos trihas kamiloy kai zonin dermatinin peri ten osfun autou, kai esthon akridas kai meli agrion.
verses.translation: And John was clothed with camel’s hair, and with a girdle of a skin about his loins; and he did eat locusts and wild honey;

verses.original: καὶ ἐκήρυσσεν λέγων· Ἔρχεται ὁ ἰσχυρότερός μου ὀπίσω μου, οὗ οὐκ εἰμὶ ἱκανὸς κύψας λῦσαι τὸν ἱμάντα τῶν ὑποδημάτων αὐτοῦ·
verses.translit: kai ekiryssen legon* Erhetai o ishyroteros moy opiso moy, ou ouk eimi ikanos kypsas lusai ton imanta ton upodimaton autou*
verses.translation: And preached, saying, There cometh one mightier than I after me, the latchet of whose shoes I am not worthy to stoop down and unloose.

verses.original: ⸀ἐγὼ ἐβάπτισα ⸀ὑμᾶς ὕδατι, αὐτὸς δὲ βαπτίσει ὑμᾶς ⸀ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ.
verses.translit: ego evaptisa umas udati, autos de vaptisei umas en pneymati agio.
verses.translation: I indeed have baptized you with water: but he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις ἦλθεν Ἰησοῦς ἀπὸ Ναζαρὲτ τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ ἐβαπτίσθη ⸂εἰς τὸν Ἰορδάνην ὑπὸ Ἰωάννου⸃.
verses.translit: Kai egeneto en ekeinais tais emerais elthen Iisous apo Nazaret tes Galilaias kai evaptisthi eis ton Iordanin upo Ioannoy.
verses.translation: And it came to pass in those days, that Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee, and was baptized of John in Jordan.

verses.original: καὶ ⸀εὐθὺς ἀναβαίνων ⸀ἐκ τοῦ ὕδατος εἶδεν σχιζομένους τοὺς οὐρανοὺς καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα ⸀ὡς περιστερὰν καταβαῖνον ⸀εἰς αὐτόν·
verses.translit: kai euthus anavainon ek tou udatos eiden shizomenoys tous ouranous kai to pneuma os peristeran katavainon eis auton*
verses.translation: And straightway coming up out of the water, he saw the heavens opened, and the Spirit like a dove descending upon him:

verses.original: καὶ φωνὴ ἐγένετο ἐκ τῶν οὐρανῶν· Σὺ εἶ ὁ υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός, ἐν ⸀σοὶ εὐδόκησα.
verses.translit: kai fone egeneto ek ton ouranon* Su ei o yios moy o agapitos, en soi eudokisa.
verses.translation: And there came a voice from heaven, saying , Thou art my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.

verses.original: Καὶ εὐθὺς τὸ πνεῦμα αὐτὸν ἐκβάλλει εἰς τὴν ἔρημον.
verses.translit: Kai euthus to pneuma auton ekvallei eis ten erimon.
verses.translation: And immediately the Spirit driveth him into the wilderness.

verses.original: καὶ ⸀ἦν ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ ⸂τεσσεράκοντα ἡμέρας⸃ πειραζόμενος ὑπὸ τοῦ Σατανᾶ, καὶ ἦν μετὰ τῶν θηρίων, καὶ οἱ ἄγγελοι διηκόνουν αὐτῷ.
verses.translit: kai en en te erimo tesserakonta emeras peirazomenos upo tou Satana, kai en meta ton thirion, kai oi aggeloi diikonoyn auto.
verses.translation: And he was there in the wilderness forty days, tempted of Satan; and was with the wild beasts; and the angels ministered unto him.

verses.original: ⸂Καὶ μετὰ⸃ τὸ παραδοθῆναι τὸν Ἰωάννην ἦλθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν κηρύσσων τὸ ⸀εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ θεοῦ
verses.translit: Kai meta to paradothenai ton Ioannin elthen o Iisous eis ten Galilaian kirysson to euaggelion tou theou
verses.translation: Now after that John was put in prison, Jesus came into Galilee, preaching the gospel of the kingdom of God,

verses.original: καὶ λέγων ὅτι Πεπλήρωται ὁ καιρὸς καὶ ἤγγικεν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ· μετανοεῖτε καὶ πιστεύετε ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ.
verses.translit: kai legon oti Peplirotai o kairos kai eggiken e vasileia tou theou* metanoeite kai pisteyete en to euaggelio.
verses.translation: And saying, The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand: repent ye, and believe the gospel.

verses.original: ⸂Καὶ παράγων⸃ παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν τῆς Γαλιλαίας εἶδεν Σίμωνα καὶ Ἀνδρέαν τὸν ⸀ἀδελφὸν Σίμωνος ⸀ἀμφιβάλλοντας ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ, ἦσαν γὰρ ἁλιεῖς·
verses.translit: Kai paragon para ten thalassan tes Galilaias eiden Simona kai Andrean ton adelfon Simonos amfivallontas en te thalasse, esan gar alieis*
verses.translation: Now as he walked by the sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and Andrew his brother casting a net into the sea: for they were fishers.

verses.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Δεῦτε ὀπίσω μου, καὶ ποιήσω ὑμᾶς γενέσθαι ἁλιεῖς ἀνθρώπων.
verses.translit: kai eipen autois o Iisous* Deute opiso moy, kai poiiso umas genesthai alieis anthropon.
verses.translation: And Jesus said unto them, Come ye after me, and I will make you to become fishers of men.

verses.original: καὶ ⸀εὐθὺς ἀφέντες τὰ ⸀δίκτυα ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ.
verses.translit: kai euthus afentes ta diktya ekoloythisan auto.
verses.translation: And straightway they forsook their nets, and followed him.

verses.original: καὶ ⸀προβὰς ὀλίγον εἶδεν Ἰάκωβον τὸν τοῦ Ζεβεδαίου καὶ Ἰωάννην τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ, καὶ αὐτοὺς ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ καταρτίζοντας τὰ δίκτυα,
verses.translit: kai provas oligon eiden Iakovon ton tou Zevedaioy kai Ioannin ton adelfon autou, kai autous en to ploio katartizontas ta diktya,
verses.translation: And when he had gone a little further thence, he saw James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, who also were in the ship mending their nets.

verses.original: καὶ ⸀εὐθὺς ἐκάλεσεν αὐτούς. καὶ ἀφέντες τὸν πατέρα αὐτῶν Ζεβεδαῖον ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ μετὰ τῶν μισθωτῶν ἀπῆλθον ὀπίσω αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai euthus ekalesen autoys. kai afentes ton patera auton Zevedaion en to ploio meta ton misthoton apelthon opiso autou.
verses.translation: And straightway he called them: and they left their father Zebedee in the ship with the hired servants, and went after him.

verses.original: Καὶ εἰσπορεύονται εἰς Καφαρναούμ. καὶ ⸀εὐθὺς τοῖς σάββασιν ⸂ἐδίδασκεν εἰς τὴν συναγωγήν⸃.
verses.translit: Kai eisporeyontai eis Kafarnaoym. kai euthus tois savvasin edidasken eis ten synagogin.
verses.translation: And they went into Capernaum; and straightway on the sabbath day he entered into the synagogue, and taught.

verses.original: καὶ ἐξεπλήσσοντο ἐπὶ τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ, ἦν γὰρ διδάσκων αὐτοὺς ὡς ἐξουσίαν ἔχων καὶ οὐχ ὡς οἱ γραμματεῖς.
verses.translit: kai exeplissonto epi te didahe autou, en gar didaskon autous os exoysian ehon kai ouh os oi grammateis.
verses.translation: And they were astonished at his doctrine: for he taught them as one that had authority, and not as the scribes.

verses.original: καὶ ⸀εὐθὺς ἦν ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ αὐτῶν ἄνθρωπος ἐν πνεύματι ἀκαθάρτῳ καὶ ἀνέκραξεν
verses.translit: kai euthus en en te synagoge auton anthropos en pneymati akatharto kai anekraxen
verses.translation: And there was in their synagogue a man with an unclean spirit; and he cried out,

verses.original: λέγων· ⸀Τί ἡμῖν καὶ σοί, Ἰησοῦ Ναζαρηνέ; ἦλθες ἀπολέσαι ἡμᾶς; οἶδά σε τίς εἶ, ὁ ἅγιος τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: legon* Ti emin kai soi, Iisou Nazarine; elthes apolesai emas; oida se tis ei, o agios tou theou.
verses.translation: Saying, Let us alone; what have we to do with thee, thou Jesus of Nazareth? art thou come to destroy us? I know thee who thou art, the Holy One of God.

verses.original: καὶ ἐπετίμησεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγων· Φιμώθητι καὶ ἔξελθε ἐξ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai epetimisen auto o Iisous legon* Fimothiti kai exelthe ex autou.
verses.translation: And Jesus rebuked him, saying, Hold thy peace, and come out of him.

verses.original: καὶ σπαράξαν αὐτὸν τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἀκάθαρτον καὶ ⸀φωνῆσαν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ἐξῆλθεν ἐξ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai sparaxan auton to pneuma to akatharton kai fonesan fone megale exelthen ex autou.
verses.translation: And when the unclean spirit had torn him, and cried with a loud voice, he came out of him.

verses.original: καὶ ἐθαμβήθησαν ⸀ἅπαντες, ὥστε συζητεῖν ⸂πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς⸃ λέγοντας· Τί ἐστιν τοῦτο; ⸂διδαχὴ καινή⸃· κατʼ ἐξουσίαν καὶ τοῖς πνεύμασι τοῖς ἀκαθάρτοις ἐπιτάσσει, καὶ ὑπακούουσιν αὐτῷ.
verses.translit: kai ethamvithisan apantes, oste syzitein pros eaytous legontas* Ti estin touto; didahe kaini* kat' exoysian kai tois pneymasi tois akathartois epitassei, kai upakoyoysin auto.
verses.translation: And they were all amazed, insomuch that they questioned among themselves, saying, What thing is this? what new doctrine is this? for with authority commandeth he even the unclean spirits, and they do obey him.

verses.original: ⸂καὶ ἐξῆλθεν⸃ ἡ ἀκοὴ αὐτοῦ εὐθὺς ⸀πανταχοῦ εἰς ὅλην τὴν περίχωρον τῆς Γαλιλαίας.
verses.translit: kai exelthen e akoe autou euthus pantahou eis olin ten perihoron tes Galilaias.
verses.translation: And immediately his fame spread abroad throughout all the region round about Galilee.

verses.original: Καὶ ⸀εὐθὺς ἐκ τῆς συναγωγῆς ⸂ἐξελθόντες ἦλθον⸃ εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν Σίμωνος καὶ Ἀνδρέου μετὰ Ἰακώβου καὶ Ἰωάννου.
verses.translit: Kai euthus ek tes synagoges exelthontes elthon eis ten oikian Simonos kai Andreoy meta Iakovoy kai Ioannoy.
verses.translation: And forthwith, when they were come out of the synagogue, they entered into the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John.

verses.original: ἡ δὲ πενθερὰ Σίμωνος κατέκειτο πυρέσσουσα, καὶ ⸀εὐθὺς λέγουσιν αὐτῷ περὶ αὐτῆς.
verses.translit: e de penthera Simonos katekeito pyressoysa, kai euthus legoysin auto peri autes.
verses.translation: But Simon’s wife’s mother lay sick of a fever, and anon they tell him of her.

verses.original: καὶ προσελθὼν ἤγειρεν αὐτὴν κρατήσας τῆς ⸀χειρός· καὶ ἀφῆκεν αὐτὴν ὁ ⸀πυρετός, καὶ διηκόνει αὐτοῖς.
verses.translit: kai proselthon egeiren auten kratisas tes heiros* kai afeken auten o pyretos, kai diikonei autois.
verses.translation: And he came and took her by the hand, and lifted her up; and immediately the fever left her, and she ministered unto them.

verses.original: Ὀψίας δὲ γενομένης, ὅτε ⸀ἔδυ ὁ ἥλιος, ἔφερον πρὸς αὐτὸν πάντας τοὺς κακῶς ἔχοντας καὶ τοὺς δαιμονιζομένους·
verses.translit: Opsias de genomenis, ote edy o elios, eferon pros auton pantas tous kakos ehontas kai tous daimonizomenoys*
verses.translation: And at even, when the sun did set, they brought unto him all that were diseased, and them that were possessed with devils.

verses.original: καὶ ⸂ἦν ὅλη ἡ πόλις ἐπισυνηγμένη⸃ πρὸς τὴν θύραν.
verses.translit: kai en oli e polis episynigmeni pros ten thyran.
verses.translation: And all the city was gathered together at the door.

verses.original: καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν πολλοὺς κακῶς ἔχοντας ποικίλαις νόσοις, καὶ δαιμόνια πολλὰ ἐξέβαλεν, καὶ οὐκ ἤφιεν λαλεῖν τὰ δαιμόνια, ὅτι ᾔδεισαν ⸀αὐτόν.
verses.translit: kai etherapeysen pollous kakos ehontas poikilais nosois, kai daimonia polla exevalen, kai ouk efien lalein ta daimonia, oti edeisan auton.
verses.translation: And he healed many that were sick of divers diseases, and cast out many devils; and suffered not the devils to speak, because they knew him.

verses.original: Καὶ πρωῒ ἔννυχα λίαν ἀναστὰς ἐξῆλθεν καὶ ἀπῆλθεν εἰς ἔρημον τόπον κἀκεῖ προσηύχετο.
verses.translit: Kai proi ennyha lian anastas exelthen kai apelthen eis erimon topon kakei prosiyheto.
verses.translation: And in the morning, rising up a great while before day, he went out, and departed into a solitary place, and there prayed.

verses.original: καὶ ⸀κατεδίωξεν αὐτὸν ⸀Σίμων καὶ οἱ μετʼ αὐτοῦ,
verses.translit: kai katedioxen auton Simon kai oi met' autou,
verses.translation: And Simon and they that were with him followed after him.

verses.original: καὶ ⸂εὗρον αὐτὸν καὶ⸃ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ ὅτι Πάντες ⸂ζητοῦσίν σε⸃.
verses.translit: kai euron auton kai legoysin auto oti Pantes zitousin se.
verses.translation: And when they had found him, they said unto him, All men seek for thee.

verses.original: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ἄγωμεν ⸀ἀλλαχοῦ εἰς τὰς ἐχομένας κωμοπόλεις, ἵνα καὶ ἐκεῖ κηρύξω, εἰς τοῦτο γὰρ ⸀ἐξῆλθον.
verses.translit: kai legei autois* Agomen allahou eis tas ehomenas komopoleis, ina kai ekei kiryxo, eis touto gar exelthon.
verses.translation: And he said unto them, Let us go into the next towns, that I may preach there also: for therefore came I forth.

verses.original: καὶ ⸀ἦλθεν κηρύσσων ⸂εἰς τὰς συναγωγὰς⸃ αὐτῶν εἰς ὅλην τὴν Γαλιλαίαν καὶ τὰ δαιμόνια ἐκβάλλων.
verses.translit: kai elthen kirysson eis tas synagogas auton eis olin ten Galilaian kai ta daimonia ekvallon.
verses.translation: And he preached in their synagogues throughout all Galilee, and cast out devils.

verses.original: Καὶ ἔρχεται πρὸς αὐτὸν λεπρὸς παρακαλῶν αὐτὸν καὶ ⸀γονυπετῶν λέγων αὐτῷ ὅτι Ἐὰν θέλῃς δύνασαί με καθαρίσαι.
verses.translit: Kai erhetai pros auton lepros parakalon auton kai gonypeton legon auto oti Ean theles dynasai me katharisai.
verses.translation: And there came a leper to him, beseeching him, and kneeling down to him, and saying unto him, If thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.

verses.original: ⸀καὶ ⸀ὀργισθεὶς ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα ⸂αὐτοῦ ἥψατο⸃ καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Θέλω, καθαρίσθητι·
verses.translit: kai orgistheis ekteinas ten heira autou epsato kai legei auto* Thelo, katharisthiti*
verses.translation: And Jesus, moved with compassion, put forth his hand, and touched him, and saith unto him, I will; be thou clean.

verses.original: καὶ ⸀εὐθὺς ἀπῆλθεν ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ ἡ λέπρα, καὶ ἐκαθαρίσθη.
verses.translit: kai euthus apelthen ap' autou e lepra, kai ekatharisthi.
verses.translation: And as soon as he had spoken, immediately the leprosy departed from him, and he was cleansed.

verses.original: καὶ ἐμβριμησάμενος αὐτῷ ⸀εὐθὺς ἐξέβαλεν αὐτόν,
verses.translit: kai emvrimisamenos auto euthus exevalen auton,
verses.translation: And he straitly charged him, and forthwith sent him away;

verses.original: καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Ὅρα μηδενὶ μηδὲν εἴπῃς, ἀλλὰ ὕπαγε σεαυτὸν δεῖξον τῷ ἱερεῖ καὶ προσένεγκε περὶ τοῦ καθαρισμοῦ σου ἃ προσέταξεν Μωϋσῆς εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς.
verses.translit: kai legei auto* Ora mideni miden eipes, alla upage seayton deixon to ierei kai prosenegke peri tou katharismou soy a prosetaxen Moyses eis martyrion autois.
verses.translation: And saith unto him, See thou say nothing to any man: but go thy way, shew thyself to the priest, and offer for thy cleansing those things which Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ἐξελθὼν ἤρξατο κηρύσσειν πολλὰ καὶ διαφημίζειν τὸν λόγον, ὥστε μηκέτι αὐτὸν δύνασθαι φανερῶς εἰς πόλιν εἰσελθεῖν, ἀλλὰ ἔξω ⸀ἐπʼ ἐρήμοις τόποις ἦν· καὶ ἤρχοντο πρὸς αὐτὸν ⸀πάντοθεν.
verses.translit: o de exelthon erxato kiryssein polla kai diafimizein ton logon, oste miketi auton dynasthai faneros eis polin eiselthein, alla exo ep' erimois topois en* kai erhonto pros auton pantothen.
verses.translation: But he went out, and began to publish it much, and to blaze abroad the matter, insomuch that Jesus could no more openly enter into the city, but was without in desert places: and they came to him from every quarter.

verses.original: Καὶ ⸀εἰσελθὼν πάλιν εἰς Καφαρναοὺμ διʼ ⸀ἡμερῶν ἠκούσθη ὅτι ⸂ἐν οἴκῳ⸃ ἐστίν·
verses.translit: Kai eiselthon palin eis Kafarnaoum di' emeron ekoysthi oti en oiko estin*
verses.translation: And again he entered into Capernaum after some days; and it was noised that he was in the house.

verses.original: ⸀καὶ συνήχθησαν πολλοὶ ὥστε μηκέτι χωρεῖν μηδὲ τὰ πρὸς τὴν θύραν, καὶ ἐλάλει αὐτοῖς τὸν λόγον.
verses.translit: kai synihthisan polloi oste miketi horein mide ta pros ten thyran, kai elalei autois ton logon.
verses.translation: And straightway many were gathered together, insomuch that there was no room to receive them , no, not so much as about the door: and he preached the word unto them.

verses.original: καὶ ἔρχονται ⸂φέροντες πρὸς αὐτὸν παραλυτικὸν⸃ αἰρόμενον ὑπὸ τεσσάρων.
verses.translit: kai erhontai ferontes pros auton paralytikon airomenon upo tessaron.
verses.translation: And they come unto him, bringing one sick of the palsy, which was borne of four.

verses.original: καὶ μὴ δυνάμενοι ⸀προσενέγκαι αὐτῷ διὰ τὸν ὄχλον ἀπεστέγασαν τὴν στέγην ὅπου ἦν, καὶ ἐξορύξαντες χαλῶσι τὸν κράβαττον ⸀ὅπου ὁ παραλυτικὸς κατέκειτο.
verses.translit: kai me dynamenoi prosenegkai auto dia ton ohlon apestegasan ten stegin opoy en, kai exoryxantes halosi ton kravatton opoy o paralytikos katekeito.
verses.translation: And when they could not come nigh unto him for the press, they uncovered the roof where he was: and when they had broken it up, they let down the bed wherein the sick of the palsy lay.

verses.original: ⸂καὶ ἰδὼν⸃ ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὴν πίστιν αὐτῶν λέγει τῷ παραλυτικῷ· Τέκνον, ⸂ἀφίενταί σου⸃ αἱ ⸀ἁμαρτίαι.
verses.translit: kai idon o Iisous ten pistin auton legei to paralytiko* Teknon, afientai soy ai amartiai.
verses.translation: When Jesus saw their faith, he said unto the sick of the palsy, Son, thy sins be forgiven thee.

verses.original: ἦσαν δέ τινες τῶν γραμματέων ἐκεῖ καθήμενοι καὶ διαλογιζόμενοι ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις αὐτῶν·
verses.translit: esan de tines ton grammateon ekei kathimenoi kai dialogizomenoi en tais kardiais auton*
verses.translation: But there were certain of the scribes sitting there, and reasoning in their hearts,

verses.original: Τί οὗτος οὕτως λαλεῖ; ⸀βλασφημεῖ· τίς δύναται ἀφιέναι ἁμαρτίας εἰ μὴ εἷς ὁ θεός;
verses.translit: Ti outos outos lalei; vlasfimei* tis dynatai afienai amartias ei me eis o theos;
verses.translation: Why doth this man thus speak blasphemies? who can forgive sins but God only?

verses.original: καὶ ⸀εὐθὺς ἐπιγνοὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς τῷ πνεύματι αὐτοῦ ὅτι ⸀οὕτως διαλογίζονται ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ⸀λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τί ταῦτα διαλογίζεσθε ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν;
verses.translit: kai euthus epignous o Iisous to pneymati autou oti outos dialogizontai en eaytois legei autois* Ti tauta dialogizesthe en tais kardiais umon;
verses.translation: And immediately when Jesus perceived in his spirit that they so reasoned within themselves, he said unto them, Why reason ye these things in your hearts?

verses.original: τί ἐστιν εὐκοπώτερον, εἰπεῖν τῷ παραλυτικῷ· ⸀Ἀφίενταί σου αἱ ἁμαρτίαι, ἢ εἰπεῖν· ⸀Ἔγειρε καὶ ἆρον ⸂τὸν κράβαττόν σου⸃ καὶ περιπάτει;
verses.translit: ti estin eukopoteron, eipein to paralytiko* Afientai soy ai amartiai, e eipein* Egeire kai aron ton kravatton soy kai peripatei;
verses.translation: Whether is it easier to say to the sick of the palsy, Thy sins be forgiven thee; or to say, Arise, and take up thy bed, and walk?

verses.original: ἵνα δὲ εἰδῆτε ὅτι ἐξουσίαν ἔχει ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ⸂ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἀφιέναι ἁμαρτίας⸃— λέγει τῷ παραλυτικῷ·
verses.translit: ina de eidete oti exoysian ehei o yios tou anthropoy epi tes ges afienai amartias-- legei to paralytiko*
verses.translation: But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power on earth to forgive sins, (he saith to the sick of the palsy,)

verses.original: Σοὶ λέγω, ⸀ἔγειρε ἆρον τὸν κράβαττόν σου καὶ ὕπαγε εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου.
verses.translit: Soi lego, egeire aron ton kravatton soy kai upage eis ton oikon soy.
verses.translation: I say unto thee, Arise, and take up thy bed, and go thy way into thine house.

verses.original: καὶ ἠγέρθη ⸂καὶ εὐθὺς⸃ ἄρας τὸν κράβαττον ἐξῆλθεν ⸀ἔμπροσθεν πάντων, ὥστε ἐξίστασθαι πάντας καὶ δοξάζειν τὸν θεὸν λέγοντας ὅτι ⸂Οὕτως οὐδέποτε⸃ εἴδομεν.
verses.translit: kai egerthi kai euthus aras ton kravatton exelthen emprosthen panton, oste existasthai pantas kai doxazein ton theon legontas oti Outos oudepote eidomen.
verses.translation: And immediately he arose, took up the bed, and went forth before them all; insomuch that they were all amazed, and glorified God, saying, We never saw it on this fashion.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐξῆλθεν πάλιν παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν· καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος ἤρχετο πρὸς αὐτόν, καὶ ἐδίδασκεν αὐτούς.
verses.translit: Kai exelthen palin para ten thalassan* kai pas o ohlos erheto pros auton, kai edidasken autoys.
verses.translation: And he went forth again by the sea side; and all the multitude resorted unto him, and he taught them.

verses.original: καὶ παράγων εἶδεν Λευὶν τὸν τοῦ Ἁλφαίου καθήμενον ἐπὶ τὸ τελώνιον, καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Ἀκολούθει μοι. καὶ ἀναστὰς ἠκολούθησεν αὐτῷ.
verses.translit: kai paragon eiden Leyin ton tou Alfaioy kathimenon epi to telonion, kai legei auto* Akoloythei moi. kai anastas ekoloythisen auto.
verses.translation: And as he passed by, he saw Levi the son of Alphæus sitting at the receipt of custom, and said unto him, Follow me. And he arose and followed him.

verses.original: Καὶ ⸀γίνεται κατακεῖσθαι αὐτὸν ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ αὐτοῦ, καὶ πολλοὶ τελῶναι καὶ ἁμαρτωλοὶ συνανέκειντο τῷ Ἰησοῦ καὶ τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ, ἦσαν γὰρ πολλοὶ καὶ ⸀ἠκολούθουν αὐτῷ.
verses.translit: Kai ginetai katakeisthai auton en te oikia autou, kai polloi telonai kai amartoloi synanekeinto to Iisou kai tois mathitais autou, esan gar polloi kai ekoloythoyn auto.
verses.translation: And it came to pass, that, as Jesus sat at meat in his house, many publicans and sinners sat also together with Jesus and his disciples: for there were many, and they followed him.

verses.original: καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς ⸂τῶν Φαρισαίων⸃ ⸀ἰδόντες ⸂ὅτι ἐσθίει⸃ μετὰ τῶν ⸂ἁμαρτωλῶν καὶ τελωνῶν⸃ ἔλεγον τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ· ⸀Ὅτι μετὰ τῶν ⸂τελωνῶν καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν⸃ ⸀ἐσθίει;
verses.translit: kai oi grammateis ton Farisaion idontes oti esthiei meta ton amartolon kai telonon elegon tois mathitais autou* Oti meta ton telonon kai amartolon esthiei;
verses.translation: And when the scribes and Pharisees saw him eat with publicans and sinners, they said unto his disciples, How is it that he eateth and drinketh with publicans and sinners?

verses.original: καὶ ἀκούσας ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγει αὐτοῖς ⸀ὅτι Οὐ χρείαν ἔχουσιν οἱ ἰσχύοντες ἰατροῦ ἀλλʼ οἱ κακῶς ἔχοντες· οὐκ ἦλθον καλέσαι δικαίους ἀλλὰ ⸀ἁμαρτωλούς.
verses.translit: kai akoysas o Iisous legei autois oti Ou hreian ehoysin oi ishyontes iatrou all' oi kakos ehontes* ouk elthon kalesai dikaioys alla amartoloys.
verses.translation: When Jesus heard it , he saith unto them, They that are whole have no need of the physician, but they that are sick: I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.

verses.original: Καὶ ἦσαν οἱ μαθηταὶ Ἰωάννου καὶ οἱ ⸀Φαρισαῖοι νηστεύοντες. καὶ ἔρχονται καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Διὰ τί οἱ μαθηταὶ Ἰωάννου καὶ οἱ ⸀μαθηταὶ τῶν Φαρισαίων νηστεύουσιν, οἱ δὲ σοὶ μαθηταὶ οὐ νηστεύουσιν;
verses.translit: Kai esan oi mathitai Ioannoy kai oi Farisaioi nisteyontes. kai erhontai kai legoysin auto* Dia ti oi mathitai Ioannoy kai oi mathitai ton Farisaion nisteyoysin, oi de soi mathitai ou nisteyoysin;
verses.translation: And the disciples of John and of the Pharisees used to fast: and they come and say unto him, Why do the disciples of John and of the Pharisees fast, but thy disciples fast not?

verses.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Μὴ δύνανται οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ νυμφῶνος ἐν ᾧ ὁ νυμφίος μετʼ αὐτῶν ἐστιν νηστεύειν; ὅσον χρόνον ⸂ἔχουσιν τὸν νυμφίον μετʼ αὐτῶν⸃ οὐ δύνανται νηστεύειν·
verses.translit: kai eipen autois o Iisous* Me dynantai oi yioi tou nymfonos en o o nymfios met' auton estin nisteyein; oson hronon ehoysin ton nymfion met' auton ou dynantai nisteyein*
verses.translation: And Jesus said unto them, Can the children of the bridechamber fast, while the bridegroom is with them? as long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast.

verses.original: ἐλεύσονται δὲ ἡμέραι ὅταν ἀπαρθῇ ἀπʼ αὐτῶν ὁ νυμφίος, καὶ τότε νηστεύσουσιν ἐν ⸂ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ⸃.
verses.translit: eleysontai de emerai otan aparthe ap' auton o nymfios, kai tote nisteysoysin en ekeine te emera.
verses.translation: But the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them, and then shall they fast in those days.

verses.original: ⸀Οὐδεὶς ἐπίβλημα ῥάκους ἀγνάφου ἐπιράπτει ἐπὶ ⸂ἱμάτιον παλαιόν⸃· εἰ δὲ μή, αἴρει τὸ πλήρωμα ⸀ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ τὸ καινὸν τοῦ παλαιοῦ, καὶ χεῖρον σχίσμα γίνεται.
verses.translit: Oudeis epivlima Rakoys agnafoy epiraptei epi imation palaion* ei de mi, airei to pliroma ap' autou to kainon tou palaiou, kai heiron shisma ginetai.
verses.translation: No man also seweth a piece of new cloth on an old garment: else the new piece that filled it up taketh away from the old, and the rent is made worse.

verses.original: καὶ οὐδεὶς βάλλει οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς παλαιούς· εἰ δὲ μή, ⸂ῥήξει ὁ οἶνος⸃ τοὺς ἀσκούς, καὶ ὁ οἶνος ⸂ἀπόλλυται καὶ οἱ ἀσκοί⸃. ἀλλὰ οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς ⸀καινούς.
verses.translit: kai oudeis vallei oinon neon eis askous palaioys* ei de mi, Rixei o oinos tous askoys, kai o oinos apollytai kai oi askoi. alla oinon neon eis askous kainoys.
verses.translation: And no man putteth new wine into old bottles: else the new wine doth burst the bottles, and the wine is spilled, and the bottles will be marred: but new wine must be put into new bottles.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ⸂αὐτὸν ἐν τοῖς σάββασιν παραπορεύεσθαι⸃ διὰ τῶν σπορίμων, καὶ ⸂οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἤρξαντο⸃ ὁδὸν ποιεῖν τίλλοντες τοὺς στάχυας.
verses.translit: Kai egeneto auton en tois savvasin paraporeyesthai dia ton sporimon, kai oi mathitai autou erxanto odon poiein tillontes tous stahyas.
verses.translation: And it came to pass, that he went through the corn fields on the sabbath day; and his disciples began, as they went, to pluck the ears of corn.

verses.original: καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι ἔλεγον αὐτῷ· Ἴδε τί ⸀ποιοῦσιν τοῖς σάββασιν ὃ οὐκ ἔξεστιν;
verses.translit: kai oi Farisaioi elegon auto* Ide ti poiousin tois savvasin o ouk exestin;
verses.translation: And the Pharisees said unto him, Behold, why do they on the sabbath day that which is not lawful?

verses.original: καὶ ⸀λέγει αὐτοῖς· Οὐδέποτε ἀνέγνωτε τί ἐποίησεν Δαυὶδ ὅτε χρείαν ἔσχεν καὶ ἐπείνασεν αὐτὸς καὶ οἱ μετʼ αὐτοῦ;
verses.translit: kai legei autois* Oudepote anegnote ti epoiisen Dayid ote hreian eshen kai epeinasen autos kai oi met' autou;
verses.translation: And he said unto them, Have ye never read what David did, when he had need, and was an hungred, he, and they that were with him?

verses.original: ⸀πῶς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπὶ Ἀβιαθὰρ ἀρχιερέως καὶ τοὺς ἄρτους τῆς προθέσεως ἔφαγεν, οὓς οὐκ ἔξεστιν φαγεῖν εἰ μὴ ⸂τοὺς ἱερεῖς⸃, καὶ ἔδωκεν καὶ τοῖς σὺν αὐτῷ οὖσιν;
verses.translit: pos eiselthen eis ton oikon tou theou epi Aviathar arhiereos kai tous artoys tes protheseos efagen, ous ouk exestin fagein ei me tous iereis, kai edoken kai tois sun auto ousin;
verses.translation: How he went into the house of God in the days of Abiathar the high priest, and did eat the shewbread, which is not lawful to eat but for the priests, and gave also to them which were with him?

verses.original: καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Τὸ σάββατον διὰ τὸν ἄνθρωπον ἐγένετο ⸀καὶ οὐχ ὁ ἄνθρωπος διὰ τὸ σάββατον·
verses.translit: kai elegen autois* To savvaton dia ton anthropon egeneto kai ouh o anthropos dia to savvaton*
verses.translation: And he said unto them, The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath:

verses.original: ὥστε κύριός ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου καὶ τοῦ σαββάτου.
verses.translit: oste kyrios estin o yios tou anthropoy kai tou savvatoy.
verses.translation: Therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.

verses.original: Καὶ εἰσῆλθεν πάλιν ⸀εἰς συναγωγήν, καὶ ἦν ἐκεῖ ἄνθρωπος ἐξηραμμένην ἔχων τὴν χεῖρα.
verses.translit: Kai eiselthen palin eis synagogin, kai en ekei anthropos exirammenin ehon ten heira.
verses.translation: And he entered again into the synagogue; and there was a man there which had a withered hand.

verses.original: καὶ παρετήρουν αὐτὸν εἰ τοῖς σάββασιν θεραπεύσει αὐτόν, ἵνα ⸀κατηγορήσωσιν αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai paretiroyn auton ei tois savvasin therapeysei auton, ina katigorisosin autou.
verses.translation: And they watched him, whether he would heal him on the sabbath day; that they might accuse him.

verses.original: καὶ λέγει τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ τῷ ⸂τὴν χεῖρα ἔχοντι ξηράν⸃· ⸀Ἔγειρε εἰς τὸ μέσον.
verses.translit: kai legei to anthropo to ten heira ehonti xiran* Egeire eis to meson.
verses.translation: And he saith unto the man which had the withered hand, Stand forth.

verses.original: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ἔξεστιν τοῖς σάββασιν ⸀ἀγαθοποιῆσαι ἢ κακοποιῆσαι, ψυχὴν σῶσαι ἢ ἀποκτεῖναι; οἱ δὲ ἐσιώπων.
verses.translit: kai legei autois* Exestin tois savvasin agathopoiesai e kakopoiesai, psyhen sosai e apokteinai; oi de esiopon.
verses.translation: And he saith unto them, Is it lawful to do good on the sabbath days, or to do evil? to save life, or to kill? But they held their peace.

verses.original: καὶ περιβλεψάμενος αὐτοὺς μετʼ ὀργῆς, συλλυπούμενος ἐπὶ τῇ πωρώσει τῆς καρδίας αὐτῶν, λέγει τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ· Ἔκτεινον τὴν ⸀χεῖρα· καὶ ἐξέτεινεν, καὶ ἀπεκατεστάθη ἡ χεὶρ ⸀αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai perivlepsamenos autous met' orges, syllypoymenos epi te porosei tes kardias auton, legei to anthropo* Ekteinon ten heira* kai exeteinen, kai apekatestathi e heir autou.
verses.translation: And when he had looked round about on them with anger, being grieved for the hardness of their hearts, he saith unto the man, Stretch forth thine hand. And he stretched it out: and his hand was restored whole as the other.

verses.original: καὶ ἐξελθόντες οἱ Φαρισαῖοι ⸀εὐθὺς μετὰ τῶν Ἡρῳδιανῶν συμβούλιον ⸀ἐδίδουν κατʼ αὐτοῦ ὅπως αὐτὸν ἀπολέσωσιν.
verses.translit: kai exelthontes oi Farisaioi euthus meta ton Erodianon symvoylion edidoyn kat' autou opos auton apolesosin.
verses.translation: And the Pharisees went forth, and straightway took counsel with the Herodians against him, how they might destroy him.

verses.original: Καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ⸂μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ ἀνεχώρησεν⸃ πρὸς τὴν θάλασσαν· καὶ πολὺ πλῆθος ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας ⸀ἠκολούθησεν, καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰουδαίας
verses.translit: Kai o Iisous meta ton mathiton autou anehorisen pros ten thalassan* kai polu plethos apo tes Galilaias ekoloythisen, kai apo tes Ioydaias
verses.translation: But Jesus withdrew himself with his disciples to the sea: and a great multitude from Galilee followed him, and from Judæa,

verses.original: καὶ ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰδουμαίας ⸀καὶ πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου ⸁καὶ περὶ Τύρον καὶ Σιδῶνα, πλῆθος πολύ, ⸀ἀκούοντες ὅσα ⸀ἐποίει ἦλθον πρὸς αὐτόν.
verses.translit: kai apo Ierosolymon kai apo tes Idoymaias kai peran tou Iordanoy kai peri Tyron kai Sidona, plethos poly, akoyontes osa epoiei elthon pros auton.
verses.translation: And from Jerusalem, and from Idumaea, and from beyond Jordan; and they about Tyre and Sidon, a great multitude, when they had heard what great things he did, came unto him.

verses.original: καὶ εἶπεν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ ἵνα πλοιάριον προσκαρτερῇ αὐτῷ διὰ τὸν ὄχλον ἵνα μὴ θλίβωσιν αὐτόν·
verses.translit: kai eipen tois mathitais autou ina ploiarion proskartere auto dia ton ohlon ina me thlivosin auton*
verses.translation: And he spake to his disciples, that a small ship should wait on him because of the multitude, lest they should throng him.

verses.original: πολλοὺς γὰρ ἐθεράπευσεν, ὥστε ἐπιπίπτειν αὐτῷ ἵνα αὐτοῦ ἅψωνται ὅσοι εἶχον μάστιγας.
verses.translit: pollous gar etherapeysen, oste epipiptein auto ina autou apsontai osoi eihon mastigas.
verses.translation: For he had healed many; insomuch that they pressed upon him for to touch him, as many as had plagues.

verses.original: καὶ τὰ πνεύματα τὰ ἀκάθαρτα, ὅταν αὐτὸν ⸂ἐθεώρουν, προσέπιπτον⸃ αὐτῷ καὶ ⸀ἔκραζον ⸀λέγοντα ὅτι Σὺ εἶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: kai ta pneymata ta akatharta, otan auton etheoroyn, prosepipton auto kai ekrazon legonta oti Su ei o yios tou theou.
verses.translation: And unclean spirits, when they saw him, fell down before him, and cried, saying, Thou art the Son of God.

verses.original: καὶ πολλὰ ἐπετίμα αὐτοῖς ἵνα μὴ ⸂αὐτὸν φανερὸν⸃ ⸀ποιήσωσιν.
verses.translit: kai polla epetima autois ina me auton faneron poiisosin.
verses.translation: And he straitly charged them that they should not make him known.

verses.original: Καὶ ἀναβαίνει εἰς τὸ ὄρος καὶ προσκαλεῖται οὓς ἤθελεν αὐτός, καὶ ἀπῆλθον πρὸς αὐτόν.
verses.translit: Kai anavainei eis to oros kai proskaleitai ous ethelen autos, kai apelthon pros auton.
verses.translation: And he goeth up into a mountain, and calleth unto him whom he would: and they came unto him.

verses.original: καὶ ἐποίησεν ⸀δώδεκα, ἵνα ὦσιν μετʼ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἵνα ἀποστέλλῃ αὐτοὺς κηρύσσειν
verses.translit: kai epoiisen dodeka, ina osin met' autou kai ina apostelle autous kiryssein
verses.translation: And he ordained twelve, that they should be with him, and that he might send them forth to preach,

verses.original: καὶ ἔχειν ⸀ἐξουσίαν ἐκβάλλειν τὰ δαιμόνια·
verses.translit: kai ehein exoysian ekvallein ta daimonia*
verses.translation: And to have power to heal sicknesses, and to cast out devils:

verses.original: καὶ ⸂ἐποίησεν τοὺς δώδεκα, καὶ⸃ ἐπέθηκεν ⸂ὄνομα τῷ Σίμωνι⸃ Πέτρον,
verses.translit: kai epoiisen tous dodeka, kai epethiken onoma to Simoni Petron,
verses.translation: And Simon he surnamed Peter;

verses.original: καὶ Ἰάκωβον τὸν τοῦ Ζεβεδαίου καὶ Ἰωάννην τὸν ἀδελφὸν τοῦ Ἰακώβου (καὶ ἐπέθηκεν αὐτοῖς ⸀ὀνόματα Βοανηργές, ὅ ἐστιν Υἱοὶ Βροντῆς),
verses.translit: kai Iakovon ton tou Zevedaioy kai Ioannin ton adelfon tou Iakovoy (kai epethiken autois onomata Voanirges, o estin Yioi Vrontes),
verses.translation: And James the son of Zebedee, and John the brother of James; and he surnamed them Boanerges, which is, The sons of thunder:

verses.original: καὶ Ἀνδρέαν καὶ Φίλιππον καὶ Βαρθολομαῖον καὶ Μαθθαῖον καὶ Θωμᾶν καὶ Ἰάκωβον τὸν τοῦ Ἁλφαίου καὶ Θαδδαῖον καὶ Σίμωνα τὸν ⸀Καναναῖον
verses.translit: kai Andrean kai Filippon kai Vartholomaion kai Maththaion kai Thoman kai Iakovon ton tou Alfaioy kai Thaddaion kai Simona ton Kananaion
verses.translation: And Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus, and Simon the Canaanite,

verses.original: καὶ Ἰούδαν ⸀Ἰσκαριώθ, ὃς καὶ παρέδωκεν αὐτόν.
verses.translit: kai Ioydan Iskarioth, os kai paredoken auton.
verses.translation: And Judas Iscariot, which also betrayed him: and they went into an house.

verses.original: Καὶ ⸀ἔρχεται εἰς οἶκον· καὶ συνέρχεται πάλιν ⸀ὁ ὄχλος, ὥστε μὴ δύνασθαι αὐτοὺς ⸀μηδὲ ἄρτον φαγεῖν.
verses.translit: Kai erhetai eis oikon* kai synerhetai palin o ohlos, oste me dynasthai autous mide arton fagein.
verses.translation: And the multitude cometh together again, so that they could not so much as eat bread.

verses.original: καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ παρʼ αὐτοῦ ἐξῆλθον κρατῆσαι αὐτόν, ἔλεγον γὰρ ὅτι ἐξέστη.
verses.translit: kai akoysantes oi par' autou exelthon kratesai auton, elegon gar oti exesti.
verses.translation: And when his friends heard of it , they went out to lay hold on him: for they said, He is beside himself.

verses.original: καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς οἱ ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων καταβάντες ἔλεγον ὅτι Βεελζεβοὺλ ἔχει καὶ ὅτι ἐν τῷ ἄρχοντι τῶν δαιμονίων ἐκβάλλει τὰ δαιμόνια.
verses.translit: kai oi grammateis oi apo Ierosolymon katavantes elegon oti Veelzevoul ehei kai oti en to arhonti ton daimonion ekvallei ta daimonia.
verses.translation: And the scribes which came down from Jerusalem said, He hath Beelzebub, and by the prince of the devils casteth he out devils.

verses.original: καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος αὐτοὺς ἐν παραβολαῖς ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Πῶς δύναται Σατανᾶς Σατανᾶν ἐκβάλλειν;
verses.translit: kai proskalesamenos autous en paravolais elegen autois* Pos dynatai Satanas Satanan ekvallein;
verses.translation: And he called them unto him , and said unto them in parables, How can Satan cast out Satan?

verses.original: καὶ ἐὰν βασιλεία ἐφʼ ἑαυτὴν μερισθῇ, οὐ δύναται σταθῆναι ἡ βασιλεία ἐκείνη·
verses.translit: kai ean vasileia ef' eayten meristhe, ou dynatai stathenai e vasileia ekeini*
verses.translation: And if a kingdom be divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.

verses.original: καὶ ἐὰν οἰκία ἐφʼ ἑαυτὴν μερισθῇ, οὐ ⸀δυνήσεται ⸂ἡ οἰκία ἐκείνη σταθῆναι⸃·
verses.translit: kai ean oikia ef' eayten meristhe, ou dynisetai e oikia ekeini stathenai*
verses.translation: And if a house be divided against itself, that house cannot stand.

verses.original: καὶ εἰ ὁ Σατανᾶς ἀνέστη ἐφʼ ἑαυτὸν καὶ ⸀ἐμερίσθη, οὐ δύναται ⸀στῆναι ἀλλὰ τέλος ἔχει.
verses.translit: kai ei o Satanas anesti ef' eayton kai emeristhi, ou dynatai stenai alla telos ehei.
verses.translation: And if Satan rise up against himself, and be divided, he cannot stand, but hath an end.

verses.original: ⸂ἀλλʼ οὐδεὶς δύναται⸃ ⸂εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν τοῦ ἰσχυροῦ εἰσελθὼν τὰ σκεύη⸃ αὐτοῦ διαρπάσαι ἐὰν μὴ πρῶτον τὸν ἰσχυρὸν δήσῃ, καὶ τότε τὴν οἰκίαν αὐτοῦ ⸀διαρπάσει.
verses.translit: all' oudeis dynatai eis ten oikian tou ishyrou eiselthon ta skeyi autou diarpasai ean me proton ton ishyron dise, kai tote ten oikian autou diarpasei.
verses.translation: No man can enter into a strong man’s house, and spoil his goods, except he will first bind the strong man; and then he will spoil his house.

verses.original: Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πάντα ἀφεθήσεται ⸂τοῖς υἱοῖς τῶν ἀνθρώπων, τὰ ἁμαρτήματα⸃ καὶ ⸂αἱ βλασφημίαι ὅσα ἐὰν⸃ βλασφημήσωσιν·
verses.translit: Amen lego umin oti panta afethisetai tois yiois ton anthropon, ta amartimata kai ai vlasfimiai osa ean vlasfimisosin*
verses.translation: Verily I say unto you, All sins shall be forgiven unto the sons of men, and blasphemies wherewith soever they shall blaspheme:

verses.original: ὃς δʼ ἂν βλασφημήσῃ εἰς τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, οὐκ ἔχει ἄφεσιν εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, ἀλλὰ ἔνοχός ἐστιν αἰωνίου ⸀ἁμαρτήματος.
verses.translit: os d' an vlasfimise eis to pneuma to agion, ouk ehei afesin eis ton aiona, alla enohos estin aionioy amartimatos.
verses.translation: But he that shall blaspheme against the Holy Ghost hath never forgiveness, but is in danger of eternal damnation:
