verses.original: καὶ ἐπετίμησεν αὐτοῖς ἵνα μηδενὶ λέγωσιν περὶ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai epetimisen autois ina mideni legosin peri autou.
verses.translation: And he charged them that they should tell no man of him.

verses.original: Καὶ ἤρξατο διδάσκειν αὐτοὺς ὅτι δεῖ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου πολλὰ παθεῖν καὶ ἀποδοκιμασθῆναι ⸀ὑπὸ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων καὶ τῶν ἀρχιερέων καὶ τῶν γραμματέων καὶ ἀποκτανθῆναι καὶ μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας ἀναστῆναι·
verses.translit: Kai erxato didaskein autous oti dei ton yion tou anthropoy polla pathein kai apodokimasthenai upo ton presvyteron kai ton arhiereon kai ton grammateon kai apoktanthenai kai meta treis emeras anastenai*
verses.translation: And he began to teach them, that the Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders, and of the chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again.

verses.original: καὶ παρρησίᾳ τὸν λόγον ἐλάλει. καὶ προσλαβόμενος ⸂ὁ Πέτρος αὐτὸν⸃ ἤρξατο ἐπιτιμᾶν αὐτῷ.
verses.translit: kai parrisia ton logon elalei. kai proslavomenos o Petros auton erxato epitiman auto.
verses.translation: And he spake that saying openly. And Peter took him, and began to rebuke him.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ἐπιστραφεὶς καὶ ἰδὼν τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ ἐπετίμησεν ⸀Πέτρῳ ⸂καὶ λέγει⸃· Ὕπαγε ὀπίσω μου, Σατανᾶ, ὅτι οὐ φρονεῖς τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ ἀλλὰ τὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων.
verses.translit: o de epistrafeis kai idon tous mathitas autou epetimisen Petro kai legei* Upage opiso moy, Satana, oti ou froneis ta tou theou alla ta ton anthropon.
verses.translation: But when he had turned about and looked on his disciples, he rebuked Peter, saying, Get thee behind me, Satan: for thou savourest not the things that be of God, but the things that be of men.

verses.original: Καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος τὸν ὄχλον σὺν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· ⸂Εἴ τις⸃ θέλει ὀπίσω μου ⸀ἐλθεῖν, ἀπαρνησάσθω ἑαυτὸν καὶ ἀράτω τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀκολουθείτω μοι.
verses.translit: Kai proskalesamenos ton ohlon sun tois mathitais autou eipen autois* Ei tis thelei opiso moy elthein, aparnisastho eayton kai arato ton stayron autou kai akoloytheito moi.
verses.translation: And when he had called the people unto him with his disciples also, he said unto them, Whosoever will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.

verses.original: ὃς γὰρ ⸀ἐὰν θέλῃ τὴν ⸂ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ⸃ σῶσαι ἀπολέσει αὐτήν· ὃς δʼ ἂν ⸀ἀπολέσει τὴν ⸄ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ⸅ ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ καὶ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου ⸀σώσει αὐτήν.
verses.translit: os gar ean thele ten psyhen autou sosai apolesei autin* os d' an apolesei ten psyhen autou eneken emou kai tou euaggelioy sosei autin.
verses.translation: For whosoever will save his life shall lose it; but whosoever shall lose his life for my sake and the gospel’s, the same shall save it.

verses.original: τί γὰρ ⸀ὠφελεῖ ⸀ἄνθρωπον ⸂κερδῆσαι τὸν κόσμον ὅλον καὶ ζημιωθῆναι⸃ τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ;
verses.translit: ti gar ofelei anthropon kerdesai ton kosmon olon kai zimiothenai ten psyhen autou;
verses.translation: For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?

verses.original: ⸂τί γὰρ⸃ ⸀δοῖ ἄνθρωπος ἀντάλλαγμα τῆς ψυχῆς αὐτοῦ;
verses.translit: ti gar doi anthropos antallagma tes psyhes autou;
verses.translation: Or what shall a man give in exchange for his soul?

verses.original: ὃς γὰρ ἐὰν ἐπαισχυνθῇ με καὶ τοὺς ἐμοὺς λόγους ἐν τῇ γενεᾷ ταύτῃ τῇ μοιχαλίδι καὶ ἁμαρτωλῷ, καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐπαισχυνθήσεται αὐτὸν ὅταν ἔλθῃ ἐν τῇ δόξῃ τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ μετὰ τῶν ἀγγέλων τῶν ἁγίων.
verses.translit: os gar ean epaishynthe me kai tous emous logoys en te genea tayte te moihalidi kai amartolo, kai o yios tou anthropoy epaishynthisetai auton otan elthe en te doxe tou patros autou meta ton aggelon ton agion.
verses.translation: Whosoever therefore shall be ashamed of me and of my words in this adulterous and sinful generation; of him also shall the Son of man be ashamed, when he cometh in the glory of his Father with the holy angels.

verses.original: καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι εἰσίν τινες ⸂τῶν ὧδε⸃ ἑστηκότων οἵτινες οὐ μὴ γεύσωνται θανάτου ἕως ἂν ἴδωσιν τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ ἐληλυθυῖαν ἐν δυνάμει.
verses.translit: kai elegen autois* Amen lego umin oti eisin tines ton ode estikoton oitines ou me geysontai thanatoy eos an idosin ten vasileian tou theou elilythyian en dynamei.
verses.translation: And he said unto them, Verily I say unto you, That there be some of them that stand here, which shall not taste of death, till they have seen the kingdom of God come with power.

verses.original: Καὶ μετὰ ἡμέρας ἓξ παραλαμβάνει ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὸν Πέτρον καὶ τὸν Ἰάκωβον ⸀καὶ Ἰωάννην, καὶ ἀναφέρει αὐτοὺς εἰς ὄρος ὑψηλὸν κατʼ ἰδίαν μόνους. καὶ μετεμορφώθη ἔμπροσθεν αὐτῶν,
verses.translit: Kai meta emeras ex paralamvanei o Iisous ton Petron kai ton Iakovon kai Ioannin, kai anaferei autous eis oros upsilon kat' idian monoys. kai metemorfothi emprosthen auton,
verses.translation: And after six days Jesus taketh with him Peter, and James, and John, and leadeth them up into an high mountain apart by themselves: and he was transfigured before them.

verses.original: καὶ τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ ⸀ἐγένετο στίλβοντα λευκὰ ⸀λίαν οἷα γναφεὺς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς οὐ δύναται ⸀οὕτως λευκᾶναι.
verses.translit: kai ta imatia autou egeneto stilvonta leyka lian oia gnafeus epi tes ges ou dynatai outos leykanai.
verses.translation: And his raiment became shining, exceeding white as snow; so as no fuller on earth can white them.

verses.original: καὶ ὤφθη αὐτοῖς Ἠλίας σὺν Μωϋσεῖ, καὶ ἦσαν συλλαλοῦντες τῷ Ἰησοῦ.
verses.translit: kai ofthi autois Elias sun Moysei, kai esan syllalountes to Iisou.
verses.translation: And there appeared unto them Elias with Moses: and they were talking with Jesus.

verses.original: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Πέτρος λέγει τῷ Ἰησοῦ· Ῥαββί, καλόν ἐστιν ἡμᾶς ὧδε εἶναι, καὶ ποιήσωμεν ⸂τρεῖς σκηνάς⸃, σοὶ μίαν καὶ Μωϋσεῖ μίαν καὶ Ἠλίᾳ μίαν.
verses.translit: kai apokritheis o Petros legei to Iisou* Ravvi, kalon estin emas ode einai, kai poiisomen treis skinas, soi mian kai Moysei mian kai Elia mian.
verses.translation: And Peter answered and said to Jesus, Master, it is good for us to be here: and let us make three tabernacles; one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias.

verses.original: οὐ γὰρ ᾔδει τί ⸀ἀποκριθῇ, ⸂ἔκφοβοι γὰρ ἐγένοντο⸃.
verses.translit: ou gar edei ti apokrithe, ekfovoi gar egenonto.
verses.translation: For he wist not what to say; for they were sore afraid.

verses.original: καὶ ἐγένετο νεφέλη ἐπισκιάζουσα αὐτοῖς, καὶ ⸀ἐγένετο φωνὴ ἐκ τῆς νεφέλης· Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός, ⸂ἀκούετε αὐτοῦ⸃.
verses.translit: kai egeneto nefeli episkiazoysa autois, kai egeneto fone ek tes nefelis* Outos estin o yios moy o agapitos, akoyete autou.
verses.translation: And there was a cloud that overshadowed them: and a voice came out of the cloud, saying, This is my beloved Son: hear him.

verses.original: καὶ ἐξάπινα περιβλεψάμενοι οὐκέτι οὐδένα εἶδον ⸂ἀλλὰ τὸν Ἰησοῦν μόνον μεθʼ ἑαυτῶν⸃.
verses.translit: kai exapina perivlepsamenoi ouketi oudena eidon alla ton Iisoun monon meth' eayton.
verses.translation: And suddenly, when they had looked round about, they saw no man any more, save Jesus only with themselves.

verses.original: ⸂Καὶ καταβαινόντων⸃ αὐτῶν ⸀ἐκ τοῦ ὄρους διεστείλατο αὐτοῖς ἵνα μηδενὶ ⸂ἃ εἶδον διηγήσωνται⸃, εἰ μὴ ὅταν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστῇ.
verses.translit: Kai katavainonton auton ek tou oroys diesteilato autois ina mideni a eidon diigisontai, ei me otan o yios tou anthropoy ek nekron anaste.
verses.translation: And as they came down from the mountain, he charged them that they should tell no man what things they had seen, till the Son of man were risen from the dead.

verses.original: καὶ τὸν λόγον ἐκράτησαν πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς συζητοῦντες τί ἐστιν τὸ ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστῆναι.
verses.translit: kai ton logon ekratisan pros eaytous syzitountes ti estin to ek nekron anastenai.
verses.translation: And they kept that saying with themselves, questioning one with another what the rising from the dead should mean.

verses.original: καὶ ἐπηρώτων αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Ὅτι λέγουσιν οἱ γραμματεῖς ὅτι Ἠλίαν δεῖ ἐλθεῖν πρῶτον;
verses.translit: kai epiroton auton legontes* Oti legoysin oi grammateis oti Elian dei elthein proton;
verses.translation: And they asked him, saying, Why say the scribes that Elias must first come?

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ⸀ἔφη αὐτοῖς· Ἠλίας μὲν ἐλθὼν πρῶτον ⸀ἀποκαθιστάνει πάντα, καὶ πῶς γέγραπται ἐπὶ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἵνα πολλὰ πάθῃ καὶ ⸀ἐξουδενηθῇ;
verses.translit: o de efi autois* Elias men elthon proton apokathistanei panta, kai pos gegraptai epi ton yion tou anthropoy ina polla pathe kai exoydenithe;
verses.translation: And he answered and told them, Elias verily cometh first, and restoreth all things; and how it is written of the Son of man, that he must suffer many things, and be set at nought.

verses.original: ἀλλὰ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι καὶ Ἠλίας ἐλήλυθεν, καὶ ἐποίησαν αὐτῷ ὅσα ⸀ἤθελον, καθὼς γέγραπται ἐπʼ αὐτόν.
verses.translit: alla lego umin oti kai Elias elilythen, kai epoiisan auto osa ethelon, kathos gegraptai ep' auton.
verses.translation: But I say unto you, That Elias is indeed come, and they have done unto him whatsoever they listed, as it is written of him.

verses.original: Καὶ ⸂ἐλθόντες πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς εἶδον⸃ ὄχλον πολὺν περὶ αὐτοὺς καὶ γραμματεῖς συζητοῦντας ⸂πρὸς αὐτούς⸃.
verses.translit: Kai elthontes pros tous mathitas eidon ohlon polun peri autous kai grammateis syzitountas pros autoys.
verses.translation: And when he came to his disciples, he saw a great multitude about them, and the scribes questioning with them.

verses.original: καὶ ⸀εὐθὺς πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος ⸂ἰδόντες αὐτὸν ἐξεθαμβήθησαν⸃, καὶ προστρέχοντες ἠσπάζοντο αὐτόν.
verses.translit: kai euthus pas o ohlos idontes auton exethamvithisan, kai prostrehontes espazonto auton.
verses.translation: And straightway all the people, when they beheld him, were greatly amazed, and running to him saluted him.

verses.original: καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν ⸀αὐτούς· Τί συζητεῖτε πρὸς ⸀αὑτούς;
verses.translit: kai epirotisen autoys* Ti syziteite pros autoys;
verses.translation: And he asked the scribes, What question ye with them?

verses.original: καὶ ⸂ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῷ εἷς ἐκ τοῦ ὄχλου⸃· Διδάσκαλε, ἤνεγκα τὸν υἱόν μου πρὸς σέ, ἔχοντα πνεῦμα ἄλαλον·
verses.translit: kai apekrithi auto eis ek tou ohloy* Didaskale, enegka ton yion moy pros se, ehonta pneuma alalon*
verses.translation: And one of the multitude answered and said, Master, I have brought unto thee my son, which hath a dumb spirit;

verses.original: καὶ ὅπου ⸀ἐὰν αὐτὸν καταλάβῃ ῥήσσει αὐτόν, καὶ ἀφρίζει καὶ τρίζει τοὺς ⸀ὀδόντας καὶ ξηραίνεται· καὶ εἶπα τοῖς μαθηταῖς σου ἵνα αὐτὸ ἐκβάλωσιν, καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυσαν.
verses.translit: kai opoy ean auton katalave Rissei auton, kai afrizei kai trizei tous odontas kai xirainetai* kai eipa tois mathitais soy ina auto ekvalosin, kai ouk ishysan.
verses.translation: And wheresoever he taketh him, he teareth him: and he foameth, and gnasheth with his teeth, and pineth away: and I spake to thy disciples that they should cast him out; and they could not.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς ⸀αὐτοῖς λέγει· Ὦ γενεὰ ἄπιστος, ἕως πότε πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἔσομαι; ἕως πότε ἀνέξομαι ὑμῶν; φέρετε αὐτὸν πρός με.
verses.translit: o de apokritheis autois legei* O genea apistos, eos pote pros umas esomai; eos pote anexomai umon; ferete auton pros me.
verses.translation: He answereth him, and saith, O faithless generation, how long shall I be with you? how long shall I suffer you? bring him unto me.

verses.original: καὶ ἤνεγκαν αὐτὸν πρὸς αὐτόν. καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτὸν ⸂τὸ πνεῦμα εὐθὺς⸃ ⸀συνεσπάραξεν αὐτόν, καὶ πεσὼν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἐκυλίετο ἀφρίζων.
verses.translit: kai enegkan auton pros auton. kai idon auton to pneuma euthus synesparaxen auton, kai peson epi tes ges ekylieto afrizon.
verses.translation: And they brought him unto him: and when he saw him, straightway the spirit tare him; and he fell on the ground, and wallowed foaming.

verses.original: καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ· Πόσος χρόνος ἐστὶν ὡς τοῦτο γέγονεν αὐτῷ; ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· ⸀Ἐκ παιδιόθεν·
verses.translit: kai epirotisen ton patera autou* Posos hronos estin os touto gegonen auto; o de eipen* Ek paidiothen*
verses.translation: And he asked his father, How long is it ago since this came unto him? And he said, Of a child.

verses.original: καὶ πολλάκις ⸂καὶ εἰς πῦρ αὐτὸν⸃ ἔβαλεν καὶ εἰς ὕδατα ἵνα ἀπολέσῃ αὐτόν· ἀλλʼ εἴ τι ⸀δύνῃ, βοήθησον ἡμῖν σπλαγχνισθεὶς ἐφʼ ἡμᾶς.
verses.translit: kai pollakis kai eis pur auton evalen kai eis udata ina apolese auton* all' ei ti dyne, voithison emin splaghnistheis ef' emas.
verses.translation: And ofttimes it hath cast him into the fire, and into the waters, to destroy him: but if thou canst do any thing, have compassion on us, and help us.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Τὸ Εἰ ⸀δύνῃ, πάντα δυνατὰ τῷ πιστεύοντι.
verses.translit: o de Iisous eipen auto* To Ei dyne, panta dynata to pisteyonti.
verses.translation: Jesus said unto him, If thou canst believe, all things are possible to him that believeth.

verses.original: ⸀εὐθὺς κράξας ὁ πατὴρ τοῦ ⸀παιδίου ἔλεγεν· ⸀Πιστεύω· βοήθει μου τῇ ἀπιστίᾳ.
verses.translit: euthus kraxas o pater tou paidioy elegen* Pisteyo* voithei moy te apistia.
verses.translation: And straightway the father of the child cried out, and said with tears, Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief.

verses.original: ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι ἐπισυντρέχει ὄχλος ἐπετίμησεν τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἀκαθάρτῳ λέγων αὐτῷ· Τὸ ⸂ἄλαλον καὶ κωφὸν πνεῦμα⸃, ἐγὼ ⸂ἐπιτάσσω σοι⸃, ἔξελθε ἐξ αὐτοῦ καὶ μηκέτι εἰσέλθῃς εἰς αὐτόν.
verses.translit: idon de o Iisous oti episyntrehei ohlos epetimisen to pneymati to akatharto legon auto* To alalon kai kofon pneuma, ego epitasso soi, exelthe ex autou kai miketi eiselthes eis auton.
verses.translation: When Jesus saw that the people came running together, he rebuked the foul spirit, saying unto him, Thou dumb and deaf spirit, I charge thee, come out of him, and enter no more into him.

verses.original: καὶ ⸂κράξας καὶ πολλὰ σπαράξας⸃ ἐξῆλθεν· καὶ ἐγένετο ὡσεὶ νεκρὸς ὥστε ⸀τοὺς πολλοὺς λέγειν ὅτι ἀπέθανεν.
verses.translit: kai kraxas kai polla sparaxas exelthen* kai egeneto osei nekros oste tous pollous legein oti apethanen.
verses.translation: And the spirit cried, and rent him sore, and came out of him: and he was as one dead; insomuch that many said, He is dead.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς κρατήσας ⸂τῆς χειρὸς αὐτοῦ⸃ ἤγειρεν αὐτόν, καὶ ἀνέστη.
verses.translit: o de Iisous kratisas tes heiros autou egeiren auton, kai anesti.
verses.translation: But Jesus took him by the hand, and lifted him up; and he arose.

verses.original: καὶ ⸂εἰσελθόντος αὐτοῦ⸃ εἰς οἶκον οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ⸂κατʼ ἰδίαν ἐπηρώτων αὐτόν⸃· Ὅτι ἡμεῖς οὐκ ἠδυνήθημεν ἐκβαλεῖν αὐτό;
verses.translit: kai eiselthontos autou eis oikon oi mathitai autou kat' idian epiroton auton* Oti emeis ouk edynithimen ekvalein auto;
verses.translation: And when he was come into the house, his disciples asked him privately, Why could not we cast him out?

verses.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τοῦτο τὸ γένος ἐν οὐδενὶ δύναται ἐξελθεῖν εἰ μὴ ἐν ⸀προσευχῇ.
verses.translit: kai eipen autois* Touto to genos en oudeni dynatai exelthein ei me en proseyhe.
verses.translation: And he said unto them, This kind can come forth by nothing, but by prayer and fasting.

verses.original: Κἀκεῖθεν ἐξελθόντες ⸀παρεπορεύοντο διὰ τῆς Γαλιλαίας, καὶ οὐκ ἤθελεν ἵνα τις γνοῖ·
verses.translit: Kakeithen exelthontes pareporeyonto dia tes Galilaias, kai ouk ethelen ina tis gnoi*
verses.translation: And they departed thence, and passed through Galilee; and he would not that any man should know it .

verses.original: ἐδίδασκεν γὰρ τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς ὅτι Ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδοται εἰς χεῖρας ἀνθρώπων, καὶ ἀποκτενοῦσιν αὐτόν, καὶ ἀποκτανθεὶς ⸂μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας⸃ ἀναστήσεται.
verses.translit: edidasken gar tous mathitas autou kai elegen autois oti O yios tou anthropoy paradidotai eis heiras anthropon, kai apoktenousin auton, kai apoktantheis meta treis emeras anastisetai.
verses.translation: For he taught his disciples, and said unto them, The Son of man is delivered into the hands of men, and they shall kill him; and after that he is killed, he shall rise the third day.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ ἠγνόουν τὸ ῥῆμα, καὶ ἐφοβοῦντο αὐτὸν ἐπερωτῆσαι.
verses.translit: oi de egnooyn to Rema, kai efovounto auton eperotesai.
verses.translation: But they understood not that saying, and were afraid to ask him.

verses.original: Καὶ ⸀ἦλθον εἰς Καφαρναούμ. καὶ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ γενόμενος ἐπηρώτα αὐτούς· Τί ἐν τῇ ⸀ὁδῷ διελογίζεσθε;
verses.translit: Kai elthon eis Kafarnaoym. kai en te oikia genomenos epirota autoys* Ti en te odo dielogizesthe;
verses.translation: And he came to Capernaum: and being in the house he asked them, What was it that ye disputed among yourselves by the way?

verses.original: οἱ δὲ ἐσιώπων, πρὸς ἀλλήλους γὰρ διελέχθησαν ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ τίς μείζων.
verses.translit: oi de esiopon, pros alliloys gar dielehthisan en te odo tis meizon.
verses.translation: But they held their peace: for by the way they had disputed among themselves, who should be the greatest.

verses.original: καὶ καθίσας ἐφώνησεν τοὺς δώδεκα καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Εἴ τις θέλει πρῶτος εἶναι ἔσται πάντων ἔσχατος καὶ πάντων διάκονος.
verses.translit: kai kathisas efonisen tous dodeka kai legei autois* Ei tis thelei protos einai estai panton eshatos kai panton diakonos.
verses.translation: And he sat down, and called the twelve, and saith unto them, If any man desire to be first, the same shall be last of all, and servant of all.

verses.original: καὶ λαβὼν παιδίον ἔστησεν αὐτὸ ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῶν καὶ ἐναγκαλισάμενος αὐτὸ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς·
verses.translit: kai lavon paidion estisen auto en meso auton kai enagkalisamenos auto eipen autois*
verses.translation: And he took a child, and set him in the midst of them: and when he had taken him in his arms, he said unto them,

verses.original: Ὃς ⸀ἂν ἓν τῶν τοιούτων παιδίων δέξηται ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου, ἐμὲ δέχεται· καὶ ὃς ⸁ἂν ἐμὲ ⸀δέχηται, οὐκ ἐμὲ δέχεται ἀλλὰ τὸν ἀποστείλαντά με.
verses.translit: Os an en ton toioyton paidion dexitai epi to onomati moy, eme dehetai* kai os an eme dehitai, ouk eme dehetai alla ton aposteilanta me.
verses.translation: Whosoever shall receive one of such children in my name, receiveth me: and whosoever shall receive me, receiveth not me, but him that sent me.

verses.original: ⸂Ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰωάννης⸃· Διδάσκαλε, εἴδομέν τινα ⸀ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί σου ἐκβάλλοντα δαιμόνια, ⸂καὶ ἐκωλύομεν αὐτόν, ὅτι οὐκ ἠκολούθει ἡμῖν⸃.
verses.translit: Efi auto o Ioannis* Didaskale, eidomen tina en to onomati soy ekvallonta daimonia, kai ekolyomen auton, oti ouk ekoloythei emin.
verses.translation: And John answered him, saying, Master, we saw one casting out devils in thy name, and he followeth not us: and we forbad him, because he followeth not us.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Μὴ κωλύετε αὐτόν, οὐδεὶς γάρ ἐστιν ὃς ποιήσει δύναμιν ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου καὶ δυνήσεται ταχὺ κακολογῆσαί με·
verses.translit: o de Iisous eipen* Me kolyete auton, oudeis gar estin os poiisei dynamin epi to onomati moy kai dynisetai tahu kakologesai me*
verses.translation: But Jesus said, Forbid him not: for there is no man which shall do a miracle in my name, that can lightly speak evil of me.

verses.original: ὃς γὰρ οὐκ ἔστιν καθʼ ⸂ἡμῶν, ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν⸃ ἐστιν.
verses.translit: os gar ouk estin kath' emon, uper emon estin.
verses.translation: For he that is not against us is on our part.

verses.original: Ὃς γὰρ ἂν ποτίσῃ ὑμᾶς ποτήριον ὕδατος ἐν ⸀ὀνόματι ὅτι χριστοῦ ἐστε, ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ⸀ὅτι οὐ μὴ ⸀ἀπολέσῃ τὸν μισθὸν αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: Os gar an potise umas potirion udatos en onomati oti hristou este, amen lego umin oti ou me apolese ton misthon autou.
verses.translation: For whosoever shall give you a cup of water to drink in my name, because ye belong to Christ, verily I say unto you, he shall not lose his reward.

verses.original: Καὶ ὃς ⸀ἂν σκανδαλίσῃ ἕνα τῶν μικρῶν ⸀τούτων τῶν πιστευόντων ⸂εἰς ἐμέ⸃, καλόν ἐστιν αὐτῷ μᾶλλον εἰ περίκειται ⸂μύλος ὀνικὸς⸃ περὶ τὸν τράχηλον αὐτοῦ καὶ βέβληται εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν.
verses.translit: Kai os an skandalise ena ton mikron toyton ton pisteyonton eis eme, kalon estin auto mallon ei perikeitai mylos onikos peri ton trahilon autou kai vevlitai eis ten thalassan.
verses.translation: And whosoever shall offend one of these little ones that believe in me, it is better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and he were cast into the sea.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐὰν ⸀σκανδαλίζῃ σε ἡ χείρ σου, ἀπόκοψον αὐτήν· καλόν ⸂ἐστίν σε⸃ κυλλὸν ⸂εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν ζωὴν⸃ ἢ τὰς δύο χεῖρας ἔχοντα ἀπελθεῖν εἰς τὴν γέενναν, εἰς τὸ πῦρ τὸ ⸀ἄσβεστον.
verses.translit: Kai ean skandalize se e heir soy, apokopson autin* kalon estin se kyllon eiselthein eis ten zoen e tas dyo heiras ehonta apelthein eis ten geennan, eis to pur to asveston.
verses.translation: And if thy hand offend thee, cut it off: it is better for thee to enter into life maimed, than having two hands to go into hell, into the fire that never shall be quenched:
Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.

verses.original: καὶ ἐὰν ὁ πούς σου σκανδαλίζῃ σε, ἀπόκοψον αὐτόν· καλόν ἐστίν ⸀σε εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν ζωὴν χωλὸν ἢ τοὺς δύο πόδας ἔχοντα βληθῆναι εἰς τὴν ⸀γέενναν.
verses.translit: kai ean o poys soy skandalize se, apokopson auton* kalon estin se eiselthein eis ten zoen holon e tous dyo podas ehonta vlithenai eis ten geennan.
verses.translation: And if thy foot offend thee, cut it off: it is better for thee to enter halt into life, than having two feet to be cast into hell, into the fire that never shall be quenched:
Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.

verses.original: καὶ ἐὰν ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου σκανδαλίζῃ σε, ἔκβαλε αὐτόν· καλόν ⸀σέ ἐστιν μονόφθαλμον εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ ἢ δύο ὀφθαλμοὺς ἔχοντα βληθῆναι εἰς ⸀τὴν ⸀γέενναν,
verses.translit: kai ean o ofthalmos soy skandalize se, ekvale auton* kalon se estin monofthalmon eiselthein eis ten vasileian tou theou e dyo ofthalmous ehonta vlithenai eis ten geennan,
verses.translation: And if thine eye offend thee, pluck it out: it is better for thee to enter into the kingdom of God with one eye, than having two eyes to be cast into hell fire:

verses.original: ὅπου ὁ σκώληξ αὐτῶν οὐ τελευτᾷ καὶ τὸ πῦρ οὐ σβέννυται.
verses.translit: opoy o skolix auton ou teleyta kai to pur ou svennytai.
verses.translation: Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.

verses.original: Πᾶς γὰρ πυρὶ ⸀ἁλισθήσεται.
verses.translit: Pas gar pyri alisthisetai.
verses.translation: For every one shall be salted with fire, and every sacrifice shall be salted with salt.

verses.original: καλὸν τὸ ἅλας· ἐὰν δὲ τὸ ἅλας ἄναλον γένηται, ἐν τίνι αὐτὸ ἀρτύσετε; ἔχετε ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ⸀ἅλα, καὶ εἰρηνεύετε ἐν ἀλλήλοις.
verses.translit: kalon to alas* ean de to alas analon genitai, en tini auto artysete; ehete en eaytois ala, kai eirineyete en allilois.
verses.translation: Salt is good: but if the salt have lost his saltness, wherewith will ye season it? Have salt in yourselves, and have peace one with another.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐκεῖθεν ἀναστὰς ἔρχεται εἰς τὰ ὅρια τῆς Ἰουδαίας ⸀καὶ πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου, καὶ συμπορεύονται πάλιν ὄχλοι πρὸς αὐτόν, καὶ ὡς εἰώθει πάλιν ἐδίδασκεν αὐτούς.
verses.translit: Kai ekeithen anastas erhetai eis ta oria tes Ioydaias kai peran tou Iordanoy, kai symporeyontai palin ohloi pros auton, kai os eiothei palin edidasken autoys.
verses.translation: And he arose from thence, and cometh into the coasts of Judæa by the farther side of Jordan: and the people resort unto him again; and, as he was wont, he taught them again.

verses.original: ⸀Καὶ ⸀ἐπηρώτων αὐτὸν εἰ ἔξεστιν ἀνδρὶ γυναῖκα ἀπολῦσαι, πειράζοντες αὐτόν.
verses.translit: Kai epiroton auton ei exestin andri gynaika apolusai, peirazontes auton.
verses.translation: And the Pharisees came to him, and asked him, Is it lawful for a man to put away his wife? tempting him.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τί ὑμῖν ἐνετείλατο Μωϋσῆς;
verses.translit: o de apokritheis eipen autois* Ti umin eneteilato Moyses;
verses.translation: And he answered and said unto them, What did Moses command you?

verses.original: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· ⸂Ἐπέτρεψεν Μωϋσῆς⸃ βιβλίον ἀποστασίου γράψαι καὶ ἀπολῦσαι.
verses.translit: oi de eipan* Epetrepsen Moyses vivlion apostasioy grapsai kai apolusai.
verses.translation: And they said, Moses suffered to write a bill of divorcement, and to put her away.

verses.original: ⸂ὁ δὲ⸃ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πρὸς τὴν σκληροκαρδίαν ὑμῶν ἔγραψεν ὑμῖν τὴν ἐντολὴν ταύτην·
verses.translit: o de Iisous eipen autois* Pros ten sklirokardian umon egrapsen umin ten entolen taytin*
verses.translation: And Jesus answered and said unto them, For the hardness of your heart he wrote you this precept.

verses.original: ἀπὸ δὲ ἀρχῆς κτίσεως ἄρσεν καὶ θῆλυ ἐποίησεν ⸀αὐτούς·
verses.translit: apo de arhes ktiseos arsen kai thely epoiisen autoys*
verses.translation: But from the beginning of the creation God made them male and female.

verses.original: ἕνεκεν τούτου καταλείψει ἄνθρωπος τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν μητέρα ⸂καὶ προσκολληθήσεται πρὸς τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ⸃,
verses.translit: eneken toytoy kataleipsei anthropos ton patera autou kai ten mitera kai proskollithisetai pros ten gynaika autou,
verses.translation: For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and cleave to his wife;

verses.original: καὶ ἔσονται οἱ δύο εἰς σάρκα μίαν· ὥστε οὐκέτι εἰσὶν δύο ἀλλὰ μία σάρξ·
verses.translit: kai esontai oi dyo eis sarka mian* oste ouketi eisin dyo alla mia sarx*
verses.translation: And they twain shall be one flesh: so then they are no more twain, but one flesh.

verses.original: ὃ οὖν ὁ θεὸς συνέζευξεν ἄνθρωπος μὴ χωριζέτω.
verses.translit: o oun o theos synezeyxen anthropos me horizeto.
verses.translation: What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder.

verses.original: Καὶ ⸂εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν⸃ πάλιν οἱ μαθηταὶ ⸂περὶ τούτου⸃ ⸀ἐπηρώτων αὐτόν.
verses.translit: Kai eis ten oikian palin oi mathitai peri toytoy epiroton auton.
verses.translation: And in the house his disciples asked him again of the same matter .

verses.original: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ὃς ⸀ἂν ἀπολύσῃ τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ καὶ γαμήσῃ ἄλλην μοιχᾶται ἐπʼ αὐτήν,
verses.translit: kai legei autois* Os an apolyse ten gynaika autou kai gamise allin moihatai ep' autin,
verses.translation: And he saith unto them, Whosoever shall put away his wife, and marry another, committeth adultery against her.

verses.original: καὶ ἐὰν ⸂αὐτὴ ἀπολύσασα τὸν ἄνδρα αὐτῆς γαμήσῃ ἄλλον⸃ μοιχᾶται.
verses.translit: kai ean aute apolysasa ton andra autes gamise allon moihatai.
verses.translation: And if a woman shall put away her husband, and be married to another, she committeth adultery.

verses.original: Καὶ προσέφερον αὐτῷ παιδία ἵνα ⸂αὐτῶν ἅψηται⸃· οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ ⸂ἐπετίμησαν αὐτοῖς⸃.
verses.translit: Kai proseferon auto paidia ina auton apsitai* oi de mathitai epetimisan autois.
verses.translation: And they brought young children to him, that he should touch them: and his disciples rebuked those that brought them .

verses.original: ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἠγανάκτησεν καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἄφετε τὰ παιδία ἔρχεσθαι πρός με, μὴ κωλύετε αὐτά, τῶν γὰρ τοιούτων ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: idon de o Iisous eganaktisen kai eipen autois* Afete ta paidia erhesthai pros me, me kolyete auta, ton gar toioyton estin e vasileia tou theou.
verses.translation: But when Jesus saw it , he was much displeased, and said unto them, Suffer the little children to come unto me, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God.

verses.original: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ὃς ⸀ἂν μὴ δέξηται τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ ὡς παιδίον, οὐ μὴ εἰσέλθῃ εἰς αὐτήν.
verses.translit: amen lego umin, os an me dexitai ten vasileian tou theou os paidion, ou me eiselthe eis autin.
verses.translation: Verily I say unto you, Whosoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a little child, he shall not enter therein.

verses.original: καὶ ἐναγκαλισάμενος αὐτὰ ⸂κατευλόγει τιθεὶς τὰς χεῖρας ἐπʼ αὐτά⸃.
verses.translit: kai enagkalisamenos auta kateylogei titheis tas heiras ep' auta.
verses.translation: And he took them up in his arms, put his hands upon them, and blessed them.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐκπορευομένου αὐτοῦ εἰς ὁδὸν προσδραμὼν εἷς καὶ γονυπετήσας αὐτὸν ἐπηρώτα αὐτόν· Διδάσκαλε ἀγαθέ, τί ποιήσω ἵνα ζωὴν αἰώνιον κληρονομήσω;
verses.translit: Kai ekporeyomenoy autou eis odon prosdramon eis kai gonypetisas auton epirota auton* Didaskale agathe, ti poiiso ina zoen aionion klironomiso;
verses.translation: And when he was gone forth into the way, there came one running, and kneeled to him, and asked him, Good Master, what shall I do that I may inherit eternal life?

verses.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Τί με λέγεις ἀγαθόν; οὐδεὶς ἀγαθὸς εἰ μὴ εἷς ὁ θεός.
verses.translit: o de Iisous eipen auto* Ti me legeis agathon; oudeis agathos ei me eis o theos.
verses.translation: And Jesus said unto him, Why callest thou me good? there is none good but one, that is , God.

verses.original: τὰς ἐντολὰς οἶδας· Μὴ ⸂φονεύσῃς, Μὴ μοιχεύσῃς⸃, Μὴ κλέψῃς, Μὴ ψευδομαρτυρήσῃς, Μὴ ἀποστερήσῃς, Τίμα τὸν πατέρα σου καὶ τὴν μητέρα.
verses.translit: tas entolas oidas* Me foneyses, Me moiheyses, Me klepses, Me pseydomartyrises, Me aposterises, Tima ton patera soy kai ten mitera.
verses.translation: Thou knowest the commandments, Do not commit adultery, Do not kill, Do not steal, Do not bear false witness, Defraud not, Honour thy father and mother.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ⸀ἔφη αὐτῷ· Διδάσκαλε, ταῦτα πάντα ἐφυλαξάμην ἐκ νεότητός μου.
verses.translit: o de efi auto* Didaskale, tauta panta efylaxamin ek neotitos moy.
verses.translation: And he answered and said unto him, Master, all these have I observed from my youth.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἐμβλέψας αὐτῷ ἠγάπησεν αὐτὸν καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἕν ⸀σε ὑστερεῖ· ὕπαγε ὅσα ἔχεις πώλησον καὶ δὸς ⸀τοῖς πτωχοῖς, καὶ ἕξεις θησαυρὸν ἐν οὐρανῷ, καὶ δεῦρο ἀκολούθει ⸀μοι.
verses.translit: o de Iisous emvlepsas auto egapisen auton kai eipen auto* En se usterei* upage osa eheis polison kai dos tois ptohois, kai exeis thisayron en ourano, kai deuro akoloythei moi.
verses.translation: Then Jesus beholding him loved him, and said unto him, One thing thou lackest: go thy way, sell whatsoever thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come, take up the cross, and follow me.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ στυγνάσας ἐπὶ τῷ λόγῳ ἀπῆλθεν λυπούμενος, ἦν γὰρ ἔχων κτήματα πολλά.
verses.translit: o de stygnasas epi to logo apelthen lypoymenos, en gar ehon ktimata polla.
verses.translation: And he was sad at that saying, and went away grieved: for he had great possessions.

verses.original: Καὶ περιβλεψάμενος ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγει τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ· Πῶς δυσκόλως οἱ τὰ χρήματα ἔχοντες εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ εἰσελεύσονται.
verses.translit: Kai perivlepsamenos o Iisous legei tois mathitais autou* Pos dyskolos oi ta hrimata ehontes eis ten vasileian tou theou eiseleysontai.
verses.translation: And Jesus looked round about, and saith unto his disciples, How hardly shall they that have riches enter into the kingdom of God!

verses.original: οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ ἐθαμβοῦντο ἐπὶ τοῖς λόγοις αὐτοῦ. ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς πάλιν ἀποκριθεὶς λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τέκνα, πῶς δύσκολόν ⸀ἐστιν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ εἰσελθεῖν·
verses.translit: oi de mathitai ethamvounto epi tois logois autou. o de Iisous palin apokritheis legei autois* Tekna, pos dyskolon estin eis ten vasileian tou theou eiselthein*
verses.translation: And the disciples were astonished at his words. But Jesus answereth again, and saith unto them, Children, how hard is it for them that trust in riches to enter into the kingdom of God!

verses.original: εὐκοπώτερόν ἐστιν κάμηλον διὰ ⸂τῆς τρυμαλιᾶς τῆς⸃ ῥαφίδος ⸀διελθεῖν ἢ πλούσιον εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ εἰσελθεῖν.
verses.translit: eukopoteron estin kamilon dia tes trymalias tes Rafidos dielthein e ploysion eis ten vasileian tou theou eiselthein.
verses.translation: It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ περισσῶς ἐξεπλήσσοντο λέγοντες πρὸς ⸀ἑαυτούς· Καὶ τίς δύναται σωθῆναι;
verses.translit: oi de perissos exeplissonto legontes pros eaytoys* Kai tis dynatai sothenai;
verses.translation: And they were astonished out of measure, saying among themselves, Who then can be saved?

verses.original: ⸀ἐμβλέψας αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγει· Παρὰ ἀνθρώποις ἀδύνατον ἀλλʼ οὐ παρὰ θεῷ, πάντα γὰρ ⸀δυνατὰ παρὰ τῷ θεῷ.
verses.translit: emvlepsas autois o Iisous legei* Para anthropois adynaton all' ou para theo, panta gar dynata para to theo.
verses.translation: And Jesus looking upon them saith, With men it is impossible, but not with God: for with God all things are possible.

verses.original: Ἤρξατο ⸂λέγειν ὁ Πέτρος⸃ αὐτῷ· Ἰδοὺ ἡμεῖς ἀφήκαμεν πάντα καὶ ⸀ἠκολουθήκαμέν σοι.
verses.translit: Erxato legein o Petros auto* Idou emeis afikamen panta kai ekoloythikamen soi.
verses.translation: Then Peter began to say unto him, Lo, we have left all, and have followed thee.

verses.original: ⸂ἔφη ὁ Ἰησοῦς⸃· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐδείς ἐστιν ὃς ἀφῆκεν οἰκίαν ἢ ἀδελφοὺς ἢ ἀδελφὰς ἢ ⸂μητέρα ἢ πατέρα⸃ ἢ τέκνα ἢ ἀγροὺς ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ καὶ ἕνεκεν τοῦ εὐαγγελίου,
verses.translit: efi o Iisous* Amen lego umin, oudeis estin os afeken oikian e adelfous e adelfas e mitera e patera e tekna e agrous eneken emou kai eneken tou euaggelioy,
verses.translation: And Jesus answered and said, Verily I say unto you, There is no man that hath left house, or brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands, for my sake, and the gospel’s,

verses.original: ἐὰν μὴ λάβῃ ἑκατονταπλασίονα νῦν ἐν τῷ καιρῷ τούτῳ οἰκίας καὶ ἀδελφοὺς καὶ ἀδελφὰς καὶ ⸀μητέρας καὶ τέκνα καὶ ἀγροὺς μετὰ διωγμῶν, καὶ ἐν τῷ αἰῶνι τῷ ἐρχομένῳ ζωὴν αἰώνιον.
verses.translit: ean me lave ekatontaplasiona nun en to kairo toyto oikias kai adelfous kai adelfas kai miteras kai tekna kai agrous meta diogmon, kai en to aioni to erhomeno zoen aionion.
verses.translation: But he shall receive an hundredfold now in this time, houses, and brethren, and sisters, and mothers, and children, and lands, with persecutions; and in the world to come eternal life.

verses.original: πολλοὶ δὲ ἔσονται πρῶτοι ἔσχατοι καὶ ⸀οἱ ἔσχατοι πρῶτοι.
verses.translit: polloi de esontai protoi eshatoi kai oi eshatoi protoi.
verses.translation: But many that are first shall be last; and the last first.

verses.original: Ἦσαν δὲ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ ἀναβαίνοντες εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα, καὶ ἦν προάγων αὐτοὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς, καὶ ἐθαμβοῦντο, ⸂οἱ δὲ⸃ ἀκολουθοῦντες ἐφοβοῦντο. καὶ παραλαβὼν πάλιν τοὺς δώδεκα ἤρξατο αὐτοῖς λέγειν τὰ μέλλοντα αὐτῷ συμβαίνειν
verses.translit: Esan de en te odo anavainontes eis Ierosolyma, kai en proagon autous o Iisous, kai ethamvounto, oi de akoloythountes efovounto. kai paralavon palin tous dodeka erxato autois legein ta mellonta auto symvainein
verses.translation: And they were in the way going up to Jerusalem; and Jesus went before them: and they were amazed; and as they followed, they were afraid. And he took again the twelve, and began to tell them what things should happen unto him,

verses.original: ὅτι Ἰδοὺ ἀναβαίνομεν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα, καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδοθήσεται τοῖς ἀρχιερεῦσιν καὶ ⸀τοῖς γραμματεῦσιν, καὶ κατακρινοῦσιν αὐτὸν θανάτῳ καὶ παραδώσουσιν αὐτὸν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν
verses.translit: oti Idou anavainomen eis Ierosolyma, kai o yios tou anthropoy paradothisetai tois arhiereusin kai tois grammateusin, kai katakrinousin auton thanato kai paradosoysin auton tois ethnesin
verses.translation: Saying , Behold, we go up to Jerusalem; and the Son of man shall be delivered unto the chief priests, and unto the scribes; and they shall condemn him to death, and shall deliver him to the Gentiles:

verses.original: καὶ ἐμπαίξουσιν αὐτῷ καὶ ⸂ἐμπτύσουσιν αὐτῷ καὶ μαστιγώσουσιν αὐτὸν⸃ καὶ ⸀ἀποκτενοῦσιν, καὶ ⸂μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας⸃ ἀναστήσεται.
verses.translit: kai empaixoysin auto kai emptysoysin auto kai mastigosoysin auton kai apoktenousin, kai meta treis emeras anastisetai.
verses.translation: And they shall mock him, and shall scourge him, and shall spit upon him, and shall kill him: and the third day he shall rise again.

verses.original: Καὶ προσπορεύονται αὐτῷ Ἰάκωβος καὶ Ἰωάννης ⸀οἱ υἱοὶ Ζεβεδαίου λέγοντες ⸀αὐτῷ· Διδάσκαλε, θέλομεν ἵνα ὃ ἐὰν αἰτήσωμέν ⸀σε ποιήσῃς ἡμῖν.
verses.translit: Kai prosporeyontai auto Iakovos kai Ioannis oi yioi Zevedaioy legontes auto* Didaskale, thelomen ina o ean aitisomen se poiises emin.
verses.translation: And James and John, the sons of Zebedee, come unto him, saying, Master, we would that thou shouldest do for us whatsoever we shall desire.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τί θέλετε ⸀ποιήσω ὑμῖν;
verses.translit: o de eipen autois* Ti thelete poiiso umin;
verses.translation: And he said unto them, What would ye that I should do for you?

verses.original: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Δὸς ἡμῖν ἵνα εἷς ⸂σου ἐκ δεξιῶν⸃ καὶ εἷς ἐξ ⸀ἀριστερῶν καθίσωμεν ἐν τῇ δόξῃ σου.
verses.translit: oi de eipan auto* Dos emin ina eis soy ek dexion kai eis ex aristeron kathisomen en te doxe soy.
verses.translation: They said unto him, Grant unto us that we may sit, one on thy right hand, and the other on thy left hand, in thy glory.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Οὐκ οἴδατε τί αἰτεῖσθε· δύνασθε πιεῖν τὸ ποτήριον ὃ ἐγὼ πίνω, ⸀ἢ τὸ βάπτισμα ὃ ἐγὼ βαπτίζομαι βαπτισθῆναι;
verses.translit: o de Iisous eipen autois* Ouk oidate ti aiteisthe* dynasthe piein to potirion o ego pino, e to vaptisma o ego vaptizomai vaptisthenai;
verses.translation: But Jesus said unto them, Ye know not what ye ask: can ye drink of the cup that I drink of? and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with?

verses.original: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Δυνάμεθα. ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· ⸀Τὸ ποτήριον ὃ ἐγὼ πίνω πίεσθε καὶ τὸ βάπτισμα ὃ ἐγὼ βαπτίζομαι βαπτισθήσεσθε,
verses.translit: oi de eipan auto* Dynametha. o de Iisous eipen autois* To potirion o ego pino piesthe kai to vaptisma o ego vaptizomai vaptisthisesthe,
verses.translation: And they said unto him, We can. And Jesus said unto them, Ye shall indeed drink of the cup that I drink of; and with the baptism that I am baptized withal shall ye be baptized:

verses.original: τὸ δὲ καθίσαι ἐκ δεξιῶν μου ⸀ἢ ἐξ εὐωνύμων οὐκ ἔστιν ἐμὸν δοῦναι, ἀλλʼ οἷς ἡτοίμασται.
verses.translit: to de kathisai ek dexion moy e ex euonymon ouk estin emon dounai, all' ois etoimastai.
verses.translation: But to sit on my right hand and on my left hand is not mine to give; but it shall be given to them for whom it is prepared.

verses.original: Καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ δέκα ἤρξαντο ἀγανακτεῖν περὶ Ἰακώβου καὶ Ἰωάννου.
verses.translit: Kai akoysantes oi deka erxanto aganaktein peri Iakovoy kai Ioannoy.
verses.translation: And when the ten heard it , they began to be much displeased with James and John.

verses.original: ⸂καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος αὐτοὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς⸃ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Οἴδατε ὅτι οἱ δοκοῦντες ἄρχειν τῶν ἐθνῶν κατακυριεύουσιν αὐτῶν καὶ οἱ μεγάλοι αὐτῶν κατεξουσιάζουσιν αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: kai proskalesamenos autous o Iisous legei autois* Oidate oti oi dokountes arhein ton ethnon katakyrieyoysin auton kai oi megaloi auton katexoysiazoysin auton.
verses.translation: But Jesus called them to him , and saith unto them, Ye know that they which are accounted to rule over the Gentiles exercise lordship over them; and their great ones exercise authority upon them.

verses.original: οὐχ οὕτως δέ ⸀ἐστιν ἐν ὑμῖν· ἀλλʼ ὃς ⸀ἂν θέλῃ ⸂μέγας γενέσθαι⸃ ἐν ὑμῖν, ἔσται ὑμῶν διάκονος,
verses.translit: ouh outos de estin en umin* all' os an thele megas genesthai en umin, estai umon diakonos,
verses.translation: But so shall it not be among you: but whosoever will be great among you, shall be your minister:

verses.original: καὶ ὃς ⸀ἂν θέλῃ ⸂ἐν ὑμῖν εἶναι⸃ πρῶτος, ἔσται πάντων δοῦλος·
verses.translit: kai os an thele en umin einai protos, estai panton doulos*
verses.translation: And whosoever of you will be the chiefest, shall be servant of all.

verses.original: καὶ γὰρ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου οὐκ ἦλθεν διακονηθῆναι ἀλλὰ διακονῆσαι καὶ δοῦναι τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ λύτρον ἀντὶ πολλῶν.
verses.translit: kai gar o yios tou anthropoy ouk elthen diakonithenai alla diakonesai kai dounai ten psyhen autou lytron anti pollon.
verses.translation: For even the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.

verses.original: Καὶ ἔρχονται εἰς Ἰεριχώ. καὶ ἐκπορευομένου αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ Ἰεριχὼ καὶ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ καὶ ὄχλου ἱκανοῦ ⸀ὁ υἱὸς Τιμαίου Βαρτιμαῖος ⸀τυφλὸς ⸂προσαίτης ἐκάθητο παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν⸃.
verses.translit: Kai erhontai eis Ieriho. kai ekporeyomenoy autou apo Ieriho kai ton mathiton autou kai ohloy ikanou o yios Timaioy Vartimaios tyflos prosaitis ekathito para ten odon.
verses.translation: And they came to Jericho: and as he went out of Jericho with his disciples and a great number of people, blind Bartimæus, the son of Timæus, sat by the highway side begging.

verses.original: καὶ ἀκούσας ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ὁ ⸀Ναζαρηνός ἐστιν ἤρξατο κράζειν καὶ λέγειν· ⸀Υἱὲ Δαυὶδ Ἰησοῦ, ἐλέησόν με.
verses.translit: kai akoysas oti Iisous o Nazarinos estin erxato krazein kai legein* Yie Dayid Iisou, eleison me.
verses.translation: And when he heard that it was Jesus of Nazareth, he began to cry out, and say, Jesus, thou Son of David, have mercy on me.

verses.original: καὶ ἐπετίμων αὐτῷ πολλοὶ ἵνα σιωπήσῃ· ὁ δὲ πολλῷ μᾶλλον ἔκραζεν· Υἱὲ Δαυίδ, ἐλέησόν με.
verses.translit: kai epetimon auto polloi ina siopise* o de pollo mallon ekrazen* Yie Dayid, eleison me.
verses.translation: And many charged him that he should hold his peace: but he cried the more a great deal, Thou Son of David, have mercy on me.

verses.original: καὶ στὰς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· ⸂Φωνήσατε αὐτόν⸃. καὶ φωνοῦσι τὸν τυφλὸν λέγοντες αὐτῷ· Θάρσει, ⸀ἔγειρε, φωνεῖ σε.
verses.translit: kai stas o Iisous eipen* Fonisate auton. kai fonousi ton tyflon legontes auto* Tharsei, egeire, fonei se.
verses.translation: And Jesus stood still, and commanded him to be called. And they call the blind man, saying unto him, Be of good comfort, rise; he calleth thee.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ἀποβαλὼν τὸ ἱμάτιον αὐτοῦ ⸀ἀναπηδήσας ἦλθεν πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν.
verses.translit: o de apovalon to imation autou anapidisas elthen pros ton Iisoun.
verses.translation: And he, casting away his garment, rose, and came to Jesus.

verses.original: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ⸂αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν⸃· Τί ⸂σοι θέλεις ποιήσω⸃; ὁ δὲ τυφλὸς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ραββουνι, ἵνα ἀναβλέψω.
verses.translit: kai apokritheis auto o Iisous eipen* Ti soi theleis poiiso; o de tyflos eipen auto* Ravvoyni, ina anavlepso.
verses.translation: And Jesus answered and said unto him, What wilt thou that I should do unto thee? The blind man said unto him, Lord, that I might receive my sight.

verses.original: ⸂καὶ ὁ⸃ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ὕπαγε, ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε. καὶ ⸀εὐθὺς ἀνέβλεψεν, καὶ ἠκολούθει ⸀αὐτῷ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ.
verses.translit: kai o Iisous eipen auto* Upage, e pistis soy sesoken se. kai euthus anevlepsen, kai ekoloythei auto en te odo.
verses.translation: And Jesus said unto him, Go thy way; thy faith hath made thee whole. And immediately he received his sight, and followed Jesus in the way.

verses.original: Καὶ ὅτε ἐγγίζουσιν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα εἰς Βηθφαγὴ καὶ Βηθανίαν πρὸς τὸ Ὄρος τῶν Ἐλαιῶν, ἀποστέλλει δύο τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ
verses.translit: Kai ote eggizoysin eis Ierosolyma eis Vithfage kai Vithanian pros to Oros ton Elaion, apostellei dyo ton mathiton autou
verses.translation: And when they came nigh to Jerusalem, unto Bethphage and Bethany, at the mount of Olives, he sendeth forth two of his disciples,

verses.original: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ὑπάγετε εἰς τὴν κώμην τὴν κατέναντι ὑμῶν, καὶ ⸀εὐθὺς εἰσπορευόμενοι εἰς αὐτὴν εὑρήσετε πῶλον δεδεμένον ἐφʼ ὃν οὐδεὶς ⸀οὔπω ἀνθρώπων ⸀ἐκάθισεν· ⸂λύσατε αὐτὸν καὶ φέρετε⸃.
verses.translit: kai legei autois* Upagete eis ten komin ten katenanti umon, kai euthus eisporeyomenoi eis auten eurisete polon dedemenon ef' on oudeis oupo anthropon ekathisen* lysate auton kai ferete.
verses.translation: And saith unto them, Go your way into the village over against you: and as soon as ye be entered into it, ye shall find a colt tied, whereon never man sat; loose him, and bring him .

verses.original: καὶ ἐάν τις ὑμῖν εἴπῃ· Τί ποιεῖτε τοῦτο; εἴπατε ⸀ὅτι Ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ χρείαν ἔχει· καὶ ⸀εὐθὺς αὐτὸν ἀποστέλλει ⸀πάλιν ὧδε.
verses.translit: kai ean tis umin eipe* Ti poieite touto; eipate oti O kyrios autou hreian ehei* kai euthus auton apostellei palin ode.
verses.translation: And if any man say unto you, Why do ye this? say ye that the Lord hath need of him; and straightway he will send him hither.

verses.original: ⸂καὶ ἀπῆλθον⸃ καὶ εὗρον πῶλον δεδεμένον ⸀πρὸς θύραν ἔξω ἐπὶ τοῦ ἀμφόδου, καὶ λύουσιν αὐτόν.
verses.translit: kai apelthon kai euron polon dedemenon pros thyran exo epi tou amfodoy, kai lyoysin auton.
verses.translation: And they went their way, and found the colt tied by the door without in a place where two ways met; and they loose him.

verses.original: καί τινες τῶν ἐκεῖ ἑστηκότων ἔλεγον αὐτοῖς· Τί ποιεῖτε λύοντες τὸν πῶλον;
verses.translit: kai tines ton ekei estikoton elegon autois* Ti poieite lyontes ton polon;
verses.translation: And certain of them that stood there said unto them, What do ye, loosing the colt?

verses.original: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτοῖς καθὼς ⸀εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς· καὶ ἀφῆκαν αὐτούς.
verses.translit: oi de eipan autois kathos eipen o Iisous* kai afekan autoys.
verses.translation: And they said unto them even as Jesus had commanded: and they let them go.

verses.original: καὶ ⸀φέρουσιν τὸν πῶλον πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν, καὶ ⸀ἐπιβάλλουσιν αὐτῷ τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτῶν, καὶ ἐκάθισεν ἐπʼ ⸀αὐτόν.
verses.translit: kai feroysin ton polon pros ton Iisoun, kai epivalloysin auto ta imatia auton, kai ekathisen ep' auton.
verses.translation: And they brought the colt to Jesus, and cast their garments on him; and he sat upon him.

verses.original: ⸂καὶ πολλοὶ⸃ τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτῶν ἔστρωσαν εἰς τὴν ὁδόν, ἄλλοι δὲ στιβάδας ⸂κόψαντες ἐκ τῶν ἀγρῶν⸃.
verses.translit: kai polloi ta imatia auton estrosan eis ten odon, alloi de stivadas kopsantes ek ton agron.
verses.translation: And many spread their garments in the way: and others cut down branches off the trees, and strawed them in the way.

verses.original: καὶ οἱ προάγοντες καὶ οἱ ἀκολουθοῦντες ⸀ἔκραζον· Ὡσαννά· Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι κυρίου·
verses.translit: kai oi proagontes kai oi akoloythountes ekrazon* Osanna* Eulogimenos o erhomenos en onomati kyrioy*
verses.translation: And they that went before, and they that followed, cried, saying, Hosanna; Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord:

verses.original: Εὐλογημένη ἡ ἐρχομένη ⸀βασιλεία τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν Δαυίδ· Ὡσαννὰ ἐν τοῖς ὑψίστοις.
verses.translit: Eulogimeni e erhomeni vasileia tou patros emon Dayid* Osanna en tois upsistois.
verses.translation: Blessed be the kingdom of our father David, that cometh in the name of the Lord: Hosanna in the highest.

verses.original: Καὶ εἰσῆλθεν εἰς ⸀Ἱεροσόλυμα εἰς τὸ ἱερόν· καὶ περιβλεψάμενος πάντα ⸀ὀψὲ ἤδη οὔσης τῆς ὥρας ἐξῆλθεν εἰς Βηθανίαν μετὰ τῶν δώδεκα.
verses.translit: Kai eiselthen eis Ierosolyma eis to ieron* kai perivlepsamenos panta opse edi ousis tes oras exelthen eis Vithanian meta ton dodeka.
verses.translation: And Jesus entered into Jerusalem, and into the temple: and when he had looked round about upon all things, and now the eventide was come, he went out unto Bethany with the twelve.

verses.original: Καὶ τῇ ἐπαύριον ἐξελθόντων αὐτῶν ἀπὸ Βηθανίας ἐπείνασεν.
verses.translit: Kai te epayrion exelthonton auton apo Vithanias epeinasen.
verses.translation: And on the morrow, when they were come from Bethany, he was hungry:

verses.original: καὶ ἰδὼν συκῆν ⸀ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἔχουσαν φύλλα ἦλθεν εἰ ἄρα ⸂τι εὑρήσει⸃ ἐν αὐτῇ, καὶ ἐλθὼν ἐπʼ αὐτὴν οὐδὲν εὗρεν εἰ μὴ φύλλα, ⸂ὁ γὰρ καιρὸς οὐκ ἦν⸃ σύκων.
verses.translit: kai idon syken apo makrothen ehoysan fylla elthen ei ara ti eurisei en aute, kai elthon ep' auten ouden euren ei me fylla, o gar kairos ouk en sykon.
verses.translation: And seeing a fig tree afar off having leaves, he came, if haply he might find any thing thereon: and when he came to it, he found nothing but leaves; for the time of figs was not yet .

verses.original: καὶ ⸀ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτῇ· Μηκέτι ⸂εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα ἐκ σοῦ⸃ μηδεὶς καρπὸν φάγοι. καὶ ἤκουον οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai apokritheis eipen aute* Miketi eis ton aiona ek sou mideis karpon fagoi. kai ekoyon oi mathitai autou.
verses.translation: And Jesus answered and said unto it, No man eat fruit of thee hereafter for ever. And his disciples heard it.

verses.original: Καὶ ἔρχονται εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα. καὶ ⸀εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν ἤρξατο ἐκβάλλειν τοὺς πωλοῦντας καὶ ⸀τοὺς ἀγοράζοντας ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ, καὶ τὰς τραπέζας τῶν κολλυβιστῶν καὶ τὰς καθέδρας τῶν πωλούντων τὰς περιστερὰς κατέστρεψεν
verses.translit: Kai erhontai eis Ierosolyma. kai eiselthon eis to ieron erxato ekvallein tous polountas kai tous agorazontas en to iero, kai tas trapezas ton kollyviston kai tas kathedras ton poloynton tas peristeras katestrepsen
verses.translation: And they come to Jerusalem: and Jesus went into the temple, and began to cast out them that sold and bought in the temple, and overthrew the tables of the moneychangers, and the seats of them that sold doves;

verses.original: καὶ οὐκ ἤφιεν ἵνα τις διενέγκῃ σκεῦος διὰ τοῦ ἱεροῦ,
verses.translit: kai ouk efien ina tis dienegke skeuos dia tou ierou,
verses.translation: And would not suffer that any man should carry any vessel through the temple.

verses.original: καὶ ἐδίδασκεν ⸂καὶ ἔλεγεν⸃ ⸀αὐτοῖς· Οὐ γέγραπται ὅτι Ὁ οἶκός μου οἶκος προσευχῆς κληθήσεται πᾶσιν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν; ὑμεῖς δὲ ⸀πεποιήκατε αὐτὸν σπήλαιον λῃστῶν.
verses.translit: kai edidasken kai elegen autois* Ou gegraptai oti O oikos moy oikos proseyhes klithisetai pasin tois ethnesin; umeis de pepoiikate auton spilaion leston.
verses.translation: And he taught, saying unto them, Is it not written, My house shall be called of all nations the house of prayer? but ye have made it a den of thieves.

verses.original: καὶ ἤκουσαν οἱ ⸂ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς⸃, καὶ ἐζήτουν πῶς αὐτὸν ἀπολέσωσιν· ἐφοβοῦντο γὰρ αὐτόν, ⸂πᾶς γὰρ⸃ ὁ ὄχλος ἐξεπλήσσετο ἐπὶ τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai ekoysan oi arhiereis kai oi grammateis, kai ezitoyn pos auton apolesosin* efovounto gar auton, pas gar o ohlos exeplisseto epi te didahe autou.
verses.translation: And the scribes and chief priests heard it , and sought how they might destroy him: for they feared him, because all the people was astonished at his doctrine.

verses.original: Καὶ ⸀ὅταν ὀψὲ ἐγένετο, ⸀ἐξεπορεύοντο ἔξω τῆς πόλεως.
verses.translit: Kai otan opse egeneto, exeporeyonto exo tes poleos.
verses.translation: And when even was come, he went out of the city.

verses.original: Καὶ ⸂παραπορευόμενοι πρωῒ⸃ εἶδον τὴν συκῆν ἐξηραμμένην ἐκ ῥιζῶν.
verses.translit: Kai paraporeyomenoi proi eidon ten syken exirammenin ek Rizon.
verses.translation: And in the morning, as they passed by, they saw the fig tree dried up from the roots.

verses.original: καὶ ἀναμνησθεὶς ὁ Πέτρος λέγει αὐτῷ· Ῥαββί, ἴδε ἡ συκῆ ἣν κατηράσω ἐξήρανται.
verses.translit: kai anamnistheis o Petros legei auto* Ravvi, ide e syke en katiraso exirantai.
verses.translation: And Peter calling to remembrance saith unto him, Master, behold, the fig tree which thou cursedst is withered away.

verses.original: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ἔχετε πίστιν θεοῦ·
verses.translit: kai apokritheis o Iisous legei autois* Ehete pistin theou*
verses.translation: And Jesus answering saith unto them, Have faith in God.

verses.original: ⸀ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ὃς ἂν εἴπῃ τῷ ὄρει τούτῳ· Ἄρθητι καὶ βλήθητι εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν, καὶ μὴ διακριθῇ ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ ἀλλὰ ⸀πιστεύῃ ὅτι ⸂ὃ λαλεῖ γίνεται, ἔσται αὐτῷ⸃.
verses.translit: amen lego umin oti os an eipe to orei toyto* Arthiti kai vlithiti eis ten thalassan, kai me diakrithe en te kardia autou alla pisteye oti o lalei ginetai, estai auto.
verses.translation: For verily I say unto you, That whosoever shall say unto this mountain, Be thou removed, and be thou cast into the sea; and shall not doubt in his heart, but shall believe that those things which he saith shall come to pass; he shall have whatsoever he saith.

verses.original: διὰ τοῦτο λέγω ὑμῖν, πάντα ὅσα ⸂προσεύχεσθε καὶ αἰτεῖσθε⸃, πιστεύετε ὅτι ⸀ἐλάβετε, καὶ ἔσται ὑμῖν.
verses.translit: dia touto lego umin, panta osa proseyhesthe kai aiteisthe, pisteyete oti elavete, kai estai umin.
verses.translation: Therefore I say unto you, What things soever ye desire, when ye pray, believe that ye receive them , and ye shall have them .

verses.original: καὶ ὅταν ⸀στήκετε προσευχόμενοι, ἀφίετε εἴ τι ἔχετε κατά τινος, ἵνα καὶ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς ἀφῇ ὑμῖν τὰ παραπτώματα ⸀ὑμῶν.
verses.translit: kai otan stikete proseyhomenoi, afiete ei ti ehete kata tinos, ina kai o pater umon o en tois ouranois afe umin ta paraptomata umon.
verses.translation: And when ye stand praying, forgive, if ye have ought against any: that your Father also which is in heaven may forgive you your trespasses.
But if ye do not forgive, neither will your Father which is in heaven forgive your trespasses.

verses.original: Καὶ ἔρχονται πάλιν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα. καὶ ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ περιπατοῦντος αὐτοῦ ἔρχονται πρὸς αὐτὸν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι
verses.translit: Kai erhontai palin eis Ierosolyma. kai en to iero peripatountos autou erhontai pros auton oi arhiereis kai oi grammateis kai oi presvyteroi
verses.translation: And they come again to Jerusalem: and as he was walking in the temple, there come to him the chief priests, and the scribes, and the elders,

verses.original: καὶ ⸀ἔλεγον αὐτῷ· Ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιεῖς; ⸀ἢ τίς σοι ⸂ἔδωκεν τὴν ἐξουσίαν ταύτην⸃ ἵνα ταῦτα ποιῇς;
verses.translit: kai elegon auto* En poia exoysia tauta poieis; e tis soi edoken ten exoysian taytin ina tauta poies;
verses.translation: And say unto him, By what authority doest thou these things? and who gave thee this authority to do these things?

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ⸀Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἐπερωτήσω ⸀ὑμᾶς ἕνα λόγον, καὶ ἀποκρίθητέ μοι, καὶ ἐρῶ ὑμῖν ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιῶ·
verses.translit: o de Iisous eipen autois* Eperotiso umas ena logon, kai apokrithite moi, kai ero umin en poia exoysia tauta poio*
verses.translation: And Jesus answered and said unto them, I will also ask of you one question, and answer me, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things.

verses.original: τὸ βάπτισμα ⸀τὸ Ἰωάννου ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἦν ἢ ἐξ ἀνθρώπων; ἀποκρίθητέ μοι.
verses.translit: to vaptisma to Ioannoy ex ouranou en e ex anthropon; apokrithite moi.
verses.translation: The baptism of John, was it from heaven, or of men? answer me.

verses.original: καὶ ⸀διελογίζοντο πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς λέγοντες· ⸂Τί εἴπωμεν;⸃ ἐὰν εἴπωμεν· Ἐξ οὐρανοῦ, ἐρεῖ· Διὰ τί ⸀οὖν οὐκ ἐπιστεύσατε αὐτῷ;
verses.translit: kai dielogizonto pros eaytous legontes* Ti eipomen; ean eipomen* Ex ouranou, erei* Dia ti oun ouk episteysate auto;
verses.translation: And they reasoned with themselves, saying, If we shall say, From heaven; he will say, Why then did ye not believe him?

verses.original: ἀλλὰ εἴπωμεν· Ἐξ ἀνθρώπων;— ἐφοβοῦντο τὸν ⸀ὄχλον, ἅπαντες γὰρ εἶχον τὸν Ἰωάννην ⸂ὄντως ὅτι⸃ προφήτης ἦν.
verses.translit: alla eipomen* Ex anthropon;-- efovounto ton ohlon, apantes gar eihon ton Ioannin ontos oti profitis en.
verses.translation: But if we shall say, Of men; they feared the people: for all men counted John, that he was a prophet indeed.

verses.original: καὶ ἀποκριθέντες ⸂τῷ Ἰησοῦ λέγουσιν⸃· Οὐκ οἴδαμεν. καὶ ὁ ⸀Ἰησοῦς λέγει αὐτοῖς· Οὐδὲ ἐγὼ λέγω ὑμῖν ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιῶ.
verses.translit: kai apokrithentes to Iisou legoysin* Ouk oidamen. kai o Iisous legei autois* Oude ego lego umin en poia exoysia tauta poio.
verses.translation: And they answered and said unto Jesus, We cannot tell. And Jesus answering saith unto them, Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.

verses.original: Καὶ ἤρξατο αὐτοῖς ἐν παραβολαῖς ⸀λαλεῖν· Ἀμπελῶνα ⸂ἄνθρωπος ἐφύτευσεν⸃, καὶ περιέθηκεν φραγμὸν καὶ ὤρυξεν ὑπολήνιον καὶ ᾠκοδόμησεν πύργον, καὶ ἐξέδετο αὐτὸν γεωργοῖς, καὶ ἀπεδήμησεν.
verses.translit: Kai erxato autois en paravolais lalein* Ampelona anthropos efyteysen, kai periethiken fragmon kai oryxen upolinion kai okodomisen pyrgon, kai exedeto auton georgois, kai apedimisen.
verses.translation: And he began to speak unto them by parables. A certain man planted a vineyard, and set an hedge about it , and digged a place for the winefat, and built a tower, and let it out to husbandmen, and went into a far country.

verses.original: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν πρὸς τοὺς γεωργοὺς τῷ καιρῷ δοῦλον, ἵνα παρὰ τῶν γεωργῶν λάβῃ ἀπὸ ⸂τῶν καρπῶν⸃ τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος·
verses.translit: kai apesteilen pros tous georgous to kairo doulon, ina para ton georgon lave apo ton karpon tou ampelonos*
verses.translation: And at the season he sent to the husbandmen a servant, that he might receive from the husbandmen of the fruit of the vineyard.

verses.original: ⸀καὶ λαβόντες αὐτὸν ἔδειραν καὶ ἀπέστειλαν κενόν.
verses.translit: kai lavontes auton edeiran kai apesteilan kenon.
verses.translation: And they caught him , and beat him, and sent him away empty.

verses.original: καὶ πάλιν ἀπέστειλεν πρὸς αὐτοὺς ἄλλον δοῦλον· ⸀κἀκεῖνον ⸀ἐκεφαλίωσαν καὶ ⸀ἠτίμασαν.
verses.translit: kai palin apesteilen pros autous allon doulon* kakeinon ekefaliosan kai etimasan.
verses.translation: And again he sent unto them another servant; and at him they cast stones, and wounded him in the head, and sent him away shamefully handled.

verses.original: ⸀καὶ ἄλλον ἀπέστειλεν· κἀκεῖνον ἀπέκτειναν, καὶ πολλοὺς ἄλλους, ⸂οὓς μὲν δέροντες οὓς δὲ ἀποκτέννοντες⸃.
verses.translit: kai allon apesteilen* kakeinon apekteinan, kai pollous alloys, ous men derontes ous de apoktennontes.
verses.translation: And again he sent another; and him they killed, and many others; beating some, and killing some.

verses.original: ἔτι ⸂ἕνα εἶχεν, υἱὸν ἀγαπητόν· ἀπέστειλεν⸃ αὐτὸν ⸂ἔσχατον πρὸς αὐτοὺς⸃ λέγων ὅτι Ἐντραπήσονται τὸν υἱόν μου.
verses.translit: eti ena eihen, yion agapiton* apesteilen auton eshaton pros autous legon oti Entrapisontai ton yion moy.
verses.translation: Having yet therefore one son, his wellbeloved, he sent him also last unto them, saying, They will reverence my son.

verses.original: ἐκεῖνοι δὲ οἱ γεωργοὶ ⸂πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς εἶπαν⸃ ὅτι Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ κληρονόμος· δεῦτε ἀποκτείνωμεν αὐτόν, καὶ ἡμῶν ἔσται ἡ κληρονομία.
verses.translit: ekeinoi de oi georgoi pros eaytous eipan oti Outos estin o klironomos* deute apokteinomen auton, kai emon estai e klironomia.
verses.translation: But those husbandmen said among themselves, This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and the inheritance shall be ours.

verses.original: καὶ λαβόντες ⸂ἀπέκτειναν αὐτόν, καὶ ἐξέβαλον αὐτὸν⸃ ἔξω τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος.
verses.translit: kai lavontes apekteinan auton, kai exevalon auton exo tou ampelonos.
verses.translation: And they took him, and killed him , and cast him out of the vineyard.

verses.original: ⸀τί ποιήσει ὁ κύριος τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος; ἐλεύσεται καὶ ἀπολέσει τοὺς γεωργούς, καὶ δώσει τὸν ἀμπελῶνα ἄλλοις.
verses.translit: ti poiisei o kyrios tou ampelonos; eleysetai kai apolesei tous georgoys, kai dosei ton ampelona allois.
verses.translation: What shall therefore the lord of the vineyard do? he will come and destroy the husbandmen, and will give the vineyard unto others.

verses.original: οὐδὲ τὴν γραφὴν ταύτην ἀνέγνωτε· Λίθον ὃν ἀπεδοκίμασαν οἱ οἰκοδομοῦντες, οὗτος ἐγενήθη εἰς κεφαλὴν γωνίας·
verses.translit: oude ten grafen taytin anegnote* Lithon on apedokimasan oi oikodomountes, outos egenithi eis kefalen gonias*
verses.translation: And have ye not read this scripture; The stone which the builders rejected is become the head of the corner:

verses.original: παρὰ κυρίου ἐγένετο αὕτη, καὶ ἔστιν θαυμαστὴ ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς ἡμῶν;
verses.translit: para kyrioy egeneto auti, kai estin thaymaste en ofthalmois emon;
verses.translation: This was the Lord’s doing, and it is marvellous in our eyes?

verses.original: Καὶ ἐζήτουν αὐτὸν κρατῆσαι, καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν τὸν ὄχλον, ἔγνωσαν γὰρ ὅτι πρὸς αὐτοὺς τὴν παραβολὴν εἶπεν. καὶ ἀφέντες αὐτὸν ἀπῆλθον.
verses.translit: Kai ezitoyn auton kratesai, kai efovithisan ton ohlon, egnosan gar oti pros autous ten paravolen eipen. kai afentes auton apelthon.
verses.translation: And they sought to lay hold on him, but feared the people: for they knew that he had spoken the parable against them: and they left him, and went their way.

verses.original: Καὶ ἀποστέλλουσιν πρὸς αὐτόν τινας τῶν Φαρισαίων καὶ τῶν Ἡρῳδιανῶν ἵνα αὐτὸν ἀγρεύσωσιν λόγῳ.
verses.translit: Kai apostelloysin pros auton tinas ton Farisaion kai ton Erodianon ina auton agreysosin logo.
verses.translation: And they send unto him certain of the Pharisees and of the Herodians, to catch him in his words.

verses.original: ⸀καὶ ἐλθόντες λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Διδάσκαλε, οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἀληθὴς εἶ καὶ οὐ μέλει σοι περὶ οὐδενός, οὐ γὰρ βλέπεις εἰς πρόσωπον ἀνθρώπων, ἀλλʼ ἐπʼ ἀληθείας τὴν ὁδὸν τοῦ θεοῦ διδάσκεις· ἔξεστιν ⸂δοῦναι κῆνσον Καίσαρι⸃ ἢ οὔ; δῶμεν ἢ μὴ δῶμεν;
verses.translit: kai elthontes legoysin auto* Didaskale, oidamen oti alithes ei kai ou melei soi peri oudenos, ou gar vlepeis eis prosopon anthropon, all' ep' alitheias ten odon tou theou didaskeis* exestin dounai kenson Kaisari e ou; domen e me domen;
verses.translation: And when they were come, they say unto him, Master, we know that thou art true, and carest for no man: for thou regardest not the person of men, but teachest the way of God in truth: Is it lawful to give tribute to Cæsar, or not?

verses.original: ὁ δὲ εἰδὼς αὐτῶν τὴν ὑπόκρισιν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τί με πειράζετε; φέρετέ μοι δηνάριον ἵνα ἴδω.
verses.translit: o de eidos auton ten upokrisin eipen autois* Ti me peirazete; ferete moi dinarion ina ido.
verses.translation: Shall we give, or shall we not give? But he, knowing their hypocrisy, said unto them, Why tempt ye me? bring me a penny, that I may see it .

verses.original: οἱ δὲ ἤνεγκαν. καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τίνος ἡ εἰκὼν αὕτη καὶ ἡ ἐπιγραφή; οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Καίσαρος.
verses.translit: oi de enegkan. kai legei autois* Tinos e eikon auti kai e epigrafi; oi de eipan auto* Kaisaros.
verses.translation: And they brought it . And he saith unto them, Whose is this image and superscription? And they said unto him, Cæsar’s.

verses.original: ⸂ὁ δὲ⸃ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν ⸀αὐτοῖς· ⸂Τὰ Καίσαρος ἀπόδοτε⸃ Καίσαρι καὶ τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ τῷ θεῷ. καὶ ⸀ἐξεθαύμαζον ἐπʼ αὐτῷ.
verses.translit: o de Iisous eipen autois* Ta Kaisaros apodote Kaisari kai ta tou theou to theo. kai exethaymazon ep' auto.
verses.translation: And Jesus answering said unto them, Render to Cæsar the things that are Cæsar’s, and to God the things that are God’s. And they marvelled at him.

verses.original: Καὶ ἔρχονται Σαδδουκαῖοι πρὸς αὐτόν, οἵτινες λέγουσιν ἀνάστασιν μὴ εἶναι, καὶ ⸀ἐπηρώτων αὐτὸν λέγοντες·
verses.translit: Kai erhontai Saddoykaioi pros auton, oitines legoysin anastasin me einai, kai epiroton auton legontes*
verses.translation: Then come unto him the Sadducees, which say there is no resurrection; and they asked him, saying,

verses.original: Διδάσκαλε, Μωϋσῆς ἔγραψεν ἡμῖν ὅτι ἐάν τινος ἀδελφὸς ἀποθάνῃ καὶ καταλίπῃ γυναῖκα καὶ ⸂μὴ ἀφῇ τέκνον⸃, ἵνα λάβῃ ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ τὴν ⸀γυναῖκα καὶ ἐξαναστήσῃ σπέρμα τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: Didaskale, Moyses egrapsen emin oti ean tinos adelfos apothane kai katalipe gynaika kai me afe teknon, ina lave o adelfos autou ten gynaika kai exanastise sperma to adelfo autou.
verses.translation: Master, Moses wrote unto us, If a man’s brother die, and leave his wife behind him , and leave no children, that his brother should take his wife, and raise up seed unto his brother.

verses.original: ἑπτὰ ἀδελφοὶ ἦσαν· καὶ ὁ πρῶτος ἔλαβεν γυναῖκα, καὶ ἀποθνῄσκων οὐκ ἀφῆκεν σπέρμα·
verses.translit: epta adelfoi esan* kai o protos elaven gynaika, kai apothneskon ouk afeken sperma*
verses.translation: Now there were seven brethren: and the first took a wife, and dying left no seed.

verses.original: καὶ ὁ δεύτερος ἔλαβεν αὐτήν, καὶ ἀπέθανεν ⸂μὴ καταλιπὼν⸃ σπέρμα, καὶ ὁ τρίτος ὡσαύτως·
verses.translit: kai o deyteros elaven autin, kai apethanen me katalipon sperma, kai o tritos osaytos*
verses.translation: And the second took her, and died, neither left he any seed: and the third likewise.

verses.original: καὶ ⸂οἱ ἑπτὰ⸃ οὐκ ἀφῆκαν σπέρμα· ⸀ἔσχατον πάντων ⸂καὶ ἡ γυνὴ ἀπέθανεν⸃.
verses.translit: kai oi epta ouk afekan sperma* eshaton panton kai e gyne apethanen.
verses.translation: And the seven had her, and left no seed: last of all the woman died also.

verses.original: ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει ⸂ὅταν ἀναστῶσιν⸃ τίνος αὐτῶν ἔσται γυνή; οἱ γὰρ ἑπτὰ ἔσχον αὐτὴν γυναῖκα.
verses.translit: en te anastasei otan anastosin tinos auton estai gyni; oi gar epta eshon auten gynaika.
verses.translation: In the resurrection therefore, when they shall rise, whose wife shall she be of them? for the seven had her to wife.

verses.original: ⸂ἔφη αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς⸃· Οὐ διὰ τοῦτο πλανᾶσθε μὴ εἰδότες τὰς γραφὰς μηδὲ τὴν δύναμιν τοῦ θεοῦ;
verses.translit: efi autois o Iisous* Ou dia touto planasthe me eidotes tas grafas mide ten dynamin tou theou;
verses.translation: And Jesus answering said unto them, Do ye not therefore err, because ye know not the scriptures, neither the power of God?

verses.original: ὅταν γὰρ ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστῶσιν, οὔτε γαμοῦσιν οὔτε ⸀γαμίζονται, ἀλλʼ εἰσὶν ὡς ⸀ἄγγελοι ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς·
verses.translit: otan gar ek nekron anastosin, oute gamousin oute gamizontai, all' eisin os aggeloi en tois ouranois*
verses.translation: For when they shall rise from the dead, they neither marry, nor are given in marriage; but are as the angels which are in heaven.

verses.original: περὶ δὲ τῶν νεκρῶν ὅτι ἐγείρονται οὐκ ἀνέγνωτε ἐν τῇ βίβλῳ Μωϋσέως ἐπὶ τοῦ βάτου ⸀πῶς εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ θεὸς λέγων· Ἐγὼ ὁ θεὸς Ἀβραὰμ καὶ ⸂ὁ θεὸς Ἰσαὰκ καὶ ὁ⸃ θεὸς Ἰακώβ;
verses.translit: peri de ton nekron oti egeirontai ouk anegnote en te vivlo Moyseos epi tou vatoy pos eipen auto o theos legon* Ego o theos Avraam kai o theos Isaak kai o theos Iakov;
verses.translation: And as touching the dead, that they rise: have ye not read in the book of Moses, how in the bush God spake unto him, saying, I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob?

verses.original: οὐκ ἔστιν ⸀θεὸς νεκρῶν ⸀ἀλλὰ ζώντων· ⸀πολὺ πλανᾶσθε.
verses.translit: ouk estin theos nekron alla zonton* polu planasthe.
verses.translation: He is not the God of the dead, but the God of the living: ye therefore do greatly err.

verses.original: Καὶ προσελθὼν εἷς τῶν γραμματέων ἀκούσας αὐτῶν συζητούντων, ⸀ἰδὼν ὅτι καλῶς ⸂ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς⸃, ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτόν· Ποία ἐστὶν ⸂ἐντολὴ πρώτη πάντων⸃;
verses.translit: Kai proselthon eis ton grammateon akoysas auton syzitoynton, idon oti kalos apekrithi autois, epirotisen auton* Poia estin entole proti panton;
verses.translation: And one of the scribes came, and having heard them reasoning together, and perceiving that he had answered them well, asked him, Which is the first commandment of all?

verses.original: ⸂ἀπεκρίθη ὁ Ἰησοῦς⸃ ὅτι Πρώτη ⸀ἐστίν· Ἄκουε, Ἰσραήλ, κύριος ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶν κύριος εἷς ἐστιν,
verses.translit: apekrithi o Iisous oti Proti estin* Akoye, Israil, kyrios o theos emon kyrios eis estin,
verses.translation: And Jesus answered him, The first of all the commandments is , Hear, O Israel; The Lord our God is one Lord:

verses.original: καὶ ἀγαπήσεις κύριον τὸν θεόν σου ἐξ ὅλης ⸀τῆς καρδίας σου καὶ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς ψυχῆς σου καὶ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς διανοίας σου καὶ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς ἰσχύος ⸀σου.
verses.translit: kai agapiseis kyrion ton theon soy ex olis tes kardias soy kai ex olis tes psyhes soy kai ex olis tes dianoias soy kai ex olis tes ishyos soy.
verses.translation: And thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind, and with all thy strength: this is the first commandment.

verses.original: ⸀δευτέρα αὕτη· Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν. μείζων τούτων ἄλλη ἐντολὴ οὐκ ἔστιν.
verses.translit: deytera auti* Agapiseis ton plision soy os seayton. meizon toyton alli entole ouk estin.
verses.translation: And the second is like, namely this, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. There is none other commandment greater than these.

verses.original: ⸀καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ γραμματεύς· Καλῶς, διδάσκαλε, ἐπʼ ἀληθείας εἶπες ὅτι εἷς ἐστιν καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν ἄλλος πλὴν αὐτοῦ·
verses.translit: kai eipen auto o grammateys* Kalos, didaskale, ep' alitheias eipes oti eis estin kai ouk estin allos plen autou*
verses.translation: And the scribe said unto him, Well, Master, thou hast said the truth: for there is one God; and there is none other but he:

verses.original: καὶ τὸ ἀγαπᾶν αὐτὸν ἐξ ὅλης ⸀τῆς καρδίας καὶ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς ⸀συνέσεως καὶ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς ἰσχύος καὶ τὸ ἀγαπᾶν τὸν πλησίον ὡς ἑαυτὸν ⸀περισσότερόν ἐστιν πάντων τῶν ὁλοκαυτωμάτων καὶ θυσιῶν.
verses.translit: kai to agapan auton ex olis tes kardias kai ex olis tes syneseos kai ex olis tes ishyos kai to agapan ton plision os eayton perissoteron estin panton ton olokaytomaton kai thysion.
verses.translation: And to love him with all the heart, and with all the understanding, and with all the soul, and with all the strength, and to love his neighbour as himself, is more than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.

verses.original: καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἰδὼν ⸀αὐτὸν ὅτι νουνεχῶς ἀπεκρίθη εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Οὐ μακρὰν εἶ ἀπὸ τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ θεοῦ. καὶ οὐδεὶς οὐκέτι ἐτόλμα αὐτὸν ἐπερωτῆσαι.
verses.translit: kai o Iisous idon auton oti noynehos apekrithi eipen auto* Ou makran ei apo tes vasileias tou theou. kai oudeis ouketi etolma auton eperotesai.
verses.translation: And when Jesus saw that he answered discreetly, he said unto him, Thou art not far from the kingdom of God. And no man after that durst ask him any question.

verses.original: Καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἔλεγεν διδάσκων ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ· Πῶς λέγουσιν οἱ γραμματεῖς ὅτι ὁ χριστὸς υἱὸς ⸂Δαυίδ ἐστιν⸃;
verses.translit: Kai apokritheis o Iisous elegen didaskon en to iero* Pos legoysin oi grammateis oti o hristos yios Dayid estin;
verses.translation: And Jesus answered and said, while he taught in the temple, How say the scribes that Christ is the Son of David?

verses.original: ⸀αὐτὸς Δαυὶδ εἶπεν ἐν ⸂τῷ πνεύματι τῷ⸃ ἁγίῳ· ⸀Εἶπεν ⸀κύριος τῷ κυρίῳ μου· ⸀Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου ⸀ὑποκάτω τῶν ποδῶν σου.
verses.translit: autos Dayid eipen en to pneymati to agio* Eipen kyrios to kyrio moy* Kathoy ek dexion moy eos an tho tous ehthroys soy upokato ton podon soy.
verses.translation: For David himself said by the Holy Ghost, The LORD said to my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand, till I make thine enemies thy footstool.

verses.original: ⸀αὐτὸς Δαυὶδ λέγει αὐτὸν κύριον, καὶ πόθεν ⸂αὐτοῦ ἐστιν υἱός⸃; καὶ ὁ πολὺς ὄχλος ἤκουεν αὐτοῦ ἡδέως.
verses.translit: autos Dayid legei auton kyrion, kai pothen autou estin yios; kai o polus ohlos ekoyen autou edeos.
verses.translation: David therefore himself calleth him Lord; and whence is he then his son? And the common people heard him gladly.

verses.original: Καὶ ⸂ἐν τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ ἔλεγεν⸃· Βλέπετε ἀπὸ τῶν γραμματέων τῶν θελόντων ἐν στολαῖς περιπατεῖν καὶ ἀσπασμοὺς ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς
verses.translit: Kai en te didahe autou elegen* Vlepete apo ton grammateon ton thelonton en stolais peripatein kai aspasmous en tais agorais
verses.translation: And he said unto them in his doctrine, Beware of the scribes, which love to go in long clothing, and love salutations in the marketplaces,

verses.original: καὶ πρωτοκαθεδρίας ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ πρωτοκλισίας ἐν τοῖς δείπνοις,
verses.translit: kai protokathedrias en tais synagogais kai protoklisias en tois deipnois,
verses.translation: And the chief seats in the synagogues, and the uppermost rooms at feasts:

verses.original: οἱ κατεσθίοντες τὰς οἰκίας τῶν χηρῶν καὶ προφάσει μακρὰ προσευχόμενοι· οὗτοι λήμψονται περισσότερον κρίμα.
verses.translit: oi katesthiontes tas oikias ton hiron kai profasei makra proseyhomenoi* outoi limpsontai perissoteron krima.
verses.translation: Which devour widows’ houses, and for a pretence make long prayers: these shall receive greater damnation.

verses.original: Καὶ ⸀καθίσας ⸀κατέναντι τοῦ γαζοφυλακίου ἐθεώρει πῶς ὁ ὄχλος βάλλει χαλκὸν εἰς τὸ γαζοφυλάκιον· καὶ πολλοὶ πλούσιοι ἔβαλλον πολλά·
verses.translit: Kai kathisas katenanti tou gazofylakioy etheorei pos o ohlos vallei halkon eis to gazofylakion* kai polloi ploysioi evallon polla*
verses.translation: And Jesus sat over against the treasury, and beheld how the people cast money into the treasury: and many that were rich cast in much.

verses.original: καὶ ἐλθοῦσα μία χήρα πτωχὴ ἔβαλεν λεπτὰ δύο, ὅ ἐστιν κοδράντης.
verses.translit: kai elthousa mia hira ptohe evalen lepta dyo, o estin kodrantis.
verses.translation: And there came a certain poor widow, and she threw in two mites, which make a farthing.

verses.original: καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ ⸀εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἡ χήρα αὕτη ἡ πτωχὴ πλεῖον πάντων ⸀ἔβαλεν τῶν βαλλόντων εἰς τὸ γαζοφυλάκιον·
verses.translit: kai proskalesamenos tous mathitas autou eipen autois* Amen lego umin oti e hira auti e ptohe pleion panton evalen ton vallonton eis to gazofylakion*
verses.translation: And he called unto him his disciples, and saith unto them, Verily I say unto you, That this poor widow hath cast more in, than all they which have cast into the treasury:

verses.original: πάντες γὰρ ἐκ τοῦ περισσεύοντος αὐτοῖς ἔβαλον, αὕτη δὲ ἐκ τῆς ὑστερήσεως αὐτῆς πάντα ὅσα εἶχεν ἔβαλεν, ὅλον τὸν βίον αὐτῆς.
verses.translit: pantes gar ek tou perisseyontos autois evalon, auti de ek tes usteriseos autes panta osa eihen evalen, olon ton vion autes.
verses.translation: For all they did cast in of their abundance; but she of her want did cast in all that she had, even all her living.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐκπορευομένου αὐτοῦ ἐκ τοῦ ἱεροῦ λέγει αὐτῷ εἷς τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ· Διδάσκαλε, ἴδε ποταποὶ λίθοι καὶ ποταπαὶ οἰκοδομαί.
verses.translit: Kai ekporeyomenoy autou ek tou ierou legei auto eis ton mathiton autou* Didaskale, ide potapoi lithoi kai potapai oikodomai.
verses.translation: And as he went out of the temple, one of his disciples saith unto him, Master, see what manner of stones and what buildings are here !

verses.original: καὶ ὁ ⸀Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Βλέπεις ταύτας τὰς μεγάλας οἰκοδομάς; οὐ μὴ ἀφεθῇ ⸀ὧδε λίθος ἐπὶ ⸀λίθον ὃς οὐ μὴ καταλυθῇ.
verses.translit: kai o Iisous eipen auto* Vlepeis taytas tas megalas oikodomas; ou me afethe ode lithos epi lithon os ou me katalythe.
verses.translation: And Jesus answering said unto him, Seest thou these great buildings? there shall not be left one stone upon another, that shall not be thrown down.

verses.original: Καὶ καθημένου αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸ Ὄρος τῶν Ἐλαιῶν κατέναντι τοῦ ἱεροῦ ⸀ἐπηρώτα αὐτὸν κατʼ ἰδίαν Πέτρος καὶ Ἰάκωβος καὶ Ἰωάννης καὶ Ἀνδρέας·
verses.translit: Kai kathimenoy autou eis to Oros ton Elaion katenanti tou ierou epirota auton kat' idian Petros kai Iakovos kai Ioannis kai Andreas*
verses.translation: And as he sat upon the mount of Olives over against the temple, Peter and James and John and Andrew asked him privately,

verses.original: Εἰπὸν ἡμῖν πότε ταῦτα ἔσται, καὶ τί τὸ σημεῖον ὅταν μέλλῃ ⸂ταῦτα συντελεῖσθαι πάντα⸃.
verses.translit: Eipon emin pote tauta estai, kai ti to simeion otan melle tauta synteleisthai panta.
verses.translation: Tell us, when shall these things be? and what shall be the sign when all these things shall be fulfilled?

verses.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ⸂ἤρξατο λέγειν αὐτοῖς⸃· Βλέπετε μή τις ὑμᾶς πλανήσῃ·
verses.translit: o de Iisous erxato legein autois* Vlepete mi tis umas planise*
verses.translation: And Jesus answering them began to say, Take heed lest any man deceive you:

verses.original: ⸀πολλοὶ ἐλεύσονται ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου λέγοντες ὅτι Ἐγώ εἰμι, καὶ πολλοὺς πλανήσουσιν.
verses.translit: polloi eleysontai epi to onomati moy legontes oti Ego eimi, kai pollous planisoysin.
verses.translation: For many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ ; and shall deceive many.

verses.original: ὅταν δὲ ⸀ἀκούσητε πολέμους καὶ ἀκοὰς πολέμων, μὴ θροεῖσθε· ⸀δεῖ γενέσθαι, ἀλλʼ οὔπω τὸ τέλος.
verses.translit: otan de akoysite polemoys kai akoas polemon, me throeisthe* dei genesthai, all' oupo to telos.
verses.translation: And when ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars, be ye not troubled: for such things must needs be; but the end shall not be yet.

verses.original: ἐγερθήσεται γὰρ ἔθνος ἐπʼ ἔθνος καὶ βασιλεία ἐπὶ βασιλείαν, ⸀ἔσονται σεισμοὶ κατὰ τόπους, ⸁ἔσονται ⸀λιμοί· ⸀ἀρχὴ ὠδίνων ταῦτα.
verses.translit: egerthisetai gar ethnos ep' ethnos kai vasileia epi vasileian, esontai seismoi kata topoys, esontai limoi* arhe odinon tauta.
verses.translation: For nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom: and there shall be earthquakes in divers places, and there shall be famines and troubles: these are the beginnings of sorrows.

verses.original: βλέπετε δὲ ὑμεῖς ἑαυτούς· ⸀παραδώσουσιν ὑμᾶς εἰς συνέδρια καὶ εἰς συναγωγὰς δαρήσεσθε καὶ ἐπὶ ἡγεμόνων καὶ βασιλέων σταθήσεσθε ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς.
verses.translit: vlepete de umeis eaytoys* paradosoysin umas eis synedria kai eis synagogas darisesthe kai epi egemonon kai vasileon stathisesthe eneken emou eis martyrion autois.
verses.translation: But take heed to yourselves: for they shall deliver you up to councils; and in the synagogues ye shall be beaten: and ye shall be brought before rulers and kings for my sake, for a testimony against them.

verses.original: καὶ εἰς πάντα τὰ ἔθνη ⸂πρῶτον δεῖ⸃ κηρυχθῆναι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον.
verses.translit: kai eis panta ta ethni proton dei kiryhthenai to euaggelion.
verses.translation: And the gospel must first be published among all nations.

verses.original: ⸂καὶ ὅταν⸃ ⸀ἄγωσιν ὑμᾶς παραδιδόντες, μὴ προμεριμνᾶτε τί ⸀λαλήσητε, ἀλλʼ ὃ ἐὰν δοθῇ ὑμῖν ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ τοῦτο λαλεῖτε, οὐ γάρ ἐστε ὑμεῖς οἱ λαλοῦντες ἀλλὰ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον.
verses.translit: kai otan agosin umas paradidontes, me promerimnate ti lalisite, all' o ean dothe umin en ekeine te ora touto laleite, ou gar este umeis oi lalountes alla to pneuma to agion.
verses.translation: But when they shall lead you , and deliver you up, take no thought beforehand what ye shall speak, neither do ye premeditate: but whatsoever shall be given you in that hour, that speak ye: for it is not ye that speak, but the Holy Ghost.

verses.original: ⸂καὶ παραδώσει⸃ ἀδελφὸς ἀδελφὸν εἰς θάνατον καὶ πατὴρ τέκνον, καὶ ἐπαναστήσονται τέκνα ἐπὶ γονεῖς καὶ θανατώσουσιν αὐτούς·
verses.translit: kai paradosei adelfos adelfon eis thanaton kai pater teknon, kai epanastisontai tekna epi goneis kai thanatosoysin autoys*
verses.translation: Now the brother shall betray the brother to death, and the father the son; and children shall rise up against their parents, and shall cause them to be put to death.

verses.original: καὶ ἔσεσθε μισούμενοι ὑπὸ πάντων διὰ τὸ ὄνομά μου. ὁ δὲ ὑπομείνας εἰς τέλος οὗτος σωθήσεται.
verses.translit: kai esesthe misoymenoi upo panton dia to onoma moy. o de upomeinas eis telos outos sothisetai.
verses.translation: And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved.

verses.original: Ὅταν δὲ ἴδητε τὸ βδέλυγμα τῆς ἐρημώσεως ⸀ἑστηκότα ὅπου οὐ δεῖ, ὁ ἀναγινώσκων νοείτω, τότε οἱ ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ φευγέτωσαν εἰς τὰ ὄρη,
verses.translit: Otan de idite to vdelygma tes erimoseos estikota opoy ou dei, o anaginoskon noeito, tote oi en te Ioydaia feygetosan eis ta ori,
verses.translation: But when ye shall see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing where it ought not, (let him that readeth understand,) then let them that be in Judæa flee to the mountains:

verses.original: ⸀ὁ ἐπὶ τοῦ δώματος μὴ ⸀καταβάτω μηδὲ εἰσελθάτω ⸂τι ἆραι⸃ ἐκ τῆς οἰκίας αὐτοῦ,
verses.translit: o epi tou domatos me katavato mide eiselthato ti arai ek tes oikias autou,
